question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool assign a probability of at least 60% on 2025-10-17 to the Fed lowering the target federal funds upper bound by at least 25 basis points at its next scheduled FOMC meeting after 2025-09-17?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a market-implied indicator of whether the Federal Reserve is on a path toward further easing by January 2026. After the 2025-09-17 FOMC meeting, multiple contemporaneous reports stated that the Fed cut rates by 25 bps to a target range of 4.00%-4.25%, implying an upper bound of 4.25%, and that at least one dissenter preferred a larger 50 bps cut. See reporting from Mint (https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/us-fed-meeting-jerome-powell-led-fomc-cuts-interest-rate-by-25-bps-5-key-highlights-11758139030274.html) and other outlets in the prompt. The official Federal Reserve page publishes FOMC statements and implementation details for the target range: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

The CME FedWatch Tool translates 30-Day Federal Funds futures pricing into implied probabilities for upcoming FOMC target ranges. Because the ultimate question asks whether the Fed will deliver a cumulative 50+ bps decrease by the January 2026 meeting relative to the pre-meeting level, rising market-implied odds of another cut at the next meeting are an informative near-term signal that easing momentum is building. CME describes FedWatch methodology here: https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/quikstrike/cme-fedwatch-tool-user-guide.html and hosts the tool here: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html.

A threshold of 60% is chosen to avoid an almost-certain or almost-impossible event while still capturing a meaningful market consensus for another cut at the next meeting. If markets strongly expect another cut in October/November, that generally makes a 50+ bps cumulative decline by January more plausible; if not, the January 2026 50+ bps outcome becomes less likely.

Sources:
Federal Reserve - Monetary Policy / Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
Federal Reserve - FOMC calendars: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
CME FedWatch Tool User Guide: https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/quikstrike/cme-fedwatch-tool-user-guide.html
Mint report on 2025-09-17 FOMC cut: https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/us-fed-meeting-jerome-powell-led-fomc-cuts-interest-rate-by-25-bps-5-key-highlights-11758139030274.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 inclusive, the value observed on 2025-10-17 on the CME FedWatch Tool for the next scheduled FOMC meeting after 2025-09-17 shows a probability of at least 60.0% for any target range whose upper bound is at least 25 basis points below 4.25% (the upper bound reported after the 2025-09-17 meeting). In practice, this means the summed probability on 2025-10-17 of target ranges with an upper bound of 4.00% or lower must be at least 60.0%.

This question resolves No if the corresponding summed probability on 2025-10-17 is below 60.0%.

Primary source: CME FedWatch Tool, https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Methodology reference: CME FedWatch Tool User Guide, https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/quikstrike/cme-fedwatch-tool-user-guide.html
Reference for the current target range / upper bound after the 2025-09-17 meeting: Federal Reserve monetary policy page, https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If the FedWatch page layout changes, resolution should use the official CME page or downloadable/archived CME data showing the same probabilities for 2025-10-17. If CME ceases publishing the tool entirely before 2025-10-17 and no archived official CME value for that date is available, this question should be considered unresolvable. If the next scheduled FOMC meeting after 2025-09-17 is canceled or materially restructured such that CME no longer lists meeting-specific probabilities in the usual way, resolve using the closest official CME meeting-specific probabilities corresponding to that next scheduled decision date; if no such official CME probabilities exist, unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question concerns whether the Fed will have cut rates by 50+ bps by the January 2026 meeting. Market-implied odds of another cut at the very next meeting are a strong early indicator of the direction and pace of easing. If markets assign a high probability to another near-term cut, that materially raises the plausibility of cumulative 50+ bps easing by January.

question: Trump declassifies UFO files in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump administration declassifies any previously classified files pertaining to extraterrestrial life and/or unexplained arial phenomena by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements of declassifications that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not count.

The primary resolution source for declassification will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets or a House committee officially announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, a hearing or public briefing scheduled to occur by 2025-12-31 that is primarily focused on UAPs, UFOs, or extraterrestrial-related government records?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether the Trump administration will declassify UFO/UAP-related files in 2025 is whether congressional allies create formal public pressure through an announced hearing or briefing on the topic. Recent reporting indicates sustained political interest in UAP transparency. ABC News reported in June 2025 that the Pentagon's All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) is working to release more information and that some lawmakers are pressing for release of government files related to extraterrestrial mysteries: https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/ufo-sleuths-secrets-trump-era-investigations/story?id=122535535 . Reporting in August 2025 also highlighted Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, described as chair of the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, publicly pushing for more access to hidden UAP information: https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/trump-insider-makes-bombshell-claim-on-ufo-and-aliens-very-credible-people-have-101755071299632.html .

Formal congressional scheduling matters because public hearings and briefings often precede document releases, inter-agency requests, and politically salient transparency actions. The House Oversight Committee and related House entities routinely publish official hearing notices, and Congress.gov tracks formal committee activity and hearing materials. If such a hearing is officially announced in September 2025, it would be evidence that the issue is active enough to increase odds of declassification by year-end.

Relevant official sources for such announcements include the House Oversight Committee website https://oversight.house.gov/ , Congress.gov committee activity pages https://www.congress.gov/committees , and the House Clerk hearing repository https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar .

Sources:
ABC News - UFO sleuths want fewer secrets in Trump-era investigations - https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/ufo-sleuths-secrets-trump-era-investigations/story?id=122535535
Hindustan Times - Trump insider makes bombshell claim on UFO and aliens - https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/trump-insider-makes-bombshell-claim-on-ufo-and-aliens-very-credible-people-have-101755071299632.html
U.S. House Oversight Committee - https://oversight.house.gov/
Congress.gov Committees - https://www.congress.gov/committees
U.S. House Committee Calendar - https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), an official U.S. House source announces a hearing or public briefing that is scheduled to occur on or before 2025-12-31 and whose primary subject is UAPs, UFOs, unidentified anomalous phenomena, extraterrestrial life, or declassification of related government records.

Qualifying official sources are limited to: (a) a notice, press release, event page, or hearing page on an official House committee or task force website such as https://oversight.house.gov/ ; (b) an entry in the official House committee calendar at https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar ; or (c) an official Congress.gov committee activity or hearing listing at https://www.congress.gov/committees .

The announcement must clearly indicate that the event is a hearing or public briefing, and the event description, title, or accompanying materials must make UAP/UFO/extraterrestrial-related records a primary topic rather than a passing mention.

This question resolves No if no such official announcement appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

If an event is merely rumored in media reports but not officially announced by one of the above official sources within the resolution window, it does not count. If an announcement occurs within the window for an event scheduled after 2025-12-31, it does not count. If the relevant official pages are unavailable at resolution time, archived versions from the Internet Archive https://web.archive.org/ may be used as a fallback, provided they clearly show the publication date and content of the official announcement.
subquestions.rationale: An officially announced House hearing or briefing would be a concrete signal of elite political attention and pressure for disclosure, which could materially raise the odds of executive-branch declassification later in 2025 without merely restating the ultimate question.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for September 2025 be at least 4.4% as reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics?
subquestions.background_information:
Labor-market deterioration is one of the clearest near-term indicators for a U.S. recession, and it is central to recession-dating frameworks such as the Sahm rule. The official U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) is published monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) in the Employment Situation release. As of the latest data available before 2025-09-01, recent commentary cited the unemployment rate at 4.2% and noted that a rise of roughly 0.1 percentage point per month through September would bring recession-warning indicators closer to their trigger range. See BLS labor force statistics at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm and BLS series page for the unemployment rate at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE .

The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will experience a recession in 2025, resolved partly by NBER recession dating or by two consecutive negative GDP quarters. Although GDP already rebounded strongly in Q2 2025 after a negative Q1, recessions often become clearer first in labor-market data rather than in contemporaneous GDP headlines. The NBER’s Business Cycle Dating Committee emphasizes broad, economy-wide indicators including employment, real income, production, and sales, not just GDP alone: https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating .

A September 2025 unemployment rate of 4.4% or higher would represent a meaningful deterioration from the roughly 4.2% level discussed in mid-2025 commentary and would be evidence that economic weakness is broadening beyond tariff- and trade-distorted GDP components. That would raise the odds that either the NBER later dates a 2025 recession or that growth weakens enough to produce another negative GDP quarter. Conversely, a September rate below 4.4% would be some evidence of continued labor-market resilience.

Sources:
BLS Employment Situation release: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm
FRED UNRATE series: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE
NBER Business Cycle Dating: https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports the U.S. seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) for September 2025 as 4.4% or higher in an Employment Situation release published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive of both dates, UTC-based for the window). It resolves No if the first BLS Employment Situation release that reports the September 2025 unemployment rate is published within that same window and reports a rate below 4.4%.

Primary resolution source: the BLS Employment Situation news release at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm . The relevant statistic is the official U-3 unemployment rate for September 2025, seasonally adjusted.

Fallback source: if the BLS news-release page is unavailable or materially altered, resolve using the St. Louis Fed FRED series UNRATE at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE , using the value labeled for 2025-09, provided it is clearly sourced from BLS.

If no BLS release containing the September 2025 unemployment rate is published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, this question should be considered unresolvable rather than defaulting to No, because the qualifying data would not have arrived within the stated resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: A rise in unemployment is a classic early signal of recession and closely related to how the NBER assesses business-cycle turning points. This is not just the ultimate question with an earlier deadline; it is a different observable indicator that helps distinguish between a temporary GDP wobble and a broader downturn.

question: Will Max Verstappen be the 2025 Drivers Champion?
description:
This market will resolve according to the driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2025 F1 season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

As soon as the results for the final scheduled race of the 2025 F1 season are known this market will resolve.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2025 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), this market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

subquestions.question: Will Max Verstappen outscore both Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris combined across all 2025 Formula 1 World Championship sessions counted for points between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a near-term performance indicator for whether Max Verstappen can still win the 2025 Drivers' Championship, without merely restating the title question. By late September, Verstappen was reported to be 69 points behind Oscar Piastri with seven rounds remaining, after winning at Monza and Baku, suggesting a Red Bull resurgence but still a substantial deficit to the McLaren drivers. Motorsport.com described Singapore as a key benchmark for Verstappen's title hopes and noted Red Bull believed it had made a significant step forward with recent upgrades: https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-heres-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappens-f1-title-hopes/10735536/

Earlier in the season, Verstappen was still viewed as clearly in contention despite trailing the McLarens. Sky Sports reported on 2025-05-29 that Verstappen was only 25 points behind Piastri at that time and that Norris and Piastri both explicitly said he remained in the title race: https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/13376163/lando-norris-and-oscar-piastri-insist-rival-max-verstappen-remains-in-2025-f1-title-race

By August, however, McLaren's drivers had become the central title protagonists. Motorsport.com wrote that, entering the final 10 races, Norris and Piastri were separated by only 9 points, with Verstappen needing unusual swings to re-enter the fight: https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/key-storylines-for-the-second-half-of-the-2025-f1-season/10726218/

A useful crux, then, is whether Verstappen can meaningfully outperform both McLarens over a defined October window. If he cannot outscore them combined over that period, his path to the championship becomes much narrower. If he can, especially over multiple grands prix and sprint sessions, that would be strong evidence that Red Bull pace and Verstappen's form are sufficient to keep the title alive.

For scoring context, Formula 1 awards championship points in grands prix to the top 10 finishers (25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1), plus one point for fastest lap only under the current regulations if applicable; sprint events also award points to the top finishers according to FIA/F1 sporting regulations and official classification. Official standings and event results are published by Formula 1 and the FIA: https://www.formula1.com/ and https://www.fia.com/

Sources:
Sky Sports - Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri insist rival Max Verstappen remains in 2025 F1 title race - https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/13376163/lando-norris-and-oscar-piastri-insist-rival-max-verstappen-remains-in-2025-f1-title-race
Motorsport.com - Key Storylines for the Second Half of the 2025 F1 Season - https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/key-storylines-for-the-second-half-of-the-2025-f1-season/10726218/
Motorsport.com - After Baku brilliance, here's why Singapore GP is key for Max Verstappen's F1 title hopes - https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-heres-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappens-f1-title-hopes/10735536/
Formula 1 official site - https://www.formula1.com/
FIA official site - https://www.fia.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Max Verstappen earns strictly more FIA Formula 1 World Drivers' Championship points than Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris combined from all points-scoring 2025 F1 championship sessions that occur between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

This question resolves No if, over the same window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive, Verstappen does not earn strictly more points than Piastri and Norris combined.

Scoring counted for this question:
- Count all official 2025 FIA Formula 1 World Championship points awarded to each of the three drivers for any sprint and grand prix sessions whose official classification is published for events occurring between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.
- Use the official championship points as reflected in Formula 1's official Drivers' Standings and/or official event classification pages on Formula1.com.
- Penalties or classification changes announced after an event but before final resolution should be incorporated if they alter the official points totals for sessions in the window.

Primary source:
- Formula 1 official Drivers' Standings: https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html/2025/drivers.html
- Formula 1 official race results archive: https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html

Fallback source if Formula1.com is unavailable or incomplete:
- FIA official documents and classifications: https://www.fia.com/documents

Method of resolution:
1. Record each driver's official championship points total immediately before the first points-scoring session on or after 2025-10-01, using Formula1.com standings.
2. Record each driver's official championship points total after the final points-scoring session held on or before 2025-10-31.
3. Compute points earned during the window for Verstappen, Piastri, and Norris by subtraction.
4. Resolve Yes if Verstappen's window total is greater than the sum of Piastri's and Norris's window totals; otherwise resolve No.

If no points-scoring 2025 F1 championship session is held between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, this question should resolve No, because Verstappen would not outscore the McLaren pair combined during the stated window.

If an event begins in the window but its relevant points-scoring session is postponed beyond 2025-10-31, those postponed points do not count. Only sessions occurring between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: Verstappen likely needs to gain points rapidly on both McLaren drivers to win the title. Whether he can outscore the two principal rivals combined over October is a strong indicator of whether the championship fight is genuinely swinging back toward him.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States announce between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22 (inclusive) that it is deploying at least one additional aircraft carrier strike group or bomber task force to the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term increase in U.S. force posture in the Middle East would be a meaningful indicator for the ultimate question because major strike operations against Iran would usually be preceded or accompanied by added air and naval assets, logistics, and signaling. The U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility includes the Middle East and surrounding region, including the Persian Gulf and Arabian Sea: https://www.centcom.mil/AREA-OF-RESPONSIBILITY/

Carrier strike groups and bomber task forces are standard instruments for U.S. coercive signaling and strike preparation. The U.S. Navy publicly tracks carrier strike group deployments and locations: https://www.navy.mil/Press-Office/News-Stories/ and the fleet overview is available via the U.S. Navy: https://www.navy.mil/

The U.S. Air Force also publicly announces bomber task force deployments and missions, including B-1, B-2, and B-52 deployments to forward regions: https://www.af.mil/News/ and U.S. Central Command regularly announces major force movements and operations: https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/

Recent reporting indicates the regional environment remains militarized after the June 2025 Israel-Iran war and subsequent U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities. Iran has continued major missile and naval drills in late 2025, including ballistic and cruise missile launches in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz, underscoring persistent escalation risk (Straits Times, Dec. 5, 2025): https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets

Because the ultimate question concerns U.S. aerial strikes on Iranian soil or official diplomatic premises, a fresh U.S. deployment of a carrier strike group or bomber task force into CENTCOM would be a concrete, observable precursor that should materially update forecasts upward.

Sources:
U.S. Central Command Area of Responsibility — https://www.centcom.mil/AREA-OF-RESPONSIBILITY/
U.S. Central Command Press Releases — https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/
U.S. Air Force News — https://www.af.mil/News/
U.S. Navy — https://www.navy.mil/
The Straits Times, Iran holds drills in Gulf — https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf-firing-ballistic-cruise-missiles-at-simulated-targets
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Central Command, U.S. Navy, or U.S. Air Force publicly announces that at least one additional aircraft carrier strike group or bomber task force is being deployed, ordered, extended, or repositioned into the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility.

For this question:
- 'Aircraft carrier strike group' means a U.S. Navy carrier strike group centered on a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier.
- 'Bomber task force' means a publicly announced deployment of U.S. strategic bombers (e.g., B-1, B-2, or B-52) to a base or operational area in the CENTCOM region under a named or clearly described bomber task force mission.
- 'Additional' means a newly announced deployment, extension, or repositioning beyond the force posture publicly acknowledged as of 2025-12-23.

Primary resolution sources will be official announcements from:
- U.S. Central Command press releases: https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/
- U.S. Department of Defense news/releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- U.S. Navy news: https://www.navy.mil/Press-Office/News-Stories/
- U.S. Air Force news: https://www.af.mil/News/

If multiple official sources conflict, the most specific later-dated official statement controls. If no official announcement is made but there is overwhelming consensus reporting from Reuters and the Associated Press citing named U.S. officials that such a deployment order occurred within the window, the question may resolve Yes based on that consensus reporting:
- Reuters World/Middle East: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/
- AP Middle East: https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east

Routine port calls, already-scheduled transits not described as a response to regional tensions, or mere speculation about possible deployments do not count. If the only evidence is anonymous-source media speculation without a clear statement that the deployment was ordered or executed within the window, resolve No. If an announcement is made after 2026-01-22 about a deployment that explicitly states the order/execution occurred between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22, it counts. Otherwise, events outside the window do not count.
subquestions.rationale: A significant U.S. reinforcement of strike-capable forces in CENTCOM is a strong leading indicator of willingness and readiness to conduct air or missile strikes on Iran, while still being distinct from the ultimate question itself.

question: Will Trump meet with Xi Jinping by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump meets with Xi Jinping between July 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs publicly announce between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 that Trump and Xi are expected to meet in person later in 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A formal public announcement of an expected in-person Trump-Xi meeting would be a strong near-term indicator for whether such a meeting actually occurs by the end of October. Current reporting already links progress in U.S.-China trade diplomacy to the possibility of a leaders' meeting. Reuters-republished coverage on 2025-07-28 said a 90-day extension of the tariff truce was widely expected and 'may ease way for Trump-Xi meet,' with reporting that a meeting could occur in late October or early November: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/US-China-trade-truce-extension-seen-may-ease-way-for-Trump-Xi-meet-50624653/ . Other reports on the Stockholm talks similarly said an extended truce could create space for a Trump-Xi meeting: https://www.indiatoday.in/world/us-news/story/us-china-trade-truce-extension-trump-xi-meet-stockholm-talks-2766457-2025-07-28 and https://www.firstpost.com/world/very-close-to-china-deal-trump-hopeful-as-trade-negotiators-meet-in-stockholm-13942274.html .

As of 2025-09-01, there is no public indication in the materials provided that either government has officially announced a Trump-Xi summit date, venue, or expectation. Because state visits and leader summits typically require advance diplomatic signaling, a public announcement by either side before October would be an informative leading indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question. Relevant official channels likely to carry such announcements include White House statements and schedules at https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ and China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs news/press releases at https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/ .

Sources:
MarketScreener/Reuters - US-China trade truce extension seen, may ease way for Trump-Xi meet: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/US-China-trade-truce-extension-seen-may-ease-way-for-Trump-Xi-meet-50624653/
India Today - Trump to meet Xi? US, China to resume talks in effort to extend trade truce: https://www.indiatoday.in/world/us-news/story/us-china-trade-truce-extension-trump-xi-meet-stockholm-talks-2766457-2025-07-28

White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China (English): https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either (a) the White House or (b) the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China publishes an official statement, readout, advisory, schedule, press release, spokesperson transcript, or equivalent public communication explicitly indicating that Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are expected or planned to meet in person later in calendar year 2025.

Qualifying examples include language such as: 'President Trump will meet President Xi,' 'the two leaders are expected to meet,' 'preparations are underway for a Trump-Xi summit,' or an official schedule/advisory naming both leaders for a bilateral meeting. The announcement does not need to specify a date before 2025-10-31, but it must clearly refer to an in-person meeting expected later in 2025.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official public announcement appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

For resolution, primary sources are:
- White House official site, including the Briefing Room and presidential schedule materials: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs official English site, including news, spokesperson transcripts, and statements: https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/

If one of these sites is unavailable, archived versions or mirrors of the same official materials may be used, provided the content is clearly attributable to the same government source. If only credible media report an expected meeting without any qualifying official public announcement from either government during the window, the question resolves No. If an announcement is made outside the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public official announcement of an expected Trump-Xi in-person meeting would materially raise the odds of the ultimate event occurring by October 31, while the absence of such signaling by October 1 would be evidence against sufficient diplomatic momentum.

question: Will Artificial Intelligence be TIME's Person of the Year for 2025?
description:
If listed person/thing is named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if listed person is named TIME's Person of the Year either alone or in conjunction with any other person or thing which is not named in this market, so long as the term is explicitly named. 

For example, if the Person of the Year is "Donald Trump and the MAGA movement", this would qualify to resolve this market to “Trump”. However if the Person of the Year is "The MAGA movement", this would not qualify to resolve this market to “Trump” regardless of whether Trump is depicted on the cover. 

If two or more people or things which are named in this market are named TIME's Person of the Year, this market will resolve in favor of whichever person or thing is listed first. For example if TIME's Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, the market for Joe Biden would resolve to “Yes” and the market for Kamala Harris would resolve to “No”. 

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. Other Time webpages which differ from the cover will not be considered.

This market can resolve after the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is announced by TIME magazine. If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: this event is mutually exclusive.

subquestions.question: Will TIME publish at least one new AI-focused cover story between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive) in which the cover line explicitly contains the phrase "Artificial Intelligence" or the standalone term "AI"?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME has recently been devoting substantial editorial attention to artificial intelligence. In August 2025, TIME published its TIME100 AI 2025 list, describing the list as the result of months of research and consultation with industry leaders, which suggests sustained editorial investment in AI as a major public theme. See TIME100 AI coverage and related reporting: https://time.com/collections/time100-ai-2025/ and https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2025/08/30/tahnoon-bin-zayed-named-in-time100-ai-2025-list . TIME has also prominently featured AI in prior years through recurring franchises and cover/feature packages, indicating that AI is an editorially salient topic rather than a one-off story. If TIME continues to elevate AI onto its cover in September 2025, that would be an observable signal that its editors see AI as one of the defining forces of the year—relevant evidence for whether AI could ultimately be selected as 2025 Person of the Year.

This is not the same as asking whether AI will be Person of the Year. Many cover stories do not become Person of the Year, but a fresh AI-centered cover in September would indicate unusually high editorial salience, which should update forecasts upward relative to a world where TIME's covers in this period focus instead on war, U.S. politics, natural disasters, or individual political figures.

Sources:
TIME100 AI 2025 collection: https://time.com/collections/time100-ai-2025/
The Star on TIME100 AI 2025: https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2025/08/30/tahnoon-bin-zayed-named-in-time100-ai-2025-list
TIME homepage / magazine covers archive entry point: https://time.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), TIME publishes at least one new magazine cover story for the U.S. or global print magazine in which the cover text explicitly includes either the exact phrase "Artificial Intelligence" or the standalone acronym "AI" (case-insensitive) as part of the main cover line or a clearly readable secondary cover line.

This question resolves No if no such TIME cover is published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Resolution will be based primarily on TIME's official site and official cover images, including pages on https://time.com/ and any relevant cover or issue pages hosted on time.com. If TIME maintains an official covers archive or issue page showing the relevant cover, that will be used. If TIME publishes multiple regional or subscriber/newsstand variants, any official TIME cover variant published in the window counts, provided it is clearly a TIME magazine cover and the qualifying text appears on the cover itself.

Important clarifications:
- Only covers first published during the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 count.
- Mere article headlines on time.com do not count unless they correspond to an official magazine cover.
- The term "AI" must appear as the standalone acronym on the cover, not merely as part of another word.
- If the cover story is about a specific company or person and discusses AI in the article but the cover text does not explicitly contain "Artificial Intelligence" or standalone "AI," it does not count.

Primary source for resolution: https://time.com/
Fallback source: TIME's official magazine/cover pages on time.com, if separately hosted. If TIME's site becomes unavailable, archived snapshots from the Internet Archive of official TIME cover pages may be used as a fallback: https://web.archive.org/ .
subquestions.rationale: A new AI-focused TIME cover before October would be a strong early indicator that TIME's editors view AI as one of the year's defining themes. Since Person of the Year is an editorial judgment about who or what most shaped the year, elevated cover-level attention to AI should materially increase the plausibility that AI itself could be chosen in December.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will there be a publicly acknowledged interdiction or boarding by U.S. military or U.S. Coast Guard personnel of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel in the Caribbean Sea between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful near-term indicator for direct U.S.–Venezuela military engagement is whether the crisis escalates into hands-on maritime enforcement involving Venezuelan vessels. As of late August 2025, the U.S. had surged naval assets into the Caribbean near Venezuela. Newsweek reported on 2025-08-30 that the U.S. had more than 4,500 personnel in the Southern Caribbean, including multiple destroyers, amphibious ships, a cruiser, and a littoral combat ship, with Coast Guard and law-enforcement detachments embarked for interdiction work: https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2100000 . AFP similarly reported on 2025-08-26 that the U.S. had sent three destroyers and roughly 4,000 Marines to the region, with additional ships inbound: https://www.barrons.com/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near-c0f9f2d8 .

On the Venezuelan side, AFP reported Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced warship and drone patrols, including larger vessels in territorial waters, in response to the U.S. buildup: https://www.barrons.com/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near-c0f9f2d8 . Newsweek also reported Maduro had denounced the deployment as a threat to sovereignty and announced maritime patrols with drones and naval vessels: https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2100000 .

A boarding/interdiction of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel by U.S. military or Coast Guard personnel would be a concrete, observable escalation in operational friction short of outright bilateral combat. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it does not require an exchange of force between the U.S. and Venezuelan militaries, but it would plausibly increase the chance of such engagement by creating opportunities for confrontation at sea, especially given the stated U.S. counternarcotics mission and Venezuela's announced coastal patrol response.

Sources:
Newsweek - USS Lake Erie crosses Panama Canal as Trump's Caribbean buildup continues - https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-panama-canal-trump-caribbean-buildup-venezuela-2100000
Barron's/AFP - Venezuela deploys warships, drones as US destroyers draw near - https://www.barrons.com/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-as-us-destroyers-draw-near-c0f9f2d8
U.S. Coast Guard - About the U.S. Coast Guard - https://www.uscg.mil/About/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, at least one Venezuelan-flagged vessel is publicly reported by an authoritative source as having been interdicted, boarded, or seized by U.S. military personnel or U.S. Coast Guard personnel in the Caribbean Sea.

For this question:
- "Venezuelan-flagged vessel" means a vessel described in reporting or official statements as registered in Venezuela, sailing under the Venezuelan flag, or explicitly identified as Venezuelan.
- "U.S. military or U.S. Coast Guard personnel" includes the U.S. Navy, U.S. Marine Corps, and U.S. Coast Guard. A boarding by a mixed team counts if U.S. military or Coast Guard personnel are clearly stated to have participated.
- "Publicly acknowledged" means confirmed in at least one official statement from the U.S. government (for example U.S. Southern Command, U.S. Coast Guard, Department of Defense, or Department of Justice) or by at least two independent credible news outlets citing named officials or documentary evidence.
- The incident must occur in the Caribbean Sea; events solely in the Pacific, Atlantic outside the Caribbean, or inland waters do not count.
- Mere shadowing, hailing, warnings, overflight, or attempted approaches without an actual boarding/interdiction/seizure do not count.
- Boarding by non-U.S. partner states without U.S. personnel physically participating does not count.
- If a qualifying incident allegedly occurs within the window but is not publicly acknowledged until later, it still counts, provided the reporting clearly states the interdiction/boarding itself occurred between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.
- If reporting is too ambiguous to determine whether the vessel was Venezuelan-flagged, whether U.S. personnel physically participated, or whether the event occurred within the window, the question should resolve No unless later clarification from an authoritative source settles the ambiguity before final resolution.

Primary resolution sources:
- U.S. Coast Guard news releases: https://www.news.uscg.mil/
- U.S. Southern Command news: https://www.southcom.mil/MEDIA/NEWS-ARTICLES/
- U.S. Department of Defense news: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- U.S. Department of Justice press releases: https://www.justice.gov/news

Secondary sources for corroboration if needed:
- Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/
- Associated Press Latin America: https://apnews.com/hub/latin-america
- AFP English feed via major syndicators such as Barron's: https://www.barrons.com/

If no qualifying interdiction/boarding/seizure is publicly acknowledged as specified above for the period between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. boarding or interdiction of a Venezuelan-flagged vessel would be a strong operational escalation that increases opportunities for Venezuelan military intervention, retaliation, or miscalculation. It is a meaningful early indicator of whether the maritime standoff is moving from signaling into direct encounters, without merely restating the ultimate engagement question.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 inclusive, that its Austin Robotaxi service has opened to the general public rather than remaining invite-only or limited to testers?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term crux for whether Tesla will launch a qualifying driverless Robotaxi service by October 31 is whether Tesla first broadens access from its current limited pilot to the general public. Multiple pre-September reports say Tesla's Austin Robotaxi service exists but is not yet a fully open public service. ABC7 reported on 2025-08-18 that Tesla had launched a robotaxi pilot in Austin on 2025-06-22, but that it was invite-only, geographically limited, and used a front-seat safety monitor rather than fully driverless operation: https://abc7news.com/post/how-mercedes-benz-beat-tesla-become-1st-offer-level-3-autonomous-personal-car-driverless-tomorrow/17025582/ . GuruFocus similarly reported on 2025-08-22 that Tesla's Austin robotaxi pilot had a limited fleet and small user base, and cited Elon Musk saying the service was slated to open to the public in September: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3013882/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi . Tesla North also reported on 2025-08-21 that the Austin robotaxi beta would open to the general public in September: https://teslanorth.com/2025/08/21/tesla-hints-at-chicago-robotaxi-launch-with-new-job-listings/ . NewsBytes likewise summarized Musk as confirming a public rollout in September: https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/musk-confirms-tesla-robotaxi-rollout-for-the-public-in-september/story .

This is informative because an open-to-general-public announcement would be a concrete commercialization step that plausibly precedes, and may be necessary for, any later qualifying fully driverless public service. It is not the same as the ultimate question: the service could open to the public while still using a safety monitor or other non-qualifying supervision, but such an opening would still be evidence that Tesla is operationalizing and scaling the product.

Sources:
ABC7 San Francisco - How Mercedes-Benz beat Tesla to become 1st to offer level 3 autonomous personal car: https://abc7news.com/post/how-mercedes-benz-beat-tesla-become-1st-offer-level-3-autonomous-personal-car-driverless-tomorrow/17025582/
GuruFocus - Barclays Expects Long Approval Process for Tesla's Robotaxi: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3013882/barclays-expects-long-approval-process-for-teslas-tsla-robotaxi
Tesla North - Tesla Hints at Chicago Robotaxi Launch with New Job Listings: https://teslanorth.com/2025/08/21/tesla-hints-at-chicago-robotaxi-launch-with-new-job-listings/
NewsBytes - Musk confirms Tesla robotaxi rollout for the public in September: https://www.newsbytesapp.com/news/science/musk-confirms-tesla-robotaxi-rollout-for-the-public-in-september/story
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 inclusive, Tesla publicly states that the Austin Robotaxi service is open to members of the general public, meaning access is no longer restricted solely to employees, invite-only users, closed-beta testers, or similar limited cohorts.

Qualifying evidence must come from at least one of the following publicly accessible sources dated within the window 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-08: (a) an official Tesla post or page, including Tesla's website or newsroom (https://www.tesla.com/ , https://www.tesla.com/blog ); (b) a public statement from Elon Musk or Tesla on X that explicitly says the Austin service is now open to the public (https://x.com/elonmusk , https://x.com/Tesla ); or (c) at least two independent reputable news reports published during the window that quote or document Tesla making such an announcement.

The announcement must specifically concern Austin, Texas. Statements merely saying Tesla hopes, plans, or expects to open later do not count. Reports that the service remains invite-only, requires a code, or is limited to a waitlist/test cohort do not count as Yes. Whether the service is fully driverless is irrelevant for this subquestion.

If by 2025-09-08 23:59:59 UTC no such public announcement is available, resolve No.

If the relevant official source is deleted or inaccessible, archived copies and contemporaneous reporting from Reuters or other major outlets may be used as fallback evidence. Suggested resolution sources include Tesla official pages (https://www.tesla.com/), Tesla on X (https://x.com/Tesla), Elon Musk on X (https://x.com/elonmusk), and Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: Opening Austin Robotaxi access to the general public is a meaningful operational and commercial milestone distinct from the ultimate question. If Tesla cannot even broaden access beyond a limited pilot by early September, that is negative evidence for a qualifying driverless public launch by late October. If it does broaden access, that materially increases the plausibility of later removing the remaining supervision constraints.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI publicly releases a standalone web browser that is intended for general web browsing and is available for use by the public in at least one country or region by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes," such a browser must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling free waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, a beta, preview, or waitlist for a new standalone desktop or mobile application explicitly described as a web browser or as being built for general web browsing?
subquestions.background_information:
A public browser launch by OpenAI by late October would likely be preceded by an earlier observable commitment signal: a public beta, preview, or waitlist announcement for a standalone browser product. This is distinct from the ultimate question because it asks about an earlier product-stage milestone rather than full public release.

There is relevant competitive pressure in the market. Perplexity has already launched an agentic browser, Comet, in July 2025, according to Windows Central, and the article also notes OpenAI as a rumored entrant alongside other AI-browser efforts: https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you. Anthropic has also moved toward browser-use products, though via a Chrome extension in closed beta rather than a standalone browser; ZDNet reported this on 2025-08-28: https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/.

Meanwhile, OpenAI has recently been shipping more end-user and developer-facing products at a rapid cadence. Reporting on late-August releases describes OpenAI expanding Codex into IDEs and GitHub workflows (WinBuzzer, 2025-08-28): https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent-with-ide-integration-gpt-5-power-and-github-reviews-xcxwbn/ and making its Realtime API generally available for voice agents (PYMNTS, 2025-08-28): https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2025/openai-says-new-speech-to-speech-model-designed-for-customer-support/. This recent launch tempo makes a browser-related preview or waitlist a plausible near-term leading indicator if a full browser release is coming by October.

The threshold here is meaningful because a public browser beta/preview/waitlist announcement would indicate that OpenAI has progressed beyond rumor into public go-to-market execution. At the same time, it is not so strong as to merely restate the ultimate question: Open beta, preview, or waitlist status can happen without a general-public browser becoming available by the final deadline.

Sources:
Windows Central - Let me scam that for you. https://www.windowscentral.com/software-apps/let-me-scam-that-for-you
ZDNet - Anthropic's Claude Chrome browser extension rolls out - how to get early access. https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/
WinBuzzer - OpenAI Supercharges Codex AI Coding Agent With IDE Integration, GPT-5 Power, and GitHub Reviews. https://winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent-with-ide-integration-gpt-5-power-and-github-reviews-xcxwbn/
PYMNTS - OpenAI Says New Speech-to-Speech Model Designed for Customer Support. https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2025/openai-says-new-speech-to-speech-model-designed-for-customer-support/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), OpenAI makes a public announcement of a new product that satisfies all of the following:
1. The product is a standalone software application (desktop and/or mobile app), not merely a browser extension, plugin, SDK, API, feature inside ChatGPT, or integration within a third-party browser.
2. OpenAI explicitly describes it as a "browser," "web browser," or as a product intended for general web browsing.
3. OpenAI publicly announces that the product is available via a beta, preview, or waitlist open to the general public in at least one country or region.

This question resolves No if no such announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

Closed betas, invite-only private tests, leaked builds, job postings, code references, or credible media reports without a public OpenAI announcement do not count. Browser extensions or in-browser assistants do not count. If OpenAI announces only an API, operator, or browsing feature within ChatGPT, that does not count.

Primary source: official OpenAI communication channels, including the OpenAI blog/newsroom and official OpenAI X/Twitter or other verified company accounts.
- OpenAI News: https://openai.com/news/
- OpenAI Blog index: https://openai.com/blog/
- OpenAI X account: https://x.com/OpenAI

If there is ambiguity about whether the product is standalone or intended for general web browsing, a consensus of at least two credible technology outlets may be used as secondary evidence, provided they are clearly interpreting an official OpenAI announcement rather than rumor. Examples of secondary sources include The Verge (https://www.theverge.com/), TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/), and Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/).

If OpenAI announces such a product during the window but states that public beta/preview/waitlist access will begin only after 2025-10-01, this question resolves No. If the announcement is made within the window and public beta/preview/waitlist access is stated to be open immediately within the window, it resolves Yes.
subquestions.rationale: A public beta/preview/waitlist announcement for a standalone browser is a strong leading indicator that OpenAI is serious about a browser launch and has advanced far enough in productization, branding, and distribution to make the ultimate October release more likely. It is also not just the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, because it concerns an earlier-stage public commitment rather than public availability of the browser itself.

question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) or Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) issue a new advisory between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 reporting a threat, attack, boarding, detention, mine risk, or official warning specifically affecting commercial vessel transit in or immediately adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term precursor to an actual closure of the Strait of Hormuz would likely be a sharp deterioration in the maritime security environment, reflected in official or industry security advisories to shipping. Iran has a long history of ship seizures, harassment, and threats in Gulf waters. The U.S. Energy Information Administration says roughly 20% of global petroleum liquids consumption moved through the Strait of Hormuz in 2024, making it one of the world's most important energy chokepoints: https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65764 . Reuters and other outlets reported in June 2025 that heightened U.S.-Iran tensions were already causing some operators to reduce transits, while shipping groups warned that any Iranian retaliation against vessels would likely reduce traffic further: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-tensions-slow-tanker-traffic-through-strait-hormuz-trade-group-2025-06-23/ . Reports in June 2025 also stated that Iran's parliament had approved or backed a measure to close the Strait, though implementation would require action by higher authorities such as the Supreme National Security Council; this indicates that closure rhetoric had already moved beyond mere speculation: https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-of-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2745323-2025-06-22 and https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-on-iran-tehrans-top-security-council-to-decide-on-strait-of-hormuz-closure-after-parliamentary-nod/articleshow/122013935.cms . Official maritime warning channels are therefore useful leading indicators: if they begin reporting new threats or incidents specifically tied to Hormuz transit, that would materially raise the probability of an eventual Iranian restriction or closure attempt. UKMTO publishes notices to merchant shipping in the Middle East region: https://www.ukmto.org/ . JMIC, based in Bahrain, publishes regional maritime security advisories for commercial shipping: https://www.jmic-bahrain.com/ .

Sources:
U.S. EIA Today in Energy — World oil transit chokepoints / Strait of Hormuz https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=65764
Reuters — US-Iran tensions slow tanker traffic through Strait of Hormuz: trade group https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-iran-tensions-slow-tanker-traffic-through-strait-hormuz-trade-group-2025-06-23/
India Today — Iran approves closure of oil corridor, Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes: Report https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2745323-2025-06-22
Times of India — Tehran's top security council to decide on Strait of Hormuz closure after parliamentary nod https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/middle-east/us-strikes-on-iran-tehrans-top-security-council-to-decide-on-strait-of-hormuz-closure-after-parliamentary-nod/articleshow/122013935.cms
UKMTO official site https://www.ukmto.org/
JMIC official site https://www.jmic-bahrain.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), either UKMTO or JMIC publishes at least one new advisory, warning, incident bulletin, or notice that explicitly refers to commercial vessel transit in the Strait of Hormuz (or the Hormuz Traffic Separation Scheme / approaches immediately adjacent to the Strait) and states one or more of the following: (a) a threat or attack against a merchant/commercial vessel; (b) boarding, seizure, detention, or harassment of a merchant/commercial vessel; (c) a mine, explosive, missile, drone, or similar kinetic risk to commercial navigation; or (d) an official warning that commercial vessels should avoid, delay, or exercise exceptional caution specifically when transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying UKMTO or JMIC publication appears during the window from 2025-11-06 through 2025-12-06 inclusive.

Resolution should use the official UKMTO alerts/news page and official JMIC advisories archive as primary sources: https://www.ukmto.org/ and https://www.jmic-bahrain.com/ . If one site is unavailable at resolution time, archived copies on the organization's official social channels or the Internet Archive may be used to verify publication timing and contents. General regional advisories that mention the Gulf, Arabian Sea, or Red Sea without specifically affecting transit in or immediately adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz do not count. Advisories first published before 2025-11-06 do not count, even if still active during the window. If an incident occurs during the window but is not publicly reported by UKMTO or JMIC until after 2025-12-06, it does not count. If publication dates cannot be established from official pages or reliable archives, the question should resolve as unresolvable rather than inferred from secondary media alone.
subquestions.rationale: A formal maritime security warning specific to Hormuz transit would be a strong early signal that conditions are moving from rhetorical threats toward operational disruption. Such advisories often precede or accompany reductions in tanker traffic, spikes in insurance costs, and naval incidents, all of which are meaningful indicators for the ultimate question of whether Iran will actually attempt to close or severely restrict passage through the Strait.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses shows 'Wicked: For Good' (2025) as the film with the highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will Fandango list "Wicked: For Good" among its top 3 best-selling movies by weekly ticket pre-sales at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A strong early indicator for whether "Wicked: For Good" can become the top-grossing domestic calendar-release title of 2025 is unusually strong advance ticket demand well before release. The film is scheduled for U.S. theatrical release on November 21, 2025, giving it only about six weeks of domestic calendar gross in 2025; to finish #1 for the year despite that late release, it likely needs exceptional opening-weekend demand and strong pre-release momentum. Universal and trade coverage have highlighted high audience interest: the first trailer reportedly drew 113 million views in its first 24 hours, exceeding the first film's trailer according to coverage citing Universal, and the original "Wicked" was a major theatrical success with about $756 million worldwide and around $473 million domestic according to Box Office Mojo and related reporting. See Box Office Mojo for the first film's grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1262426/ and reporting on trailer interest: https://www.cbr.com/wicked-for-good-trailer-record/. Fandango regularly publishes weekly "best-selling tickets" rankings for upcoming films, which are widely cited as a public readout of near-term consumer demand: https://www.fandango.com/movie-news.

Because the ultimate market is about domestic calendar gross in 2025, a subquestion about whether the sequel reaches a very high pre-sales ranking during September would be informative: if it cannot crack the top tier of Fandango pre-sales before October, that would be some evidence against an extraordinary late-year domestic run; if it does, that supports the view that the film could open at a level needed to challenge the year's leaders.

Sources:
Box Office Mojo - Wicked (2024): https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1262426/
CBR - Wicked: For Good Has Already Beaten the First Movie in 1 Major Way Months Ahead of Release: https://www.cbr.com/wicked-for-good-trailer-record/
Fandango Movie News: https://www.fandango.com/movie-news
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Fandango publishes a weekly "best-selling tickets" or equivalent weekly ticket pre-sales ranking for movies and "Wicked: For Good" appears in the top 3 positions on that published ranking.

Primary source for resolution: Fandango's Movie News pages and articles containing weekly best-selling ticket rankings: https://www.fandango.com/movie-news

Resolution steps:
1. Review Fandango articles published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive for weekly best-selling ticket rankings.
2. If any such article explicitly lists "Wicked: For Good" in 1st, 2nd, or 3rd place, resolve Yes.
3. If no qualifying Fandango weekly ranking published in that window places the film in the top 3, resolve No.

Definitions and edge cases:
- "Wicked: For Good" includes clearly equivalent formatting of the title used by Fandango, so long as it unambiguously refers to the 2025 Universal theatrical release.
- "Weekly ticket pre-sales ranking" means a Fandango-published ranking described as weekly best-selling tickets, top advance ticket sellers, or a substantially equivalent recurring weekly chart of ticket sales on Fandango. One-off editorial lists, fan polls, or trailer-popularity lists do not count.
- If Fandango publishes multiple qualifying weekly rankings in the window, any one of them with the film in the top 3 is sufficient for Yes.
- If a relevant Fandango page is unavailable at resolution time, archived copies from the Internet Archive may be used to verify the original Fandango publication date and ranking: https://web.archive.org/ .
- If no qualifying weekly ranking is published by Fandango at all between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, resolve No rather than unresolvable, because the condition did not occur within the window.

Fallback sources for corroboration only (not primary unless Fandango pages are inaccessible): press articles that directly quote or reproduce the relevant Fandango weekly ranking, such as Deadline https://deadline.com/ or Variety https://variety.com/ .
subquestions.rationale: A late-November release can only top the domestic 2025 calendar chart if it behaves like an event movie. Reaching Fandango's top 3 weekly pre-sales rankings in September would be an early, externally visible signal of unusually strong audience demand and opening-weekend potential, which materially bears on the ultimate question without merely restating year-end box office performance.

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia officially announce the establishment of diplomatic relations between Janaury 26, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia publicly host or co-host, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, an official multilateral meeting or conference statement that explicitly includes both "normalization with Israel" and "Palestinian statehood" as linked agenda items or deliverables?
subquestions.background_information:
A key obstacle to Israel–Saudi normalization in 2025 has been Riyadh's insistence that recognition of Israel is tied to progress on Palestinian statehood and an end to the Gaza war. On 2025-07-28, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan said Saudi Arabia would not normalize relations with Israel without establishing a Palestinian state, and that normalization could only be discussed once the Gaza conflict ends and suffering is alleviated (Anadolu Ajansı, 2025-07-28: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-no-normalization-with-israel-without-establishing-palestinian-state/3642948). Earlier reporting likewise said Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman had reassured Palestinian officials that Riyadh would not normalize absent an end to the war and a two-state path (The Times of Israel, 2025-05-09: https://www.timesofisrael.com/saudi-crown-prince-said-to-reassure-abbas-deputy-riyadh-wont-ink-israel-deal/).

At the same time, Saudi Arabia has remained diplomatically active on a framework that pairs Palestinian statehood with regional normalization. A Saudi-French effort at the UN on the two-state solution explicitly focused on four pillars including international recognition of a Palestinian state and normalization with Israel, showing that Riyadh is willing to discuss normalization in a multilateral framework when tied to Palestinian-statehood diplomacy (Asharq Al-Awsat, 2025-05-24: https://english.aawsat.com/gulf/5146123-preparations-intensify-un-two-state-solution-conference-led-saudi-arabia-and). This makes near-term Saudi sponsorship of an official event explicitly linking the two issues a useful indicator: if Riyadh publicly advances such a framework in September 2025, that would be evidence that normalization remains on the active diplomatic agenda rather than fully shelved.

Because the ultimate question asks whether official diplomatic relations are established by the end of 2025, a near-term observable precursor is whether Saudi Arabia publicly creates official diplomatic space for normalization discussions at all. An explicit Saudi-hosted or Saudi-co-hosted statement that treats normalization with Israel as a live deliverable, even conditionally, would likely move forecasts upward; the absence of such language during the short window would be evidence against a rapid 2025 breakthrough.

Sources:
Anadolu Ajansı - Saudi Arabia says no normalization with Israel without establishing Palestinian state - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-no-normalization-with-israel-without-establishing-palestinian-state/3642948
The Times of Israel - Saudi crown prince reportedly reassured Abbas deputy that Riyadh won't ink deal with Israel absent end to war, two-state path - https://www.timesofisrael.com/saudi-crown-prince-said-to-reassure-abbas-deputy-riyadh-wont-ink-israel-deal/
Asharq Al-Awsat English - Preparations Intensify for UN Two-State Solution Conference Led by Saudi Arabia and France - https://english.aawsat.com/gulf/5146123-preparations-intensify-un-two-state-solution-conference-led-saudi-arabia-and
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), there is an official statement, communique, agenda document, or final declaration from either (a) the Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs, (b) the Saudi Press Agency, (c) the Saudi Embassy to the UN / Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's UN mission, or (d) an official host institution of a meeting that Saudi Arabia officially co-hosts, and that document explicitly mentions both (1) normalization with Israel (or equivalent phrases such as "normalization of relations with Israel" or "normalization between Arab states/Saudi Arabia and Israel") and (2) Palestinian statehood / two-state solution as linked agenda items, pillars, or deliverables.

The event does not need to include Israel as a participant, and it does not need to announce normalization itself. The key condition is explicit official linkage in a Saudi-hosted or Saudi-co-hosted diplomatic context during the window from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01.

This question resolves No if no such official document is published during that window.

Resolution sources, in order of priority:
1. Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs official website: https://www.mofa.gov.sa/en
2. Saudi Press Agency: https://www.spa.gov.sa/en
3. Permanent Mission of Saudi Arabia to the United Nations / related official Saudi UN pages, if available
4. If the above publish inaccessible or broken pages, archived official copies or mirrored text from UN official pages may be used, such as https://www.un.org/ or UN meeting pages, provided the text clearly identifies Saudi Arabia as host or co-host.

Edge cases:
- A mere media report quoting unnamed officials does not count without an official published document.
- A statement that mentions only Palestinian statehood, or only normalization, does not count.
- A statement using vague language like "regional peace" without explicit reference to normalization with Israel does not count.
- If an event is announced within the window but the official statement/document is first published after 2025-10-01, it does not count.
- If no authoritative official text can be located and only secondary reporting exists, the question should resolve No rather than rely on inference.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia has publicly tied normalization to Palestinian-statehood progress. A Saudi-backed official document that explicitly keeps normalization with Israel on the diplomatic agenda, in tandem with Palestinian statehood, would be a meaningful early signal that Riyadh still sees a pathway to a 2025 deal. If no such public diplomatic framing appears by 2025-10-01, that weakens the case for official normalization by year-end.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire before 2026?
description:
