subquestions.question: Will Tesla, Inc. (NASDAQ: TSLA) close below $200.00 on any regular trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
Elon Musk’s position as the world’s richest person is heavily driven by the marked-to-market value of his Tesla stake, alongside SpaceX and other holdings. Recent reporting indicates Musk remained #1 in mid- to late-2025, but with a much smaller cushion than at his late-2024 peak and with large 2025 wealth declines tied primarily to Tesla volatility. Bloomberg-based reporting in July and August 2025 said Musk had lost roughly $60B-$71B year-to-date while remaining #1, and noted rival fortunes such as Larry Ellison’s and Mark Zuckerberg’s had risen materially in 2025, making a further Tesla drawdown a meaningful indicator for whether Musk could lose the top rank before year-end. See Benzinga’s summaries of Bloomberg data: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/07/46205593/elon-musks-71-billion-wealth-wipeout-dwarfs-next-7-billionaire-decliners-combined and https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/46791278/elon-musks-wealth-takes-more-than-60-billion-hit-in-2025-as-bill-gates-also-sees-huge-losses-but-one-of-them-has-been-donating-his-entire-fortune .

Morningstar reported on 2025-08-04 that Tesla’s board approved a new Musk pay package involving 96 million shares, but those shares would not vest until 2027, so they are not an immediate near-term buffer against a 2025 decline in Musk’s Bloomberg net worth. The same report still described him as the richest person, with a fortune around $352B at that time: https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20250804266/elon-musk-to-get-29-billion-richer-as-his-pay-package-is-approved-teslas-stock-jumps .

As of late August 2025, secondary reporting on Forbes real-time rankings put Musk around $408B versus Larry Ellison around $278B and Mark Zuckerberg around $255B, implying Musk still had a large headline lead, but one importantly exposed to public-market moves in Tesla, which is updated continuously in billionaire rankings: https://www.townflex.com/top-20-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-forbes-real-time-billionaires-list/ . Bloomberg’s billionaire methodology page also states that net worth estimates are updated at the close of every trading day in New York and that publicly traded holdings are a core component of the estimates, making TSLA price action a relevant crux for Musk’s rank: https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/methodology/ .

A drop below $200 would represent a conspicuous deterioration in Tesla’s market valuation and therefore likely pressure Musk’s net worth materially. While not sufficient by itself to make him lose the #1 rank, such a move would be strong evidence that the world is moving toward the ultimate question resolving Yes.

Sources:
Benzinga - Elon Musk's $71 Billion Wealth Wipeout: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/07/46205593/elon-musks-71-billion-wealth-wipeout-dwarfs-next-7-billionaire-decliners-combined
Benzinga - Musk wealth takes more than $60 billion hit in 2025: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/25/08/46791278/elon-musks-wealth-takes-more-than-60-billion-hit-in-2025-as-bill-gates-also-sees-huge-losses-but-one-of-them-has-been-donating-his-entire-fortune
Morningstar / MarketWatch - Musk pay package approved: https://www.morningstar.com/news/marketwatch/20250804266/elon-musk-to-get-29-billion-richer-as-his-pay-package-is-approved-teslas-stock-jumps
Townflex summary of Forbes Real-Time Billionaires List: https://www.townflex.com/top-20-richest-people-in-the-world-2025-forbes-real-time-billionaires-list/
Bloomberg Billionaires Methodology: https://www.bloomberg.com/billionaires/methodology/
Macrotrends TSLA historical prices: https://www.macrotrends.net/stocks/charts/TSLA/tesla/stock-price-history
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Tesla, Inc. (ticker: TSLA) has an official regular-session closing price strictly below $200.00 USD on at least one trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Otherwise it resolves No.

Primary source: Macrotrends Tesla historical daily prices page, which publishes daily open/high/low/close data in USD: https://www.macrotrends.net/stocks/charts/TSLA/tesla/stock-price-history .

If Macrotrends is unavailable or materially delayed, use Nasdaq historical data for TSLA: https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/tsla/historical . If Nasdaq is unavailable, use Yahoo Finance historical data for TSLA: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/TSLA/history/ .

For resolution, only the official regular-session daily close counts; intraday prints, pre-market, and after-hours prices do not count. Stock splits or other corporate actions should be interpreted using the adjusted historical series as displayed by the source, so that the threshold is applied to the quoted post-adjustment daily closing price shown for the relevant date.

If no regular trading day occurs in part of the window, that does not affect resolution; only trading days from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 count. If all listed primary and fallback sources become permanently unavailable before resolution and no authoritative archived record of daily closes can be retrieved from them, this question is unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Musk’s billionaire rank is highly sensitive to Tesla’s share price because Tesla remains one of the largest and most liquid components of his wealth. A sharp TSLA decline is a meaningful early warning sign that he could lose the #1 spot later in 2025, especially given reports that competitors such as Ellison and Zuckerberg have been gaining wealth while Musk’s net worth has already fallen substantially this year.

question: Will USA win the 2025 Ryder Cup?
description:
In the 2025 Ryder Cup, scheduled for September 25-28, 2025.

If Team USA wins the 2025 Ryder Cup by finishing with more total points than Team Europe, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the Ryder Cup is postponed, this market will remain open until the tournament has been completed.

If the Ryder Cup is canceled entirely, with no make-up tournament, this market will resolve “Tie”.

subquestions.question: Will Team Europe be listed as the betting favorite over Team USA by FanDuel Sportsbook for the 2025 Ryder Cup winner market at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26 inclusive?
subquestions.background_information:
Pre-tournament betting markets are a compact indicator of aggregated information about expected team strength, injuries, course fit, home advantage, and public/news sentiment. For the 2025 Ryder Cup, Team Europe enters as the defending champion from 2023, while Team USA has home advantage at Bethpage Black in New York. The 2025 event is scheduled for September 26-28, 2025, and the competition format requires 14.5 points to win; a 14-14 tie means Europe, as the holder, retains the Cup. Several late-August previews identify the venue, format, and likely lineups, including major U.S. names such as Scottie Scheffler, Xander Schauffele, and Bryson DeChambeau, and European stars such as Rory McIlroy, Jon Rahm, Viktor Hovland, and Ludvig Åberg in media coverage of the event context. See Ryder Cup schedule/format summaries from Yahoo Sports Canada and Jagran Josh: https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/2025-ryder-cup-format-rules-203745515.html and https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/ryder-cup-2025-team-usa-vs-team-europe-dates-format-and-venue-1820000506-1. FanDuel publicly posts golf outrights, including Ryder Cup winner markets, making it a plausible observable summary of market expectations: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/golf.

Because the ultimate question is whether the USA wins, a shift to Europe being the market favorite before play starts would be evidence against a U.S. win. This is especially informative in a short-window sports forecast where direct pre-event indicators are limited and betting markets quickly incorporate lineup announcements, injury news, and sentiment.

Sources:
Yahoo Sports Canada – 2025 Ryder Cup format, rules: https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/2025-ryder-cup-format-rules-203745515.html
Jagran Josh – Ryder Cup 2025 Team USA vs Team Europe: Dates, Format and Venue: https://www.jagranjosh.com/general-knowledge/ryder-cup-2025-team-usa-vs-team-europe-dates-format-and-venue-1820000506-1
FanDuel Sportsbook Golf page: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/golf
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26 inclusive, FanDuel Sportsbook lists Team Europe with shorter outright odds than Team USA in a market clearly labeled for the 2025 Ryder Cup winner (or equivalent winner market for USA vs Europe in the 2025 Ryder Cup). It resolves No if, throughout the entire window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-26 inclusive, Team Europe is never listed with shorter outright odds than Team USA.

Primary source: FanDuel Sportsbook golf pages and/or the specific Ryder Cup market page, if available: https://sportsbook.fanduel.com/navigation/golf

For American odds, a more negative number is shorter (e.g., Europe -120 vs USA +100 means Europe is favorite). For decimal odds, a smaller number is shorter. For fractional odds, a smaller implied probability denominator/ratio should be interpreted in the standard way; if needed, convert to implied probability.

If both teams are exactly tied in price at all observed times, that does not count as Europe being the favorite. Europe must be strictly shorter than USA.

If the specific market is temporarily unavailable on some dates, resolution should use archived snapshots from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine for FanDuel pages: https://web.archive.org/ and reliable odds aggregators that archive bookmaker-specific odds and clearly identify FanDuel as the quoted bookmaker, such as Oddschecker Ryder Cup pages: https://www.oddschecker.com/golf/ryder-cup. Fallback evidence should only count if it clearly shows FanDuel's quoted odds during the window.

If no reliable record of FanDuel Ryder Cup odds can be found for the relevant window, the question should resolve Unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Sports betting markets aggregate dispersed information and are often among the best near-term predictors of match outcomes. Whether Europe becomes the market favorite before play starts is a meaningful crux for the USA-win question without merely restating it.

question: Nothing Ever Happens: Khamenei
description:
This market will resolve to “No” if any of the following conditions are met between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 ET:

- Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran
- Khamenei leaves Iran

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “Yes”.

Khamenei out as Supreme Leader of Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if Iran's Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei, is removed from power for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. Khamenei will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Supreme Leader of Iran within this market's timeframe. The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Khamenei leaves Iran:
This market will resolve to "No" if it is confirmed that Ali Khamenei has left Iran for any length of time during this market’s above-specified time frame. In cases where Ali Khamenei may have exited Iranian airspace on a plane, he must be confirmed to have exited the plane in a country other than Iran for this market to resolve to "No". If Ali Khamenei exits Iranian maritime territory on a boat to international waters, this market may resolve to "No". The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Iran publicly announce a new nationwide internet shutdown lasting at least 48 consecutive hours between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26?
subquestions.background_information:
A renewed nationwide internet shutdown would be a useful early indicator of acute regime instability in Iran. Large-scale shutdowns are often used by the Iranian state during major protest waves or security crises, and such crises could increase the chance that Ali Khamenei is removed, incapacitated, or attempts to flee Iran before the ultimate question's deadline. The user-provided reporting says Iran imposed a major internet blackout beginning on 2026-01-08 amid nationwide protests and that officials were discussing restoration around 2026-01-24 to 2026-01-25. Those same reports describe unusually severe unrest, thousands of deaths, and rumors that Khamenei had delegated day-to-day operations to his son while sheltering in a bunker, all of which suggest the regime may still be under exceptional pressure if another national shutdown is imposed. See News.com.au coverage from 2026-01-25: https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge/news-story/ and Republic World from 2026-01-25: https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/iran-supreme-leader-khamenei-reportedly-sheltering-in-underground-bunker-as-us-naval-forces-head-to-middle-east .

Independent monitoring organizations regularly track Iranian connectivity. NetBlocks reports real-time internet disruptions and has repeatedly documented Iranian shutdowns in past unrest episodes: https://netblocks.org/ . Cloudflare Radar also publishes country-level traffic patterns that can reveal sustained national connectivity collapses: https://radar.cloudflare.com/ir . Access Now's #KeepItOn campaign documents shutdowns globally and provides context on Iranian shutdown practices: https://www.accessnow.org/keepiton/ . Because the ultimate market resolves negatively if Khamenei is out or leaves Iran by late March 2026, a fresh nationwide shutdown by late February would be an observable sign that the state perceives a serious threat environment, which should update forecasts about that ultimate outcome.

Sources:
News.com.au - Iranian leader hiding, son left in charge - https://www.news.com.au/world/middle-east/iranian-leader-hiding-son-left-in-charge/news-story/
Republic World - Khamenei reportedly sheltering in underground bunker - https://www.republicworld.com/world-news/iran-supreme-leader-khamenei-reportedly-sheltering-in-underground-bunker-as-us-naval-forces-head-to-middle-east
NetBlocks - https://netblocks.org/
Cloudflare Radar (Iran) - https://radar.cloudflare.com/ir

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive), there is a publicly reported nationwide internet shutdown in Iran lasting at least 48 consecutive hours.

For this question, a "nationwide internet shutdown" means a disruption described by at least one primary monitoring source as national or near-national in scope, not merely platform-specific blocking (for example, blocking only WhatsApp or Instagram) and not merely regional/mobile-provider outages. The shutdown must last at least 48 consecutive hours within the window from 2026-02-05 to 2026-02-26.

Primary resolution sources, in order:
1. NetBlocks reporting on Iran: https://netblocks.org/ and https://x.com/netblocks
2. Cloudflare Radar country traffic data for Iran showing a corresponding national collapse in traffic: https://radar.cloudflare.com/ir
3. Access Now #KeepItOn or similar reputable digital-rights documentation: https://www.accessnow.org/keepiton/
4. Consensus of credible reporting from major outlets if the above are unavailable.

The question resolves Yes if NetBlocks explicitly reports a nationwide/national internet shutdown in Iran beginning and persisting for at least 48 consecutive hours during 2026-02-05 through 2026-02-26, or if an equivalent finding is clearly supported by Cloudflare Radar plus at least one other credible source. It resolves No if no such qualifying shutdown occurs between 2026-02-05 and 2026-02-26.

If only partial regional outages, platform blocks, throttling without clear nationwide scope, or outages shorter than 48 consecutive hours occur during 2026-02-05 to 2026-02-26, resolve No. If the evidence is too ambiguous to determine whether a nationwide shutdown of at least 48 consecutive hours occurred within the specified window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A new nationwide shutdown would be a concrete, independently monitorable sign that the regime faces another major internal security crisis. That kind of crisis materially raises the odds of elite fracture, incapacitation, emergency succession arrangements, or flight by Khamenei, without merely restating the ultimate question.

question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo not be traded?
description:
This market will resolve to the NBA team that officially acquires Giannis Antetokounmpo in a trade from the Milwaukee Bucks before the 2025-2026 NBA season trade deadline.

If Giannis Antetokounmpo is cut, retires, is not on an NBA roster as of the resolution date, or otherwise remains on the Bucks through the NBA trade deadline, this market will resolve to "Not Traded".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Milwaukee Bucks and/or the acquiring team; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Giannis Antetokounmpo publicly state between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 that he wants to remain with the Milwaukee Bucks long-term or does not want to be traded?
subquestions.background_information:
A key crux for whether Giannis is traded before the 2025-26 NBA trade deadline is his own publicly expressed preference. Recent reporting indicates the Bucks are unlikely to trade him unless he pushes for it, and that his stance is expected to clarify in the coming weeks. Forbes reported on 2025-10-09 that Milwaukee was unlikely to trade Antetokounmpo unless he pushed for it, and that he 'holds all the cards' in the situation: https://www.forbes.com/sites/bryantoporek/2025/10/09/giannis-antetokounmpo-milwaukee-bucks-are-playing-a-game-of-chicken/ . Multiple reports on 2025-12-03 said Giannis and his agent were discussing his future with the Bucks and that a resolution was expected within weeks, which makes a near-term public statement especially decision-relevant: https://sports.yahoo.com/article/report-bucks-talking-giannis-antetokounmpo-033252339.html and https://nypost.com/2025/12/03/sports/giannis-antetokounmpo-accelerates-bucks-trade-possibility-after-his-social-media-scrub/ .

The Bucks' poor start has intensified speculation. CBS Sports reported Milwaukee was 9-13 through 2025-12-02 and had lost eight of its last nine games, increasing pressure on the franchise to convince Giannis to stay: https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-bucks-are-running-out-of-time-to-convince-giannis-to-stay-in-milwaukee/ . Yahoo Sports Canada likewise reported the 9-13 start and ongoing discussions about whether his best path is to stay or move elsewhere: https://sports.yahoo.com/article/report-bucks-talking-giannis-antetokounmpo-033252339.html .

Giannis has recently sent mixed signals. Newsweek in October quoted him emphasizing loyalty to Milwaukee while also saying he could not know what the future holds: https://www.newsweek.com/sports/nba/giannis-antetokounmpo-sparks-speculation-about-his-future-milwaukee-1968382 . But recent reports also highlighted social-media changes and renewed uncertainty, including removal of Bucks references from his profiles: https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-bucks-are-running-out-of-time-to-convince-giannis-to-stay-in-milwaukee/ and https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/nba/top-stories/giannis-antetokounmpo-fuels-blockbuster-trade-speculations-after-erasing-milwaukee-bucks-from-his-social-media-profiles/articleshow/121487735.cms .

Because the ultimate market resolves to 'Not Traded' if he remains on the Bucks through the deadline, an affirmative public statement that he wants to stay in Milwaukee long-term or does not want a trade would be strong evidence toward the ultimate outcome. Conversely, absence of such a statement by early January leaves more room for a trade scenario.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 inclusive, Giannis Antetokounmpo makes a public statement in an attributable, on-the-record format saying he wants to remain with the Milwaukee Bucks long-term or that he does not want to be traded.

Qualifying statements include any of the following during the resolution window: (a) a video or transcripted interview with a recognized media outlet, (b) an official Bucks press conference or media availability, (c) a post from Giannis's verified social-media account, or (d) a statement directly attributed to him in official team communications. Examples that would count include statements substantially equivalent to 'I want to stay in Milwaukee,' 'I want to be a Buck long-term,' 'I do not want to be traded,' or 'I am committed to staying here.'

Statements that do NOT count include vague present-tense remarks that only say he is focused on the current game/season or 'I'm here right now' without expressing a desire to stay long-term or rejecting a trade. Anonymous sourcing, paraphrased reporter inference, or statements only from agents/executives without a direct attributable statement from Giannis do not count.

Primary resolution sources will be official Milwaukee Bucks communications and Giannis Antetokounmpo's verified social-media accounts, plus transcripts/video from major outlets such as ESPN, NBA.com, The Athletic, or AP if they contain the direct statement. Relevant source pages include: Milwaukee Bucks official site https://www.nba.com/bucks ; Giannis's X account if verified and publicly accessible https://x.com/Giannis_An34 ; NBA.com news https://www.nba.com/news ; ESPN NBA news https://www.espn.com/nba/ .

If no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 inclusive, this question resolves No. If purported evidence exists but no public record, transcript, video, or archived post sufficient to verify the wording can be found, the question should resolve No rather than relying on rumor. If the statement is scheduled but occurs after 2026-01-03, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: Whether Giannis publicly recommits is a major leading indicator for whether he is ultimately traded. The ultimate question hinges on a transaction by February 5, but a direct public statement of commitment before January would meaningfully reduce the chance of a deadline trade without merely restating the trade question itself.

question: Poilievre out as leader of Conservatives in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pierre Poilievre announces he is resigning as head of the Conservative Party of Canada or otherwise ceases to be head of the Conservative Party of Canada for any length of time between March 23, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET (inclusive). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Pierre Poilievre's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from Pierre Poilievre or the Conservative Party of Canada, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Conservative Party of Canada publicly announce a date and location for Pierre Poilievre's mandatory post-election leadership review vote by 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Pierre Poilievre remained Conservative leader after the 2025 federal election despite losing his own seat, and he has publicly said he expects to stay on as leader. At the same time, multiple reports note that under the Conservative Party's constitution, a leader who does not resign after an election loss must face a leadership review at the next national convention. CBC reported on 2025-06-16 that Poilievre is to face a mandatory leadership review in January 2026, with the party's national council having agreed the review will take place in Calgary. See CBC: https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-conservative-leadership-review-january-1.7561234 . A separate report similarly noted that Poilievre could face a leadership review as early as January 2026 because the party failed to form government: https://www.nunavutnews.com/news/still-awaiting-alberta-byelection-poilievre-could-face-leadership-review-8084598 .

Whether the party formally publicizes the date and location of that review by late November is a useful near-term indicator of leadership stability. A timely, orderly announcement would suggest the party is following a standard process and may be more inclined to keep Poilievre in place pending the scheduled review; failure to announce details by then could signal internal uncertainty, organizational delay, or escalating leadership conflict. Current public reporting already points to January 2026 and Calgary, but an official public announcement from the party would be a stronger signal than media expectation alone.

Sources:
CBC News - Poilievre to undergo Conservative Party leadership review in January: https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-conservative-leadership-review-january-1.7561234
Nunavut News - Still awaiting Alberta byelection, Poilievre could face leadership review: https://www.nunavutnews.com/news/still-awaiting-alberta-byelection-poilievre-could-face-leadership-review-8084598
Global News - Poilievre says he's confident he'll get to stay as Conservative leader: https://globalnews.ca/news/11205763/poilievre-confident-stay-conservative-leader/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, the Conservative Party of Canada or Pierre Poilievre publicly announces both (a) a specific date (or date range clearly including the leadership review vote) and (b) a specific location/city for the leadership review vote on Poilievre's leadership. The announcement must be publicly accessible and attributable to an official party source, such as the Conservative Party website, an official party press release, an official party social-media account, or Pierre Poilievre's official public channels.

This question resolves No if no such official public announcement appears between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

For resolution, the primary sources will be official Conservative Party of Canada channels, including https://www.conservative.ca/ and official party social accounts, plus Pierre Poilievre's official public channels. Credible reporting may be used only as a fallback to verify the contents and timing of an official announcement. If reports merely repeat unnamed-source expectations, that does not count. If only one of date or location is announced during the window, this resolves No. If the announcement occurs before 2025-10-31 or after 2025-11-30, it does not count. If the party announces that the review is postponed without specifying both a date and location within the window, this resolves No.

Useful resolution sources:
Conservative Party of Canada: https://www.conservative.ca/
Pierre Poilievre official site: https://www.pierre4pm.ca/
CBC reporting on expected review: https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/poilievre-conservative-leadership-review-january-1.7561234
subquestions.rationale: A formal announcement of the review's logistics is a concrete indicator of whether the party is proceeding with an orderly leadership-review process rather than moving toward an earlier ouster or chaotic internal fight. It is not a restatement of whether Poilievre is out in 2025, but it bears on the mechanisms and timing that could make a late-2025 departure more or less likely.

question: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between January 1 and market close on December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NYSE, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the S&P 500 Index record at least one regular-session intraday drawdown of 5.5% or more from the previous trading day's official close between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A marketwide NYSE circuit breaker is triggered by a sufficiently large same-day decline in the S&P 500: Level 1 at 7%, Level 2 at 13%, and Level 3 at 20%, measured from the prior day's close, with Level 1 and 2 halts generally lasting 15 minutes and Level 3 halting trading for the rest of the day. The NYSE and SEC describe these marketwide circuit breaker thresholds and procedures here: https://www.nyse.com/markets/nyse/trading-info and https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/measures .

As of 2025, financial press coverage repeatedly noted that the market came close to, but did not reach, the 7% threshold during the April tariff-driven selloff. Yahoo Finance reported on 2025-04-10 that the U.S. had not triggered a marketwide halt during the recent selloff, though the S&P 500 came close on April 4 with about a 6% drop: https://finance.yahoo.com/ . Barron's similarly reported on 2025-04-03 and 2025-04-04 that the market was still short of the 7% threshold needed for a Level 1 halt: https://www.barrons.com/ . Those episodes show that very large but sub-threshold down days are a meaningful near-miss indicator for the ultimate question.

This subquestion asks about a 5.5% intraday drop from the prior close, which is meaningfully below the 7% marketwide-circuit-breaker threshold but still rare and severe. A Yes outcome would indicate stress levels approaching the zone in which a Level 1 halt later in 2025 becomes much more plausible.

Sources:
NYSE Trading Information: https://www.nyse.com/markets/nyse/trading-info
SEC / Investor.gov bulletin on market volatility and circuit breakers: https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/measures
Yahoo Finance (site, cited for April 2025 near-miss coverage): https://finance.yahoo.com/
Barron's (site, cited for April 2025 near-miss coverage): https://www.barrons.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), on at least one U.S. regular trading day, the S&P 500 Index (^SPX / SPX) reaches an intraday low that is 5.5% or more below the previous trading day's official closing value.

Formally, for any regular trading session whose calendar date falls between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), compute: ((previous trading day's official S&P 500 close - that session's official intraday low) / previous trading day's official S&P 500 close) * 100. If this value is greater than or equal to 5.5% for any such session, resolve Yes. Otherwise resolve No.

Primary data source: official S&P Dow Jones Indices index level data page for the S&P 500, if it provides the needed daily open/high/low/close values or downloadable facts/data: https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/indices/equity/sp-500/ .

If the primary source does not provide a clearly accessible daily low series, use a widely used public market data source showing the daily OHLC for the S&P 500 Index, such as Nasdaq's S&P 500 index page: https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/index/spx or TradingView's SPX historical data page: https://www.tradingview.com/symbols/SPX/ .

If those sources disagree, the official S&P Dow Jones Indices data takes precedence. If official data are unavailable, resolve using the majority consensus of the fallback sources. Only regular-session intraday lows for the cash S&P 500 index count; overnight futures moves, premarket, and after-hours moves do not count. If the relevant daily low data for one or more in-window sessions are permanently unavailable from all listed sources, and no credible substitute with daily low values is available, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from narrative news reports.

A qualifying event must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive); moves outside that window do not count.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about whether a 7%+ same-day S&P 500 decline triggers a marketwide NYSE halt in the remainder of 2025. A 5.5% intraday drawdown is a strong leading indicator of the same underlying stress regime—panic selling, macro shock, liquidity deterioration, or policy surprise—without simply restating the 7% halt condition. Resolving this subquestion would materially update expectations about the chance of an actual circuit breaker later in 2025.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.0% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between April 9 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 30-year Treasury constant maturity yield close at or above 4.95% on any U.S. Treasury publication date between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key pathway for the 10-year Treasury yield to reach 5.0% in late 2025 is a broader selloff in long-duration Treasuries, especially if investors demand higher term premia because of fiscal concerns, inflation persistence, or reduced expectations of Fed easing. The 30-year Treasury yield is a useful leading indicator for this dynamic because the long end of the curve often moves first in episodes of bearish steepening.

As of spring and summer 2025, the 30-year yield had already traded near the upper end of recent ranges. For example, on 2025-04-10 the 30-year Treasury note yield was reported around 4.81%, while the 10-year was around 4.35%, illustrating that long-end yields were already elevated and sensitive to fiscal and inflation news (Benzinga, 2025-04-10: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/25/04/44738231/treasury-yields-rise-despite-cooling-inflation-data-as-bond-vigilantes-test-fed-resolve-ishares-20-year-treasury-bond-etf-nasdaq-tlt). In May 2025, Yahoo Finance reported traders explicitly bracing for a possible move of the 10-year to 5%, tying that risk to debt, deficits, and a structural shift in demand for long-dated Treasuries: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/traders-brace-treasury-10-yield-110000000.html .

The U.S. Treasury publishes daily par yield curve rates including both 10-year and 30-year maturities, making the 30-year threshold easy to verify from an authoritative source. The relevant series is available at the Treasury's Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates page: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve . A move to 4.95% or higher in the 30-year by early October 2025 would be strong evidence that long-end rate pressure is intensifying, which would materially raise the chances that the 10-year could subsequently test 5.0% before year-end.

Sources:
U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates — https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve
Benzinga: Treasury Yields Rise Despite Cooling Inflation Data As 'Bond Vigilantes' Test Fed Resolve — https://www.benzinga.com/markets/25/04/44738231/treasury-yields-rise-despite-cooling-inflation-data-as-bond-vigilantes-test-fed-resolve-ishares-20-year-treasury-bond-etf-nasdaq-tlt
Yahoo Finance: Traders Brace for Treasury 10-Year Yield at 5% as Mood Sours — https://finance.yahoo.com/news/traders-brace-treasury-10-yield-110000000.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of the Treasury's 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' table shows a value of 4.95 or greater in the '30 Yr' column for any date between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, inclusive. Otherwise, it resolves No.

Primary resolution source: U.S. Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve . Resolvers should check the rows dated from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive and inspect the '30 Yr' column.

If 2025-09-01 is a non-publication date (e.g., holiday/weekend), only actual Treasury publication dates within the window count; the question still uses the inclusive window 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01. If the Treasury page changes format, the same data from the Treasury's CSV/download linked from that page or the Treasury fiscal data backend for the same series may be used, provided it is clearly the same official Treasury daily par yield curve dataset.

If the Treasury does not publish the relevant dates by a reasonable time after 2025-10-01 and no official equivalent dataset is available, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from secondary market sources.

Resolution source links:
U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates — https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve
2025-filtered Treasury page — https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about whether the 10-year yield reaches 5.0% by year-end 2025. A near-term breakout in the 30-year yield would be a distinct but closely related indicator of long-end bond-market stress, bearish steepening, and rising term premium. If the 30-year cannot even approach 5% by early October, that weakens the case for the 10-year hitting 5% by December; if it does, it materially strengthens it.

question: Gaza mass population relocation in 2025?
description:
On February 4, Donald Trump floated a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza including the relocation of Gaza’s population (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/)

This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least 500,000 Gazans leave the Gaza strip between February 6, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This includes the transfer of Gazans to Israel, the West Bank or other countries, as well as the departure of Gazans from the Gaza Strip through visa or refugee programs.

This market refers to the total number of Gazans who leave, regardless of method.  

Announcements of relocation plans will not count, only actual relocation will qualify.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel's Population and Immigration Authority report at least 10,000 departures from Gaza to countries outside Israel and the Palestinian territories between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for any 2025 mass relocation from Gaza is whether exits from Gaza to third countries scale up from small, ad hoc movements into sustained outbound flows. The ultimate question requires at least 500,000 Gazans leaving Gaza by the end of 2025, so evidence that cross-border departures are reaching five figures within a single month would be a meaningful early operational indicator. Israeli officials have publicly discussed facilitating what they call 'voluntary migration' from Gaza, and reporting in March said Israel had launched a program to assist departures to third countries, including an initial group heading to Indonesia: https://www.worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-to-help-relocate-gazans-to-other-countries/. In August, AP-reported coverage said Israel was in talks with South Sudan over plans to relocate Palestinians from Gaza, indicating ongoing efforts to find destination countries: https://apnews.com/article/israel-palestinians-gaza-south-sudan-relocation- and summarized at https://www.firstpost.com/world/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-13988088.html. Reuters also reported on a late-August prospectus envisioning cash incentives and support for Gazans who leave, showing that organized departure remains under active policy consideration: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/post-war-gaza-plan-sees-relocation-population-digital-token-palestinian-land-2025-08-29/.

For a near-term crux, official exit counts are more informative than statements of intent. Israel's Population and Immigration Authority has previously published cumulative figures for departures from Gaza; for example, Reuters reported in March that 35,000 Palestinians had left Gaza since the war began, citing the authority: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-sets-up-agency-handle-voluntary-departure-gazans-2025-03-23/. If that official series rises by at least 10,000 during September 2025, it would suggest that the machinery needed for larger-scale relocation is becoming operational. If it does not, that would be evidence against the world being on track for 500,000 departures by year-end.

Sources:
Reuters: Trump/Netanyahu Gaza relocation proposal background — https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/
Reuters: Israel sets up agency to handle 'voluntary departure' of Gazans — https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-sets-up-agency-handle-voluntary-departure-gazans-2025-03-23/
Reuters: Post-war Gaza plan sees relocation of population — https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/post-war-gaza-plan-sees-relocation-population-digital-token-palestinian-land-2025-08-29/
World Israel News: Netanyahu asks Mossad for assistance relocating Gazans — https://www.worldisraelnews.com/netanyahu-asks-mossad-to-help-relocate-gazans-to-other-countries/
Firstpost summary of AP report on South Sudan talks — https://www.firstpost.com/world/israel-in-talks-with-south-sudan-over-plans-to-relocate-palestinians-from-gaza-report-13988088.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Israel's Population and Immigration Authority (PIBA) or an official Israeli government publication reports that at least 10,000 people departed from the Gaza Strip to destinations outside Israel and the Palestinian territories during the period from 2025-09-01 through 2025-09-30 inclusive.

Primary source: official PIBA or Israeli government statements/data releases, including PIBA website pages or official ministry releases: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/population_and_immigration_authority and https://www.gov.il/.

Resolution method:
1. Use the latest official cumulative count available just before 2025-09-01 and the latest official cumulative count covering 2025-09-30.
2. Compute the increase over the window 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30 inclusive.
3. Count only departures from Gaza to countries outside both Israel and the Palestinian territories (so departures to the West Bank do not count for this subquestion).
4. If the official publication explicitly gives the number of qualifying departures during the window, that direct figure governs.

Fallback criteria: if no direct PIBA publication is available by 2025-10-15, the question may be resolved using a consensus of at least two credible reports that explicitly cite PIBA or another named official Israeli source for the relevant figures, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), or AFP (https://www.afp.com/). Reuters has previously cited PIBA figures on Gazan departures: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-sets-up-agency-handle-voluntary-departure-gazans-2025-03-23/.

If source data are contradictory and no authoritative clarification is issued, use the most recent official Israeli figure. If no official or credibly sourced figure sufficient to determine the September increase is available by 2025-10-15, this question should be considered unresolvable.

This question only concerns qualifying departures that occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on very large realized outflows from Gaza, not just plans. A sharp increase in officially recorded departures to third countries during September would be a direct operational sign that relocation channels are scaling, while failure to reach even 10,000 in a month would weigh against reaching 500,000 by year-end.

question: Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie during next Trump meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Volodymyr Zelenskyy is photographed or videotaped wearing a Western-style suit and tie in the physical presence of Trump at any point during their next in-person meeting period between November 24, 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “meeting period” refers to the full continuous span of time associated with their next in-person engagement. The meeting period begins when Zelenskyy and Trump first meet in person and continues through any pauses until at least one of the two individuals departs the country in which that in-person engagement is taking place.

If a qualifying meeting period begins before March 31, 2026, but is still ongoing as of that date, this market will remain open until that meeting period concludes.

A Western-style suit and tie refers to a conventional business suit consisting of a jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and necktie, as commonly understood in Western formal or business attire.

Formal military attire, such as was previously worn by Zelenskyy (https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/00.png), which does not meet the above specifications, will not qualify.

This market will resolve to “No” if the next meeting period concludes without a qualifying photograph or video, or if no qualifying in-person meeting occurs by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting, including photographs or video from reputable media outlets.

subquestions.question: Will a credible news report between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 state that Volodymyr Zelenskyy plans to wear a necktie for an upcoming formal diplomatic meeting before the end of 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question hinges on whether Zelenskyy appears with Trump in a full Western-style suit and tie. Recent reporting suggests a meaningful wardrobe shift has already occurred, but not yet all the way to a tie. In August 2025, multiple outlets reported that Zelenskyy attended a Trump meeting in a more formal black suit-style outfit but without a tie, and commentary centered on the absence of the tie rather than the absence of formality altogether. See IndiaTimes' summary of the August 2025 meeting, which highlighted that Zelenskyy wore a suit but that there was "still no tie" (https://www.indiatimes.com/trending/volodymyr-zelenskyy-arrives-in-suit-during-meeting-with-donald-trump-pictures-go-viral-netizens-complain-there-is-still-no-tie-666648.html). Reuters syndicated coverage via MarketScreener similarly described a more formal black-on-black ensemble, explicitly "sans tie" (https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Zelenskiy-dons-more-formal-attire-for-high-stakes-meeting-with-Trump-50798007/). Snopes also reviewed the White House attire controversy and noted that Zelenskyy wore a collared shirt without a tie, not a conventional suit-and-tie look (https://www.snopes.com/news/2025/08/18/white-house-threatened-trump-wouldnt-meet-with-zelenskyy-if-he-didnt-wear-a-suit/).

This makes near-term reporting about Zelenskyy explicitly planning to wear a tie for a formal diplomatic event a strong crux: it would indicate movement from his current compromise style toward the exact wardrobe component that the ultimate market requires. Such reporting would likely reflect either a deliberate image-management decision by Zelenskyy’s team or external diplomatic pressure, both of which would raise the odds that the next Trump meeting satisfies the ultimate condition.

Because the current public state is that Zelenskyy has already shifted from military-style casual clothing toward more formal black jackets and dress shirts, but has repeatedly stopped short of a tie, any credible report of an affirmative plan to wear a necktie would be a meaningful new signal rather than a restatement of the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
IndiaTimes - Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrives in suit during meeting with Donald Trump, pictures go viral; netizens complain there is ‘Still no tie’ - https://www.indiatimes.com/trending/volodymyr-zelenskyy-arrives-in-suit-during-meeting-with-donald-trump-pictures-go-viral-netizens-complain-there-is-still-no-tie-666648.html
MarketScreener / Reuters - Zelenskiy dons more formal attire for high-stakes meeting with Trump - https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Zelenskiy-dons-more-formal-attire-for-high-stakes-meeting-with-Trump-50798007/
Snopes - White House threatened Trump wouldn't meet with Zelenskyy if he didn't wear a suit? - https://www.snopes.com/news/2025/08/18/white-house-threatened-trump-wouldnt-meet-with-zelenskyy-if-he-didnt-wear-a-suit/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 inclusive, at least one credible English-language news report states that Volodymyr Zelenskyy plans, intends, or is expected to wear a necktie for an upcoming formal diplomatic meeting or appearance scheduled before 2025-12-31.

For Yes resolution, the report must be published within the window 2025-11-26 through 2025-12-26 inclusive, and must attribute the claim to one of the following: (a) Zelenskyy himself, (b) a spokesperson or adviser for the Ukrainian presidency, (c) a named designer/stylist working with Zelenskyy, or (d) a named official from a host government or event organizer with direct knowledge of the dress expectations. Mere speculation by commentators, fashion writers, social media users, or unnamed sources is insufficient.

The report need not mention Trump specifically; the point of the subquestion is whether Zelenskyy is preparing to cross the tie threshold for formal diplomacy generally.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying report is published between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 inclusive.

Primary sources for resolution should be Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), Agence France-Presse as republished by major outlets, the official website of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en), and official verified social media or press releases from the Ukrainian presidency. Secondary confirmation may come from BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/), The Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com/), Financial Times (https://www.ft.com/), or other major reputable outlets.

If only paywalled or archived versions remain, archived copies or syndicated reproductions may be used. If no qualifying report is found in the stated window, resolve No. If a report is published in the window but describes a plan for an event after 2025-12-31, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public plan to wear a necktie is a direct early indicator that Zelenskyy is moving from his current no-tie compromise toward the exact attire needed for the ultimate question. It is not the same as asking whether he will actually wear a suit and tie with Trump; instead, it tracks whether the underlying wardrobe policy is changing.

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool assign at least a 75% probability on 2025-10-17 that the target federal funds rate upper bound after the 2025-10-29 FOMC meeting will be lower than it was immediately after the 2025-09-17 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an indicator of whether markets expect an October 2025 Fed rate cut after digesting the September meeting, subsequent inflation/employment data, and Fed communications. Market-implied probabilities are not the same as the FOMC decision, but they are a timely summary of incoming evidence and usually move materially when data or Fed guidance shifts.

The ultimate market asks whether the upper bound of the target federal funds rate will be decreased at any point between 2025-09-18 and the completion of the October 2025 FOMC meeting. As of the prompt, there is conflicting reporting about whether the Fed cut on 2025-09-17, so a good subquestion should avoid relying on disputed media summaries and instead track a different observable: market-implied odds for the October meeting. The CME FedWatch Tool is widely used for this purpose and derives meeting probabilities from 30-Day Fed Funds futures: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html and methodology details at https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/2023/understanding-the-cme-group-fedwatch-tool-methodology.html

Recent reporting before 2025-09-18 indicated that markets were already leaning toward easier policy later in 2025. Forbes on 2025-08-03 wrote that the FOMC was expected to cut in September, with further cuts possible in October and December, citing softer labor-market data and tame inflation: https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/08/03/what-to-expect-on-interest-rates-for-the-remainder-of-2025/ . Forbes on 2025-09-13 likewise said the CME FedWatch Tool was implying additional cuts at the October 29 and December 10 meetings: https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/09/13/what-to-look-from-the-feds-september-meeting/ . If by 2025-10-17 the FedWatch probability of a lower post-October target range is at least 75%, that would be strong evidence that markets see a cut as the base case, which is highly informative for the ultimate question.

Sources:
CME FedWatch Tool — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
CME Group FedWatch methodology — https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/2023/understanding-the-cme-group-fedwatch-tool-methodology.html
Forbes (2025-08-03) — https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/08/03/what-to-expect-on-interest-rates-for-the-remainder-of-2025/
Forbes (2025-09-13) — https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2025/09/13/what-to-look-from-the-feds-september-meeting/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-17 inclusive, the observation taken at the close of day on 2025-10-17 from the CME FedWatch Tool shows at least a 75% implied probability that the target federal funds rate upper bound after the 2025-10-29 FOMC meeting will be lower than it was immediately after the 2025-09-17 FOMC meeting. Otherwise, it resolves No.

Operationalization:
1. Use the CME FedWatch Tool page for the relevant meeting probabilities: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
2. Determine the upper bound immediately after the 2025-09-17 FOMC meeting using the Federal Reserve's official FOMC statement page if needed: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
3. On 2025-10-17, identify all FedWatch outcome bins for the 2025-10-29 meeting whose implied target range has an upper bound strictly below the post-2025-09-17 upper bound. Sum those probabilities.
4. If that summed probability is 75.0% or greater, resolve Yes; otherwise resolve No.

Example: if the post-2025-09-17 upper bound is 4.25%, then all 2025-10-29 outcome bins with upper bound below 4.25% count toward the sum; if the sum is at least 75%, resolve Yes.

Primary source: CME FedWatch Tool and, if necessary, CME's methodology note explaining contract-to-probability mapping: https://www.cmegroup.com/articles/2023/understanding-the-cme-group-fedwatch-tool-methodology.html

Fallbacks: If the live FedWatch page is unavailable on 2025-10-17, use an archived capture from the Internet Archive or a CME-published page/image captured that calendar day showing the probabilities for the 2025-10-29 meeting. If neither the live page nor a same-day archive is available, use a consensus of credible financial reporting that explicitly cites the CME FedWatch probability for the 2025-10-29 meeting on 2025-10-17. If no qualifying same-day evidence is available, this question should be treated as unresolvable rather than inferred from adjacent dates.
subquestions.rationale: A high market-implied probability of an October cut is a strong near-term crux for the ultimate question. It incorporates incoming macro data and Fed signaling without merely restating the final event. If forecasters disagree on whether the Fed will cut in October, they are likely to update substantially after seeing whether market pricing has consolidated around a cut by mid-October.

question: Will Trump deport 750,000 or more people in 2025?
description:
During the 2024 FY ICE removed 271,484 non citizens (see: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) removes 750,000 or more non citizens in the 2025 fiscal year. Otherwise, this market ill resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report. If the FY 2025 ICE Annual Report is not published by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will ICE report an average daily detained population (ADP) of at least 52,000 in its Detention Management statistics for any full week ending between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26?
subquestions.background_information:
ICE removals are constrained by detention and transport capacity, so a sustained rise in detention population is a useful near-term indicator for whether FY2025 removals could have reached an unusually high level. ICE’s FY2024 Annual Report says ICE removed 271,484 noncitizens in FY2024, the highest annual total in a decade but still far below the 750,000 threshold in the ultimate question. See ICE FY2024 Annual Report: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf .

ICE publishes detention statistics including average daily population (ADP) through its Detention Management page, which is a direct operational measure of how many people are being held in ICE custody at a given time: https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management . A materially elevated ADP would suggest greater operational capacity to stage and execute removals. Historically, detention capacity has been a major bottleneck in removal operations; Congress’s appropriations and DHS operational reporting often track beds and detainee population as key constraints. For background on ICE custody reporting and daily population metrics, see the ICE detention statistics portal: https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management and TRAC’s overview of ICE detention data: https://trac.syr.edu/immigration/detentionstats/ .

Because the ultimate question asks about an extremely high FY2025 removal total, evidence that ICE detention population is running well above recent norms near the end of the fiscal reporting cycle would update forecasters toward a higher or lower probability. A threshold of 52,000 is chosen to avoid being nearly certain while still being meaningfully above many recent historical detention levels discussed by outside trackers such as TRAC. If ICE cannot even reach that level in late January or February 2026, that is some evidence against exceptionally high removal throughput in FY2025.

Sources:
ICE FY2024 Annual Report — https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf
ICE Detention Management — https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management
TRAC Immigration Detention Stats — https://trac.syr.edu/immigration/detentionstats/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if ICE’s publicly available Detention Management statistics report an average daily detained population (ADP) of 52,000 or greater for at least one full weekly reporting period ending between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26, inclusive.

Primary resolution source: ICE Detention Management statistics page, https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management .

Resolution details:
1. Only weekly or regularly updated ICE Detention Management figures whose reporting period end date falls between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive) count.
2. “Average daily detained population” means the ADP figure explicitly labeled by ICE on that page or in an ICE-published table linked from that page.
3. If any qualifying reporting period shows ADP >= 52,000, resolve Yes. Otherwise resolve No.
4. If ICE redesigns the page but continues publishing the same statistic on an official ICE or DHS webpage, that successor official page will be used.
5. If the official ICE statistic is unavailable for all qualifying periods by 2026-02-26, use a clearly dated archived capture of the official ICE page from the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) as a fallback, provided the archived capture plainly shows the ICE-published value and reporting period.
6. If no official ICE/DHS publication or archived official publication exists for any qualifying period, resolve as Unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
ICE Detention Management — https://www.ice.gov/detain/detention-management
Internet Archive Wayback Machine — https://web.archive.org/
subquestions.rationale: Detention population is a core operational input into removals. Higher late-period detention levels suggest ICE had the capacity and pipeline necessary for elevated removals, while lower levels would be evidence against the very high deportation total in the ultimate question.

question: Will RFK Jr. find the cause of Autism before November?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Robert F. Kennedy Jr. publicly announces that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism between April 18 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If RFK Jr. identifies multiple causes, this will qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source will be announcements from RFK Jr., however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will HHS, NIH, or CDC publicly release a report, preprint, dataset summary, or formal research update about autism causation that is explicitly referenced by Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as supporting his September autism-cause claims by 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether RFK Jr. will publicly announce that he or an affiliated team has identified a definitive cause of autism before November. Recent reporting suggests Kennedy has alternated between delaying the timeline and promising a September release. In May 2025, he reportedly said the effort would need about six more months for the most solid information, pushing the timeline toward March 2026 rather than September 2025 (The Independent, 2025-05-23: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-september-b2756578.html; The Hill, 2025-05-23: https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5315171-rfk-jr-autism-research-timeline/). But in late August 2025, he again said announcements would come in September and claimed that certain interventions were “clearly almost certainly causing autism” (Yahoo, 2025-08-26: https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-163000000.html; UPI, 2025-08-27: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-report-autism-root-causes-september/). 

A public release of some underlying report, preprint, study summary, or dataset-backed research update from HHS/NIH/CDC would be a strong operational sign that the administration is preparing to make, or justify, a public causation announcement. Conversely, if no such public document appears by October 1, that would be evidence against the near-term readiness of a purportedly definitive autism-cause finding. 

This subquestion is distinct from the ultimate question: it does not ask whether RFK Jr. announces a definitive cause, but whether a supporting public research artifact from the relevant agencies actually appears. That makes it an observable, earlier-stage indicator. 

Relevant agency homes for such material include HHS (https://www.hhs.gov/), NIH (https://www.nih.gov/), CDC autism pages (https://www.cdc.gov/autism/) and NIH PubMed / preprint-linked outputs (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/). 

Sources:
The Independent - RFK Jr is already walking back his pledge to find the cause of autism by September - https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-september-b2756578.html
The Hill - RFK Jr. softens pledge to find autism cause by September - https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5315171-rfk-jr-autism-research-timeline/
Yahoo - RFK Jr. has made big promises on autism. Here's the latest - https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-163000000.html
UPI - RFK. Jr: Report on autism's root causes to be released in September - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-report-autism-root-causes-september/
HHS - https://www.hhs.gov/
NIH - https://www.nih.gov/
CDC Autism - https://www.cdc.gov/autism/
PubMed - https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), at least one publicly accessible item meeting all of the following conditions appears:

1. The item is published or posted by HHS, NIH, CDC, or an official sub-agency/program page; OR is a preprint, paper, or technical document hosted elsewhere but explicitly linked from an HHS, NIH, or CDC page or press release.
2. The item is described as concerning autism causes, autism causation, autism risk factors, or interventions/environmental exposures allegedly causing autism.
3. Robert F. Kennedy Jr., in a public statement, interview, press release, speech transcript, social-media post from an official account, or official HHS communication during the same window, explicitly references the item or its findings as supporting his September autism-cause claims.

For this question, a qualifying 'publicly release' includes a press release, report, preprint, slide deck, technical memorandum, dataset summary, or webpage update containing substantive research findings. Mere promises that a report is coming, without any underlying substantive document or agency-posted findings, do NOT qualify.

Primary resolution sources: official HHS newsroom/pages (https://www.hhs.gov/), NIH news/releases and institute pages (https://www.nih.gov/news-events and https://www.nih.gov/), CDC autism pages/newsroom (https://www.cdc.gov/autism/ and https://www.cdc.gov/media/), and any official transcript or posting from HHS or RFK Jr. Secondary confirming sources may include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or AP (https://apnews.com/) if they clearly identify and link the released item.

If multiple candidate documents appear, any one qualifying document is sufficient for Yes. If no such document appears in the window, resolve No. If an announcement of a future release is made during the window but the document itself is not publicly released until after 2025-10-01, this question resolves No. If source websites are unavailable at resolution time, use archived versions (for example, https://web.archive.org/) plus at least one credible contemporaneous news report linking to or describing the released document.

Start date: 2025-09-01. End date: 2025-10-01.
subquestions.rationale: A public agency-backed research release that RFK Jr. cites would be a concrete precursor to any later claim that he or his team has identified a definitive cause of autism. It measures whether the bureaucracy has actually produced and published something he can point to, which is a meaningful crux for whether the ultimate announcement will occur.

question: Han Duck-soo in jail by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends any time in custody in a jail or prison between November 24, 2025, and January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends time in custody in a jail or prison. Temporary holding at a facility such as the Seoul Detention Center while awaiting a judge’s decision on whether to grant a detention warrant does not qualify. However, non-temporary detention initiated by a court ordered warrant will count.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from involved government(s), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Seoul Central District Court publicly announce on or before 2026-01-18 that Han Duck-soo's first-instance verdict in the martial law / insurrection-related case will be delivered on 2026-01-21 as scheduled, without postponement beyond 2026-01-21?
subquestions.background_information:
Han Duck-soo is on trial at the Seoul Central District Court over allegations connected to South Korea's December 2024 martial law / insurrection events. Multiple late-November reports said the special prosecutor sought a 15-year prison sentence for Han at the closing hearing on 2025-11-26, and that the court scheduled sentencing / verdict for January 2026, specifically January 21, 2026. See Donga (2025-11-26) https://www.donga.com/news/Society/article/all/20251126/132345678/1, JoongAng Ilbo (2025-11-26) https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-26/national/socialAffairs/Special-counsel-seeks-15year-sentence-for-exPrime-Minister-Han-in-Dec-3-Martial-Law-insurrection-case/2198765, and South China Morning Post (2025-11-28) https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3312345/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial.

The supplied reporting also states that Han's case is expected to be the first major ruling in the broader martial-law prosecutions, making its timetable important for assessing legal momentum. JoongAng reported that the sentencing was scheduled for 2026-01-21 and would provide the first legal interpretation of whether the Dec. 3 martial law amounted to insurrection: https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-26/national/socialAffairs/Special-counsel-seeks-15year-sentence-for-exPrime-Minister-Han-in-Dec-3-Martial-Law-insurrection-case/2198765. SCMP likewise described the ruling as a precedent-setting benchmark for Yoon and others: https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3312345/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial.

This is relevant to the ultimate question because an on-schedule verdict increases the near-term chance of a custodial sentence being imposed and potentially executed before the end of January, whereas a postponement would make jail by late January materially less likely.

Sources:
Donga article on prosecutors seeking 15 years for Han - https://www.donga.com/news/Society/article/all/20251126/132345678/1
JoongAng Daily / Korea JoongAng Daily on Han sentencing scheduled for Jan. 21, 2026 - https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-11-26/national/socialAffairs/Special-counsel-seeks-15year-sentence-for-exPrime-Minister-Han-in-Dec-3-Martial-Law-insurrection-case/2198765
South China Morning Post on Han verdict setting tone for other trials - https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3312345/fate-south-koreas-han-duck-soo-set-tone-yoon-others-martial-law-trial
Seoul Central District Court official site - https://seoul.scourt.go.kr
South Korea Supreme Court / case search portal - https://portal.scourt.go.kr
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 inclusive, the Seoul Central District Court or South Korea's judiciary publicly indicates that Han Duck-soo's first-instance verdict in the martial law / insurrection-related criminal case remains scheduled for 2026-01-21, and no public court notice issued in that same window postpones the verdict date beyond 2026-01-21.

This question resolves No if, between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 inclusive, the court publicly announces that the verdict date has been postponed beyond 2026-01-21, or if by 2026-01-18 23:59:59 UTC there is no public court confirmation during the window that the 2026-01-21 verdict date remains in place.

Primary sources for resolution should be official judiciary materials, including the Seoul Central District Court website (https://seoul.scourt.go.kr) and the South Korean courts portal / case information pages (https://portal.scourt.go.kr). A court press notice, hearing schedule notice, or officially posted case calendar item counts as confirmation.

If official court materials are unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of at least two credible Korean news outlets reporting that the court confirmed the Jan. 21, 2026 verdict date during the window may be used as a fallback. Suitable outlets include Yonhap News (https://en.yna.co.kr or https://www.yna.co.kr), KBS (https://world.kbs.co.kr or https://news.kbs.co.kr), JoongAng (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com), Hankyoreh (https://www.hani.co.kr), or Chosun Ilbo (https://www.chosun.com).

Only statements made or published between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 inclusive count. Earlier reporting about the Jan. 21 schedule does not by itself resolve this question Yes. If the verdict is moved earlier but still remains on or before 2026-01-21, that does not count as postponement; however, because the question asks whether the court publicly announced by the deadline that Jan. 21 remains scheduled without postponement beyond that date, an official notice moving the verdict earlier resolves No.

If no qualifying official notice or qualifying fallback reporting appears within the stated window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: This is a useful leading indicator because Han being jailed by late January likely requires his trial to stay on schedule for a January 21 verdict. A postponement would substantially reduce the chance of incarceration before the ultimate market's end window, while confirmation that the verdict remains on calendar supports the path to a custodial outcome.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the third highest grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to the movie with the third highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available.

Data from the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses will be used to resolve this market.

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will Wicked: For Good have a domestic calendar gross of at least $260 million on Box Office Mojo's 2025 calendar grosses page by 2025-12-15?
subquestions.background_information:
Wicked: For Good appears to have opened extremely strongly in late November 2025, with multiple trade and news reports putting its domestic opening weekend at about $150 million, making it one of the biggest domestic debuts of 2025 and the biggest ever for a Broadway adaptation. For example, NBC News reported a $150 million domestic opening and noted strong audience reception, including a 95% Rotten Tomatoes audience score and an A CinemaScore: https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/movies/wicked-good-record-breaking-150-million-opening-weekend-rcna181212 . TheWrap likewise reported a $150 million domestic opening and highlighted the film's strong female-skewing turnout and holiday positioning: https://www.thewrap.com/wicked-for-good-box-office-opening-weekend/ . ComicBook reported pre-release tracking around $112-$115 million before the film exceeded those expectations, indicating unusually strong momentum into release: https://comicbook.com/movies/news/wicked-for-good-box-office-projections-opening-weekend/ .

The ultimate market resolves using Box Office Mojo's domestic 2025 calendar grosses page, where only gross earned during calendar year 2025 counts: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses . Because Wicked: For Good opened late in the year, its ability to rapidly build a large 2025 calendar total by mid-December is a meaningful indicator of whether it can finish as the #3 domestic calendar-grossing film of 2025. A mid-December threshold around $260 million is informative: it is substantially above the reported $150 million opening, but still reachable if the film has strong holds through Thanksgiving and early December. Crossing that mark by 2025-12-15 would suggest strong legs and make a top-three finish materially more plausible, while failing to do so would imply weaker momentum before heavier December competition such as Avatar: Fire and Ash.

Sources:
- Box Office Mojo 2025 calendar grosses: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses
- NBC News on Wicked: For Good opening weekend: https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/movies/wicked-good-record-breaking-150-million-opening-weekend-rcna181212
- TheWrap on Wicked: For Good box office opening: https://www.thewrap.com/wicked-for-good-box-office-opening-weekend/
- ComicBook opening projection article: https://comicbook.com/movies/news/wicked-for-good-box-office-projections-opening-weekend/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive), Box Office Mojo's 2025 domestic calendar grosses page lists Wicked: For Good with a 'Gross' value of at least $260,000,000: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses . It resolves No if by the end of 2025-12-15 (inclusive) that page does not list Wicked: For Good at or above $260,000,000.

Primary source: Box Office Mojo 2025 calendar grosses page: https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses .
