subquestions.rationale: Exclusive negotiations are a distinct observable milestone in M&A processes. If WBD enters exclusivity with Paramount, that would meaningfully increase the probability of the ultimate acquisition announcement while remaining different from the final outcome itself.

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 5 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will NASA JPL's Fireball and Bolide Data list at least one natural fireball event with impact energy of 1.0 kiloton or greater occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A 5 kt atmospheric bolide in late 2025 is rare, so a useful early indicator is whether Earth experiences any moderately energetic bolide soon after the market start. Recent 2025 activity shows that nontrivial bolides are occurring: NASA/CNEOS recorded an event over southern Japan on 2025-08-19 with preliminary impact energy around 1.6 kt, which is below the ultimate market threshold but demonstrates that kiloton-class airbursts do occur on relevant timescales. The NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data table is the standard public catalog for such events and reports date/time, location, altitude, velocity, and impact energy in kilotons for detected fireballs: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. NASA describes bolides/fireballs and maintains this dataset through CNEOS: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/ and https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/asteroid-watch/next-five-approaches.

Using a 1.0 kt threshold makes this subquestion meaningfully different from the ultimate question: it tracks whether the near-term environment is producing unusually energetic but sub-ultimate events, which would modestly increase the plausibility of a 5 kt event later in 2025. It is also grounded in current observations because the August 2025 Japan event was already in the kiloton range. A threshold much lower than 1 kt would be too common and less informative; a threshold near 5 kt would be too close to restating the ultimate question.

Sources:
- NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
- NASA JPL Asteroid Watch / CNEOS: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/asteroid-watch/next-five-approaches
- The Watchers report on 2025-08-19 Japan fireball: https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-on-august-19-2025/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/) lists at least one event whose observed date/time falls between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), and whose "Impact Energy (kt)" value is greater than or equal to 1.0, and which is a natural fireball/bolide rather than an artificial object or reentry.

This question resolves No if, after the resolution check date, the repository lists no such qualifying event in that window.

Primary source: NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data table at https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/.

Resolution timing: because this dataset can be updated with delay, the question should be checked on or after 2025-10-15 UTC. If by then the dataset is unavailable or plainly incomplete for the window from 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01, fallback sources may be used: ESA NEO Coordination Centre https://neo.ssa.esa.int/, International Asteroid Warning Network https://iawn.net/, or an official NASA/JPL release such as https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/asteroid-watch/ .

If a candidate event in the window is later reclassified by NASA or authoritative fallback sources as an artificial object/reentry, it does not count. If the source data remain unavailable and no authoritative fallback can establish whether a qualifying natural event occurred in the stated window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A kiloton-class bolide in September would be an informative early signal about the near-term tail of the bolide energy distribution. Observing a 1+ kt event shortly after market start would update forecasters upward on the chance of a rarer 5 kt event before year-end, without merely repeating the ultimate question at an earlier date.

question: Will Gold close between $3900 and $4000 at the end of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the price of the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) as of the final market close price in 2025.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The resolution source will be COMEX trading data for the Gold Continuous Contract (https://www.google.com/finance/quote/GCW00:COMEX).

subquestions.question: Will the CME Group-reported open interest in COMEX Gold futures exceed 700,000 contracts on any trading day between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive?
subquestions.background_information:
A sharp rise in COMEX gold futures open interest would indicate unusually heavy speculative and/or hedging participation in gold markets, which is a meaningful near-term indicator for whether gold can sustain extremely elevated prices into year-end 2025. The ultimate question asks whether the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract will finish 2025 in the narrow $3,900-$4,000 range. A market that is maintaining prices near or above $4,000 late in 2025 would often be accompanied by elevated futures participation rather than a thin, illiquid spike.

Gold has already had a very strong 2025. A Morningstar / Dow Jones data report said front-month COMEX gold settled at $3,736.90 on 2025-09-25, up 42.13% year-to-date, after reaching a 52-week high of $3,780.60 on 2025-09-23: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202509259625/comex-gold-settles-013-higher-at-373690-data-talk . Another report said gold settled at $3,431.80 on 2025-08-28, already up 30.53% year-to-date by then: https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508289547/comex-gold-settles-075-higher-at-343180-data-talk .

The user-provided news also notes an October 2025 breakout above $4,000 in COMEX futures and spot markets, suggesting that gold is already trading in the vicinity relevant to the ultimate market. If that breakout is accompanied by very high open interest through November, it would be evidence that the move is broad and persistent rather than fleeting. CME publishes daily volume and open interest statistics for COMEX gold futures, making this observable and tightly resolvable: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.volume.html and contract specifications are here: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.contractSpecs.html .

A threshold of 700,000 contracts is chosen because it is high enough to be informative but plausible in a period of exceptional price action and investor attention. Crossing such a threshold by late November would support the view that gold's rally has strong market participation, which makes a high year-end close more credible.

Sources:
Morningstar / Dow Jones: Comex Gold Settles 0.13% Higher at $3736.90 -- Data Talk — https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202509259625/comex-gold-settles-013-higher-at-373690-data-talk
Morningstar / Dow Jones: Comex Gold Settles 0.75% Higher at $3431.80 -- Data Talk — https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202508289547/comex-gold-settles-075-higher-at-343180-data-talk
CME Group Gold futures volume/open interest page — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.volume.html
CME Group Gold contract specs — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.contractSpecs.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if CME Group reports total open interest for COMEX Gold futures greater than 700,000 contracts on at least one trading day between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. It resolves No if no such trading day occurs in that window.

Primary resolution source: the CME Group Gold futures volume/open interest page for the relevant daily figures: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.volume.html .

Resolver should use the daily 'Open Interest' value reported by CME for COMEX Gold futures (the standard Gold futures contract listed on the above page). If CME presents daily data in downloadable tables or linked historical reports, those CME-published figures govern.

If CME redesigns the webpage or removes the historical table, fallback sources are other CME-published historical market data pages for Gold futures, including contract pages and downloadable daily bulletins, so long as the figure is explicitly CME-reported: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.html and https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data/volume-open-interest.html .

Only trading days between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive count. Data published after 2025-11-30 about those trading days is allowed for verification, but trading days outside that window do not count. If CME ceases publishing accessible open-interest data for that period and no authoritative CME historical bulletin or archive can be located, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than guessed.

Sources:
CME Group Gold futures volume/open interest page — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.volume.html
CME Group Gold futures overview — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/metals/precious/gold.html
CME Group volume/open interest data hub — https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data/volume-open-interest.html
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether gold can hold an exceptionally high level into the final close of 2025. Daily open interest is not the same as price, so this is not a restatement. Instead, it measures market participation and conviction. Exceptionally high open interest in November would be evidence of strong, persistent engagement by hedgers and speculators, which increases the plausibility that gold remains near the targeted year-end range rather than quickly reversing.

question: Will Sam Altman get OpenAI equity in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Sam Altman formally takes equity in OpenAI by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Taking equity is defined as Sam Altman acquiring or being granted shares, stock options, or any other form of ownership interest in OpenAI.

Any pre-existing interest held through Y Combinator's investment fund or other indirect holdings made prior to Altman becoming full-time at OpenAI will not count toward this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly announce, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, that it has changed or plans to change its governance or corporate structure in a way that explicitly allows employee or executive equity ownership in a new equity-based entity?
subquestions.background_information:
Whether Sam Altman gets OpenAI equity by the end of 2025 likely depends less on a one-off compensation decision and more on whether OpenAI completes or advances a broader restructuring that creates ordinary equity to grant. Recent reporting says OpenAI has been negotiating changes to replace parts of its unusual capped-profit / profit-sharing structure with equity ownership for investors, and that these talks are tied to a possible future IPO and fresh funding. Benzinga, citing reporting on 2025-08-27, said OpenAI is "working to replace its profit-sharing structure with equity ownership for investors" and that restructuring faces regulatory and legal hurdles, including state AG approvals and Elon Musk's lawsuit: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/08/47064961/whats-going-on-with-microsoft-stock-wednesday

At the same time, multiple reports emphasize that Altman currently has no OpenAI equity. Fortune reported on 2025-08-21 that Altman has no equity in OpenAI and earns a salary of $76,001, while a spokesperson said an earlier indirect YC-linked interest had already been sold: https://fortune.com/2025/08/21/openai-sam-altman-no-equity-76001-salary-500-billion-valuation/ Benzinga similarly summarized that Altman has said he has no equity and that a for-profit restructuring could allow equity in the future: https://www.benzinga.com/general/social-media/25/08/47115902/heres-why-sam-altman-wont-make-a-fortune-from-openai-reddit-nyse-rddt

OpenAI also recently stressed that transfers of real OpenAI equity require company approval, in response to Robinhood's tokenized offering. Business Insider reported OpenAI said the tokens were not actual equity and that any transfer of OpenAI equity requires OpenAI's approval: https://www.businessinsider.com/openai-robinhood-tokenized-stock-not-real-equity-please-be-careful-2025-7

This makes a public governance/corporate-structure announcement a meaningful near-term crux. If OpenAI explicitly announces a structure that permits conventional equity ownership by employees or executives in a new entity, that would be a strong indicator that granting Altman equity in 2025 has become operationally and legally easier. If no such announcement appears by the end of October, the path to Altman receiving equity by year-end looks narrower.

Sources:
Fortune - OpenAI may soon be the world's most valuable private company -- but CEO Sam Altman won't profit much, with no equity and just a $76,001 salary - https://fortune.com/2025/08/21/openai-sam-altman-no-equity-76001-salary-500-billion-valuation/
Benzinga - What's Going On With Microsoft Stock Wednesday? - https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/08/47064961/whats-going-on-with-microsoft-stock-wednesday
Benzinga - Here's Why Sam Altman Won't Make A Fortune From OpenAI - https://www.benzinga.com/general/social-media/25/08/47115902/heres-why-sam-altman-wont-make-a-fortune-from-openai-reddit-nyse-rddt
Business Insider - OpenAI warns its tokenized stock offered by Robinhood isn't real equity: 'Please be careful' - https://www.businessinsider.com/openai-robinhood-tokenized-stock-not-real-equity-please-be-careful-2025-7
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, OpenAI publishes or formally authorizes a public announcement stating that it has changed, approved, or formally proposed a governance or corporate-structure change that explicitly allows equity ownership in a new or restructured OpenAI-related entity by employees or executives. The announcement must be public during the resolution window and must come from at least one of the following: (a) an official OpenAI website page or blog post, https://openai.com/ ; (b) an OpenAI filing or legal document made public by the company or an official regulator/court source; or (c) at least two independent credible news outlets reporting that OpenAI itself announced or confirmed the change.

For Yes, the public announcement must explicitly indicate one or more of the following:
1. OpenAI is converting, reorganizing, or creating an entity with conventional equity/share ownership; or
2. OpenAI is replacing or supplementing profit-participation interests with equity; or
3. OpenAI states that employees and/or executives will be eligible to hold equity in the new/restructured entity.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

Important exclusions: mere media speculation, anonymous-source reporting without company confirmation, discussion of investor equity only with no indication of employee/executive eligibility, or statements solely about tokenized products that OpenAI says are not real equity do not count. A generic report that restructuring talks continue does not count unless the announcement explicitly states the governance/corporate-structure change and its equity-bearing nature.

Primary resolution sources: official OpenAI communications at https://openai.com/ ; SEC EDGAR if any filing is involved at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/ ; Delaware court or California AG/public regulator materials if applicable; and corroborating coverage from Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ , Bloomberg https://www.bloomberg.com/ , The Information https://www.theinformation.com/ , CNBC https://www.cnbc.com/ . If sources conflict, official OpenAI statements and formal public filings take precedence. If an announcement is made within the window but withdrawn or corrected within the same window so that it no longer explicitly allows employee/executive equity ownership, resolve based on the final public position as of 2025-10-31 23:59:59 UTC.
subquestions.rationale: Altman receiving equity is more likely if OpenAI first creates or publicly commits to a structure that supports conventional equity ownership for insiders. This is a distinct, observable corporate event that should materially update forecasts on the ultimate question without merely restating whether Altman himself gets equity.

question: Will Kim Keon Hee be sentenced to prison by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kim Keon Hee is sentenced to any time in jail/prison for any charges, including but not limited to allegations of stock price manipulation, bribery, election interference, abuse of power, or criminal acts related to Yoon Suk Yeol’s martial law declaration and related subsequent actions, by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will remain open through March 31, 2026 or until Kim Keon Hee is sentenced to time in jail/prison, regardless of any initial sentencing that does not include prison. Any sentencing will qualify, regardless of subsequent appeals or changes to the sentence.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean government and law enforcement; however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a South Korean court grant prosecutors' request to continue Kim Keon Hee's detention (or issue any new detention order keeping her in custody pending trial) between 2025-12-03 and 2026-01-02?
subquestions.background_information:
Kim Keon Hee was arrested in August 2025 and then indicted while in detention on charges including influence-peddling in the 2022 by-elections, stock-price manipulation, and bribery, according to The Korea Herald. The same report says she became the first former South Korean first lady to be indicted while under arrest, indicating that courts had already found sufficient grounds for pretrial detention at least once. https://www.koreaherald.com/ 

Subsequent reporting says Kim's trial opened on September 24, 2025, on charges including stock manipulation, bribery, and other corruption offenses; prosecutors also sought to freeze her assets pending trial. A court decision to keep her detained, extend detention, or re-detain her during the next month would be a strong near-term indicator that judges continue to view the case as serious and that flight-risk or evidence-tampering concerns remain material—factors that generally correlate with a higher chance of eventual imprisonment if convicted. https://www.koreaherald.com/ 

Reporting from AFP, Al Jazeera, and The Straits Times on related bribery allegations involving Unification Church leader Han Hak-ja also emphasizes prosecutorial concerns about evidence tampering in the broader Kim-linked bribery investigation, reinforcing the salience of custody decisions as a crux in the case trajectory. https://www.aljazeera.com/ https://www.straitstimes.com/ 

Because the ultimate question asks about whether Kim will be sentenced to prison by late March 2026, a court decision in December 2025 or early January 2026 to keep her in detention pending trial would be a meaningful early indicator of legal jeopardy without merely restating the final sentencing question.

Sources:
The Korea Herald - Kim Keon Hee becomes 1st former first lady to be indicted: https://www.koreaherald.com/
The Korea Herald - Kim Keon Hee trial begins: https://www.koreaherald.com/
Al Jazeera - South Korean prosecutors seek arrest of 'Moonies' leader in bribery probe: https://www.aljazeera.com/
The Straits Times - South Korea prosecutors seek arrest of Unification Church leader: https://www.straitstimes.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-03 and 2026-01-02 (inclusive), a South Korean court formally grants a prosecutors' request that results in Kim Keon Hee remaining in custodial detention pending trial, or issues any new detention order/warrant that keeps or returns her to custody in connection with the currently reported criminal cases.

This question resolves No if no such court decision is reported by 2026-01-02 23:59:59 UTC.

For avoidance of doubt:
- Qualifying events include: a court decision extending pretrial detention, rejecting a release request, granting a new detention warrant after lapse/release, or any equivalent judicial action that clearly results in Kim being legally detained pending trial during the resolution window.
- Non-qualifying events include: mere prosecutorial requests not yet ruled on, routine trial hearings with no custody ruling, or reports about detention status that do not identify a court decision within the window.
- If Kim is already detained on 2025-12-03, the question still requires a qualifying court decision between 2025-12-03 and 2026-01-02; mere continued detention absent a new court action does not count.
- If available sources conflict, the primary source will be an official South Korean court, prosecution service, or Ministry of Justice announcement. If no official statement is available, a consensus of at least two credible reports from major outlets may be used.

Primary sources for resolution:
- Supreme Court of Korea / court-related announcements: https://www.scourt.go.kr/
- Supreme Prosecutors' Office of the Republic of Korea: https://www.spo.go.kr/
- Ministry of Justice, Republic of Korea: https://www.moj.go.kr/

Secondary sources if needed:
- Yonhap News Agency: https://en.yna.co.kr/
- The Korea Herald: https://www.koreaherald.com/
- Reuters World News: https://www.reuters.com/world/

If no authoritative or consensus reporting establishes whether such a court decision occurred within the window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Custody decisions are a strong procedural signal of case seriousness, evidentiary strength, and judicial concern about tampering or flight. A fresh decision to keep Kim detained before trial would materially increase the likelihood that she faces a prison sentence by March 2026, while a release or absence of renewed detention pressure would point in the opposite direction.

question: Pepe ETF in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any spot Pepe (https://etherscan.io/token/0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933) ETF receives approval from the SEC by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will any issuer publicly file an initial or amended SEC Form S-1 for a U.S. spot Pepe ETF between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A spot Pepe ETF cannot launch without a Securities Act registration statement, typically on Form S-1, becoming effective. That makes an S-1 filing a meaningful near-term indicator for the ultimate question of whether any spot Pepe ETF will receive SEC approval by the end of 2025. Recent SEC policy changes have made this especially relevant: on September 18, 2025, the SEC approved generic listing standards for certain commodity-based crypto ETPs, and by late September the SEC had reportedly asked issuers in several altcoin ETF cases to withdraw 19b-4 filings and proceed via S-1s instead, potentially compressing timelines substantially. See Yahoo Finance coverage of the new framework and withdrawal requests: https://finance.yahoo.com/ and CoinDesk reporting that issuers now may need only an S-1 and that approvals could move very quickly: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/29/sec-tells-issuers-to-pull-19b-4s-etfs-could-be-approved-absurdly-fast/ .

The ultimate market concerns a very small-cap memecoin, Pepe, specifically the ERC-20 token at contract address 0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933 on Ethereum: https://etherscan.io/token/0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933 . Compared with larger tokens like SOL, XRP, LTC, ADA, and DOGE, there is no widely reported mainstream U.S. ETF filing activity for Pepe as of 2025-10-01 in the materials provided. That means an actual S-1 filing for a Pepe ETF in October 2025 would be a substantial update toward the ultimate approval question, while the absence of such a filing by month-end would be evidence against fast-track approval by year-end.

Because the SEC's new framework appears to have shifted many crypto ETF pathways away from exchange rule-change filings and toward issuer registration statements, a Pepe-specific S-1 filing is more informative than simply asking whether a Pepe ETF is approved by an earlier date. It tracks whether any sponsor is seriously attempting to bring such a product to market under the current regime.

Sources:
Etherscan Pepe token page — https://etherscan.io/token/0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933
CoinDesk, "SEC Tells Issuers to Pull 19b-4s; ETFs Could Be Approved 'Absurdly Fast'" — https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/29/sec-tells-issuers-to-pull-19b-4s-etfs-could-be-approved-absurdly-fast/
SEC EDGAR company filings search — https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/
SEC Forms List (including S-1) — https://www.sec.gov/forms
Yahoo Finance crypto ETF framework coverage — https://finance.yahoo.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, the SEC EDGAR system shows a publicly available filing of an initial Form S-1 or an amended registration statement (for example, S-1/A) for a U.S. exchange-traded fund, trust, or similar vehicle that explicitly states in the filing that it seeks to provide spot exposure to Pepe, and where Pepe refers to the token with Ethereum contract address 0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933.

This question resolves No if no such filing becomes publicly available on SEC EDGAR during that window.

For avoidance of doubt:
- The qualifying event must occur between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, based on the filing date shown on EDGAR.
- The filing must be public on SEC EDGAR: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/
- The filing must explicitly identify Pepe exposure; mere rumors, press releases, state-level trust registrations, ticker reservations, or exchange listing applications without an S-1 do not count.
- Filings for futures-based, leveraged, inverse, or basket funds do not count unless the filing explicitly states the product is a spot Pepe fund or trust whose principal intended exposure is to spot Pepe.
- If the filing names "Pepe" ambiguously, resolution should rely on the text of the filing. It counts only if the filing clearly refers to the ERC-20 token at 0x6982508145454ce325ddbe47a25d4ec3d2311933 or otherwise unambiguously identifies the same asset.
- If a filing is submitted during the window but only becomes public on EDGAR after 2025-10-31, it does not count for Yes.
- If EDGAR is unavailable, a fallback source is the SEC's main filings/news pages or a consensus of at least two credible reports that link to the underlying SEC filing. Primary source remains SEC EDGAR.

Primary resolution source: SEC EDGAR search, https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/
Fallback source: SEC website, https://www.sec.gov/
Reference on Form S-1: https://www.sec.gov/forms
subquestions.rationale: A Pepe ETF approval by year-end is much more plausible if at least one issuer files a Pepe-specific S-1 in October. An S-1 filing is a concrete signal of sponsor intent, legal preparation, and willingness to test SEC receptivity under the new crypto ETF framework. It is a different observable event from approval itself and should materially update forecasts on the ultimate question.

question: Will Michael Anton be next National Security Advisor?
description:
This market will resolve according to the next person Donald Trump appoints to the National Security Advisor position by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on Trump's first announcement - if Trump announces another person to this position first, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

This market refers to the first permanent National Security Advisor following Mike Waltz's departure from the role; any acting advisor or otherwise temporary advisor will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly state between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 that Marco Rubio will remain National Security Advisor on a permanent basis or that he does not plan to appoint a separate permanent National Security Advisor in 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question turns on who Trump appoints as the first permanent National Security Advisor after Mike Waltz's departure. Public signaling from Trump about whether he intends to keep Secretary of State Marco Rubio in the role, rather than appoint someone else, is a strong leading indicator because the market resolves on Trump's first appointment announcement. Reporting before 2025-11-30 indicates that Rubio has been serving in the role after Waltz's removal, and that the White House had not yet named a permanent replacement. The Hill reported in July 2025 that 'Secretary of State Marco Rubio will lead the NSA after Waltz's departure,' while criticizing the dual-hat arrangement as unusual and potentially dysfunctional: https://thehill.com/opinion/national-security/5399357-trumps-non-security-council-is-another-ticking-time-bomb/ .

Separately, Mike Waltz was confirmed in September 2025 as U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, making a return to the NSA role unlikely and reinforcing that the administration had moved on from him. PBS/AP reported the confirmation on 2025-09-19: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/senate-confirms-former-national-security-adviser-mike-waltz-as-trumps-un-ambassador ; NBC also reported the confirmation and noted Waltz had served briefly as national security adviser before removal: https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senate-confirms-former-trump-national-security-adviser-ambassador-un-rcna230000 .

Because Marco Rubio is already the acting or dual-hatted incumbent, a clear Trump statement that Rubio will remain in the post permanently, or that no separate permanent NSA will be named in 2025, would materially reduce the probability that Michael Anton becomes the next National Security Advisor. Conversely, the absence of such a statement leaves more room for an outside appointment such as Anton.

Sources:
The Hill - Trump's 'non-security council' is another ticking time bomb - https://thehill.com/opinion/national-security/5399357-trumps-non-security-council-is-another-ticking-time-bomb/
PBS NewsHour / AP - Senate confirms former national security adviser Mike Waltz as Trump's UN ambassador - https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/senate-confirms-former-national-security-adviser-mike-waltz-as-trumps-un-ambassador
NBC News - Senate confirms former Trump national security adviser as ambassador to the U.N. - https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/senate-confirms-former-trump-national-security-adviser-ambassador-un-rcna230000
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive, Donald Trump publicly states in an official or clearly attributable public forum that either: (a) Marco Rubio will remain National Security Advisor on a permanent basis, or (b) Trump does not plan to appoint a separate permanent National Security Advisor in 2025.

Qualifying statements include: remarks published by the White House transcript archive (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), a White House press gaggle/transcript, a post from Trump's official Truth Social account if archived by a credible source, or on-the-record quotes reported by multiple credible outlets such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/), or PBS NewsHour (https://www.pbs.org/newshour/).

Examples that count:
- 'Marco Rubio is my permanent National Security Advisor.'
- 'I'm not naming anyone else; Rubio will keep the job.'
- 'We are not filling the National Security Advisor post separately this year.'

Examples that do not count:
- Generic praise of Rubio without reference to permanency or appointment plans.
- Statements by press secretaries, aides, or anonymous sources unless Trump himself is directly quoted on the record.
- Reporting that Rubio is still acting advisor absent a Trump statement about permanence or no further appointment.

If Trump makes contradictory statements during the window, the question resolves Yes if at least one qualifying affirmative statement occurred during the window. If no such statement occurs between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive, resolve No.

Primary sources for resolution: White House official transcripts and statements at https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ ; secondary confirmation from Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ and AP https://apnews.com/ .
subquestions.rationale: This is a distinct observable indicator, not a restatement of whether Anton is appointed. If Trump publicly commits to Rubio remaining in the role or to not naming a separate permanent NSA in 2025, Anton's chances should fall sharply. The subquestion directly tracks whether the administration is even looking for an outside permanent pick.

question: U.S. forces in Gaza in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if active regular US military personnel physically enter Gaza at any point between July 28, 2025, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. 

US military personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify. 

US military personnel entering buffer zones under control of Israel will not qualify.

High ranking U.S. service members entering Gaza for diplomatic purposes (and their accompanying entourage), military contractors, military advisors, and special operation forces will not qualify. 

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. government publicly announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, that U.S. military personnel will participate in an international or multinational mission operating inside Gaza?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether regular U.S. forces might physically enter Gaza by the end of 2025, because an official U.S. commitment to a mission operating inside Gaza would materially increase the chance of later on-the-ground U.S. military presence, even if the initial stated role is monitoring, logistics, engineering, or force protection rather than combat. Recent reporting indicates the U.S. has already deployed roughly 200 troops to Israel to support Gaza ceasefire implementation and a coordination cell, while multiple outlets reported that Washington and European partners have been discussing an international stabilization force for Gaza under some form of external mandate. At the same time, several reports say the U.S. has publicly ruled out U.S. combat troops for Gaza, making any reversal or partial commitment informative rather than trivial.

Relevant current state:
- ABC/other cited reporting summarized by Хартия 97 said U.S. military personnel began arriving in Israel on 2025-10-11 to establish a coordination center and that they would support implementation of the ceasefire "without entering Gaza". https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/10/11/615728/
- Saudi Gazette similarly reported at least 200 U.S. personnel operating from Hatzor Air Base in Israel to monitor the ceasefire, in the context of a broader multinational stabilization effort. https://saudigazette.com.sa/article/000000
- News18 reported on 2025-10-26 that the Trump administration was considering an international force for Gaza while ruling out U.S. troops, and that Israel would control which foreign troops could enter Gaza. https://www.news18.com/world/we-are-in-control-netanyahu-says-israel-will-choose-which-foreign-troops-can-enter-gaza-000000.html
- Ynet reported on 2025-10-18 that U.S. and European officials were advancing a UN Security Council draft resolution for a Gaza stabilization force, while saying British and U.S. combat troops were excluded and the U.S. role centered on a cell in Israel. https://www.ynetnews.com/article/000000
- Times of Israel reported on 2025-10-26 that Egyptian military forces and heavy equipment had entered Gaza and that U.S. drones were operating over Gaza, suggesting foreign operational involvement around Gaza is already expanding even absent acknowledged U.S. ground entry. https://www.timesofisrael.com/daily-briefing-oct-26-day-751-egyptians-enter-gaza-as-us-drones-fly-above-strip/

Because the ultimate market excludes diplomatic visits, contractors, advisors, and special operations forces, a public announcement that regular U.S. military personnel will participate in a mission operating inside Gaza is not identical to the ultimate question. But it is a strong crux: if such an announcement happens, forecasters should update upward on the probability that regular U.S. forces later physically enter Gaza.

Sources:
- Charter97 summary of ABC reporting: https://charter97.org/en/news/2025/10/11/615728/
- News18: https://www.news18.com/world/we-are-in-control-netanyahu-says-israel-will-choose-which-foreign-troops-can-enter-gaza-000000.html
- Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/daily-briefing-oct-26-day-751-egyptians-enter-gaza-as-us-drones-fly-above-strip/
- Ynetnews: https://www.ynetnews.com/article/000000
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, the U.S. federal government publicly announces that U.S. military personnel will participate in an international, multinational, stabilization, monitoring, peace implementation, ceasefire monitoring, humanitarian-security, or similar mission that is explicitly stated to operate inside the Gaza Strip.

Qualifying announcements must meet all of the following:
1. They are issued or clearly attributed to an official U.S. government source, such as the White House, U.S. Department of Defense, CENTCOM, U.S. Department of State, or a named U.S. official speaking on the record in a formal briefing or official statement.
2. They explicitly state that U.S. military personnel will participate in a mission operating inside Gaza, or that U.S. military personnel are authorized/deployed/assigned to such a mission inside Gaza.
3. The announcement concerns U.S. military personnel (not only contractors, intelligence officers, diplomats, or unspecified "American personnel").

This question resolves No if no such official public announcement occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

Clarifications:
- The question is about a public announcement, not whether the mission actually deploys within the window.
- The announcement need not specify combat duties; logistics, engineering, monitoring, force protection, or coordination roles count, provided the mission is explicitly described as operating inside Gaza.
- Announcements limited to operations in Israel, offshore, in Gaza airspace only, or at border crossings outside Gaza do not count.
- Announcements limited to special operations forces, advisors, diplomats, or contractors do not count unless they also explicitly include regular U.S. military personnel.
- Leaks or anonymous press reports alone do not count unless later confirmed by an official U.S. public statement within the window.
- If official U.S. statements are internally contradictory, resolution should follow the latest clear official statement issued within the window.

Primary resolution sources:
- White House statements/briefings: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- U.S. Department of Defense news/releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/
- U.S. Central Command news: https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/NEWS-ARTICLES/
- U.S. Department of State press statements: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/

Fallback source:
- If the above sites are unavailable, resolution may rely on contemporaneous reporting from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or AP News (https://apnews.com/) that quotes the official announcement verbatim or links directly to it.
subquestions.rationale: A formal U.S. announcement committing military personnel to a mission inside Gaza would be a strong precursor event for the ultimate question. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it concerns policy commitment rather than actual physical entry, yet it would substantially raise the likelihood that regular U.S. forces later enter Gaza before year-end.

question: Will TIME's Person of the Year for 2025 be a human?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any human is named TIME's Person of the Year for 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, any person or group of people will count as “humans.” This includes explicitly named individuals and their titles such as "Taylor Swift" or "Bad Bunny", general public designations such as “You” (i.e., internet users), and collective entities such as “The Protester” or “The Silence Breakers.”

In the event that multiple entities are named TIME's 2025 Person of the Year, this market will resolve to "No" if at least one of them is not a human.

If, for any reason, the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will TIME publish, between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02 inclusive, at least one cover story, homepage feature, or interview package primarily focused on Donald Trump?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME's Person of the Year is often awarded to a figure who dominated the year's news cycle, and major TIME editorial attention late in the year can be an informative signal about likely candidates. Donald Trump has previously been named TIME Person of the Year (2016), and a September 30, 2025 entertainment report citing Politico said Trump was reportedly set to be named TIME's 2025 Person of the Year, though this remains unconfirmed and should be treated as a rumor rather than a resolution source (https://www.justjared.com/2025/09/30/time-latest-articles-news-and-photos/). Because the ultimate market resolves Yes if the honoree is any human and No if any non-human is included, evidence that TIME is centering a specific human candidate such as Trump is directionally relevant.

TIME continues to publish ongoing political coverage on its website and in its magazine; this makes near-term editorial emphasis observable before the December Person of the Year announcement. The official TIME site has dedicated news and politics sections where such features would appear (https://time.com/ and https://time.com/section/politics/). If TIME prominently features Trump in a cover story, homepage package, or interview during October 2025, that would be evidence that the editorial staff sees him as central to the year's narrative, increasing the chance that the eventual selection is a human rather than a non-human concept, object, or AI-related entity.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about a specific observable editorial event involving one plausible human candidate during a narrow pre-announcement window. It is grounded in current reporting and the normal publication cadence of TIME.

Sources:
TIME homepage — https://time.com/
TIME Politics section — https://time.com/section/politics/
Just Jared report citing Politico rumor — https://www.justjared.com/2025/09/30/time-latest-articles-news-and-photos/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02 inclusive, TIME publishes at least one item meeting all of the following conditions: (1) it appears on TIME's official website (https://time.com/) or is an official TIME magazine cover posted by TIME; (2) Donald Trump is the primary subject of the piece; and (3) the item is clearly one of the following: a magazine cover story, a homepage feature package, or a Q&A/interview package.

Primary source for resolution: TIME's official website search/results and archived article pages on https://time.com/.

Operational definitions:
- "Primary subject" means Trump's name and/or image is the central focus in the headline, cover line, URL slug, hero image, or article framing.
- "Homepage feature package" means a prominently featured package on TIME's homepage or a dedicated feature landing page published by TIME, not merely a brief mention inside a broader roundup.
- "Interview package" means an article or package presented by TIME as an interview/Q&A/conversation with Trump.

Resolution procedure:
1. Check TIME's official site (https://time.com/) and relevant section pages such as https://time.com/section/politics/ for items first published between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02 inclusive.
2. If a qualifying item is found, resolve Yes.
3. If no qualifying item is found by the end of 2025-11-02 UTC, resolve No.

Fallback criteria:
- If TIME's site search or section pages are unavailable, use the Internet Archive's captures of TIME pages (https://web.archive.org/) plus any still-live TIME article URLs as fallback evidence.
- Third-party reporting may be used only to locate a TIME URL, not by itself to resolve the question.
- If publication date is ambiguous, use the date shown on the TIME article page; if unavailable, use the earliest archived timestamp from the Internet Archive.

This question concerns only events occurring between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02 inclusive; items published outside that window do not count.

Resolution sources:
TIME official site — https://time.com/
TIME Politics section — https://time.com/section/politics/
Internet Archive — https://web.archive.org/
subquestions.rationale: If TIME gives major editorial prominence to Trump in October, that is a concrete indicator that a human candidate is leading the internal narrative for Person of the Year. This helps discriminate between a human honoree and possibilities such as AI, a concept, or a mixed/non-human selection.

question: Will Trump release more Epstein files in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration (including any federal court) publicly releases any files pertaining to the illegal activities of Jeffrey Epstein, which weren’t previously public between August 25 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only files which were created prior to the start of the Trump Administration (January 20, 2025, 12:00 PM ET) will qualify. 

Announcements of declassifications or releases that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-29, will the U.S. Department of Justice or FBI file or publicly post any new motion, notice, letter, or statement explicitly seeking to unseal, declassify, or release additional Jeffrey Epstein-related records that were not already public as of 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for any further 2025 Epstein-file release is whether the executive branch takes an affirmative procedural step toward disclosure. Recent reporting suggests the Trump administration has mostly resisted broader release so far: on Sept. 6, 2025, DOJ reportedly asked a judge to keep two names private in Epstein-related records rather than expand disclosure, indicating an ongoing legal fight over secrecy rather than a settled release process (FrankNez Media, 2025-09-06: https://franknez.com/trump-administration-now-asks-judge-to-keep-two-names-private-in-the-epstein-files/). PBS reported on Sept. 16, 2025 that FBI Director Kash Patel told the Senate Judiciary Committee the FBI would release whatever it is legally permitted to release, but also emphasized limits from the original investigation and protective court orders, highlighting that a fresh filing or official statement would be an important leading indicator of actual release momentum (PBS, 2025-09-16: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-sen-kennedy-presses-fbi-director-patel-to-release-the-epstein-files). 

Separately, Congress has already made some Epstein-related material public. The House Oversight Committee released roughly 33,000 pages in early September 2025 after receiving documents from DOJ, but reports indicated much of this material was already public or heavily redacted, so mere existence of congressional pressure does not imply the administration is on track to release genuinely new files (Times of India, 2025-09-02: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/epstein-files-us-house-panel-releases-first-batch-33000-investigation-documents-made-public/articleshow/123657866.cms; DNA India, 2025-09-03: https://www.dnaindia.com/world/report-epstein-files-released-amid-trump-admin-scrutiny-over-33000-investigation-documents-made-public-3167069). 

Because the ultimate question asks whether the Trump administration or a federal court will publicly release any previously nonpublic Epstein-related files later in 2025, an observable precursor is whether DOJ/FBI initiates or endorses additional disclosure during October. A new official step—such as a court filing to unseal more records, a formal declassification order, or a public DOJ/FBI posting announcing intended release of additional nonpublic Epstein materials—would materially increase the odds of actual release before year-end, while continued inaction or efforts to keep records sealed would point the other way.

Sources:
PBS NewsHour - WATCH: Sen. Kennedy presses FBI Director Patel to release the Epstein files - https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-sen-kennedy-presses-fbi-director-patel-to-release-the-epstein-files
FrankNez Media - Trump Administration Now Asks Judge To Keep Two Names Private in The Epstein Files - https://franknez.com/trump-administration-now-asks-judge-to-keep-two-names-private-in-the-epstein-files/
Times of India - Epstein Files: US House panel releases first batch; 33,000 investigation documents made public - https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us/epstein-files-us-house-panel-releases-first-batch-33000-investigation-documents-made-public/articleshow/123657866.cms
DNA India - Epstein files RELEASED: Amid Trump admin scrutiny, over 33000 investigation documents made public - https://www.dnaindia.com/world/report-epstein-files-released-amid-trump-admin-scrutiny-over-33000-investigation-documents-made-public-3167069
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-29 23:59:59 UTC (inclusive), either the U.S. Department of Justice or the Federal Bureau of Investigation does at least one of the following with explicit reference to Jeffrey Epstein, Ghislaine Maxwell, or the Epstein investigation: (1) files in a federal court a new motion, notice, letter, or memorandum seeking to unseal, disclose, declassify, or otherwise permit public release of additional records that were not already public as of 2025-10-01; or (2) posts on an official DOJ or FBI website a public statement, press release, or document announcing that it is seeking or authorizing the public release of additional nonpublic Epstein-related records.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying DOJ/FBI action occurs during that window.

For avoidance of doubt: 
- A purely congressional action, media report, or politician's statement does not count unless it is accompanied by a qualifying official DOJ/FBI filing or official DOJ/FBI web posting.
- Mere commentary such as 'we will comply with the law' does not count unless it specifically seeks or authorizes additional release of records.
- Reposting or reannouncing a pre-2025-10-01 filing or statement does not count unless the post itself contains a new substantive request or authorization for additional release.
- A filing or statement that only seeks to keep records sealed, maintain redactions, or oppose disclosure does not count as Yes.
- If the relevant court docket or official page is temporarily unavailable, resolution should use archived copies or credible reporting that quotes and links the official filing, but priority goes to the original official source.

Primary sources for resolution:
- U.S. Department of Justice website: https://www.justice.gov/
- FBI News / Press Releases: https://www.fbi.gov/news
- PACER / federal court dockets (resolver may need the relevant case docket if identified): https://pacer.uscourts.gov/

Secondary confirmation sources if needed:
- CourtListener: https://www.courtlistener.com/
- PBS NewsHour politics coverage: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question turns on whether any previously nonpublic Epstein-related files are actually released later in 2025. A strong near-term precursor is whether DOJ or FBI takes a fresh official step toward disclosure. Such action would likely be necessary before any later release and would meaningfully update forecasters, while continued absence of action or further defensive sealing behavior would reduce the chance of release.

question: Trump imposes tariff on semiconductors by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action enacting a tariff on imports of semiconductors into the United States by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only tariffs specifically targeting semiconductors will qualify. For example, a general tariff (tariffs on all imports into the U.S.) or country-specific tariff (tariffs on all imports from China) will not count toward this market's resolution.

Tariffs on semiconductors from a specific country will qualify.

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration publish, between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23, a formal semiconductor-import tariff proposal or notice in the Federal Register, on regulations.gov, or on an official White House/Commerce/USTR webpage that specifies either a tariff rate or a concrete tariff-trigger mechanism for semiconductor imports?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator because the ultimate question asks whether Trump will actually enact a semiconductor-specific tariff by 2025-12-31. By late 2025, there had already been repeated public statements from Trump that such a tariff was coming. On 2025-08-06/07, Trump said the U.S. would impose about a 100% tariff on chips and semiconductors, with exemptions for firms building in the U.S., as reported by Reuters-republished coverage and other outlets such as MarketScreener: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Trump-says-US-will-levy-100-tariff-on-some-chip-imports-50786769/ . In early September he again said a tariff would come "very shortly" and be "fairly substantial," according to Taipei Times coverage of his remarks: https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2025/09/06/2003832876 .

There were also reports in late September that the administration was considering more concrete implementation mechanisms. The Economic Times, citing a Wall Street Journal report, said U.S. officials were discussing a 1:1 ratio rule under which firms would need to produce domestically as many chips as they import or else face a tariff: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/global-trends/us-plans-to-require-a-11-ratio-of-domestically-made-to-imported-chips-wsj-reports/articleshow/123944519.cms . Another report said officials were weighing tariffs on electronics based on chip content: https://www.econotimes.com/Trump-Administration-Weighs-Tariffs-on-Electronics-Based-on-Chip-Content-1719138 .

However, public threats are not the same as formal policy steps. For a semiconductor tariff to become real, the administration would likely need to move from speeches and leaks to a published official proposal, notice, determination, or implementation document. Such publication would be a strong leading indicator that the administration is serious, coordinated, and legally prepared enough to impose a qualifying tariff before year-end.

The likely official venues for such a step are the Federal Register (for notices, proposed rules, determinations, or implementation notices), regulations.gov (if a rulemaking or comment process is opened), or official pages from the White House, the U.S. Department of Commerce, or the Office of the United States Trade Representative. Federal Register search portal: https://www.federalregister.gov/ ; regulations.gov search portal: https://www.regulations.gov/ ; White House briefing room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ ; Commerce news room: https://www.commerce.gov/news ; USTR press releases: https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases .

Sources:
MarketScreener - Trump says US will levy 100% tariff on some chip imports - https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Trump-says-US-will-levy-100-tariff-on-some-chip-imports-50786769/
Taipei Times - US to tax chip imports from non-US investing firms - https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2025/09/06/2003832876
Economic Times - US plans to require a 1:1 ratio of domestically made to imported chips - https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/global-trends/us-plans-to-require-a-11-ratio-of-domestically-made-to-imported-chips-wsj-reports/articleshow/123944519.cms
EconoTimes - Trump Administration Weighs Tariffs on Electronics Based on Chip Content - https://www.econotimes.com/Trump-Administration-Weighs-Tariffs-on-Electronics-Based-on-Chip-Content-1719138
Federal Register - https://www.federalregister.gov/
regulations.gov - https://www.regulations.gov/
White House Briefing Room - https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
U.S. Department of Commerce News - https://www.commerce.gov/news
USTR Press Releases - https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive), at least one official U.S. government publication appears in any of the following sources: the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov/), regulations.gov (https://www.regulations.gov/), the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), the U.S. Department of Commerce website (https://www.commerce.gov/), or the USTR website (https://ustr.gov/), and that publication explicitly concerns tariffs on imports of semiconductors, chips, or closely synonymous semiconductor products into the United States, and also does at least one of the following:
1) states a numerical tariff rate, or
2) states a concrete tariff-trigger mechanism (for example, a domestic-production ratio rule, investment-based exemption rule, country-specific semiconductor tariff scheme, or other operational condition under which semiconductor imports would incur a tariff), or
3) opens a formal process to implement such a semiconductor-specific tariff policy.

For avoidance of doubt, the publication must be more formal than a mere speech transcript or vague statement of intent; it must be a notice, proposed rule, determination, implementation guidance, request for comments, fact sheet tied to a specific policy rollout, executive order text, proclamation text, or comparable official policy document. A speech transcript alone counts only if it is published as the text of an executive order, proclamation, memorandum, determination, or other operative official action.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official publication appears between 2025-10-24 and 2025-11-23 (inclusive).

A general tariff proposal not specifically targeting semiconductors does not count. A country-specific tariff counts only if semiconductors/chips are specifically identified as the subject goods. A proposal targeting finished electronics based on chip content does not count unless the official document explicitly proposes a tariff on semiconductor imports themselves or clearly defines semiconductor imports as covered goods.

Primary source for resolution will be the official publication itself in the sources above. If publication timing is disputed, the timestamp shown on the official page or Federal Register/regulations.gov entry will govern. If one of the listed official sources is unavailable, archived copies and corroboration from another listed official source may be used. If no authoritative timestamped official document can be verified, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A formal published proposal is a strong precursor to actual enactment. It captures whether the administration is moving from rhetoric and trial balloons to concrete policy machinery, which should substantially raise the odds of a semiconductor-specific tariff being imposed by year-end.

question: US Treasury transactions on blockchain in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Department of the Treasury sends any funds or assets via a blockchain between February 4, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes", the payment must be a publicly announced, official transaction involving the sending of assets or funds; exploratory or experimental transactions will not count toward the resolution of this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any U.S. federal executive department or agency publicly announce, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive, a new program to use a public blockchain for official record publication, payments infrastructure, or asset/token issuance?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful leading indicator for whether the U.S. Treasury will send funds or assets via a blockchain in late 2025 is whether federal agencies continue expanding from blockchain data publication into additional official use cases. On August 28, 2025, the U.S. Commerce Department announced that it had begun publishing GDP and other economic data to multiple public blockchains, reportedly the first time a federal agency published economic data on-chain. This suggests growing executive-branch comfort with blockchain as official infrastructure rather than just private-sector experimentation. See Decrypt's coverage of the Commerce announcement: https://decrypt.co/ and Business Standard's report: https://www.business-standard.com/finance/personal-finance/us-govt-puts-gdp-data-on-the-public-blockchain-in-trump-s-crypto-push-125082800062_1.html .

The provided news summary states Commerce partnered with Chainlink and Pyth and that Coinbase, Kraken, and Gemini helped purchase cryptocurrency to pay gas fees for publishing data on-chain, indicating not only messaging support but operational implementation. If additional federal agencies announce comparable or more advanced blockchain programs during September 2025, that would be evidence that the administration is normalizing blockchain use across government functions, increasing the plausibility that Treasury itself could execute a qualifying blockchain transfer before year-end.

Broader policy context also points in this direction. Reporting notes the Trump administration's broader embrace of digital assets, including a strategic Bitcoin reserve and crypto-friendly agency heads, while legal commentary in 2025 has highlighted momentum around stablecoin regulation and reduced supervisory barriers for crypto-related activity. See JD Supra on U.S. blockchain/legal developments: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-august-2025-5591854/ and https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/blockchain-bi-weekly-highlights-of-the-3882263/ . A September announcement by another federal entity would be a more proximal signal than general crypto sentiment because it would show continued real adoption inside government operations.

Sources:
- Business Standard, "US govt puts GDP data on the public blockchain in Trump's crypto push" — https://www.business-standard.com/finance/personal-finance/us-govt-puts-gdp-data-on-the-public-blockchain-in-trump-s-crypto-push-125082800062_1.html
- JD Supra, "Weekly Blockchain Blog - August 2025 #4" — https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/weekly-blockchain-blog-august-2025-5591854/
- JD Supra, "Blockchain+ Bi-Weekly; Highlights of the Last Two Weeks in Web3 Law: May 8, 2025" — https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/blockchain-bi-weekly-highlights-of-the-3882263/
- Decrypt homepage/search root for article lookup on Commerce blockchain announcement — https://decrypt.co/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive, any U.S. federal executive department or agency publicly announces a new program, pilot, launch, or formal partnership to use a public blockchain for at least one of the following official-government functions: (a) publication/attestation of official government records or statistics, (b) payments or settlement infrastructure, or (c) issuance, custody, or transfer of tokenized assets or stablecoins.

For avoidance of doubt, the qualifying announcement must be from a U.S. federal executive department or agency other than merely restating the already-announced August 2025 Commerce Department GDP-on-blockchain initiative. An expansion of that same Commerce initiative counts only if the agency formally announces a materially new use case or additional dataset/program beyond what had already been publicly announced before 2025-09-01.

The announcement must be public and official, such as a press release, agency blog post, agency X/social-media post, speech transcript, Federal Register notice, or posting on an official .gov website. The blockchain must be public/permissionless or explicitly described by the announcing agency as a public blockchain.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources: official U.S. government websites and agency communications, including https://www.commerce.gov/ , https://home.treasury.gov/ , https://www.federalregister.gov/ , and other relevant .gov agency sites. Secondary confirmation may come from credible reporting if the official source is hard to locate, but resolution should rely on an official public announcement when available. If a reported announcement cannot be substantiated by an official government source, it should not count. If the announcement is withdrawn or shown to be fabricated before 2025-09-30, it does not count. If the only relevant event is postponed to after 2025-09-30, the question resolves No.

Useful resolution-source directories:
- Federal Register — https://www.federalregister.gov/
- U.S. Department of Commerce — https://www.commerce.gov/
- U.S. Department of the Treasury — https://home.treasury.gov/
- White House briefings/statements — https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about a Treasury blockchain transfer. A strong near-term crux is whether federal blockchain adoption is still broadening after the Commerce on-chain data launch. A new federal blockchain program in September would indicate rising institutional comfort, implementation capacity, and political support for official blockchain use, all of which increase the odds Treasury executes a qualifying blockchain transaction later in 2025.

question: Will Trump establish a Gaza “Board of Peace” by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the Trump Administration formally announces the establishment of the “Board of Peace” (or a clearly equivalent oversight board fulfilling the same role) by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, resolve “No.”

Only official policy announcements will qualify.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A consensus of credible reporting confirming that the “Board of Peace” or equivalent Gaza oversight board has been established, includes U.S. participation and is operational will also qualify.  

The resolution source will be official announcements from the Trump administration however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or U.S. State Department officially announce at least one named non-U.S. government participant for a Gaza "Board of Peace" or its executive/oversight structure between 2026-01-05 and 2026-01-13?
subquestions.background_information:
A strong indicator that the Trump administration will formally establish a Gaza Board of Peace by late March is whether it can publicly line up actual participants from other governments in the near term. The ultimate market requires an official policy announcement or credible reporting that the board has been established, includes U.S. participation, and is operational. A near-term official announcement naming a foreign-government participant would be meaningful evidence that the administration has moved beyond broad planning into implementation.

Current reporting before 2026-01-05 indicates that the concept is already advanced. Multiple reports say the UN Security Council approved a U.S.-drafted resolution in November 2025 that endorsed a Gaza plan including a transitional "Board of Peace" and an international stabilization force. See AP, 2025-11-18: https://apnews.com/ and Al Jazeera, 2025-11-14: https://www.aljazeera.com/ . Reporting also says several Arab and Muslim-majority states signaled willingness to contribute to the broader effort, including Egypt, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Jordan, Türkiye, Indonesia, and Pakistan; however, those articles do not by themselves amount to a Trump administration policy announcement naming actual board participants. See AP, 2025-11-18: https://apnews.com/ and AFP/NDTV-style reporting summarized here: https://www.ndtv.com/ .

Times of Israel reported on 2025-12-10 that the U.S. was expected to unveil the Board of Peace in late December and that "Board of Peace members would be named soon," implying that as of early January 2026 the naming step may still be outstanding. https://www.timesofisrael.com/ . If the administration starts officially naming non-U.S. participants in the next week, that would materially increase the chance of the full board being formally established by March 31. Conversely, failure to name any such participants soon would be some evidence of delay, diplomatic friction, or implementation problems.

This is not just a restatement of the ultimate question: the board could still be established without named foreign participants by this date, and named participants could be announced without the board yet being formally established. But this event is a plausible crux because the Board of Peace is described in reporting as an international governance/oversight mechanism, so partner participation is likely operationally important.

Sources:
AP, "UN approves the Trump administration's plan for the future of Gaza" — https://apnews.com/
Al Jazeera, "US pushes Security Council to back Gaza plan as Russia offers counter text" — https://www.aljazeera.com/
The Times of Israel, "US expected to unveil Gaza Board of Peace in late December, around Trump-Netanyahu meeting, official says" — https://www.timesofisrael.com/
NDTV, "US Pressures UN Security Council To Adopt Trump's Gaza Peace Plan" — https://www.ndtv.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-05 and 2026-01-13 inclusive, the White House or U.S. Department of State publishes an official announcement, press release, briefing transcript, readout, fact sheet, or equivalent statement that explicitly identifies by name at least one non-U.S. government participant (for example, a state, ministry, or named official acting on behalf of a foreign government) as serving on, joining, or being appointed to the Gaza Board of Peace, or to a clearly subordinate executive/oversight body created as part of that Board of Peace structure.

This question resolves No if no such official U.S. announcement is published during that window.

Qualifying sources are limited to official U.S. government channels, primarily:
- White House official website: https://www.whitehouse.gov/
- U.S. Department of State official website: https://www.state.gov/

Definitions and edge cases:
- "Officially announce" means publication on an official U.S. government website above, or a transcript/readout hosted there.
- "Named non-U.S. government participant" requires an identifiable foreign state actor, such as "Egypt," "the UAE," "the Qatari foreign minister," etc. Vague phrases like "regional partners" or "Arab states" do not count.
- The participant must be linked specifically to the Board of Peace or its executive/oversight structure. Participation only in a stabilization force, humanitarian mechanism, reconstruction conference, or general Gaza diplomacy does not count unless the announcement explicitly ties that participant to the Board of Peace structure.
- If the announcement merely says participants are being discussed, expected, or invited, that does not count.
- If an announcement is first made within the window and later amended, the initial in-window announcement governs unless it is formally retracted before 2026-01-13 23:59:59 UTC.
- If the relevant official websites are unavailable, archived versions from the Internet Archive may be used as a fallback to verify whether an official posting appeared during the window: https://web.archive.org/ .

Resolution window: This question resolves based only on events occurring between 2026-01-05 and 2026-01-13 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: Because the proposed Board of Peace is described as an international oversight mechanism for Gaza, official naming of at least one foreign-government participant would be a concrete sign that the administration is assembling the coalition and governance structure needed for formal establishment. It is a nearer-term, distinct observable event that should meaningfully update forecasts on whether Trump will establish the board by the ultimate deadline.

question: Will Pope Leo visit another country first?
description:
This market will resolve to the first sovereign country that Pope Leo XIV visits after becoming pope.

Italy will not be considered for this market. 

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Pope Leo XIV physically entering the terrestrial territory of the listed country. Whether or not Pope Leo XIV enters the country's airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

If Pope Leo XIV doesn't visit any country by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the Holy See officially announce, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, that Pope Leo XIV will travel to Lebanon before announcing any other foreign papal trip outside Italy?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is about which sovereign country Pope Leo XIV visits first outside Italy. A useful leading indicator is which country receives the first formal Vatican trip announcement, because papal foreign visits are typically preceded by official scheduling from the Holy See Press Office or Vatican News. Recent reporting has pointed to Lebanon as a leading candidate for Pope Leo XIV's first foreign trip. UPI reported on 2025-08-21 that Pope Leo XIV was expected to visit Lebanon sometime before December 2025, citing Cardinal Bechara Boutros Rai and noting that preparations were underway, though the Vatican had not yet officially confirmed the trip: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2025/08/21/pope-leo-lebanon-first-international-trip/ . Reuters-republished coverage also said Lebanon was a likely first trip, while noting that a Turkey trip tied to the 1,700th anniversary of the Council of Nicaea was anticipated for late November: https://www.yahoo.com/news/pope-leo-visit-lebanon-cardinal-170245456.html .

Because the ultimate market resolves on the first actual physical entry into a sovereign country's terrestrial territory, the first official Vatican announcement is not determinative, but it is highly informative. If Lebanon is the first country for which the Holy See publicly announces an outbound trip, that substantially raises the probability that Lebanon will also be the first country actually visited, absent cancellation, postponement, or a surprise earlier trip elsewhere. Conversely, if another country is announced first, that would be evidence against Lebanon being first visited.

The Holy See Press Office and Vatican News are standard authoritative channels for papal travel announcements and schedules. The Holy See Press Office publishes bulletins and travel schedules at https://press.vatican.va/ , and Vatican News maintains papal itinerary coverage at https://www.vaticannews.va/ .

Sources:
