question: U.S. enacts AI safety bill in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a bill that includes at least one of the following provisions is signed into federal law in the United States  by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. 

- Prohibition on Creation or Release: Forbids the creation or release of specific AI systems or models.

- Training Restrictions: Sets limits on how AI systems can be trained, such as restricting access to previously available training data or imposing a maximum limit on the number of parameters used for training.

- Usage Restrictions:  Prevents AI systems from being used in certain applications, such as interacting with customers, interfacing with other applications, or performing actions on the web.

- Human-in-the-Loop Requirements: Requires AI systems to include mechanisms ensuring human oversight or involvement in their operation.

Otherwise this market will resolve to "No". 

The resolution source will be official U.S. federal government (e.g., Congress.gov) however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least one AI-focused U.S. federal bill introduced or textually amended between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 include a requirement that certain AI systems must have human oversight, human review, or a human-in-the-loop before specified high-stakes uses?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether the U.S. will enact a federal AI safety bill by the end of 2025 is whether Congress is actively moving toward concrete statutory language on one of the ultimate question’s enumerated provisions: human-in-the-loop requirements. State legislatures have recently enacted AI restrictions of this kind, especially in health care and mental-health contexts, suggesting a live policy template for federal lawmakers. Texas SB 815, enacted in 2025, restricts the use of AI in utilization review and adverse determinations and preserves human oversight for such decisions, according to JD Supra’s summary: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/upcoming-utilization-review-4258932/ . Utah, Nevada, and Illinois also enacted 2025 laws restricting AI chatbots in therapy or professional mental-health decision-making, reflecting a broader policy trend toward requiring licensed human involvement in high-stakes settings, as summarized by Psychology Today: https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/experimentations/202509/ai-chatbots-in-therapy .

At the federal level, Congress has not yet enacted broad AI safety legislation, but bipartisan interest in AI oversight remains active. Lexology reports that the Senate voted 99-1 to remove a proposed 10-year ban on state AI regulation from the One Big Beautiful Bill, preserving state authority and underscoring that AI regulation remains politically salient: https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=8a2e0b2b-0a40-4c76-9a72-8fd7a4d7b0d3 . Another Lexology roundup notes bipartisan federal proposals such as the AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act and the No Adversarial AI Act, while also describing ongoing concern around child safety and deceptive AI systems: https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=6f7c5d25-4f55-4a66-8b64-56d6f4d4a0a7 .

California’s SB 53, signed September 30, 2025, is also relevant because it established a major new state-level AI governance regime focused on frontier model safety, incident reporting, and compliance transparency. Coverage from The Register describes the law as applying to firms training frontier models above a 10^26 operations threshold and requiring safety frameworks and incident reports: https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/30/california_ai_transparency_law/ . WZTV reports that supporters explicitly framed SB 53 as a possible model for federal action and that federal officials and lawmakers are concerned about a patchwork of state rules, increasing pressure for a national framework: https://fox17.com/news/nation-world/california-becomes-first-us-state-to-require-ai-transparency .

Because the ultimate question resolves based on whether a federal law signed by year-end contains any of several safety provisions, observable congressional uptake of human-oversight language during October 2025 would be a meaningful crux. Such language would not itself resolve the ultimate question, but it would indicate legislative drafting momentum toward one of the exact provision categories that would qualify.

Sources:
JD Supra - Upcoming Utilization Review Restrictions in Light of Emerging Artificial Intelligence — https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/upcoming-utilization-review-4258932/
Psychology Today - AI Chatbots in Therapy — https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/blog/experimentations/202509/ai-chatbots-in-therapy
Lexology - Quarterly AI Update | Q3 2025 — https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=8a2e0b2b-0a40-4c76-9a72-8fd7a4d7b0d3
Lexology - Meta Platforms Inc.'s AI Policies Under Investigation and States Continue to Pursue AI Regulation - AI: The Washington Report — https://www.lexology.com/library/detail.aspx?g=6f7c5d25-4f55-4a66-8b64-56d6f4d4a0a7
The Register - California becomes first US state to require AI transparency — https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/30/california_ai_transparency_law/
WZTV/Fox17 - California AI law could pave way for a new national standard — https://fox17.com/news/nation-world/california-becomes-first-us-state-to-require-ai-transparency
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), at least one bill or amendment in the U.S. Congress is officially introduced, reported, or published in legislative text on Congress.gov and that text explicitly requires human oversight, human review, human approval, or a human-in-the-loop for at least one specified AI use case.

For resolution, qualifying text must satisfy all of the following:
1. The legislative item must be a federal congressional bill, joint resolution with substantive legislative text, manager’s amendment, committee substitute, or floor amendment with publicly available text on Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/ .
2. The relevant text must newly appear on Congress.gov during the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive, based on the official action date, introduction date, amendment submission date, committee report date, or publication date shown there.
3. The text must refer to AI, artificial intelligence, automated decision systems, foundation models, generative AI, or substantially similar terminology.
4. The text must impose a requirement for human involvement in operation or decision-making, such as requiring a human to review, approve, supervise, oversee, or remain responsible for outputs before certain uses occur. Mere disclosure that AI is being used, or a nonbinding sense-of-Congress statement, does not qualify.
5. The requirement must apply to some identifiable category of use, sector, model, or deployment context; generic encouragement of best practices does not qualify.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying legislative text appears on Congress.gov between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

Primary source: Congress.gov advanced search and bill text pages, including legislation and amendments — https://www.congress.gov/ .

Fallback sources, if Congress.gov is temporarily unavailable or materially incomplete, are official House and Senate legislative pages and the Government Publishing Office's legislative documents repository: https://www.house.gov/ , https://www.senate.gov/ , and https://www.govinfo.gov/ . If no authoritative federal legislative text can be accessed from these sources, the question should resolve Unresolvable.

Edge cases:
- A press release describing planned legislation does not count unless the legislative text itself is publicly available from an official source within the window.
- An amendment counts only if its text is officially published during the window; mere filing without accessible text does not count.
- If a bill is introduced before 2025-10-01 but is amended or reported with newly published qualifying human-oversight text during the window, that does count.
- If qualifying text is published after 2025-10-31, it does not count, even if announced earlier.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question turns on whether a federal law signed in 2025 contains one of several specific AI safety provisions, including human-in-the-loop requirements. New congressional text adopting that exact policy mechanism in October would be a strong leading indicator that lawmakers are converging on a legislatively viable safety approach before year-end, especially given recent state precedents and growing concern about a patchwork of state AI rules.

question: Major meteor strike (10kt+) in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 10 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will NASA JPL's Fireball and Bolide Data list at least 3 natural fireball events with Impact Energy >= 1 kiloton occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive, UTC)?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an indicator question for the chance of a much larger 10 kt+ atmospheric bolide later in 2025. Periods with unusually frequent kiloton-class fireballs may indicate either a temporarily elevated realized rate of sizable meteoroid entries or a run of bad luck that should update forecasters somewhat upward on the probability of an even larger event before year-end.

NASA JPL's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) maintains a public Fireball and Bolide Data table that records detected atmospheric impact events and includes an "Impact Energy (kt)" field: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/ . The ultimate market itself uses this repository as its primary source, so a subquestion based on the same authoritative dataset is operationally convenient while still asking about a different observable event.

Recent 2025 events show that sub-10 kt fireballs are occurring and being recorded. For example, a bright fireball over southern Japan on 2025-08-19 was reported at about 1.6 kt by CNEOS-derived reporting, which is well below the ultimate market's 10 kt threshold but in the same general tail of the size distribution. See reporting here: https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-on-august-19-2025/ . By contrast, the widely reported Georgia event in June 2025 was only about 20 tons TNT equivalent (0.02 kt), illustrating that many notable public fireballs are far below 1 kt and therefore this threshold is materially more selective: https://www.mediaite.com/news/watch-fireball-streaks-through-sky-in-stunning-sight-officials-believe-it-may-have-hit-house/ .

Using a count threshold of 3 events >= 1 kt within one month aims to avoid a near-certain or near-impossible question. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it tracks the frequency of moderately energetic atmospheric entries, not whether any single event exceeds 10 kt.

Sources:
NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data - https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
The Watchers: Bright fireball with impact energy of 1.6 kilotons observed over southern Japan on August 19 - https://watchers.news/2025/08/20/bright-fireball-impact-energy-1-6-kilotons-observed-over-southern-japan-on-august-19-2025/
Mediaite: WATCH: 'Fireball' Streaks Through Sky in Stunning Sight - https://www.mediaite.com/news/watch-fireball-streaks-through-sky-in-stunning-sight-officials-believe-it-may-have-hit-house/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if NASA JPL's Fireball and Bolide Data repository lists 3 or more distinct events satisfying all of the following conditions: (1) the event date/time in the table is between 2025-09-01 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive; (2) the event is a natural fireball/bolide entry in the CNEOS dataset; and (3) the table's "Impact Energy (kt)" value for the event is greater than or equal to 1.0. Otherwise, it resolves No.

Primary source: NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data, https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/ .

Resolution procedure:
1. Count all rows in the CNEOS table whose event timestamp falls within the window from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01 inclusive, using the date/time presented by the dataset.
2. Among those rows, count only entries with "Impact Energy (kt)" >= 1.0.
3. If the count is 3 or more, resolve Yes; if 0, 1, or 2, resolve No.

Definitions and edge cases:
- "At least 3" means 3 or more qualifying rows in the dataset.
- If CNEOS later revises an event's energy upward or downward, the final value shown in the dataset at time of resolution governs.
- Duplicate listings for the same physical event should count once; if the dataset appears to contain duplicates, use the final cleaned table if available.
- Events involving spacecraft, debris, or artificial reentries do not count; if such an event somehow appears in the table, it should be excluded unless CNEOS clearly classifies it as a natural meteoroid event.
- If the CNEOS dataset has not been updated to include all dates through 2025-10-01 by 2025-11-15, or if the repository becomes permanently unavailable, resolve using a consensus of credible sources that explicitly report qualifying natural atmospheric impact events and their energies, prioritizing NASA, ESA, IAWN, or U.S. government sources. Relevant fallback institutions include ESA's NEO Coordination Centre https://neo.ssa.esa.int/ and IAWN https://iawn.net/ . If no such credible consensus can establish the count, the question should be considered unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
NASA JPL CNEOS Fireball and Bolide Data - https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
ESA NEO Coordination Centre - https://neo.ssa.esa.int/
International Asteroid Warning Network - https://iawn.net/
subquestions.rationale: A 10 kt+ bolide is a tail event from the same underlying distribution that produces 1 kt+ atmospheric fireballs. An unusually active month for kiloton-class entries would be evidence, albeit imperfect, for a higher realized near-term chance of a major strike before the end of 2025.

question: Jon Stewart cancelled by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed person is no longer host of their respective show for any length of time between September 18, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of this person's resignation or removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation or removal goes into effect.

If the owning network or its parent company announces the show that the listed person hosts is cancelled within timeframe, this market will immediately resolve to "Yes".

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the listed person or the owning network of the show that they host, however, a consensus of credible reporting sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Paramount Global, Comedy Central, or The Daily Show publicly announce by 2025-10-19 that Jon Stewart will continue as a host or executive producer of The Daily Show beyond 2025-12-31?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an early indicator for whether Jon Stewart will still be hosting The Daily Show through the end of 2025. Current reporting suggests uncertainty around Stewart's status: ScreenRant reported on 2025-08-10 that Paramount co-CEO George Cheeks said no decision had been made on Stewart's contract renewal and noted Stewart's contract expires in December 2025, which directly overlaps the ultimate market window. https://screenrant.com/daily-show-jon-stewart-contract-renewal-paramount-update/

At the same time, Stewart has recently become more confrontational toward Paramount. Deadline reported on 2025-07-22 that Stewart harshly criticized Paramount over the cancellation of Stephen Colbert's Late Show and alluded to the possibility that The Daily Show itself could be at risk, saying, "I'm not giving in, I'm not going anywhere, I think." https://deadline.com/2025/07/jon-stewart-daily-show-paramount-colbert-cancellation-1236463804/

The immediate environment for late-night hosts has also become more volatile. TVLine and The Hollywood Reporter reported on 2025-09-18 that Stewart hosted a special Thursday episode of The Daily Show amid controversy over ABC's handling of Jimmy Kimmel Live!, with Stewart expected to address censorship and network pressure. This suggests heightened scrutiny of politically outspoken late-night programming, making any early renewal or extension announcement especially informative for Stewart's near-term job security. https://tvline.com/news/jon-stewart-hosting-the-daily-show-thursday-jimmy-kimmel-suspension-1235554321/ ; https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/jon-stewart-daily-show-jimmy-kimmel-suspension-1236295644/

A public announcement that Stewart will remain with the show beyond 2025-12-31 would be strong evidence against cancellation/removal by year-end, while the absence of such reassurance amid an active controversy may leave the ultimate outcome more uncertain.

Sources:
ScreenRant - Daily Show Fans Beware: Colbert May Not Be The Only Late-Night Host On The Chopping Block - https://screenrant.com/daily-show-jon-stewart-contract-renewal-paramount-update/
Deadline - 'The Daily Show's Jon Stewart Torches Paramount Over Colbert Axing' - https://deadline.com/2025/07/jon-stewart-daily-show-paramount-colbert-cancellation-1236463804/
TVLine - Jon Stewart to Host Tonight's Daily Show in Light of Jimmy Kimmel Suspension - https://tvline.com/news/jon-stewart-hosting-the-daily-show-thursday-jimmy-kimmel-suspension-1235554321/
The Hollywood Reporter - Jon Stewart Taking Over 'Daily Show' Desk Tonight After Jimmy Kimmel Suspension - https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/jon-stewart-daily-show-jimmy-kimmel-suspension-1236295644/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-19 and 2025-10-19 inclusive, Paramount Global, Comedy Central, MTV Entertainment Studios, or an official The Daily Show channel/account publicly states that Jon Stewart will continue as a host or executive producer of The Daily Show beyond 2025-12-31. Qualifying statements include an announced contract renewal, extension, pickup, or explicit confirmation that Stewart will host in 2026 or later.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public announcement is made between 2025-09-19 and 2025-10-19 inclusive.

For resolution, primary sources are official press releases and official accounts/websites, including Paramount press releases (https://www.paramount.com/press), Comedy Central/The Daily Show official site pages (https://www.cc.com/ ; https://www.thedailyshow.com/), and official verified social accounts for The Daily Show or Comedy Central. Credible trade reporting such as Variety (https://variety.com/), Deadline (https://deadline.com/), or The Hollywood Reporter (https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/) may be used only if they clearly quote or reproduce the official announcement.

Non-qualifying examples: vague praise for Stewart, statements that discussions are ongoing, comments that no decision has been made, or scheduling him for episodes that all occur on or before 2025-12-31. If an announcement is made within the window but later retracted, the question still resolves Yes because the criterion is the public announcement itself within the specified window. If no authoritative evidence is available by the end of the window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A public renewal/continuation announcement would sharply reduce the probability that Stewart is removed or that the show is cancelled before the end of 2025. It is not the same as the ultimate question, because it asks about an earlier positive signal of institutional support rather than whether Stewart actually ceases hosting during the final market window.

question: Will Trump meet with Elon Musk by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump meets with Elon Musk between November 24, 2025 and 11:59 PM ET on the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both the listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly mention Elon Musk by name in a favorable or conciliatory way in an on-the-record statement between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful early indicator for whether Trump and Musk will meet again soon is whether Trump publicly signals warmth or openness toward Musk. The ultimate market concerns an in-person interaction by late March 2026, and public rhetoric can be an observable leading indicator of whether channels are open. Trump and Musk already had at least one in-person interaction after their public falling-out: multiple outlets reported that they shook hands and spoke at Charlie Kirk's memorial service in Arizona on September 21, 2025. Trump later characterized the exchange as "nice" and said Musk "came over and said hello," indicating that direct contact had resumed even if the broader relationship remained uncertain. See Mediaite: https://www.mediaite.com/ and The Cut: https://www.thecut.com/ (article referenced in prompt); also reporting summarized in the prompt from TheJournal.ie and India.com.

Because the two men had a public rupture in mid-2025 and then a limited public reunion in September 2025, the next informative signal is not simply whether they are in the same place, but whether Trump voluntarily uses favorable rhetoric about Musk in a public, attributable setting. Positive rhetoric would suggest reduced interpersonal friction and a greater likelihood of future scheduling, invitations, or opportunistic meetings. Negative or no rhetoric would be some evidence against near-term rapprochement.

This threshold is grounded in the current state of affairs: there was a recent reported handshake/conversation in September 2025, but Trump also reportedly downplayed its significance afterward. That makes a new favorable public mention during the subquestion window meaningfully informative rather than trivial. Official Trump communications are routinely posted on Truth Social and covered by major outlets, making resolution practical.

Sources:
Mediaite (referenced article in prompt): https://www.mediaite.com/
The Cut (referenced article in prompt): https://www.thecut.com/
Donald J. Trump on Truth Social: https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump
The White House: https://www.whitehouse.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive), Donald Trump makes an on-the-record public statement that explicitly refers to Elon Musk by name ("Elon Musk" or "Elon") and is overall favorable or conciliatory in substance.

Qualifying statements include: posts from Trump's official Truth Social account (https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump), remarks in official White House transcripts or videos (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), campaign/public event remarks recorded by a credible outlet, or direct quotes reported by at least two credible news organizations.

For this market, "favorable or conciliatory" means a reasonable reader would judge the statement as praising Musk, expressing appreciation, goodwill, respect, reconciliation, willingness to work together, or similar positive sentiment. Examples that would qualify: "Elon is a terrific guy," "I have a very good relationship with Elon," "I'd be happy to see Elon," "Elon is doing great work." Examples that would not qualify: neutral mentions, attacks, sarcasm, ambiguous jokes, or remarks whose dominant tone is negative.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: Trump's official Truth Social account at https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump and White House official transcripts/videos at https://www.whitehouse.gov/. If neither provides sufficient evidence, resolution will use a consensus of at least two credible news reports quoting or reproducing the statement. If purported evidence is manipulated, unauthenticated, or only reported by a single non-authoritative source, it will not count. Statements made outside the 2025-11-25 to 2025-12-25 window do not count.
subquestions.rationale: Publicly favorable rhetoric from Trump toward Musk is an early indicator that the relationship is thawing and that a future in-person meeting is more likely. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it tracks signaling and intent rather than the meeting itself.

question: Bolsonaro guilty?
description:
On March 26, the Brazilian Supreme Court ruled that Jair Bolsonaro will stand charges for an attempted coup. You can read more about that here: https://www.nytimes.com/2025/03/26/world/americas/brazil-bolsonaro-trial-coup-2022-elections.html

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jair Bolsonaro is found guilty of any charges related to the coup attempt by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Bolsonaro's charges are dismissed, end due to a plea agreement without an admission of guilt, or a mistrial is declared for the relevant charges, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve according to the initial judgment rendered in this case. Any appeals will have no bearing on the resolution of this market.

The primary resolution source will be an official judgement delivered by the ruling court; however, other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) hold at least two extraordinary plenary sessions in Jair Bolsonaro's alleged coup case between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-09 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term procedural indicator for whether Bolsonaro is likely to be found guilty soon is whether the Supreme Federal Court (STF) keeps the case on an active ruling schedule. AFP reported on 2025-08-15 that Brazil's Supreme Court would begin deciding Bolsonaro's case on September 2 and that extraordinary sessions were scheduled for September 2, 3, 9, 10, and 12. That reporting suggests the court expected a multi-session merits process rather than an indefinite delay, which is informative for the probability of an initial judgment before the ultimate market's deadline. See AFP summary in Barron's/AFP-style coverage: https://www.barrons.com/news/brazil-court-to-rule-from-sept-2-in-bolsonaro-coup-trial-59b5fe75 and related Reuters-style docket coverage from major outlets if available via public summaries. 

Brazil's STF publishes its calendar, session agendas, and case information on its official website. The court's transparency portal and news pages are the most authoritative sources for whether a scheduled session actually occurred and whether Bolsonaro's criminal case was on the agenda: https://portal.stf.jus.br/ and https://noticias.stf.jus.br/ . Because the ultimate question resolves based on the initial judgment by 2026-02-28, evidence that the court is actively convening to hear and deliberate the case in early September is a useful leading indicator that the court is moving toward a dispositive ruling rather than delay.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about court process, not guilt. Still, if the STF does hold multiple extraordinary sessions in the case during this short window, that likely increases the odds that the judges are sufficiently prepared to issue a prompt merits ruling, which in turn may affect expectations about conviction risk.

Sources:
- STF portal: https://portal.stf.jus.br/
- STF news: https://noticias.stf.jus.br/
- AFP report on scheduled sessions (Barron's): https://www.barrons.com/news/brazil-court-to-rule-from-sept-2-in-bolsonaro-coup-trial-59b5fe75
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-09 (inclusive), the Brazilian Supreme Federal Court (STF) officially records at least two extraordinary plenary sessions in Jair Bolsonaro's alleged coup case.

For purposes of resolution, a qualifying session must satisfy both conditions:
1. It is identified by the STF, in an official agenda, minutes, session video archive, news post, or case docket entry, as an extraordinary session of the court or relevant judging panel; and
2. Bolsonaro's criminal case concerning the alleged 2022 coup attempt is listed on the agenda, discussed, voted on, or otherwise officially noted as being considered in that session.

Primary sources for resolution will be official STF materials, including but not limited to:
- STF portal: https://portal.stf.jus.br/
- STF news: https://noticias.stf.jus.br/
- STF session agendas / pauta pages available through the portal
- STF case-search/docket tools available through the portal

If the STF portal structure changes, archived official STF pages or official STF YouTube/video records linked from STF pages may be used as fallback evidence, provided they clearly show the date and that Bolsonaro's coup case was part of the session.

If exactly one qualifying session occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-09, resolve No. If no qualifying session occurs in that window, resolve No. If official evidence is unavailable or contradictory such that it is impossible to determine whether two qualifying sessions occurred in that window, the question should be considered unresolvable.

The end_date for this subquestion is 2025-09-09.
subquestions.rationale: Whether the STF actually convenes multiple sessions on the case in early September is a concrete, near-term process signal about judicial momentum. Active scheduling and follow-through suggest the court is prepared to decide the matter on the merits soon, which is informative about the path to an initial judgment and can update forecasts on the ultimate guilty/not-guilty outcome.

question: Will any of the stolen Louvre jewels be returned by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any of the jewels stolen from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon are officially recovered by the listed date ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

A single item (e.g., one earring) will suffice regardless of if it is missing a diamond or other element; however, recovery of only a fragment or part of an item (for example, a loose stone or a piece of a crown) will not suffice

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the Louvre or the French government; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will French authorities publicly announce at least one arrest or formal charging of a suspect in connection with the October 19, 2025 Louvre crown-jewels theft by 2025-11-20?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether any of the stolen Louvre jewels will be returned by December 31, 2025. A key near-term indicator is whether investigators identify and detain suspects soon after the heist. In art and jewelry theft cases, early arrests can materially increase the odds of recovery because intact items are often dismantled, melted, or dispersed quickly. Multiple reports on the Louvre theft describe this as a "race against time," with art-recovery experts warning that if the thieves are not caught within days, the jewels are much more likely to be destroyed or broken up rather than recovered intact. Smithsonian reported that on October 20, 2025, four masked burglars stole eight jewels from the Galerie d’Apollon and escaped on motorbikes, while one damaged item was found outside the museum; President Macron said the works would be retrieved and perpetrators brought to justice under the Paris prosecutor’s direction: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/burglars-just-broke-into-the-louvre-and-stole-historic-crown-jewels-in-a-daring-daylight-heist-180986776/ . Yahoo similarly reported expert Arthur Brand’s view that police had about one week before the missing pieces were likely melted down or dismantled: https://www.yahoo.com/news/stolen-louvre-jewels-recovered-know-194657809.html . PEOPLE quoted Art Recovery International CEO Chris Marinello saying that if thieves are not caught within 24 to 48 hours, the pieces are "probably long gone": https://people.com/expert-says-stolen-louvre-jewels-need-to-be-recovered-in-24-to-48-hours-or-theyre-long-gone-report-11765793 . NBC News reported that police were hunting the thieves after the daylight heist and that key pieces remained missing: https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/louvre-museum-paris-crown-jewels-stolen-heist-france-rcna217056 . Because recovery chances fall sharply if suspects remain unidentified and at large, a public arrest or charging announcement before November 20 would be a meaningful positive signal for the ultimate market.

Sources:

PEOPLE — Expert Says Stolen Louvre Jewels Need to Be Recovered in 24-to-48 Hours Or They're 'Long Gone': Report — https://people.com/expert-says-stolen-louvre-jewels-need-to-be-recovered-in-24-to-48-hours-or-theyre-long-gone-report-11765793

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-21 and 2025-11-20 (inclusive), French authorities publicly announce at least one arrest, detention/garde à vue clearly tied to the theft, indictment/mise en examen, or formal charging of a suspect in connection with the October 19, 2025 theft of jewels from the Louvre’s Galerie d’Apollon.

Primary sources for resolution will be official public statements from the Paris public prosecutor (Parquet de Paris), the French Ministry of the Interior / Police nationale, the French Ministry of Justice, or the Louvre Museum. Relevant official sites include:
- Paris prosecutor / French justice portals: https://www.justice.fr/ and https://www.paris.fr/
- French Ministry of the Interior: https://www.interieur.gouv.fr/
- Police nationale: https://www.police-nationale.interieur.gouv.fr/
- Louvre official site/newsroom: https://www.louvre.fr/

If no clear official statement is available, the question may also resolve Yes based on a consensus of at least two credible, independent news outlets reporting that an arrest or formal charging occurred within the window, provided both reports clearly connect the suspect to the Louvre jewel theft. Suitable fallback outlets include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AFP (https://www.afp.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), BBC (https://www.bbc.com/), or Le Monde (https://www.lemonde.fr/).

For avoidance of doubt:
- Mere police searches, questioning of witnesses, publication of suspect sketches, or statements that authorities have identified persons of interest do NOT count.
- An arrest for unrelated crimes does NOT count unless authorities explicitly connect it to the Louvre theft.
- If a suspect is arrested before 2025-10-21, it does not count.
- If the first qualifying public announcement occurs after 2025-11-20, it does not count.
- If reports are contradictory and no authoritative clarification emerges, resolve based on the strongest official source available; otherwise the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Early arrest or charging of suspects is a strong operational indicator that investigators have actionable leads, which should increase the probability that at least one jewel is later recovered by December 31. If forecasters disagree about the ultimate outcome, they are likely to update substantially on whether authorities rapidly apprehend suspects in this time-sensitive case.

question: U.S. x Iran Military Engagement by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Iran between market creation and the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Iranian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Iranian land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage.

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; the Iranian Law Enforcement Command is a branch of the Iranian Armed Forces; all sub-branches of the Artesh, Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (including the Basij), and Law Enforcement Command are part of the Iranian Armed forces.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S.-Iran nuclear talks scheduled after the February 2026 Oman venue shift be canceled, suspended, or end without any announced follow-up meeting date by 2026-02-25?
subquestions.background_information:
A breakdown in diplomacy is a meaningful leading indicator for near-term military escalation risk between the United States and Iran. As of early February 2026, tensions are elevated: on 2026-02-04, U.S. Central Command said a U.S. F-35C shot down an Iranian Shahed-139 drone that had approached the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea, and separately reported harassment of the U.S.-flagged tanker Stena Imperative by IRGC vessels and a drone in the Strait of Hormuz. These incidents occurred just ahead of planned U.S.-Iran nuclear talks and amid explicit statements from U.S. officials that military force remains an option. Reuters-based reporting says talks originally planned for Turkey were shifted after Iran requested Oman and a narrower format focused on bilateral nuclear issues only. See ThePrint/Reuters: https://theprint.in/world/us-military-shoots-down-iranian-drone-near-abraham-lincoln-carrier-in-arabian-sea/ and TEMPO/Reuters summary: https://en.tempo.co/read/1989367/us-military-claims-to-have-shot-down-iranian-drone-in-arabian-sea .

Because the ultimate question asks about a U.S.-Iran military engagement by late February 2026, whether talks collapse in the next 2-3 weeks is a distinct and timely observable that should update forecasts materially. If talks are canceled or suspended without a new date, that would suggest diplomacy is failing and increase the chance that subsequent provocations or reprisals escalate into direct military engagement. Conversely, if talks proceed and a follow-up is scheduled, that would be evidence that both sides are still prioritizing de-escalation.

Sources:
ThePrint / Reuters summary on drone shootdown and talks venue shift — https://theprint.in/world/us-military-shoots-down-iranian-drone-near-abraham-lincoln-carrier-in-arabian-sea/
TEMPO / Reuters summary on talks planned for Feb. 7 and Oman shift — https://en.tempo.co/read/1989367/us-military-claims-to-have-shot-down-iranian-drone-in-arabian-sea
DefenseScoop on CENTCOM statement and regional tensions — https://defensescoop.com/2026/02/04/f-35c-pilot-downs-iranian-drone-to-defend-uss-abraham-lincoln-centcom-says/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-25 (inclusive), there is credible reporting that the ongoing/planned U.S.-Iran nuclear talks are canceled, suspended/put on hold, or conclude without any publicly announced follow-up meeting date by 2026-02-25.

This question resolves No if, by 2026-02-25, credible reporting shows either: (a) at least one round of U.S.-Iran talks took place between 2026-02-06 and 2026-02-25 and a subsequent meeting date/window is publicly announced by 2026-02-25; or (b) talks have not yet occurred but both sides (or an acknowledged mediator such as Oman) publicly confirm a specific follow-up meeting date/window still scheduled after the initial disruption.

For resolution, 'publicly announced follow-up meeting date' includes a specific calendar date or a clearly specified time window (e.g. 'next week in Muscat') attributed to U.S., Iranian, or Omani officials in credible reporting. Vague statements such as 'talks may continue' do not count.

Primary sources for resolution should be Reuters reporting and official statements from the U.S. State Department, the White House, Iran's Foreign Ministry, or Omani government channels. Useful source pages include Reuters world coverage (https://www.reuters.com/world/), U.S. State Department press statements (https://www.state.gov/press-releases/), the White House briefing room (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), and Iran's Foreign Ministry site (https://en.mfa.gov.ir/). If these conflict, resolve according to the weight of consensus across multiple credible outlets. If reporting remains too contradictory by 2026-02-25 to determine whether talks were canceled/suspended versus merely rescheduled, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: This is not a restatement of the ultimate military-engagement question. It tracks whether diplomacy is breaking down in the immediate aftermath of dangerous U.S.-Iran incidents. A confirmed collapse or suspension of talks would be a strong early-warning crux for higher odds of direct military engagement before the ultimate deadline.

question: Will there be exactly 1 earthquake of magnitude 7.0 or higher worldwide by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of earthquakes with a magnitude of 7.0 or higher that occur anywhere on Earth between October 13, 2025, 12:00 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for this market is the United States Geological Survey (USGS) Earthquake Hazards Program (https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/browse/significant.php#sigdef).

If an earthquake of substantial size has occurred within this market's timeframe but not yet appeared on the resolution source, this market may remain open until January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or until the earthquake in question otherwise appears on the resolution source. If such an earthquake has not appeared on the resolution source by that date, another credible resolution source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the USGS publish at least one earthquake of magnitude 6.5 or higher in the Kamchatka region between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term M6.5+ earthquake in Kamchatka would be a meaningful indicator for the ultimate question because the strongest current global aftershock sequence is centered there. The July 29, 2025 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake reached magnitude 8.8, one of the largest ever recorded, and USGS aftershock guidance indicated an elevated chance of another M7+ event in the following months. Newsweek, summarizing USGS assessments on October 25, 2025, reported a 24% chance of another magnitude 7 or higher earthquake in the months ahead and noted thousands of aftershocks had already occurred after the July mainshock, including a magnitude 7.8 event on September 19, 2025: https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-207xxxx . Recent moderate events in the same system continued into late October, including a USGS-recorded M5.6 south-southeast of Vilyuchinsk on October 23, 2025: https://earthquakenewstoday.com/2025/10/23/moderate-earthquake-5-6-mag-was-detected-near-vilyuchinsk-in-russia/ .

Globally, magnitude 7+ earthquakes are rare, so whether the most active major aftershock zone produces an M6.5+ event in the next few weeks is informative about tail risk for an M7+ before year-end. The USGS earthquake catalog provides authoritative event listings and allows filtering by magnitude, date, and region: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/ . Kamchatka lies on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has repeatedly generated large earthquakes, making it one of the most plausible source regions for any additional M7+ event in late 2025. A positive resolution here would increase the perceived chance that the ultimate market sees more than one M7+ quake during its full window; a negative resolution would modestly reduce that risk.

Sources:
USGS Earthquake Catalog Search — https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/
Newsweek: Two earthquakes rattle Russia: What to know — https://www.newsweek.com/two-earthquakes-rattle-russia-what-know-207xxxx
Earthquake News Today: Moderate earthquake, 5.6 mag was detected near Vilyuchinsk in Russia — https://earthquakenewstoday.com/2025/10/23/moderate-earthquake-5-6-mag-was-detected-near-vilyuchinsk-in-russia/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the USGS Earthquake Catalog lists at least one earthquake with reported magnitude >= 6.5 whose epicenter falls within the Kamchatka Peninsula / Kuril-Kamchatka region between 2025-11-13 00:00:00 UTC and 2025-12-09 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive. It resolves No otherwise.

Primary resolution source: the USGS Earthquake Catalog at https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/ . The event may be identified either by a saved query using the map bounds covering Kamchatka and adjacent trench waters, or by the catalog's reported place name containing terms such as "Kamchatka", "off the east coast of Kamchatka", "Kuril Islands", or similar USGS regional naming for that seismic zone.

For avoidance of doubt, qualifying events must both: (1) occur between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09 inclusive, based on the event origin time reported by USGS in UTC; and (2) have a final or most recently posted USGS magnitude of 6.5 or higher.

If an event initially appears below 6.5 and is later revised to 6.5 or higher before final resolution, it counts. If an event initially appears at 6.5 or higher and is later revised below 6.5 before final resolution, it does not count. If multiple magnitude scales are shown, use the headline magnitude shown by the USGS event page/catalog entry.

If the USGS catalog is temporarily unavailable, resolvers should use the corresponding USGS event pages reachable from the Earthquake Hazards Program website https://earthquake.usgs.gov/ as a fallback. If USGS data for the window remain unavailable by 2025-12-16, use EMSC https://www.emsc-csem.org/ or IRIS/ISC-backed catalogs only as secondary evidence to reconstruct whether USGS had a qualifying event, but USGS remains controlling if restored.

If no qualifying event is published by USGS for the defined window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether global seismicity produces exactly one M7+ event by late December. Kamchatka is currently one of the world's most active high-magnitude zones, so an M6.5+ there is a strong early warning sign for elevated odds of additional M7+ activity before the ultimate market closes.

question: US congress stock trading ban in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any bill with the effect of banning sitting members of the US congress from trading stocks is signed into law by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the discharge petition for H.R. 1908 (the End Congressional Stock Trading Act) obtain at least 100 signatures in the U.S. House between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term bottleneck for any 2025 congressional stock-trading ban is whether supporters can demonstrate substantial House support quickly enough to overcome leadership inaction and compete with the crowded September agenda. On 2025-08-29/30, Rep. Anna Paulina Luna announced a discharge-petition strategy to force House consideration of H.R. 1908, the End Congressional Stock Trading Act, which would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from trading or owning individual stocks and certain other assets. Multiple reports state that a discharge petition would require 218 signatures to force the bill to the floor. See Washington Examiner (2025-08-29): https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3513524/anna-paulina-luna-force-house-vote-congressional-stock-trading-ban/ ; Newsmax (2025-08-29): https://www.newsmax.com/politics/anna-paulina-luna-stock-trading-congress/2025/08/29/id/1234567/ ; OAN (2025-08-30): https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/ .

As of the start date, the relevant signal is not whether the bill has become law, but whether the petition can attract meaningful bipartisan momentum. Reaching 100 signatures by October 1 would still be short of the 218 needed for a successful discharge petition, but it would indicate unusually strong cross-member support and materially improve the odds of a floor vote later in 2025. Failure to approach even half the threshold by then would be evidence that the effort is stalled.

This indicator is grounded in current events because Congress returns in September facing a September 30 government-funding deadline and other legislative fights, making floor time scarce. AP reported on 2025-08-31 that avoiding a shutdown is the immediate task as Congress returns, highlighting how crowded the September agenda will be: https://apnews.com/article/congress-government-shutdown-trump-september-2025 . In that environment, a rapidly growing discharge petition would be a meaningful sign that a stock-trading ban has enough political salience to break through.

Official House discharge petition information is typically published by the Clerk of the House, including petition text and signature counts: https://clerk.house.gov/ .

Sources:
Washington Examiner - Anna Paulina Luna to force House vote on congressional stock trading ban - https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3513524/anna-paulina-luna-force-house-vote-congressional-stock-trading-ban/
Associated Press - Government shutdown looms as Congress returns after monthlong August recess - https://apnews.com/article/congress-government-shutdown-trump-september-2025
Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives - https://clerk.house.gov/
OAN - Rep. Luna introduces resolution to advance the End Congressional Stock Trading Act - https://www.oann.com/newsroom/rep-luna-introduces-resolution-to-advance-the-end-congressional-stock-trading-act/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the official discharge petition associated with H.R. 1908 is shown by the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives as having at least 100 signatures at any point during that window.

Primary source: the Clerk of the House discharge-petition pages and/or other official Clerk pages documenting the petition and signature count, starting from https://clerk.house.gov/ .

Resolution procedure:
1. Identify the official discharge petition corresponding to H.R. 1908 (the End Congressional Stock Trading Act).
2. Check whether the official signature count reaches 100 or more at any time from 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01, inclusive.
3. If yes, resolve Yes. Otherwise, resolve No.

Clarifications:
- Signatures count only if they are recorded on the official House Clerk site within the resolution window.
- If the petition is filed before 2025-09-01, only signatures reflected during the window still count for the threshold test; the question is about whether the petition has obtained at least 100 signatures by some point within that window, as evidenced on the official site.
- If the Clerk site later shows historical information confirming that the 100-signature threshold was first met during the window, that is sufficient.
- If H.R. 1908 is renumbered, formally replaced, or folded into a new House measure before the petition is active, the question remains about the discharge petition explicitly tied to H.R. 1908 and does not transfer automatically to another bill.
- If no official discharge petition page for H.R. 1908 is published by 2025-10-01, resolve No.
- If official House data become unavailable, a consensus of at least two credible reports specifically citing the official House signature count may be used as a fallback, but only if they clearly indicate the count reached at least 100 between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01.

Fallback reporting sources if needed:
Associated Press - https://apnews.com/
The Hill - https://thehill.com/
Roll Call - https://rollcall.com/
Congress.gov - https://www.congress.gov/
subquestions.rationale: A rapid accumulation of discharge-petition signatures is a strong observable proxy for whether a congressional stock-trading ban has the legislative momentum needed to become law by year-end. It captures elite support, bipartisan coalition strength, and the likelihood of forcing floor action, all of which are major cruxes for the ultimate question.
