subquestions.question: Will CME FedWatch assign at least an 85% probability to a 25-basis-point-or-larger rate cut at the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting at any time between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-26?
subquestions.background_information:
A key way the ultimate market can resolve to “No” is if the Fed cuts twice during the specified late-2025 window. Because one cut had already occurred in September 2025 and markets were reportedly assigning very high odds to an October 28-29 cut, expectations for the subsequent December meeting are an important early indicator of whether the world is on track toward a second cut in the relevant period. Investopedia reported on 2025-09-29 that markets expected the October 2025 meeting to deliver a 25 bp cut to a 3.75%-4.00% range, while Reuters-covered reporting on 2025-10-15 said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent planned to present Fed-chair candidates after Thanksgiving, implying no near-term chair announcement before late November and making rate-path expectations especially salient for the ultimate question's outcome. A high implied probability of a December cut by CME FedWatch before late November would be strong evidence that the “Fed cuts twice” leg of the ultimate market is becoming more likely. CME FedWatch is a widely watched market-implied tracker of FOMC probabilities based on 30-Day Fed Funds futures: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html .

Relevant context: the Federal Reserve's scheduled 2025 FOMC meetings include October 28-29 and December 9-10, 2025, according to the Federal Reserve Board calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm . Reporting before 2025-10-27 indicated markets saw the October meeting as very likely to produce a cut and were also raising the probability of a December cut; for example, The Financial Express on 2025-10-14 said markets assigned a 100% probability to an October cut and an 88% chance in December: https://www.financialexpress.com/business/banking-finance-all-eyes-on-jerome-powells-speech-in-his-first-public-appearance-since-the-september-rate-cut-3814974/ . Because the ultimate market turns on whether “nothing happens” with respect to Powell/Fed drama, a sharp rise to very high market-implied odds of a December cut is a meaningful lead indicator that “something” is likely to happen via monetary policy rather than personnel or rhetoric.

Sources:
CME FedWatch Tool — https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Federal Reserve FOMC calendars — https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
Investopedia, Next Fed Meeting: When It Is In October And What To Expect — https://www.investopedia.com/next-fed-meeting-when-it-is-and-what-to-expect-11775064
The Financial Express, All eyes on Jerome Powell's speech in his first public appearance since the September rate cut — https://www.financialexpress.com/business/banking-finance-all-eyes-on-jerome-powells-speech-in-his-first-public-appearance-since-the-september-rate-cut-3814974/
Devdiscourse, Bessent says he plans to present Fed chief candidates to Trump in December — https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/law-order/3350788-update-1-bessent-says-he-plans-to-present-fed-chief-candidates-to-trump-in-december
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-26 inclusive, the CME FedWatch Tool ever shows a probability of 85.0% or greater for a target-rate outcome at the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting that implies a cut of at least 25 basis points relative to the target range in effect immediately after the October 29, 2025 FOMC decision.

Operationally:
1. Use the CME FedWatch Tool page at https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html and/or CME pages directly displaying meeting probabilities for the December 10, 2025 FOMC meeting.
2. Determine the target range in effect immediately after the October 29, 2025 FOMC decision using the Federal Reserve's FOMC statement page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm .
3. A qualifying “cut” outcome is any December 10, 2025 target range whose upper bound is at least 25 basis points lower than that post-October-29 upper bound.
4. If at any time during the window from 2025-10-27 through 2025-11-26 inclusive the displayed probability for all such qualifying cut outcomes sums to 85.0% or more, resolve Yes. Otherwise resolve No.

Primary evidence should be CME-published probability tables or archived CME FedWatch snapshots. If live CME pages are unavailable at resolution, archived snapshots from the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) of the CME FedWatch Tool for dates within 2025-10-27 to 2025-11-26 may be used. If neither CME live data nor archived snapshots are available, use major financial media reports explicitly citing CME FedWatch probabilities for the December 10, 2025 meeting within the window, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/), or the Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/).

If CME changes the interface but still publishes equivalent meeting probability data, equivalent CME-published data controls. If no authoritative source can establish whether the threshold was reached during the specified window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: This is a distinct observable indicator, not a restatement of the ultimate market. The ultimate question can fail because of two cuts, a chair announcement, Powell mentioning Trump, or Lisa Cook leaving. Among these, the most market-sensitive near-term path is a second rate cut in December. If market-implied odds of a December cut become very high before late November, forecasters should materially update toward the ultimate market resolving “No,” even though no qualifying ultimate event has yet occurred.

question: Will there be at least 500 measles cases in the U.S. in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there have been the specified amount or more confirmed cases of Measles (Rubeola) in humans in the territory of the United States of America in 2026 according to the CDC case counter between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter (see: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html) at the resolution time. If the counter becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

Note: Only cases reported by the CDC Measles (Rubeola) counter will qualify, regardless of reports from U.S. State agencies or other sources.

subquestions.question: Will the United States still have an active measles outbreak listed on the CDC measles outbreaks page on 2026-01-01?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator for whether the U.S. will have at least 500 confirmed measles cases in 2026 because sustained transmission crossing into January 2026 would suggest continued chains of spread, a larger susceptible population, and elevated risk of substantial case counts in early 2026. As of mid-November 2025, the CDC had reported 1,723 confirmed measles cases nationwide in 2025, with 87% linked to 45 outbreaks, according to reporting on CDC findings by The Boston Globe: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/18/nation/cdc-links-measles-outbreaks-multiple-states-first-time/ . Other late-2025 reporting described the U.S. as close to losing measles elimination status if transmission continued into January 2026, which underscores that ongoing outbreaks at year-end are highly decision-relevant for 2026 case totals: The Hill, https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5000000-canada-loses-its-measles-elimination-status-and-the-us-is-close-behind/ ; Scientific American, https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/measles-elimination-status-threatened-in-u-s-and-canada/ .

The CDC maintains a measles cases and outbreaks page, including outbreak counts and case totals, which is the most natural authoritative source for whether there are still active outbreaks entering 2026: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html . CDC defines an outbreak as 3 or more related cases, and in recent years a large majority of 2025 cases were outbreak-associated, making outbreak persistence a more informative crux than a simple end-of-year case count. CDC background on measles and outbreaks is here: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/about/index.html .

This subquestion is not just the ultimate question with an earlier date: it asks about whether outbreak transmission remains active at the turn of the year, which is a different observable epidemiological state and a strong leading indicator of whether 2026 will begin with ongoing transmission momentum.

Sources:
CDC Measles Cases and Outbreaks: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
CDC About Measles: https://www.cdc.gov/measles/about/index.html
The Boston Globe - CDC links measles outbreaks in multiple states for first time: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/11/18/nation/cdc-links-measles-outbreaks-multiple-states-first-time/
The Hill - Canada loses its measles elimination status, and the US is close behind: https://thehill.com/policy/healthcare/5000000-canada-loses-its-measles-elimination-status-and-the-us-is-close-behind/
Scientific American - Measles Elimination Status Threatened in U.S. and Canada: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/measles-elimination-status-threatened-in-u-s-and-canada/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-01, inclusive, the CDC measles data/outbreaks page indicates that at least one measles outbreak in the United States remains active as of 2026-01-01, or equivalently if on 2026-01-01 the CDC still lists one or more current/ongoing outbreaks on its measles outbreaks reporting page. It resolves No if, on 2026-01-01, the CDC outbreaks page indicates zero active/current U.S. measles outbreaks.

Primary source: CDC Measles Cases and Outbreaks page, https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html . If CDC provides a dedicated outbreaks page linked from there, that linked CDC page should be used.

Definition of "active outbreak": an outbreak that the CDC still treats as ongoing/current on 2026-01-01, rather than historical/closed/resolved. If CDC does not use the word "active" but presents a list of current outbreaks or indicates outbreaks are ongoing, that will count. If CDC only publishes a numeric outbreak count without explicit active/closed labeling, the question resolves Yes if CDC reporting on 2026-01-01 clearly states at least 1 outbreak is ongoing/current; otherwise unresolved unless fallback sources below clarify.

Fallback criteria: if the CDC outbreaks page is unavailable or substantially changed, use archived CDC pages captured on or after 2026-01-01 via the Internet Archive https://web.archive.org/ together with any CDC press release or Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report page published by 2026-01-01 that explicitly states whether there are ongoing outbreaks. If CDC materials remain unavailable or ambiguous, use the Johns Hopkins county-level measles tracker described by CIDRAP, if publicly accessible, only to determine whether at least one CDC-recognized outbreak remained ongoing on 2026-01-01: CIDRAP article https://www.cidrap.umn.edu/measles/researchers-introduce-tool-featuring-timely-county-level-us-measles-data-maps .

If no authoritative source allows a clear determination of whether any outbreak was active on 2026-01-01, this question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: If there is still an active CDC-listed outbreak on 2026-01-01, that means transmission has not been extinguished before the new year. That materially raises the odds that 2026 begins with ongoing spread, imported follow-on cases, and additional outbreak seeding, making 500+ U.S. measles cases in 2026 more likely. Conversely, if all outbreaks are closed by then, the 2026 count must build from new importations or new chains, which is evidence against very high annual totals.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of Personnel Management's operating status page first indicate that the U.S. federal government shutdown has ended on or before 2025-10-17?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate market asks whether the next BLS Employment Situation report will be released before the shutdown ends. A major driver of that outcome is simply how long the shutdown lasts. If the shutdown ends relatively quickly, BLS is more likely to resume operations and either release delayed data or return to its normal publication schedule before the next key deadline. If the shutdown persists deeper into October, delays to BLS releases become more likely.

The shutdown began on October 1, 2025, after funding lapsed. Multiple contemporaneous reports state that BLS suspended the October 3 Employment Situation release because of the shutdown, and that BLS would resume normal operations once funding is restored and then notify the public of schedule changes. See Yahoo Finance on Oct. 1, 2025: https://finance.yahoo.com/ ; AFP on Oct. 3, 2025: https://www.barrons.com/news/us-delays-key-jobs-report-due-to-government-shutdown-7d4c3b36 ; and U.S. News on Oct. 6, 2025: https://www.usnews.com/news/economy/articles/2025-10-06/missing-data-leaves-economy-flying-blind

OPM maintains the federal government's official operating status page, which is also named in the ultimate market description as a resolution source: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/

This subquestion is informative because an early end to the shutdown by mid-October would materially raise the chance that BLS can process and publish the delayed jobs report before much later deadlines, while a shutdown lasting beyond mid-October points the other way. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it asks about shutdown duration, not about whether BLS publishes before reopening.

Sources:
OPM Operating Status page — https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/
Barron's / AFP on delayed jobs report — https://www.barrons.com/news/us-delays-key-jobs-report-due-to-government-shutdown-7d4c3b36
U.S. News on missing BLS data during shutdown — https://www.usnews.com/news/economy/articles/2025-10-06/missing-data-leaves-economy-flying-blind
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-17 inclusive, the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) publicly indicates on its Operating Status page that the federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on 2025-10-01. It resolves No otherwise.

Primary source: OPM Operating Status page at https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/

For resolution, the first date on which OPM's page indicates normal operations have resumed or otherwise clearly states that the shutdown is over will be used. Partial shutdowns still count as shutdowns, consistent with the ultimate market description; therefore, if OPM indicates some agencies have reopened but the federal government remains in a partial shutdown, that does not qualify for Yes.

If OPM's page is unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of credible contemporaneous reporting from major U.S. outlets and/or official White House or OMB statements may be used as fallback evidence to determine whether an official announcement that the shutdown ended occurred within the window. Fallback official sources include https://www.whitehouse.gov/ and https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/ .

If no clear official or consensus-supported indication that the shutdown ended appears between 2025-10-08 and 2025-10-17 inclusive, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The duration of the shutdown is a core crux for whether BLS can release the Employment Situation report before reopening. An early reopening by mid-October would strongly increase the odds of a pre-reopening or shortly post-resumption data release path, whereas a longer shutdown would make the ultimate Yes less likely.

question: Lee Jun-seok in jail in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Lee Jun-seok serves any time in custody in any prison between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean Government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will South Korean prosecutors or a special counsel publicly indict Lee Jun-seok on any criminal charge between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A formal indictment of Lee Jun-seok would be a strong near-term indicator for the ultimate question of whether he serves jail time later in 2025, because imprisonment in South Korea generally requires either pretrial detention following serious charges or a later custodial sentence after prosecution. South Korean politics is currently experiencing aggressive legal action against prominent figures tied to the recent political crisis. Former President Yoon Suk Yeol has reportedly been jailed since July 10, 2025, and former first lady Kim Keon-hee was arrested and indicted in August 2025, while former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo was also indicted, though not detained. See the recent reporting on widening special-counsel investigations: Al Jazeera, Aug. 29, 2025, https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/29/south-korea-indicts-former-first-lady-for-bribery-ex-pm-over-martial-law and Korea Herald, Aug. 25, 2025, https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10564844.

This broader environment matters because if prosecutors expand investigations to opposition figures such as Lee Jun-seok, that would materially increase the probability that he could enter custody before year-end. An indictment is not the same as imprisonment, but it is a distinct and observable legal escalation that can precede detention requests, arrest warrants, or convictions. Conversely, the absence of any indictment through Oct. 1 would be evidence against rapid movement toward incarceration before Dec. 31, 2025.

Because the ultimate market concerns custody in a prison during Aug. 4-Dec. 31, 2025, a subquestion about indictment is useful precisely because it is different from the ultimate question: it tracks prosecutorial escalation rather than incarceration itself.

Sources:
Al Jazeera - South Korea indicts former first lady for bribery, ex-PM over martial law: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/8/29/south-korea-indicts-former-first-lady-for-bribery-ex-pm-over-martial-law
The Korea Herald - Special counsel raids Justice Ministry, Supreme Prosecutors' Office: https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10564844
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Lee Jun-seok is publicly reported by an official South Korean prosecutorial body or officially appointed special counsel as having been indicted on one or more criminal charges between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources: official announcements or publicly accessible case notices from the Supreme Prosecutors' Office of the Republic of Korea, a district prosecutors' office, the Ministry of Justice, or an officially appointed special counsel. Relevant official portals include the Supreme Prosecutors' Office https://www.spo.go.kr/ and the Ministry of Justice https://www.moj.go.kr/.

If no clear official statement is available, a consensus of at least two credible news reports that explicitly state Lee Jun-seok was indicted within the window may be used. Examples of acceptable backup outlets include Yonhap News Agency https://en.yna.co.kr/ and The Korea Herald https://www.koreaherald.com/.

For avoidance of doubt:
- The qualifying event is indictment, not mere investigation, search, questioning, complaint, or request for indictment.
- An arrest, detention, or warrant without an indictment does not by itself resolve Yes.
- If reports only say prosecutors are considering charges or seeking to summon him, resolve No unless an actual indictment is confirmed.
- The date used is the date the indictment is officially announced or credibly reported as having occurred in South Korea; if sources disagree, use the earliest date supported by the primary official source.
- If the indictment occurs before 2025-09-01 or after 2025-10-01, this question resolves No.
- If by 2025-10-01 no authoritative information exists and available reporting is contradictory such that it cannot be determined whether an indictment occurred within the window, the question should resolve as Unresolvable.

Resolution window: This question only considers qualifying events occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

Sources for resolution:
Supreme Prosecutors' Office: https://www.spo.go.kr/
Ministry of Justice (ROK): https://www.moj.go.kr/
Yonhap News Agency: https://en.yna.co.kr/
The Korea Herald: https://www.koreaherald.com/
subquestions.rationale: An indictment is a meaningful legal escalation that would substantially raise the odds of detention or a custodial sentence later in 2025, while still being distinct from the ultimate jail question.

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:
This market will resolve according to the country that wins the second most medals (including gold, silver, and bronze) at the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics, scheduled for February 6-22, 2026.

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Italy rank in the top 3 countries by total medals on the official Milano Cortina 2026 medal table at the end of 2026-02-19 UTC?
subquestions.background_information:
Italy is the host nation for the 2026 Winter Olympics, which often boosts medal performance through home advantage. Early results suggest Italy started well: AP reported that on the first day Italy won a gold in women's 3,000m speed skating plus silver and bronze in the men's downhill, giving the hosts an early multi-medal start (https://apnews.com/). GEO TV also reported that as of 2026-02-07, Italy had 2 medals in one tally summary, while the broader point across early coverage is that Italy was already near the top of the standings and the table remained highly fluid with many events still to come through February 22 (https://www.geo.tv/latest/). The Games feature 116 medal events across 19 days, so being top-3 by total medals by February 19 would be a meaningful late-stage indicator of whether Italy can ultimately finish as high as second overall by February 22 (https://www.independent.co.uk/). 

Historical and pre-Games context suggests Italy is not the default favorite for second in total medals. Norway dominated Beijing 2022 with 37 total medals, while Germany and the United States were also projected before Milano-Cortina 2026 to be among the leading teams by total medals; Bleacher Report projected the United States, Norway, and Germany to lead the medal count and all exceed 25 medals (https://bleacherreport.com/). CBS Sports likewise highlighted strong medal prospects for the United States across hockey, speed skating, snowboarding, alpine skiing, and figure skating, while Norway remained the benchmark Winter Olympics power (https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-count/). 

Because the ultimate question is whether Italy finishes exactly second in total medals after all events, Italy being top 3 with only a few competition days remaining is a useful crux: if Italy is outside the top 3 by 2026-02-19, its path to second becomes much narrower; if it is inside the top 3, especially as host nation with momentum, the case for an eventual second-place finish strengthens materially.

Sources:
AP News Olympics coverage — https://apnews.com/
The Independent, Winter Olympics schedule and day-by-day events — https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/winter-olympics-2026-schedule-results-b2678605.html
Bleacher Report, Milano Cortina final medal count predictions — https://bleacherreport.com/
CBS Sports, 2026 Winter Olympics medal count — https://www.cbssports.com/olympics/news/2026-winter-olympics-medal-count/
GEO TV Olympics medal race report — https://www.geo.tv/latest/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, on the official country medal table for the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympics published by Olympics.com, Italy is ranked 1st, 2nd, or 3rd by total medals at the end of 2026-02-19 UTC. This question resolves No otherwise.

Resolution window: This question concerns the official medal-table status between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-19, and specifically resolves based on the medal table as it stands at 2026-02-19 23:59:59 UTC.

Primary source: the official Milano Cortina 2026 medal table on Olympics.com, such as https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/milano-cortina-2026/medals .

Ranking method: use the ranking/order displayed by Olympics.com on that medal table page at the resolution time. If Olympics.com offers multiple sort options, use the default displayed country ranking/order on the page. If the page clearly lists total medals and rank, that displayed rank controls.

Fallbacks: If the specific Milano Cortina medal page is unavailable at resolution time, use another official Olympics.com page for Milano Cortina 2026 medal standings or results archive. If no official Olympics.com medal table snapshot for 2026-02-19 is available, use the latest official Olympics.com medal table published before 2026-02-20 00:00:00 UTC. If the Olympics.com official site is wholly unavailable, archived captures of the same official Olympics.com page (for example via the Internet Archive) may be used to establish the displayed ranking.

If the Games are suspended or materially interrupted before 2026-02-19 and no official medal table is published for that date, this question resolves based on the latest official Olympics.com medal table published within the window from 2026-02-08 through 2026-02-19 inclusive. If no such official medal table exists, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
Olympics.com Milano Cortina 2026 medals page — https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/milano-cortina-2026/medals
Olympics.com main site — https://www.olympics.com/
subquestions.rationale: This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about Italy being top 3 at an intermediate date rather than finishing exactly second at the end. It is a strong indicator because the final few days rarely allow a nation far down the table to leap into second in total medals, especially against powers like Norway, the United States, and Germany. Knowing whether Italy is top 3 by February 19 should substantially update forecasts for whether it can finish second by February 22.

question: James Comey indicted before October?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any Federal or State jurisdiction of the United States formally charges or otherwise announces a criminal indictment of James Comey between July 8 and September 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

For the purposes of this market the District of Columbia and any county, municipality, or other subdivision of a State shall be included within the definition of a State.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from US governmental sources, however a wide consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any U.S. federal law-enforcement or prosecutorial authority publicly confirm between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 that James Comey is the subject of an active criminal investigation?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term public confirmation that James Comey is an active criminal target or subject of investigation would be a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question about indictment before late September 2025. Indictments typically follow investigative steps such as witness interviews, document collection, grand-jury activity, or formal public statements by prosecutors or investigators. While media commentary alone is weak evidence, an official confirmation from the Department of Justice, an FBI field office, a U.S. Attorney's Office, a state attorney general, or a local district attorney would materially increase the probability of a near-term indictment.

There has already been public speculation that Comey may be under scrutiny. Fox News legal analyst Gregg Jarrett said in July 2025 that prosecutors might seek an indictment of Comey or John Brennan and that a grand jury in Washington, D.C. could be involved, though this was commentary rather than an official announcement: https://conservativenewstoday.com/gregg-jarrett-explains-why-a-dc-jury-handling-comey-or-brennan-case-might-be-a-fools-errand/ . Separately, some partisan outlets in July 2025 claimed the Trump DOJ was preparing a criminal conspiracy case involving Comey, but those reports did not constitute an official governmental confirmation and cited no charging document: https://www.russia-news-now.com/a-new-age-of-accountability-trump-doj-preps-criminal-conspiracy-case-against-russiagate-architects/ .

Official DOJ practice is that criminal investigations and charges are ordinarily announced via press releases, court filings, or public statements from the responsible office. The Department of Justice newsroom is the main central source for federal charging announcements: https://www.justice.gov/news . U.S. Attorneys' Offices also publish district-level charging announcements, for example through their press-release pages collected at https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney . The FBI publishes major investigative announcements and public statements in its newsroom at https://www.fbi.gov/news . If authorities are moving toward an indictment of Comey in the short window relevant to the ultimate market, an official acknowledgement of an active criminal investigation is one of the most observable precursor events.

Sources:
DOJ Newsroom — https://www.justice.gov/news
Find Your United States Attorney — https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney
FBI News — https://www.fbi.gov/news
Conservative News Today (Jarrett commentary) — https://conservativenewstoday.com/gregg-jarrett-explains-why-a-dc-jury-handling-comey-or-brennan-case-might-be-a-fools-errand/
Russia News Now report — https://www.russia-news-now.com/a-new-age-of-accountability-trump-doj-preps-criminal-conspiracy-case-against-russiagate-architects/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 inclusive, any official U.S. governmental source publicly states that James Comey is the subject or target of an active criminal investigation.

Qualifying official sources include: the U.S. Department of Justice (https://www.justice.gov/news), any U.S. Attorney's Office website listed via https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney, the FBI newsroom (https://www.fbi.gov/news), a state attorney general's official website, a state or local prosecutor's official website, or an official on-the-record statement attributable to such an office and reproduced by that office.

For Yes, the official statement must explicitly name James Comey and indicate an active criminal investigation using language such as "is under criminal investigation," "is being investigated," "is the subject of an investigation," "is the target of an investigation," or functionally equivalent wording. A statement merely saying authorities are "reviewing," "looking at," or "examining" matters related to him without clearly indicating an active criminal investigation is insufficient.

This question also resolves Yes if an official filing or court proceeding published during the window explicitly states that Comey is a subject or target of a criminal investigation, even if no press release is issued.

This question resolves No if no such official public confirmation occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 inclusive.

If only anonymous-source media reports appear, with no official public confirmation in the window, resolve No. If an official source publishes after 2025-09-23 about events during the window, that does not count; the confirming public statement itself must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-23 inclusive. If there is a source outage or ambiguity, a broad consensus of credible reporting quoting a named official on the record may be used as a fallback, provided the reporting clearly attributes the confirmation to an official U.S. governmental authority.

Primary resolution sources: DOJ Newsroom https://www.justice.gov/news ; FBI News https://www.fbi.gov/news ; relevant U.S. Attorney's Office pages via https://www.justice.gov/usao/find-your-united-states-attorney .
subquestions.rationale: A public official confirmation of an active criminal investigation is a meaningful precursor to indictment and is distinct from the ultimate question. It captures whether authorities are openly moving against Comey, which would sharply update the odds of an indictment before the ultimate market closes.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will CME FedWatch assign less than a 50% probability to a December 2025 FOMC rate cut at the close of trading on 2025-12-05?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a market-based indicator for whether the Fed is likely to pause at its December 9–10, 2025 meeting, which is the first leg of the ultimate Dec–Jan–Mar path question. If market-implied odds of a December cut fall below 50% by early December, that would be evidence that investors increasingly expect a December pause, which in turn makes a Pause–Pause–Pause sequence more plausible.

As of late October 2025, the Fed had already cut rates at the September and October meetings, leaving the target range at 3.75%–4.00% after the October 29, 2025 decision, according to reporting summarizing the FOMC outcome and the Federal Reserve's policy stance. Several reports also emphasized that Chair Powell said a December cut was "not a foregone conclusion" and highlighted growing internal division, including dissents in opposite directions at the October meeting. See Yahoo Finance coverage from 2025-10-30: https://finance.yahoo.com/ and CNBC coverage of the October meeting context: https://www.cnbc.com/ . The Federal Reserve publishes meeting calendars and policy decisions at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and open market policy implementation information at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm .

CME's FedWatch Tool is widely used to infer market-implied probabilities for target-rate outcomes at upcoming FOMC meetings from 30-Day Federal Funds futures. Its methodology and data page are here: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html . Because the ultimate question hinges heavily on whether December is a pause or a cut, a drop in implied cut odds below 50% by 2025-12-05 would be a meaningful early signal favoring a pause-first path rather than continued easing.

Sources:
Federal Reserve FOMC calendars: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
Federal Reserve open market operations / policy page: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Yahoo Finance (site referenced in provided context): https://finance.yahoo.com/
CNBC Fed coverage (site): https://www.cnbc.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 inclusive, the closing reading on 2025-12-05 of CME FedWatch for the December 2025 FOMC meeting implies that the probability of any rate cut (defined as the sum of all outcomes with an upper bound below the pre-meeting upper bound of 4.00%) is less than 50.0%.

For avoidance of doubt, because the target range after the October 29, 2025 meeting is reported as 3.75%–4.00%, a "December cut" means any December 2025 target range outcome with upper bound below 4.00%. A "December pause" corresponds to 3.75%–4.00%.

Primary source: CME FedWatch Tool, December 2025 meeting probabilities: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html

Resolver should use the probabilities displayed for the December 2025 FOMC meeting at the close of trading on 2025-12-05, U.S. time. If CME provides a downloadable or archived probability table for that date, that should be used. If multiple cut outcomes are shown, their probabilities are summed.

Fallback criteria: If the interactive FedWatch page is unavailable, resolution should use an archived CME page capture for 2025-12-05 or a CME-published table/data file showing the same probabilities. If CME ceases publication entirely before 2025-12-05 and no archived 2025-12-05 reading is available, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from news reports.

Supporting reference for current target range and FOMC meeting schedule: Federal Reserve calendar and policy pages at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm .
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends crucially on whether the Fed pauses in December rather than cutting again. Market-implied odds for the December meeting are a timely, continuously updated synthesis of incoming macro data, Fed communications, and policy expectations. If cut odds are below 50% by December 5, that is strong evidence toward a December pause and thus raises the likelihood of a Pause–Pause–Pause sequence overall.

question: Progressive Cities Parlay
description:
The 2025 mayoral elections in New York City, Minneapolis, and Seattle will be held on November 4, 2025, to elect the mayors of those cities.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if all of the following conditions are met:

- Zohran Mamdani wins New York City Mayoral Election
- Omar Fateh wins Minneapolis Mayoral Election
- Katie Wilson wins Seattle Mayoral Election

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will remain open until the official results of the listed elections are published.

The full rules for this market can be found here:
https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/pc1.png

subquestions.question: Will Zohran Mamdani be listed as the leader in the final pre-Election-Day New York City mayoral poll published by Emerson College Polling, Siena College Research Institute, or Marist Poll between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator for the three-city progressive parlay because Zohran Mamdani is widely viewed as the strongest leg of the parlay, and a clear late polling lead in New York would increase the chance that the overall parlay can still hit. Recent reporting described Mamdani as "poised to become mayor" and noted that he had defeated Andrew Cuomo in the Democratic primary, with Cuomo now running as an independent but trailing significantly. https://www.yahoo.com/news/believe-not-theres-election-next-090000000.html

A Newsweek summary of late-September polling reported Mamdani at 45% and Cuomo at 25% in a Suffolk University poll, and also noted Polymarket pricing around 90% for Mamdani in early October. https://www.newsweek.com/zohran-mamdanis-odds-winning-nyc-mayoral-race-hit-new-high-2039614

FOX 5 New York also summarized a September 18-22 Fox News survey showing Mamdani at 45%, Cuomo at 27%, Sliwa at 11%, and Adams at 8%. The same report notes key election timing: voter registration deadline on October 25, early voting from October 25 to November 2, and Election Day on November 4. Late, high-quality public polling released during or just before early voting is therefore especially informative about whether Mamdani is likely to convert his apparent advantage into an actual win. https://www.fox5ny.com/news/nyc-mayoral-forum-mamdani-cuomo-sliwa-october-2025

Because the ultimate market requires all three progressive candidates to win, evidence that the most favored of the three is still leading in reputable late polling materially affects the joint probability of the parlay.

Sources:

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
Start date: 2025-10-23. End date: 2025-11-03.

This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-03 inclusive, at least one poll of the New York City 2025 mayoral election is published by Emerson College Polling, Siena College Research Institute, or Marist Poll, and the chronologically last such poll published within that window lists Zohran Mamdani in sole first place in its head-to-head or multi-candidate vote intention results for the general mayoral election.

For resolution, a "qualifying poll" must:

- Concern the 2025 New York City general election for mayor;

If the last qualifying poll shows a tie for first, this resolves No (the question requires Mamdani to be listed as the leader, i.e. sole first place).

If a pollster releases multiple versions or updates on the same day, the latest timestamped release on the pollster's official site counts.
