See reporting from UPI on Sept. 29, 2025: https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/29/government-shutdown-jobs-report-bls/ and Anadolu Ajansı on Sept. 29, 2025: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-wont-release-key-economic-data-if-government-shuts-down-report/3680064

Fortune also reported that a shutdown lasting more than a few days would halt BLS data collection and scheduled releases, including the monthly jobs report due in early October and potentially the Oct. 15 CPI if the lapse extends beyond the first week: https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/government-shutdown-jobs-report-fed-rate-cuts-bls-cpi/ . Reuters reporting carried by other outlets likewise described the Labor Department contingency plan as warning that key economic data releases would halt during a lapse in appropriations: https://www.yahoo.com/news/govt-shutdown-suspend-bls-delay-211500123.html

This is not the same as the ultimate question. A shutdown still would not by itself satisfy the ultimate market's "ceases regular publication" standard if releases are merely temporarily delayed and later resume. But whether a shutdown is still in effect by Oct. 10 is a meaningful crux because a persistent lapse makes missed releases, data-collection degradation, and later publication disruptions substantially more likely.

Sources:
UPI - BLS won't release jobs report Friday if the government shuts down - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/09/29/government-shutdown-jobs-report-bls/
Anadolu Ajansı - US won't release key economic data if government shuts down: Report - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-wont-release-key-economic-data-if-government-shuts-down-report/3680064
Fortune - A government shutdown would delay the jobs report at a critical time - https://fortune.com/2025/09/28/government-shutdown-jobs-report-fed-rate-cuts-bls-cpi/
Yahoo Finance - Govt. shutdown would suspend BLS, delay key labor data - https://www.yahoo.com/news/govt-shutdown-suspend-bls-delay-211500123.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive), a federal government funding lapse/shutdown is in effect at any time on 2025-10-10 and BLS is operating under shutdown contingency procedures on that date.

For resolution, use the following hierarchy:
1. An official U.S. Office of Management and Budget (OMB), White House, or Department of Labor/BLS statement indicating that a lapse in appropriations or shutdown remains in effect on 2025-10-10, or that BLS remains subject to shutdown contingency operations. Relevant official sites include https://www.whitehouse.gov/omb/ , https://www.dol.gov/ , and https://www.bls.gov/ .
2. If no single official statement is sufficient, a consensus of at least two credible reports from major outlets stating on or after 2025-10-10 that the shutdown/lapse remained in effect on that date and that BLS was under shutdown procedures. Example sources include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), and major national newspapers.

Resolves No if, by 2025-10-10, appropriations are in force and BLS is no longer operating under shutdown contingency procedures for all of that date, or if official/consensus reporting shows no shutdown was in effect on 2025-10-10.

If there is a brief intraday lapse on 2025-10-10 that is officially recognized as a shutdown/lapse in appropriations and BLS is under contingency procedures for any part of that date, resolve Yes. If evidence is genuinely contradictory and no consensus can be established from the above sources, resolve using the preponderance of official statements; if still impossible, the question is unresolvable.

Resolution window: only events occurring between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) count toward resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A persistent government shutdown is one of the clearest near-term causal pathways to interrupted BLS publication. Knowing whether a shutdown is still active by Oct. 10 helps distinguish between a brief procedural scare and a materially elevated risk of missed releases, degraded data collection, and possible escalation toward the ultimate outcome.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Federal Senate formally place on the Senate agenda, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, any request for impeachment of STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes for consideration by the Senate plenary or the Mesa do Senado?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for any impeachment of an STF minister is not merely the filing of petitions, but whether the Senate leadership chooses to advance one procedurally. Multiple impeachment requests against Alexandre de Moraes have reportedly already been filed; one August 2025 report described a new filing as roughly the 30th such request against him, indicating that filing alone has not been sufficient to create a credible path to impeachment. https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/

Recent reporting also indicates that after U.S. sanctions on Moraes and rising political pressure, the Senate president still declined to hold an impeachment vote, which suggests Senate agenda-setting is a highly informative near-term indicator for the ultimate question. https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7IY7YV5R4JH7XJ4N4YQX6I3G6I/

The political environment is unusually salient. The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Moraes on 2025-07-30 under the Global Magnitsky framework, increasing international and domestic controversy around him. https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0174

At the same time, Brazilian right-wing groups were reported to be planning mass demonstrations for 2025-09-07 demanding Moraes's impeachment, making the first month of September a natural window to watch for institutional follow-through. https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7IY7YV5R4JH7XJ4N4YQX6I3G6I/

Because the ultimate market resolves on a Senate vote to proceed, an earlier procedural signal is whether Senate leadership moves any impeachment request onto the formal agenda or formally submits it for consideration by the relevant Senate governing body. That event is distinct from the ultimate question but strongly related: if the Senate president still refuses to schedule or docket the matter during a period of peak attention, the odds of an impeachment vote by year-end likely fall.

Sources:
Brazil Tries to Impeach--for the 30th Time--Judge Who Put Jair Bolsonaro Under House Arrest — https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/07/brazil-tries-to-impeach-for-the-30th-time-judge-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-under-house-arrest/
Brazil's democratic quandary: How to prosecute a president — https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/brazils-democratic-quandary-how-to-prosecute-a-president/7IY7YV5R4JH7XJ4N4YQX6I3G6I/
U.S. Department of the Treasury press release on sanctions against Alexandre de Moraes — https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0174
Federal Senate of Brazil (official site) — https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/atividade
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, the President of the Federal Senate or the Senate's official systems formally place on the Senate agenda, order of business, dispatches, or other official legislative processing record any impeachment request against STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes for consideration by either (a) the Senate plenary or (b) the Mesa do Senado/Federal Senate leadership body.

This question resolves No if no such formal agenda placement or equivalent official procedural advancement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

For avoidance of doubt, the following do NOT by themselves count for Yes: (1) a new impeachment petition merely being filed or publicized; (2) speeches, interviews, or social-media statements by senators; (3) street protests; (4) media reports claiming the matter is under discussion without an official Senate record.

Qualifying evidence for Yes should come from official Senate sources such as the Senado Federal legislative portal, agenda pages, plenary agenda/order-of-the-day pages, official news releases, or official dispatch/publication records. Primary source: https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/atividade and related official Senate pages under senado.leg.br. If the Senate website structure changes, archived or successor official Senate pages may be used.

If official Senate records are unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of at least three credible Brazilian news outlets reporting that the Senate president formally pautou, incluiu na pauta, despachou for consideration, or otherwise officially advanced an impeachment request against Moraes during the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window may be used as a fallback, provided no official Senate source contradicts that reporting. Potential secondary sources include Agencia Senado https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias, G1 https://g1.globo.com/politica/, and Folha de S.Paulo https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/poder/.

If a qualifying action is announced before 2025-10-01 but the formal Senate record shows the agenda placement occurred outside the 2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01 window, it does not count. If the matter is scheduled and then withdrawn within the window, it still counts as Yes so long as official records show it was formally placed on the agenda during the window.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question hinges on whether the Senate will actually vote to proceed with impeachment. Formal agenda-setting by the Senate president is a necessary and highly informative precursor that is distinct from the ultimate outcome. Observing whether Senate leadership advances the matter during a period of intense public pressure should materially update forecasts about the probability of a vote by year-end.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States publicly acknowledge conducting at least one new drone, missile, or air strike in Syria between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-12?
subquestions.background_information:
Syria is a salient early indicator for the ultimate question because the US had already conducted a major acknowledged strike campaign there on January 10, 2026, targeting Islamic State sites after a December 2025 attack that killed US personnel. That suggests Syria was an active and plausible venue for further near-term US aerial action as of the start date. See reporting on the January 10 operation in Syria: https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-hit-islamic-state-targets-across-syria-after-attack/

The US military presence in Syria has continued under Operation Inherent Resolve, with around 1,000 US troops reportedly still deployed there and the Pentagon indicating reduction rather than a full withdrawal, which sustains the possibility of additional retaliatory or preventive strikes. Reuters has previously reported on continuing US operations against ISIS in Syria and CENTCOM announcements are a standard official source for such strikes: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-military-strikes-islamic-state-camps-syria-2024-12-08/ and https://www.centcom.mil/

This is informative for the ultimate question because if the US conducts another acknowledged strike in Syria so soon after the January 10 operation, that would be evidence of an elevated operational tempo and a greater base rate of US cross-border air/missile/drone strikes in 2026. Since the ultimate market turns on whether the US strikes the soil of 3 different countries during 2026, repeated early activity in one already-active theater increases the chance of a broader multi-country strike pattern later in the year, even though this subquestion is not itself a restatement of the ultimate question.

Sources:
OpIndia - US airstrikes hit Islamic State targets across Syria after attack - https://www.opindia.com/2026/01/us-airstrikes-hit-islamic-state-targets-across-syria-after-attack/
Reuters - US military strikes Islamic State camps in Syria - https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-military-strikes-islamic-state-camps-syria-2024-12-08/
US Central Command - https://www.centcom.mil/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-12 (inclusive), the United States publicly acknowledges conducting at least one new strike in Syria that would fit the ultimate market's strike modality: use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles launched by US military forces that impact ground territory in Syria.

For resolution, the preferred sources are official US government statements, especially US Central Command press releases or statements (https://www.centcom.mil/) and Department of Defense releases (https://www.defense.gov/). A qualifying event must be publicly acknowledged by one of those sources during the window, or clearly described by multiple credible outlets quoting named US officials.

The strike must be a new event occurring between 2026-01-13 and 2026-02-12 (inclusive). Re-reporting or further detail about the January 10, 2026 Syria strikes does not count. Intercepted missiles/drones that do not impact Syrian ground territory do not count. Surface-to-air engagements do not count. Pure ground operations, artillery, small arms, naval shelling, cyber operations, or raids without qualifying aerial bomb/drone/missile impacts do not count.

If an official US source states that US forces conducted airstrikes, drone strikes, or missile strikes in Syria during the window, that is sufficient for Yes. If no such acknowledged qualifying strike is found by the end date, resolve No.

If official sources are unavailable, fallback sources are Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), and BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), requiring a consensus of at least two of these outlets or one of them plus another major credible outlet clearly attributing the action to the US military and placing it within the window.

If reporting remains too ambiguous to determine whether a qualifying aerial strike actually impacted Syrian ground territory within the specified window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Syria was already an active US strike theater immediately before the start date. Another acknowledged Syria strike in the next month would be a strong signal that the US is on a higher-tempo strike trajectory in 2026, which meaningfully raises the odds of the US ultimately striking the territory of 3 countries during the year.

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing another Fed Governor before their term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request between August 25 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, will Donald Trump publicly announce a nominee to fill Lisa Cook’s Federal Reserve Board seat or any other Federal Reserve Board of Governors seat?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term indicator for whether Trump will try to remove another Fed governor is whether he moves quickly to capitalize on his attempted removal of Lisa Cook by naming a replacement. Multiple late-August reports said Trump had already attempted to fire Governor Lisa Cook and was seeking to reshape the Fed Board. CNN reported on 2025-08-28 that Trump had fired Cook, that Cook planned to contest the move in court, and that Trump selected Stephen Miran as a potential replacement while saying, “We’ll have a majority very shortly.” https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook The Inquirer likewise reported that Trump announced Cook was fired “effective immediately,” that Cook rejected the removal, and that Trump had also appointed Stephen Miran to a vacant Fed board seat. https://www.inquirer.com/politics/nation/trump-fires-fed-governor-lisa-cook-20250827.html Reuters/Yahoo reported that the legal fight over Cook’s status could determine whether Trump can add another member to the Fed’s seven-member Board, potentially increasing his influence over monetary policy. https://www.yahoo.com/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-204305515.html

This matters because a public nomination would be concrete evidence that the White House expects or intends to create and use additional Fed Board vacancies. If Trump announces a nominee for Cook’s seat very quickly, that would suggest he is treating governor removals as politically and legally viable, which should raise the odds of another removal attempt before 2025-10-31. By contrast, if no nominee is announced by the end of September, that would be some evidence of caution, legal uncertainty, or political difficulty.

The Fed Board normally has seven seats. Reporting before 2025-09-01 indicated that one vacancy already existed following Adriana Kugler’s resignation, and Trump’s move against Cook was widely understood as an effort to create another opening and secure a friendlier majority on the Board. CNN said advisers believed a replacement could help Trump gain influence ahead of the September policy meeting. https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook

Sources:
CNN: Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed — https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/economy/trump-federal-reserve-lisa-cook
The Philadelphia Inquirer: Trump moves to fire Fed governor, aiming to control central bank — https://www.inquirer.com/politics/nation/trump-fires-fed-governor-lisa-cook-20250827.html
Yahoo/Reuters: Trump's firing of Fed Governor Cook could be blocked by US judge — https://www.yahoo.com/news/trumps-firing-fed-governor-cook-204305515.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive, Donald Trump or the White House publicly announces a specific nominee for (a) the Federal Reserve Board seat allegedly vacated by Lisa Cook, or (b) any other specific seat on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors.

Qualifying announcements include: a White House press release; a Truth Social post or other official Trump statement naming the nominee; or formal transmission of the nomination to the U.S. Senate recorded by Congress.gov or the Senate.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 inclusive.

For avoidance of doubt:
- Mere media speculation that Trump is considering candidates does not count.
- Statements that Trump “plans to nominate someone soon” do not count unless a specific person is publicly named as nominee.
- Announcing a nominee for Fed Chair alone counts only if the announcement is explicitly for a Board of Governors seat as well; the market is about Board seats, not only internal leadership roles.
- If the announcement occurs after 2025-09-30, it does not count.
- If a purported announcement is later denied by the White House the same day, resolver should rely on the clearest final official statement as of 2025-09-30.

Primary resolution sources: White House announcements at https://www.whitehouse.gov/, Trump official communications, and Congress.gov nominations records at https://www.congress.gov/search?q=%7B%22source%22%3A%22nominations%22%7D. Secondary source: Federal Reserve Board announcements at https://www.federalreserve.gov/ and consensus reporting from Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ if needed.

If no authoritative public source remains available, a consensus of at least two independent, credible outlets reporting a named public nomination made within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-30 window may be used.
subquestions.rationale: A rapid nomination to a disputed or newly opened Fed seat would indicate that Trump is operationalizing a strategy of reshaping the Board, making another removal attempt more plausible. It is not just an earlier version of the ultimate question; it measures whether the administration is taking follow-on steps that imply confidence in and commitment to further intervention in Fed governance.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) or the White House announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, the start of a formal U.S.-Canada trade negotiation, consultation, or review explicitly aimed at modifying current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Trump will later lower tariffs on Canada is whether his administration opens a formal policy process directed at changing those tariffs. As of late 2025, the Trump administration has recently escalated trade restrictions on Canada rather than eased them. Reporting indicates that on August 1, 2025, Trump signed an executive order raising tariffs from 25% to 35% on goods from Canada not covered by USMCA/CUSMA, while other tariff actions and the removal of the de minimis exemption have added additional trade friction for Canadian exporters. See Pittsburgh's Action News 4 on the August 1 order: https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-delay/65506465 ; Global News on the end of de minimis and 35% non-CUSMA tariff treatment for Canadian goods: https://globalnews.ca/news/11366237/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses-fearful/ ; and Reuters coverage of U.S. tariff policy and official trade announcements via the White House and USTR sites: https://www.reuters.com/ .

Because the ultimate question resolves Yes if Trump later lowers, pauses, delays, or removes Canada-specific tariffs, a formal bilateral negotiation or review targeted at those tariffs would be a meaningful precursor event. Such a process would not itself lower tariffs, but it would signal political willingness to revisit them and create an administrative path for a later easing action before year-end. USTR is the principal U.S. agency for trade negotiations and publishes official notices, statements, and announcements at https://ustr.gov/ . The White House also publishes presidential statements and executive actions at https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/ and https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ .

Sources:
USTR homepage — https://ustr.gov/
White House Presidential Actions — https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
White House Briefing Room — https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
Pittsburgh's Action News 4, "New tariffs on Canada take effect Friday; Dozens of other countries delayed" — https://www.wtae.com/article/trump-tariffs-canada-delay/65506465
Global News, "Duty-free shipping to U.S. ends Friday. Canadian businesses are 'fearful'" — https://globalnews.ca/news/11366237/duty-free-shipping-us-ends-friday-canadian-businesses-fearful/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, either (a) the USTR or the White House publishes an official statement, press release, notice, readout, or presidential action explicitly announcing the start of a formal negotiation, consultation, working group, review, or similar bilateral process with Canada and explicitly stating that the process concerns modifying, reviewing, easing, pausing, or reconsidering current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods; or (b) both the U.S. and Canadian governments officially confirm such a process during that window.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published by 2025-11-30 23:59:59 UTC.

Qualifying announcements must be official and public. Primary sources are:
- USTR news/press releases and statements: https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases
- USTR homepage: https://ustr.gov/
- White House Presidential Actions: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/
- White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
- Government of Canada official trade/news releases, if needed for bilateral confirmation: https://www.canada.ca/en/global-affairs/news.html and https://www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/news.html

Non-qualifying events include: general diplomatic meetings that do not explicitly concern modifying current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods; broad trade comments without initiation of a formal process; market rumors; commentary from unnamed officials; or negotiations solely about unrelated issues such as border security, defense, or tariffs on third countries.

If an announcement occurs within the window but is later clarified within the same window to not concern modifying current U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods, it does not qualify. If relevant official webpages are unavailable at resolution time, a consensus of at least two major outlets quoting the official announcement text directly (for example Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ and AP https://apnews.com/ ) may be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: Opening a formal U.S.-Canada tariff negotiation or review would be a strong leading indicator that the administration is preparing or seriously considering a later tariff reduction. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question itself, but one that should substantially update forecasts about whether Trump will lower Canada-specific tariffs by year-end.

question: Julie Masino out as Cracker Barrel CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Julie Masino ceases to be CEO of Cracker Barrel for any length of time between August 24 and December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Julie Masino's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Cracker Barrel and/or Julie Masino, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Cracker Barrel publicly announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, that it has appointed a new permanent President in addition to Julie Masino remaining CEO?
subquestions.background_information:
A meaningful indicator for whether Julie Masino may be removed as CEO by year-end is whether the board moves to split top leadership responsibilities or install an additional senior operator above or alongside her in day-to-day management. Cracker Barrel is already under visible pressure after its failed 2025 logo redesign and subsequent reversal. Newsweek reported on 2025-08-27 that Masino was facing calls to resign after the company abruptly scrapped the new logo following backlash and a share-price drop of more than 10% (https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-under-pressure-resign-after-logo-u-turn-2105080). The New York Post likewise reported customer and investor anger and noted criticism from activist investor Sardar Biglari and others calling for the CEO’s dismissal (https://nypost.com/2025/08/27/business/cracker-barrel-shares-jump-after-backtrack-on-logo-change-but-customers-still-want-ceo-gone/).

More recently, Cracker Barrel announced organizational changes on 2025-10-03 and said it was ending its relationship with Prophet, the consultancy associated with the rebrand. That announcement indicates the company is still actively restructuring after the backlash, making further management changes plausible. Nation’s Restaurant News reported that the company was “streamlining leadership” and quoted Masino saying that “there is more to come” as the company heads into the holiday season (https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company). The Hill also reported on 2025-10-24 that Masino publicly defended the attempted logo redesign while noting the company had already reversed course and canceled remodel plans (https://thehill.com/business/5569178-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/).

If Cracker Barrel appoints a new permanent President while Masino remains CEO, that would be an observable sign that the board is redistributing authority or adding oversight rather than immediately removing her. That would generally be evidence against near-term CEO ouster, though not decisive.

Sources:
Newsweek - Cracker Barrel CEO under pressure to resign after logo U-turn - https://www.newsweek.com/cracker-barrel-ceo-under-pressure-resign-after-logo-u-turn-2105080
New York Post - Cracker Barrel shares jump 7% after backtrack on logo change - but... - https://nypost.com/2025/08/27/business/cracker-barrel-shares-jump-after-backtrack-on-logo-change-but-customers-still-want-ceo-gone/
Nation's Restaurant News - Cracker Barrel ends relationship with design company - https://www.nrn.com/casual-dining/cracker-barrel-ends-relationship-design-company
The Hill - Cracker Barrel CEO explains reason for attempt to change logo - https://thehill.com/business/5569178-cracker-barrel-ceo-explains-reason-for-attempt-to-change-logo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. publicly announces, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, that it has appointed or hired a new permanent executive with the title "President" of Cracker Barrel or "President and Chief Operating Officer" (or a clearly equivalent permanent role), while Julie Masino is still identified in the same announcement or in contemporaneous company materials as CEO.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement is made between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

For clarity:
- "Publicly announces" includes a company press release, SEC filing, or official investor-relations/newsroom posting by Cracker Barrel.
- Interim or acting appointments do not count.
- Appointments solely at a subsidiary level do not count unless the announcement clearly states the role is for Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. overall.
- A title change for an existing executive counts only if the company explicitly states that the person has been appointed to the President role during the resolution window.
- If the announcement occurs during the window but the effective date is later, it still counts.
- If no authoritative company source is available, an SEC filing takes precedence; if neither exists but multiple credible business outlets unanimously report a qualifying appointment citing the company, that may be used as fallback evidence.

Primary sources for resolution:
- Cracker Barrel Investor Relations / News: https://investor.crackerbarrel.com/
- Cracker Barrel newsroom/press releases: https://investor.crackerbarrel.com/news-events/news-releases
- SEC EDGAR company filings for Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=1067294&owner=exclude

Fallback reporting sources if needed:
- Nation's Restaurant News: https://www.nrn.com/
- Restaurant Business: https://www.restaurantbusinessonline.com/
- Wall Street Journal: https://www.wsj.com/
subquestions.rationale: A new permanent President would signal board concern about operations and a desire to dilute or support Masino’s authority without immediately firing her. That is a distinct observable event, not a restatement of the ouster question, and should materially update forecasts about whether she survives as CEO through year-end.

question: Will Microstrategy's mNAV dip to 1.00 by December 31?
description:
This market will immediately resolve to "Yes" if Microstrategy's mNAV is equal to or lower than the value specified in the title on any day by December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Resolution will be based on StrategyTracker's "NAV Premium & Performance" chart available at https://strategytracker.com/mstr/, with "1M" and "Diluted Shares" selected.

NAV data for any given date will be considered finalized once the data point for the following calendar day is published on the chart.

This market will resolve based on the specified StrategyTracker chart, not according to other sources or spot markets.

subquestions.question: Will Strategy (MicroStrategy) report at least one additional Bitcoin purchase totaling 1,000 BTC or more between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
A key driver of MicroStrategy/Strategy's mNAV is whether the company can continue the capital-markets machine that supports ongoing Bitcoin accumulation. Recent reporting suggests the firm had about 638,460 BTC as of 2025-09-08 after buying 1,955 BTC for $217 million, and that its mNAV had fallen to roughly 1.5x by then, far below late-2024 levels above 3x. CoinDesk reported on 2025-09-08 that Strategy purchased 1,955 BTC and that the stock had fallen 26% since July, while mNAV was around 1.5x: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/08/mstr-news-strategy-acquires-another-1955-btc-for-usd217m-after-missing-out-on-s-and-p-500-inclusion/ .

This matters because continued BTC purchases are evidence that Strategy still has access to financing and/or investor demand despite compression in premium. If Strategy is still able and willing to add materially to its BTC stack in October, that is evidence against an imminent collapse of the equity premium all the way to 1.00. Conversely, failure to make any meaningful BTC purchase during the month could indicate reduced financing flexibility, weaker investor demand, or management caution under lower mNAV conditions.

There is also specific recent news that Strategy relaxed its prior self-imposed restriction against issuing stock below 2.5x mNAV. CryptoSlate reported on 2025-08-19 that the company revised its stock issuance policy to allow sales below 2.5x mNAV to raise capital or accelerate Bitcoin acquisitions: https://cryptoslate.com/strategy-eases-mstr-stock-sale-limits-as-shares-hit-lowest-level-since-april/ . Bitnewsbot similarly summarized that the company dropped its 2.5x mNAV pledge and opened the door to more dilution below that threshold: https://bitnewsbot.com/microstrategy-drops-2-5x-mnav-pledge-opens-door-to-more-dilution/ .

That policy change makes October BTC-purchase disclosures especially informative. If the company continues buying BTC despite lower mNAV, markets may interpret that either as resilience or as dilution pressure; either way, it is a concrete observable that helps forecast whether mNAV will compress toward 1.00. Because recent purchases have been publicly disclosed in SEC filings and on Strategy's investor relations page, this is a relatively clean and timely indicator.

Sources:
CoinDesk - Strategy acquires another 1,955 BTC for $217M: https://www.coindesk.com/markets/2025/09/08/mstr-news-strategy-acquires-another-1955-btc-for-usd217m-after-missing-out-on-s-and-p-500-inclusion/
CryptoSlate - Strategy eases MSTR stock sale limits: https://cryptoslate.com/strategy-eases-mstr-stock-sale-limits-as-shares-hit-lowest-level-since-april/
Bitnewsbot - MicroStrategy drops 2.5x mNAV pledge: https://bitnewsbot.com/microstrategy-drops-2-5x-mnav-pledge-opens-door-to-more-dilution/
Strategy Investor Relations: https://www.strategy.com/investor-relations
SEC EDGAR company filings: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=1050446&owner=exclude
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) publicly reports, in one or more company announcements or SEC filings released between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, Bitcoin purchases totaling at least 1,000 BTC acquired during that same window.

Primary source for resolution: Strategy investor relations announcements and press releases at https://www.strategy.com/investor-relations and SEC EDGAR filings for the company at https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=1050446&owner=exclude .

Preferred evidence is an 8-K, 10-Q, prospectus supplement, or official press release stating the amount of BTC acquired. If multiple disclosures occur in the window, their reported BTC amounts are summed, but only purchases announced as having occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive count.

This question resolves No if, by the end of 2025-10-31 UTC, no qualifying official disclosure shows aggregate BTC purchases of at least 1,000 BTC during the window from 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31 inclusive.

If a disclosure is released during the window but only reports purchases executed entirely before 2025-10-01, it does not count. If a disclosure released after 2025-10-31 clearly states that qualifying purchases occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, it may be used as fallback evidence only if no contradictory official filing exists.

If Strategy changes name/ticker again, filings under the same SEC registrant (CIK 1050446) still count. If official sources become unavailable, reputable reproductions of the filing text from SEC mirrors or major financial wire services may be used as fallback, but official company or SEC sources take precedence.
subquestions.rationale: A meaningful October BTC purchase would indicate that Strategy's financing engine remains active despite mNAV compression, which is evidence against the thesis that the premium is collapsing straight to 1.00. Lack of purchases, or a pause in accumulation, would point the other way by suggesting tighter financing conditions or weaker appetite for further dilution.

question: Will Drake's next album debut No.1 on Billboard 200?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Drake’s next officially released album debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 albums chart for its first charted week following release. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Drake does not release a new album by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

This market may resolve as soon as Billboard publishes the first chart week in which the album appears.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from Billboard (https://www.billboard.com/charts/billboard-200/).

subquestions.question: Will Drake publicly announce a release date for his next album, widely reported as "Iceman," on or before 2025-11-08?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term determinant of whether Drake’s next album debuts at No. 1 is whether the release campaign becomes concrete enough for fans, retailers, DSPs, and press to mobilize around a specific launch week. As of 2025-10-09, multiple entertainment outlets report that Drake is rolling out an upcoming album commonly referred to as "Iceman," but that no release date has yet been announced. HotNewHipHop reported on 2025-09-18 that Drake was touring overseas "ahead of the release of his upcoming album 'Iceman', scheduled for later in 2025," but without a firm public date: https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/948248-drake-good-times-iceman-rollout-hip-hop-news . Earlier, HotNewHipHop noted on 2025-07-28 that the album had "not been given a release date" even as the single "Which One" was gaining traction: https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/931287-drake-central-cee-which-one-huge-chart-debut-hip-hop-news . The Express Tribune similarly described Iceman as expected later in 2025 rather than formally dated: https://tribune.com.pk/story/2557890/drake-is-billboards-hip-hop-artist-of-the-21st-century .

Drake’s chart history suggests that if he locks in and publicizes a date, his odds of a No. 1 debut rise materially because major Drake albums usually benefit from concentrated fan attention, playlisting, and large first-week consumption. Billboard has highlighted Drake’s extensive chart dominance, and People reported in July 2025 that his collaborative project with PARTYNEXTDOOR, "$ome $exy $ongs 4 U," debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200: https://people.com/drake-appears-call-out-friends-aftermath-kendrick-lamar-beef-new-song-what-did-i-miss-11768255 . Forbes also described that project as one of the most successful releases of 2025: https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2025/05/23/drake-blocked-from-his-first-no-1-in-years-by-a-frequent-collaborator/ .

Because the ultimate market resolves No if Drake does not release a new album by the end of 2025, a public release-date announcement by early November would be a meaningful signal that the album is likely to arrive on time and with a coordinated commercial push strong enough to contend for No. 1.

Sources:
HotNewHipHop - Drake Sends Odd Message About "Good Times" Amid "Iceman" Rollout - https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/948248-drake-good-times-iceman-rollout-hip-hop-news
HotNewHipHop - Drake & Central Cee's "Which One" Heads For Huge Chart Debut - https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/931287-drake-central-cee-which-one-huge-chart-debut-hip-hop-news
The Express Tribune - Drake is Billboard's hip hop artist of the 21st century - https://tribune.com.pk/story/2557890/drake-is-billboards-hip-hop-artist-of-the-21st-century
People - Drake Appears to Call Out Friends Who Didn't Stand by Him... - https://people.com/drake-appears-call-out-friends-aftermath-kendrick-lamar-beef-new-song-what-did-i-miss-11768255
Forbes - Drake Blocked From His First No. 1 In Years By A Frequent Collaborator - https://www.forbes.com/sites/hughmcintyre/2025/05/23/drake-blocked-from-his-first-no-1-in-years-by-a-frequent-collaborator/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), Drake or his label publicly announces a specific release date for Drake’s next album, and that announcement is documented by at least one primary source or two credible secondary sources.

For purposes of resolution:
- "Publicly announces" means any of the following occurring within the window 2025-10-09 through 2025-11-08 inclusive: (a) Drake posts a specific calendar date for the album on a verified social-media account or official website; (b) the album appears with a specific release date on Drake’s official store or a major DSP/retailer listing such as Apple Music, Spotify, or Amazon Music; or (c) Drake’s label/publicist issues a press release naming a specific release date.
- "Drake’s next album" means the next officially released Drake album that would count for the ultimate market, whether or not it is ultimately titled "Iceman."
- A vague statement such as "coming soon," "this fall," or "before the end of the year" does not count.
- An alleged leak or unverified rumor does not count.
- If multiple dates are announced within the window, any specific date announcement is sufficient for Yes, even if later changed.

Primary resolution sources: Drake’s verified Instagram/X accounts, official Drake website/store, or label announcements if available. Secondary confirmation sources may include Billboard, Rolling Stone, Variety, or other major music-trade reporting.

Suggested sources for resolution:
- Drake Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/champagnepapi/
- Drake X account: https://x.com/Drake
- Billboard music news: https://www.billboard.com/
- Rolling Stone music news: https://www.rollingstone.com/music/
- Variety music news: https://variety.com/v/music/
- Apple Music Drake page: https://music.apple.com/us/artist/drake/271256
- Spotify Drake page: https://open.spotify.com/artist/3TVXtAsR1Inumwj472S9r4

If no qualifying public announcement occurs between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 inclusive, this question resolves No. If the relevant primary posts/pages are deleted or unavailable at resolution time, archived versions or contemporaneous reporting from at least two credible outlets may be used as fallback evidence.
subquestions.rationale: A firm public release date is a strong leading indicator that the album rollout is real, imminent, and commercially organized. That increases the probability both that Drake releases an eligible album before the ultimate deadline and that the release has enough coordinated momentum to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.

question: Half-Life 3 released in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Half-Life 3 or a differently titled game continuing the Half-Life series is officially released in the US by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, "release" refers to the game becoming publicly available for purchase or download in the US. Early access, beta versions, other forms of pre-release availability, or leaks will not count as an official release. If the release is only for certain consoles (e.g. Xbox Series X/S) it will count.

The resolution source will be official information from Valve Corporation.

subquestions.question: Will Valve officially announce or reveal a new Half-Life game continuing the series between 2025-11-10 and 2025-12-10 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether Half-Life 3 (or a differently titled continuation of the Half-Life series) will be officially released in the US by the end of 2025. A near-term official announcement is a meaningful indicator because major commercial game releases typically follow formal reveal, store-page publication, trailer release, or press announcement by the publisher. For Valve specifically, there has been substantial late-2025 speculation that a reveal may be imminent: multiple gaming outlets summarized fan theories pointing to a possible November 18, 2025 reveal window based on an unusual gap in Steam promotional scheduling and Half-Life anniversary timing, though none of this is official confirmation from Valve (e.g. Eurogamer, ComicBook, ScreenRant, GamingBible: https://www.eurogamer.net/half-life-fans-believe-theyve-worked-out-a-possible-announcement-date-for-half-life-3-and-its-very-very-soon ; https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/half-life-3-hl3-valve-release-date-announcement/ ; https://screenrant.com/half-life-3-reveal-imminent-november-18-theory/ ; https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platform/pc/half-life-3-could-be-announced-this-month-129060-20251109).

Additional rumor reporting has claimed that a trailer is in production and that release could follow closely after announcement, but again with no official Valve confirmation as of 2025-11-10 (Notebookcheck and Gamereactor: https://www.notebookcheck.net/Half-Life-3-could-be-unveiled-in-November-2025.915012.0.html ; https://www.gamereactor.eu/half-life-3-trailer-is-reportedly-in-the-works-1457443/). Valve's official channels currently provide the authoritative basis for whether any new Half-Life title has actually been announced: Valve's news site, Steam publisher pages, and official YouTube presence are the most relevant public sources (https://store.steampowered.com/news/publisher/valve ; https://store.steampowered.com/search/?publisher=Valve ; https://www.youtube.com/@Valve).

Because the ultimate market resolves based on an official release by December 31, 2025, an official reveal by December 10 would be one of the strongest available short-horizon leading indicators that such a release is still plausible. Conversely, no official reveal by that date would weigh against a same-year launch, though it would not rule it out completely.

Sources:
Eurogamer - Half-Life fans believe they've worked out a possible announcement date for Half-Life 3 - https://www.eurogamer.net/half-life-fans-believe-theyve-worked-out-a-possible-announcement-date-for-half-life-3-and-its-very-very-soon
ComicBook - Half-Life 3 Fans May Have Figured Out When the Game Is Being Revealed - https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/half-life-3-hl3-valve-release-date-announcement/
ScreenRant - Half-Life 3 Reveal Could Finally Be Imminent - https://screenrant.com/half-life-3-reveal-imminent-november-18-theory/
GamingBible - Half-Life 3 Could Be Announced This Month - https://www.gamingbible.com/news/platform/pc/half-life-3-could-be-announced-this-month-129060-20251109
Notebookcheck - Half-Life 3 could be unveiled in November 2025 - https://www.notebookcheck.net/Half-Life-3-could-be-unveiled-in-November-2025.915012.0.html
Gamereactor - Half-Life 3 trailer is reportedly in the works - https://www.gamereactor.eu/half-life-3-trailer-is-reportedly-in-the-works-1457443/
Valve on Steam - News hub - https://store.steampowered.com/news/publisher/valve
Valve YouTube channel - https://www.youtube.com/@Valve
subquestions.rationale: An official Valve reveal is a strong leading indicator for a release by year-end 2025. It is not just the ultimate question with an earlier deadline: it asks about a different observable event—public announcement rather than release—that would substantially update expectations about whether a launch by December 31 is feasible.

question: Will Trump publicly disparage Netanyahu by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump makes any public statement in which he insults, mocks, or attacks Benjamin Netanyahu personally or professionally in a clearly negative manner by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

This includes calling Netanyahu weak, stupid, disloyal, a failure, using an insulting nickname, or using other derogatory language. Policy disagreements stated without disparaging language will not count.

Any public statement made by Trump qualifies.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly claim between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 that he had to restrain, stop, or overrule Benjamin Netanyahu on Gaza, Iran, or West Bank policy?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator for whether Trump may later publicly disparage Netanyahu, because a public narrative in which Trump casts himself as the person who had to 'stop' or 'control' Netanyahu creates visible interpersonal and political friction short of direct insult. On 2025-10-24, Trump was already quoted as saying 'I stopped Netanyahu' in a TIME interview published via his site, claiming that without his intervention the Gaza war would have 'gone on for years' and reiterating opposition to West Bank annexation. That is not itself a personal insult, but it shows Trump is already willing to publicly describe Netanyahu as someone he needed to constrain. https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/2f7f6f65-4f5c-4a9d-9d4b-4f9f5e7c0c2

There are also prior reports of substantive Trump-Netanyahu tensions. In May 2025, reporting described 'sharp disagreements' over Iran strategy, with Trump preferring diplomacy while Netanyahu pushed a harder line. https://www.worthynews.com/101234-trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy

Commentary in October 2025 also suggested that Trump’s Gaza policy depended on forcing Netanyahu into politically painful steps, implying a relationship where Trump may increasingly blame Netanyahu if events go poorly. https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/dealing-with-trumpian-uncertainty-and-no-cultural-boycotts/

Because the ultimate question asks about explicit public disparagement, a nearer-term crux is whether Trump escalates his public framing from 'I got him to do X' to repeated claims that Netanyahu had to be restrained or overruled. Repetition of that framing would make later personal attacks more plausible.

Sources:
Donald J. Trump - 'Trump: I Stopped Netanyahu' https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news/2f7f6f65-4f5c-4a9d-9d4b-4f9f5e7c0c2
Worthy Christian News - 'Trump-Netanyahu Call Reportedly Marked By Sharp Disagreements Over Iran Strategy' https://www.worthynews.com/101234-trump-netanyahu-call-reportedly-marked-by-sharp-disagreements-over-iran-strategy
Times of Israel Blogs - 'Dealing with Trumpian Uncertainty and No Cultural Boycotts!' https://blogs.timesofisrael.com/dealing-with-trumpian-uncertainty-and-no-cultural-boycotts/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), Donald Trump makes at least one public statement explicitly claiming that he had to restrain, stop, overrule, pressure, hold back, or otherwise prevent Benjamin Netanyahu from taking or continuing a course of action on Gaza, Iran, or West Bank policy.

Qualifying statements must be public and attributable to Trump directly, including: on-camera remarks, rally speeches, interviews, official statements, posts on Truth Social/X, or text/audio/video published by Trump or his official political organization. Examples that would count include formulations such as 'I stopped Bibi,' 'I had to hold Netanyahu back,' 'I overruled him on annexation,' or 'I pressured him not to attack Iran.'

Statements that only describe general policy disagreement without Trump claiming he personally restrained or overruled Netanyahu do not count. Likewise, statements made only by aides, anonymous sources, or journalists do not count unless they include a direct attributable Trump quotation published within the resolution window.

Primary resolution sources: Trump's official website/news page https://www.donaldjtrump.com/news, Trump's Truth Social account if accessible via archived/public copies, and video/interview transcripts from major outlets. Secondary confirmation may come from at least one credible report such as Reuters https://www.reuters.com/, AP https://apnews.com/, CNN https://www.cnn.com/, NBC https://www.nbcnews.com/, The New York Times https://www.nytimes.com/, or TIME https://time.com/.

If multiple credible sources quote the same Trump statement, that counts as one qualifying event. If no qualifying Trump statement occurs between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-24 (inclusive), resolve No. If a claimed statement cannot be verified from public records or credible reporting, it does not count. If source material is unavailable but at least two independent credible outlets quote the statement with substantially identical wording, that is sufficient for resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A public claim by Trump that he had to restrain or overrule Netanyahu is a concrete, observable sign of deteriorating public chemistry and blame assignment. That kind of dominance-framing often precedes Trump’s transition to overt mockery or insult, making it a meaningful early indicator for the ultimate question.

question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Toretske by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Toretske is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28, will the ISW Ukraine map show Russian control, gains in the past 24 hours, advance, or infiltration in any area within 5 kilometers of the administrative boundary of Toretsk city (excluding territory inside Toretsk itself)?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a near-term military-positioning indicator for whether Russia is likely to enter Toretsk by December 31, 2025. If Russian forces establish mapped presence very close to Toretsk's city boundary, that would be strong evidence that an entry into Toretsk is becoming more likely in the final days of December.

Toretsk is in Donetsk Oblast and remains a focal point of Russian offensive efforts in eastern Ukraine. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) publishes a daily map and control layers that are also used by the ultimate question for resolution: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 . Because the ultimate market already relies on ISW map shading, a subquestion using the same map but a different geographic condition can provide an informative early signal while avoiding being merely the same question with an earlier deadline.

Recent reporting and analyst commentary indicate that Russia's 2025 advances in Ukraine have generally been incremental, attritional, and often based on infiltration tactics rather than rapid mechanized breakthroughs. ISW's August 31, 2025 assessment argued that Russian gains in 2025 were real but slower and smaller than Russian official claims, describing many advances as gradual and costly: https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-31-2025 . That matters here because a "near-boundary but not yet inside city limits" indicator may capture the kind of stepwise progression that often precedes entry into an urban area.

Open-source reporting in 2025 also noted repeated Russian use of infiltration methods, including pipeline-related approaches in other sectors, underscoring that Russian presence can appear first on the outskirts or in adjacent zones before a clearer urban penetration is mapped. See OilPrice.com's September 19, 2025 report summarizing such tactics near Avdiivka, Sudzha, and Kupyansk: https://oilprice.com/Geopolitics/International/Russia-Leverages-Unused-Pipelines-To-Gain-Ground-in-Ukraine.html .

The 5-kilometer threshold is intended to be close enough to matter militarily for Toretsk while still being distinct from the ultimate question, which asks whether Russia enters Toretsk itself. A positive resolution here would imply that Russian forces reached the immediate approaches to the city, increasing the probability of a subsequent mapped entry before year-end.

Sources:
ISW Ukraine map (control layers): https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, August 31, 2025: https://www.understandingwar.org/backgrounder/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-august-31-2025
OilPrice.com, Russia Leverages Unused Pipelines To Gain Ground in Ukraine: https://oilprice.com/Geopolitics/International/Russia-Leverages-Unused-Pipelines-To-Gain-Ground-in-Ukraine.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-28 inclusive, the ISW Ukraine map at https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 shows any continuous shading corresponding to any of the following layers in an area that is (a) outside Toretsk city territory and (b) within 5.0 kilometers of the administrative boundary of Toretsk city: "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", "Assessed Russian Control", "Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine", or "Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours."

As with the ultimate market, a qualifying map change must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, the shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published. Temporary glitches or obvious map errors do not count.

For this subquestion, "Toretsk city territory" means the mapped administrative area of Toretsk as represented on standard publicly available map basemaps used with the ISW map. If any qualifying Russian shading lies partly inside Toretsk itself, that does NOT count for this subquestion, because the event must be outside the city boundary. If qualifying Russian shading lies outside the city boundary and any part of that shaded area is within 5.0 km straight-line distance of the city boundary, it counts.

Primary source for the military-control overlay is the ISW map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 . Distance and city-boundary checks should be made using the map's basemap and, if needed, corroborated using OpenStreetMap or Google Maps measuring tools: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ and https://www.google.com/maps .

If the ISW map becomes permanently unavailable before resolution, DeepStateMap may be used as a fallback for locating Russian-controlled/contested advances near Toretsk: https://deepstatemap.live/ . If both are permanently unavailable, the question should resolve based on a consensus of credible open-source mapping/reporting. If the available evidence does not allow a confident determination of whether qualifying Russian shading was outside Toretsk yet within 5 km of its boundary during the window from 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-28 inclusive, the question should be considered unresolvable.

This question resolves No if no qualifying event occurs in the window from 2025-11-28 to 2025-12-28 inclusive.
subquestions.rationale: Reaching the immediate approaches to Toretsk without yet entering the city is a classic leading indicator for an eventual urban entry. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it concerns proximity outside the city rather than control of any part of Toretsk itself. If this resolves Yes, forecasters should update upward on the chance that Russia enters Toretsk by December 31.

question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Office of Personnel Management report that at least 75,000 federal civilian employees submitted deferred resignation offers or equivalent voluntary separation agreements between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A large 2025 decline in the BLS 'All Employees, Federal' series would likely require either substantial involuntary layoffs, a large wave of buyouts/deferred resignations, or both. A near-term indicator is whether the federal government publicly reports a very large number of accepted or submitted voluntary separation offers. The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) is the central HR agency for the federal civilian workforce and has published governmentwide civilian employment statistics in FedScope; as of recent years, the federal civilian executive-branch workforce has been a bit above 2 million employees, so 75,000 separations would be roughly 3%+ of the workforce and therefore material for the ultimate 100k-150k cut question. See OPM FedScope employment cubes and status data: https://www.opm.gov/data/datasets/ and https://www.fedscope.opm.gov/. The ultimate market resolves using BLS series CES9091000001 ('All Employees, Federal'), available via FRED at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 and originally sourced from BLS CES. Because the final December 2025 BLS number is not available until January 2026, an official late-2025 count of voluntary federal departures is a useful leading indicator. If DOGE/Elon-driven cuts are truly on pace to reach 100k-150k by year-end, one plausible path is a very large, publicly acknowledged wave of resignations, buyouts, or deferred resignations before the end of December. Recent broader labor-data context also points to elevated uncertainty around payroll measurement and revisions, making direct personnel-action indicators more informative than extrapolating from payroll series alone. The BLS announced a preliminary benchmark revision of -911,000 jobs for the year through March 2025, underscoring data uncertainty in labor-market estimates: https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm.

Sources:
OPM Data, Analysis & Documentation Hub — https://www.opm.gov/data/datasets/
OPM FedScope — https://www.fedscope.opm.gov/
FRED: All Employees, Federal (CES9091000001) — https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001
BLS Preliminary Benchmark Revision for CES — https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesprelbmk.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 (inclusive), the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) publicly states in an official press release, official blog post, official memo posted on an official .gov website, or official testimony/document that at least 75,000 federal civilian employees submitted deferred resignation offers, accepted buyouts, or entered equivalent voluntary separation agreements under a governmentwide program during that same window or cumulatively by a date within that window.

Primary resolution sources are official OPM web pages and press releases at https://www.opm.gov/ and https://www.opm.gov/news/. If OPM publishes the figure in an official memorandum or guidance document, that also counts, provided it is hosted on an official U.S. government website ending in .gov.

The count must explicitly refer to federal civilian employees or federal workers in a way that is governmentwide or clearly broad enough to be relevant to the federal civilian workforce. Purely agency-specific figures do not count unless OPM or another official U.S. government source explicitly states they sum to at least 75,000 governmentwide. Media reports alone do not suffice unless they directly quote or reproduce an official OPM or other U.S. government source document containing the figure.

Equivalent voluntary separation agreements include programs explicitly described as deferred resignation, voluntary separation incentive payments (buyouts), or other opt-in separation programs. Involuntary layoffs, terminations, or reductions in force do not count toward this question unless the official source explicitly includes them within the reported voluntary-separation total.

If multiple official figures are published within the window, the highest clearly stated qualifying total published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 is used. If no qualifying official figure of at least 75,000 is published within that window, resolve No.

If an official source later retracts a figure before 2025-12-30 and replaces it with a lower figure below 75,000, the corrected figure governs. If all relevant official publications are removed and no archived official copy is available, resolver should use the Internet Archive version of the official page, if available: https://web.archive.org/. If no official or archived official source can establish the figure, resolve No rather than using unsourced media estimates.
subquestions.rationale: A very large reported wave of voluntary federal departures by late December would be strong evidence that the government is on track to post a 100k-150k year-over-year drop in federal employment in the December 2025 BLS data. It is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it tracks a different mechanism—voluntary separation program uptake—rather than the final BLS employment level itself.

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pakistan initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Indian territory by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Pakistani military forces that impact Indian territory (e.g., if a Pakistani missile or drone hits a target within India’s borders, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Indian territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Indian soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Pakistani ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will India publicly announce between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 (inclusive) that it has intercepted or shot down at least 10 Pakistani military drones in Indian airspace or over Indian territory since 2025-10-15?
subquestions.background_information:
A renewed burst of Pakistani drone activity would be a meaningful early-warning indicator for the ultimate question, because the May 2025 crisis appears to have escalated from drone and missile attacks into broader cross-border strikes before a halt in military operations was announced. Multiple reports from May 2025 describe Pakistan launching drones and missiles toward Indian targets across several states, with India claiming many were intercepted. For example, India's Ministry of Defence said Pakistani-origin drones and missiles targeted military stations at Jammu, Pathankot and Udhampur on May 8, 2025, and that the threats were neutralised; Firstpost quoted the ministry on this point: https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/how-india-foiled-pakistans-overnight-air-attacks-with-advanced-defence-systems-and-blackouts-13888474.html . India Today reported on May 10, 2025 that Pakistan targeted 26 locations and that debris was recovered in Sirsa, Barmer, and Jalandhar: https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pakistan-strikes-missile-debris-found-in-haryana-rajasthan-punjab-2722846-2025-05-10 . News18 likewise reported Pakistani drone incursions across 26 locations and repeated Indian interceptions: https://www.news18.com/india/indian-army-razes-terrorist-launchpads-near-loc-in-response-to-pak-drone-strikes-video-9350516.html .

The ultimate market only resolves Yes on a Pakistani drone, missile, or air strike that actually impacts Indian territory. But before such a qualifying strike occurs, a visible precursor could be a sharp rise in attempted Pakistani drone penetrations. If India is publicly reporting double-digit military drone interceptions over a one-month period, that would suggest a materially worsened cross-border aerial posture and increase the odds of eventual leakage or escalation to a successful strike before year-end. Conversely, continued absence of such reports would be some evidence against imminent aerial escalation.

This subquestion is not just the main question with a shorter deadline: it tracks attempted Pakistani aerial activity that falls short of the ultimate market's impact requirement. It therefore serves as an operational indicator of escalation pressure rather than a restatement of the end event.

Sources:
Firstpost - How India foiled Pakistan's overnight air attacks with advanced defence systems and blackouts - https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/how-india-foiled-pakistans-overnight-air-attacks-with-advanced-defence-systems-and-blackouts-13888474.html
India Today - Missile Debris Found in Indian Border States Following Pakistani Strikes - https://www.indiatoday.in/india/story/pakistan-strikes-missile-debris-found-in-haryana-rajasthan-punjab-2722846-2025-05-10
News18 - Indian Army Razes Terrorist Launchpads Near LoC In Response To Pak Drone Strikes - https://www.news18.com/india/indian-army-razes-terrorist-launchpads-near-loc-in-response-to-pak-drone-strikes-video-9350516.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive, the Government of India, Indian Armed Forces, Indian Ministry of Defence, or a named senior Indian official speaking in an official briefing or statement publicly announces that at least 10 Pakistani military drones have been intercepted, neutralised, or shot down in Indian airspace or over Indian territory since 2025-10-15.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement is made by 2025-11-14 23:59:59 UTC.

For resolution, the count must refer to Pakistani drones attributable to Pakistani military forces or official Pakistani cross-border military activity; purely civilian quadcopters, smuggling drones, hobby drones, or unattributed UAV incidents do not count. The announcement may aggregate incidents across multiple days within the window, but all counted interceptions must have occurred between 2025-10-15 and 2025-11-14 inclusive. Statements that only say drones were "spotted" or "detected" do not count unless they also say they were intercepted, neutralised, or shot down. If India announces a lower bound such as "more than 10" or "at least 10," that counts. If multiple official statements conflict, the latest official clarification by 2025-11-14 23:59:59 UTC governs.

Primary sources for resolution: official releases from the Press Information Bureau of India (https://pib.gov.in/), the Indian Ministry of Defence (https://mod.gov.in/), and official Indian Army / Indian Air Force / HQ IDS accounts or websites, including https://indianarmy.nic.in/ and https://indianairforce.nic.in/ . Secondary confirmation may come from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/india/), AP (https://apnews.com/hub/india), or BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news/world/asia/india) if they directly quote the official Indian announcement. If no official source is archived but multiple major wire services quote the same official statement, that is sufficient.

If by the end date there is no clear public official statement meeting the threshold, resolve No. If reporting is too ambiguous to determine whether the threshold of 10 military drones was met within the stated window, resolve No rather than extrapolating.
subquestions.rationale: A surge in officially acknowledged Pakistani drone interceptions would indicate renewed cross-border aerial operations and heightened escalation risk. That would increase the chance that, before the ultimate market deadline, at least one Pakistani drone or missile penetrates defenses and impacts Indian territory, satisfying the main market.
