subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), OpenAI or an official Atlas communication channel publicly states that a Windows version of Atlas is available through a beta, preview, early-access, or waitlist program.

Qualifying evidence includes any of the following published within the resolution window:
1. A post or page on an OpenAI-owned domain (for example openai.com, chatgpt.com, or help.openai.com) explicitly announcing a Windows beta/preview/early access/waitlist for Atlas.
2. A post from an official OpenAI social account or official Atlas account explicitly announcing the same.
3. An official app distribution page operated or linked by OpenAI that offers Windows beta/preview enrollment for Atlas.

For Yes, the announcement must specifically mention Windows and Atlas, and must indicate some public-facing availability or signup mechanism (for example: "Windows beta now available," "join the Windows preview," or "Windows waitlist open"). A purely vague statement such as "Windows coming soon" does not count. A private/internal test with no public statement or no public signup path does not count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement appears between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive).

If all relevant official pages are unavailable at resolution time, archived captures (for example Internet Archive) of official OpenAI pages or posts may be used as fallback evidence, supplemented by at least two independent credible reports quoting or screenshotting the official announcement.

Primary sources for resolution:
OpenAI news/blog: https://openai.com/news/
OpenAI main site: https://openai.com/
OpenAI Help Center: https://help.openai.com/
OpenAI X account: https://x.com/OpenAI
OpenAI YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@OpenAI

Fallback archival source:
Internet Archive Wayback Machine: https://web.archive.org/
subquestions.rationale: A public Windows beta/preview or waitlist is a concrete precursor milestone that would substantially increase the odds of a full Windows release by December 31. Its absence by late November would be evidence against the ultimate question.

question: Will Graham Platner drop out of Maine Senate race by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Graham Platner withdraws from or officially announces his withdrawal from the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race, or announces the suspension of his 2026 Senate campaign, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Graham Platner or his official/legal representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any federal or Maine state campaign-finance filing for Graham Platner's 2026 U.S. Senate campaign, made public by 2025-11-22, show more than $500,000 in net operating expenditures during the period 2025-10-23 through 2025-11-22?
subquestions.background_information:
A sharp slowdown in campaign spending after a major scandal can be an early indicator that a candidate is retrenching, unable to sustain operations, or preparing to exit, even if they have not yet formally withdrawn. Graham Platner entered the Maine Democratic Senate primary in August 2025 and had substantial early fundraising momentum: reporting before the current controversy said he had raised about $1 million in under ten days, and later reporting said his campaign had raised nearly $5 million since launch. See Boston Globe coverage from September 2025 (https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/09/03/metro/maine-senate-susan-collins-andrew-kleban/) and Maine Wire reporting from October 19, 2025 (https://www.themainewire.com/2025/10/graham-platners-political-director-resigns/). 

Since mid-October, Platner has faced escalating negative attention. His political director Genevieve McDonald resigned on October 19 after reports on controversial old online posts, calling them values she could not stand behind (https://www.themainewire.com/2025/10/graham-platners-political-director-resigns/). On October 22, the Associated Press reported that Platner apologized over a tattoo widely recognized as associated with Nazi police imagery and said he planned to remove or cover it, while also saying he would remain in the race (AP via article excerpt provided by user; related AP-hosted reporting is syndicated widely, e.g. https://apnews.com/). Yahoo and HuffPost also reported that fellow candidate Jordan Wood urged him to drop out while Platner insisted he was staying in (https://www.yahoo.com/news/maine-senate-candidate-platner-says-211038316.html, https://www.huffpost.com/entry/graham-platner-nazi-symbol-tattoo-maine-senate_n_68f7c3f0e4b0f0d0f3c8d2d7). 

Campaign-finance activity is a distinct observable indicator from formal withdrawal. If Platner continues spending heavily on staff, media, travel, and voter outreach in the month after October 23, that would suggest campaign continuation despite controversy. Conversely, very low net operating expenditures would be evidence of a possible wind-down and could raise the odds of eventual withdrawal by year-end. The Federal Election Commission publishes Senate campaign finance filings, and Maine campaign-finance records can provide corroborating information where relevant (https://www.fec.gov/data/, https://mainecampaignfinance.com/). 

Sources:
FEC campaign finance data — https://www.fec.gov/data/
Maine Campaign Finance Portal — https://mainecampaignfinance.com/
Boston Globe (Sept. 3, 2025) — https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/09/03/metro/maine-senate-susan-collins-andrew-kleban/
The Maine Wire (Oct. 19, 2025) — https://www.themainewire.com/2025/10/graham-platners-political-director-resigns/
Yahoo News (Oct. 22, 2025) — https://www.yahoo.com/news/maine-senate-candidate-platner-says-211038316.html
HuffPost (Oct. 22, 2025) — https://www.huffpost.com/entry/graham-platner-nazi-symbol-tattoo-maine-senate_n_68f7c3f0e4b0f0d0f3c8d2d7
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a federal or Maine state campaign-finance filing for Graham Platner's 2026 U.S. Senate campaign, publicly available by 2025-11-22, reports more than $500,000 in net operating expenditures attributable to the period between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive). 

For resolution, use the first publicly available item from the following sources in order:
1. Federal Election Commission filings/data for Graham Platner's principal campaign committee: https://www.fec.gov/data/
2. If a relevant FEC filing is unavailable or non-itemized for this period by the resolution date, use the campaign's next publicly posted FEC report PDF or electronically filed report accessible via FEC candidate/committee pages.
3. If federal data are temporarily unavailable, corroborating Maine campaign-finance records may be consulted at https://mainecampaignfinance.com/, but because this is a federal Senate race, FEC records take precedence.

Net operating expenditures for this question means the sum of disbursements for ordinary campaign activity during the window 2025-10-23 through 2025-11-22 inclusive, excluding transfers, refunds, loan repayments to candidate, and purely accounting adjustments where these are separately identified. If the filing reports transactions item-by-item, count expenditures by disbursement date. If the filing instead provides only aggregate totals covering a broader period, the question is unresolved unless the report clearly breaks out disbursements for the exact window or a narrower subperiod wholly contained within it that already exceeds $500,000.

A transaction counts only if the filing shows a disbursement date between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 inclusive. Amendments filed after 2025-11-22 may be used only if they correct a filing that was already public by 2025-11-22 and clearly change the answer. If no qualifying public filing with sufficient detail exists by 2025-11-22, this question should resolve Unresolvable rather than No.
subquestions.rationale: Campaign spending is an observable near-term indicator of whether Platner is still operating a serious campaign after the scandals. Sustained heavy spending would suggest he is less likely to drop out by December 31, while a rapid spending collapse would be evidence of retrenchment and increase the chance of withdrawal. This is meaningfully different from the ultimate question because it tracks campaign behavior rather than asking directly whether he exits.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ConsenSys (the parent company of MetaMask) completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by the listed date ET, as confirmed by official company announcements and credible news sources. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If ConsenSys is acquired by another company that is already public, this market will immediately resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will ConsenSys publicly announce or file that it has confidentially submitted a draft registration statement for a U.S. IPO between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information:
A confidential submission of a draft registration statement to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is a common late-stage step toward a U.S. IPO. Under the SEC's expanded confidential submission process, companies may submit draft registration statements for nonpublic review before a public filing, making an announced or reported confidential submission a strong near-term indicator that an IPO is actively progressing. SEC overview: https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/announcement/draft-registration-statement-process-faq

For ConsenSys specifically, reporting on 2025-10-31 said the company had hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to lead an IPO, according to Axios as cited by Yahoo Finance, but the same reporting also said the IPO could occur as early as 2026 and that the company had 'nothing to announce at this time.' This suggests IPO preparation may be underway, but that a completed IPO by 2025-12-31 remained uncertain as of late October. Yahoo Finance summary of Axios report: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-175423414.html

Crowdfund Insider similarly reported on 2025-11-01 that ConsenSys was reportedly planning an IPO and working with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs, reinforcing that there is active market speculation about a listing process rather than a completed public filing. https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/241365-ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/

A confirmed confidential submission would be materially more informative than generic IPO rumors because it would indicate that the company and its banks have moved from exploratory preparation to an actual SEC review process. That would substantially increase the chance of a near-term IPO, even if not guaranteeing pricing before year-end.

Sources:
SEC - Draft Registration Statement Process FAQ - https://www.sec.gov/corpfin/announcement/draft-registration-statement-process-faq
Yahoo Finance - MetaMask Maker Consensys Plans IPO With JPMorgan, Goldman: Axios - https://finance.yahoo.com/news/metamask-maker-consensys-plans-ipo-175423414.html
Crowdfund Insider - Ethereum and Web3 focused ConsenSys Is Reportedly Planning an IPO - https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/11/241365-ethereum-and-web3-focused-consensys-is-reportedly-planning-an-ipo/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), either: (a) ConsenSys publicly states that it has confidentially submitted, or previously confidentially submitted, a draft registration statement to the SEC for an IPO; or (b) the SEC EDGAR system shows a public filing by ConsenSys that explicitly states a draft registration statement had previously been confidentially submitted; or (c) at least two credible business/financial news outlets report during that window, citing the company, the SEC filing, or named knowledgeable sources, that ConsenSys has confidentially submitted such a draft registration statement.

This question resolves No if no such announcement, filing, or sufficiently corroborated reporting occurs between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive).

Primary resolution sources: ConsenSys official newsroom and corporate channels (https://consensys.io/newsroom), SEC EDGAR company filings search (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/), and credible financial press such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/), The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com/), Axios (https://www.axios.com/), or Yahoo Finance reproducing/attributing such reporting (https://finance.yahoo.com/).

Definitions and edge cases:
- 'Confidentially submitted' refers specifically to submission of a draft registration statement to the SEC for IPO review, not merely hiring banks, holding analyst meetings, preparing governance changes, or planning an IPO.
- A public S-1/F-1 filing also counts as Yes only if the filing itself states that a draft registration statement had been previously confidentially submitted, because the question is about evidence that this milestone occurred.
- Rumor or single-source unsourced reporting alone does not count unless directly backed by company statements or SEC filing text.
- If reports conflict and no underlying filing or company statement is available by 2025-12-29, resolve according to the preponderance of the named primary sources above; if this still cannot be determined, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
- Events outside the window do not count. A confidential submission first reported or occurring after 2025-12-29 does not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: A confidential SEC submission is a concrete, late-stage IPO process milestone. It is not the IPO itself, but if it happens before year-end it would meaningfully increase the probability that ConsenSys is far enough along to complete an IPO soon, while failure to reach this stage by 2025-12-29 would be evidence against a 2025 IPO.

question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, the White House Press Secretary, or President Trump publicly state between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31 that the administration is actively considering or preparing a national housing emergency declaration?
subquestions.background_information:
A plausible pathway to another National Emergencies Act declaration in late 2025 is a housing-related emergency. Multiple September 2025 reports said the administration was weighing such a move. Benzinga reported on 2025-09-01 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said, "We may declare a national housing emergency in the fall," while describing housing affordability as a central administration theme and discussing possible federal actions on zoning, closing costs, and tariff exemptions on construction materials: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/25/09/47182011/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency-as-costs-bite . A follow-up Benzinga report on 2025-09-17 noted Polymarket bettors pricing roughly a 34% chance of a housing emergency declaration in 2025 and cited severe affordability pressure, including mortgage rates in the mid-6% range and only 28% of listings being affordable to a median-income household: https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/25/09/47513922/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket-bettors-are-giving-it-a-34-chance-as-mortgage-distress-mounts .

This is informative because a fresh, on-record statement from senior administration officials that a housing emergency is under active consideration would be a concrete precursor signal for the ultimate question. It is not itself an emergency declaration, but it would indicate that internal deliberations are live during the period relevant to the ultimate market. Conversely, silence or walk-back from the principals most associated with the idea would be evidence against another declaration by year-end.

Current context also suggests Trump has been willing to use emergency authorities frequently in 2025. Commentary summarizing the administration's record said Trump had already declared numerous national emergencies in his second term, making another declaration more plausible than under many prior administrations. For example, RealClearPolitics summarized Fareed Zakaria's April 2025 comments that Trump had declared eight national emergencies in his first 100 days: https://www.realclearpolitics.com/video/2025/04/27/fareed_zakaria_trumps_eight_national_emergencies_in_100_days_push_boundaries_of_presidential_power.html . Separately, official White House publications show Trump continuing at least one existing national emergency in September 2025, regarding foreign interference in U.S. elections, demonstrating ongoing executive attention to NEA authorities: https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/continuation-of-the-national-emergency-with-respect-to-foreign-interference-in-or-undermining-public-confidence-in-united-states-elections/ .

Sources:
Benzinga - Trump Administration Weighs National Housing Emergency As Costs Bite - https://www.benzinga.com/markets/25/09/47182011/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency-as-costs-bite
Benzinga - Trump Could Declare Housing Emergency In 2025? - https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/25/09/47513922/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket-bettors-are-giving-it-a-34-chance-as-mortgage-distress-mounts
RealClearPolitics - Fareed Zakaria: Trump's Eight National Emergencies In 100 Days Push Boundaries Of Presidential Power - https://www.realclearpolitics.com/video/2025/04/27/fareed_zakaria_trumps_eight_national_emergencies_in_100_days_push_boundaries_of_presidential_power.html
White House - Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to Foreign Interference in or Undermining Public Confidence in United States Elections - https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/09/continuation-of-the-national-emergency-with-respect-to-foreign-interference-in-or-undermining-public-confidence-in-united-states-elections/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, there is at least one public statement by any of the following: (a) President Donald Trump, (b) Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, or (c) the White House Press Secretary, that explicitly says the administration is considering, weighing, preparing, discussing, evaluating, or has "on the table" a national housing emergency or housing-related national emergency declaration.

Qualifying statements must be public and documented in at least one of the following source types:
1. An official White House transcript, briefing, statement, fact sheet, or video posted at https://www.whitehouse.gov/ ;
2. An official U.S. Treasury press release, transcript, remarks page, or video posted at https://home.treasury.gov/ ;
3. A full-text transcript or official video of a televised interview, press gaggle, or press conference hosted by a major outlet if the official government page is unavailable.

The statement must refer specifically to a possible housing emergency declaration by the federal government; generic comments about housing affordability or executive action do not count. Statements of past reporting by journalists do not count unless the official actually makes the statement in the quoted material. A statement that the administration is not considering such a declaration resolves No unless a separate qualifying positive statement occurs within the window.

This question resolves No if no qualifying positive statement occurs between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources will be official government websites: White House presidential actions, briefings, and transcripts at https://www.whitehouse.gov/ and Treasury remarks/releases at https://home.treasury.gov/news . If those are unavailable or incomplete, secondary sources may include official video/transcript pages from major broadcasters or C-SPAN: https://www.c-span.org/ .

If a purported statement occurs within the window but no reliable public record sufficient to verify its wording is available by 2025-11-07, the question should resolve based on the best available official transcript/video evidence. If no such evidence exists, the statement does not count.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about whether Trump will declare another national emergency by December 31, 2025. Public confirmation from senior administration principals that a housing emergency is actively under consideration is a strong near-term leading indicator of that outcome. It captures movement toward a likely declaration pathway without merely restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Israeli government or IDF announce at least one aerial strike by Israeli forces on targets in Yemen between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:
A key driver of whether Israel strikes any foreign country in 2026 is whether the active Israel-Houthi exchange continues in late 2025. Yemen is especially relevant because Israel has already conducted multiple long-range strikes there in 2025, and the Houthis have continued launching missiles and drones toward Israel. On 2025-08-24/25, Israeli strikes reportedly hit targets in Sanaa including the presidential palace area, power infrastructure, and fuel facilities, according to ABC and AP reporting: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-24/israeli-retaliatory-strikes-hit-yemeni-presidential-palace/ and https://apnews.com/ . The Times of Israel also reported repeated Israeli retaliatory actions against Houthi targets during 2025 and noted that the IDF had struck Houthi positions 17 times by mid-September 2025: https://www.timesofisrael.com/ .

The Houthis have continued to attack Israel through 2025. Times of Israel reported repeated Houthi ballistic missile launches and drone attacks in August-September 2025, including claims that since March 18, 2025 the Houthis had launched dozens of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/ . LatestLY reported that on 2025-09-07, a drone launched from Yemen struck the passenger hall at Ramon Airport near Eilat, injuring one person: https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-israel-closes-airspace-at-southern-airport-after-houthi-drone-strike-6348903.html .

Because the ultimate question asks whether Israel will strike zero countries in 2026, persistence of Israeli aerial operations against Yemen in the immediate pre-2026 period is a strong indicator against a peaceful 2026. An official Israeli announcement of another Yemen strike before mid-December 2025 would suggest the conflict channel remains live and raises the chance that Israel again strikes Yemen in 2026.

Sources:
ABC News (Australia) - Israeli retaliatory strikes hit Yemeni presidential palace - https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-08-24/israeli-retaliatory-strikes-hit-yemeni-presidential-palace/
AP News - Israeli airstrikes targeting Iran-backed Houthis rock Yemen's capital - https://apnews.com/
The Times of Israel - IDF downs Yemen missile aimed at Tel Aviv; Houthis claim it had cluster bomb warhead - https://www.timesofisrael.com/
LatestLY - Israel Closes Airspace at Southern Airport After Houthi Drone Strike - https://www.latestly.com/agency-news/world-news-israel-closes-airspace-at-southern-airport-after-houthi-drone-strike-6348903.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive), the Israeli government, Israeli Ministry of Defense, Israeli Prime Minister's Office, or IDF officially announces that Israeli forces carried out at least one airstrike, missile strike, or drone strike on targets in Yemen.

For resolution, qualifying announcements include official statements published on the IDF website or IDF English/X channels, the Israeli government press office, Prime Minister's Office, or Ministry of Defense. Primary sources to use first:
- IDF official news / press releases: https://www.idf.il/en/
- IDF official X account: https://x.com/idfonline
- Israeli Prime Minister's Office: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office/govil-landing-page
- Israeli Ministry of Defense: https://www.gov.il/en/departments/ministry_of_defense/govil-landing-page

If no official Israeli statement is available or clearly archived, the question may also resolve Yes based on a consensus of at least three credible major news outlets reporting that Israel conducted such a strike in Yemen within the window. Suggested fallback sources include Reuters https://www.reuters.com/ , AP https://apnews.com/ , BBC https://www.bbc.com/news , and The Times of Israel https://www.timesofisrael.com/ .

The question resolves No if no qualifying Israeli strike in Yemen is announced or credibly reported as having occurred between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive).

Only strikes whose occurrence is reported as happening within the stated window count. Announcements made within the window about strikes that occurred before 2025-11-14 do not count. Planned, threatened, or mobilized operations that do not culminate in an actual reported strike within the window do not count. Interceptions of Houthi missiles or drones by Israel do not count. If reports are irreconcilably contradictory and no consensus can be established about whether a strike occurred in the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: Yemen is the most active non-Gaza foreign strike theater for Israel in the supplied 2025 context. Another Israeli strike on Yemen in the month before 2026 would be a direct indicator that at least one foreign aerial conflict channel remains active, making a zero-country strike year in 2026 less likely.

question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States falls below 6.00% at any point between September 2 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If, for any reason, there is no data point for this market's resolution date on either of the sources listed below, information for the nearest previously available date will be used.

The primary resolution source for this market is Freddie Mac, specifically https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms. The data that will be looked at is the "30Y FRM" as indicated on the graph titled "Primary Mortgage Market Survey®". If the resolution source is unavailable, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US will be looked at instead. If both sources are unavailable, other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool show at least a 60% probability on 2025-10-01 that the Federal Reserve will cut its target rate by at least 25 basis points at the November 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. 30-year mortgage rates are heavily influenced by longer-term Treasury yields and expectations for Federal Reserve policy. While the Fed does not directly set mortgage rates, stronger market expectations for near-term rate cuts often coincide with lower benchmark yields and easier financial conditions, which can feed through to mortgage pricing. As of late August 2025, Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey reported the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage at 6.56%, down from 6.58% a week earlier and described as a 10-month low, but still well above the 6.00% threshold in the ultimate question. See Freddie Mac PMMS: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms and the 2025-08-28 release summary: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/20250828.pdf (if archived on the PMMS site).

A key near-term indicator for whether mortgage rates could fall below 6% by year-end is whether markets come to expect additional Fed easing soon. The CME FedWatch Tool publishes market-implied probabilities for target-rate outcomes at upcoming FOMC meetings based on 30-Day Fed Funds futures, and is widely used as a real-time gauge of rate-cut expectations: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html. If by early October markets assign a clear majority probability to a cut at the November meeting, that would be evidence favoring lower mortgage rates later in 2025.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it asks about monetary-policy expectations rather than mortgage rates themselves. It is a meaningful crux because disagreement about the ultimate question may hinge on whether forecasters expect the Fed to move quickly enough to pull market rates lower by late 2025.

Sources:
Freddie Mac PMMS - https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
CME FedWatch Tool - https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
FRED 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States - https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), and specifically using the value displayed on 2025-10-01, the CME FedWatch Tool shows a probability of 60.0% or greater that the target federal funds rate after the November 2025 FOMC meeting will be at least 25 basis points lower than before that meeting.

Operationally, resolution will use the CME FedWatch Tool page for the November 2025 FOMC meeting at https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html. The relevant probability is the sum of outcome bins corresponding to a target range at least 25 bps below the pre-meeting target range, as displayed by CME on 2025-10-01.

If CME provides a direct probability for a 25 bps-or-more cut for the November 2025 meeting, that direct figure will be used. If CME only provides a distribution across target ranges, the resolver will sum all bins implying at least one 25 bps cut by that meeting.

If the CME FedWatch Tool is temporarily unavailable on 2025-10-01, the nearest previously available 2025-10-01 UTC snapshot from CME pages or CME-published data will be used. If CME permanently changes the page format or removes the tool, archived CME pages or other CME-published FedWatch materials will be used if they clearly show the same probabilities. If no authoritative CME evidence for 2025-10-01 is available, this question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from news commentary.

Primary source: CME FedWatch Tool https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Fallback context source: Federal Reserve FOMC calendar https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.rationale: A sharp rise in market-implied odds of a November Fed cut would be an early signal that rates across the curve may continue falling, improving the chances that 30-year mortgage rates dip below 6% by late 2025.

question: Will Russia capture Bilytske by February 28, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the building located at 48.40731° N, 37.17956° E in Bilytske, Donetsk Oblast, by the specified date ET.

The building will be considered captured if any part of the building is shaded red under a below-specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the building under the above-specified conditions, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Building Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP1.png

Building Location in Bilytske: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/BP2.png

question: Trump enacts a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to establish a de minimis tax exemption on cryptocurrency transactions by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a member of Congress publicly introduce a federal bill creating a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Trump will enact a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026 is whether the policy advances to the bill-introduction stage in Congress during December 2025. Recent reporting indicates that this idea is active but not yet enacted. Senator Cynthia Lummis was reported in October 2025 as 'working on' legislation to exempt small crypto transactions from capital gains taxes, with a reported structure of a $300 per-transaction exemption and a $5,000 annual cap; those reports also note that similar efforts had failed earlier in 2025 during reconciliation negotiations. See Cryptonews (2025-10-09): https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/ and Decrypt (2025-10-09): https://decrypt.co/289746/jack-dorsey-cynthia-lummis-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-btc-payments

Industry pressure also appears substantial. On November 20, 2025, more than 60 crypto organizations reportedly urged President Trump to support tax changes including a small-transaction exemption, with reported thresholds around $600. See Coinspeaker: https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-trump-tax-clarity/ and CoinCentral: https://coincentral.com/cryptos-christmas-wish-to-the-white-house-act-now-on-regulatory-clarity/

Additional November reporting suggests crypto policy advocates were directly lobbying House tax-writers and the White House for 'quick wins' including a de minimis exemption, with suggested thresholds in the $200-$600 range. See TechStory (2025-11-22): https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/

Bill introduction is not the same as enactment, but it is a meaningful crux because enactment by the end of 2025 becomes much more plausible if lawmakers have moved from informal advocacy and letters to an actual legislative text with a sponsor. Since the ultimate question allows either a law or executive action, bill introduction is not sufficient for a Yes on the ultimate market, but it is strong evidence that the policy has concrete political momentum.

Sources:
Cryptonews - Working on It: Senator Lummis Backs Jack Dorsey's Push for a Bitcoin Tax Exemption - https://cryptonews.com/news/working-on-it-senator-lummis-backs-jack-dorseys-push-for-a-bitcoin-tax-exemption/
Decrypt - Dorsey, Lummis Push for Bitcoin Tax Relief as Block Expands BTC Payments - https://decrypt.co/289746/jack-dorsey-cynthia-lummis-bitcoin-tax-relief-block-btc-payments
Coinspeaker - 66 Crypto Orgs Call on Trump for Tax Clarity - https://www.coinspeaker.com/66-crypto-orgs-call-trump-tax-clarity/
CoinCentral - Crypto’s Christmas Wish to the White House: Act Now on Regulatory Clarity - https://coincentral.com/cryptos-christmas-wish-to-the-white-house-act-now-on-regulatory-clarity/
TechStory - Crypto Titans Court D.C. in Push for Sweeping Tax Overhaul - https://techstory.in/crypto-titans-court-d-c-in-push-for-sweeping-tax-overhaul/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), a bill is formally introduced in either chamber of the U.S. Congress whose text would create a federal de minimis tax exemption for at least some cryptocurrency or digital-asset transactions by U.S. taxpayers.

For this question, 'formally introduced' means the bill receives an official bill number and appears on Congress.gov during the resolution window. Primary source: Congress.gov bill search and bill pages, https://www.congress.gov/

For this question, a qualifying bill must explicitly provide that gains, disposition, exchange, or use of qualifying cryptocurrency/digital assets below a stated threshold are excluded, disregarded, or exempted from federal tax reporting or tax liability. The exemption may apply to all crypto assets or only specific classes of crypto assets; either counts. The bill may include caps, anti-abuse rules, annual limits, or aggregation rules and still qualify.

A bill does not qualify if it only addresses staking, mining, wrapping, lending, broker reporting, retirement-plan access, securities treatment, or other crypto tax topics without a small-transaction de minimis exemption.

Resolution procedure:
1. Check Congress.gov for bills introduced between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 inclusive: https://www.congress.gov/
2. Confirm the bill text or official summary shows a de minimis exemption for crypto transactions.
3. If Congress.gov is unavailable or materially delayed, use the official House Clerk or Senate legislative pages plus the sponsoring member's official congressional press release as fallback sources: https://clerk.house.gov/ and https://www.senate.gov/ .

This question resolves No if no such bill is formally introduced during the window from 2025-11-30 to 2025-12-29 (inclusive).

If a member only announces plans, circulates a discussion draft, posts on social media, or issues a press release without formal introduction during the window, that does not count. If a bill is introduced before 2025-11-30 or after 2025-12-29, it does not count. If source records are too incomplete to determine whether formal introduction occurred within the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
Congress.gov - https://www.congress.gov/
House Clerk - https://clerk.house.gov/
U.S. Senate - https://www.senate.gov/
subquestions.rationale: A formally introduced bill is a concrete, observable step beyond lobbying, rumors, or broad pro-crypto rhetoric. If such a bill appears in December 2025, it would significantly increase the odds that Trump could sign a qualifying measure quickly or that the administration is coordinating around the policy. If no bill is introduced despite intense industry lobbying and prior public support, that is evidence against near-term enactment.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publicly launch Atlas for at least one additional platform beyond macOS (Windows, iOS, or Android) by 2025-11-23?

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

'Publicly launch' means the software is described by OpenAI as available to at least some external users (including a regional rollout, limited user cohort rollout, or beta/open preview that external eligible users can access). Primary sources for resolution will be official OpenAI channels, such as the OpenAI website, product pages, release notes, help center, app listing references from OpenAI, or official OpenAI/X posts: https://openai.com/ , https://help.openai.com/ , and https://x.com/OpenAI . subquestions.question: Will OpenAI publish an official Atlas iOS sign-up, waitlist, or TestFlight invitation page between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22?
subquestions.background_information:
Atlas launched on macOS on 2025-10-21, and multiple contemporaneous reports state that Windows, iOS, and Android versions are expected soon. That makes official pre-release iOS distribution signals—such as a dedicated waitlist, TestFlight page, or official invitation/signup flow—a meaningful near-term indicator of whether an iOS public release by year-end is on track. TechStory reported that Atlas was unveiled on October 21 and is available on macOS, with Windows, iOS, and Android planned 'in the coming weeks' (https://techstory.in/openai-unveils-chatgpt-atlas-revolutionizing-web-browsing/). VentureBeat also described Atlas as globally available on macOS, with iOS support expected soon (https://venturebeat.com/ai/openai-releases-chatgpt-atlas-an-ai-enabled-web-browser-to-challenge-google-chrome/). 

For consumer iOS software, official pre-launch distribution signals often appear before App Store release, especially when companies use Apple TestFlight or public waitlists to recruit users and gather feedback. Apple documents TestFlight as the standard framework for beta testing iOS apps before App Store release (https://developer.apple.com/testflight/). Therefore, the appearance of an official OpenAI-managed Atlas iOS sign-up, waitlist, or TestFlight page during this window would be strong evidence that OpenAI has progressed from a generic promise of 'coming soon' to operational iOS rollout work.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), OpenAI publishes or activates an official Atlas iOS pre-release access point aimed at external users in the United States. Qualifying examples include: (a) an OpenAI-hosted web page or help-center page explicitly offering an Atlas-for-iOS waitlist or signup form, (b) an official OpenAI post or support page linking to an Atlas iOS TestFlight beta, or (c) an official Atlas/OpenAI communication channel announcing that U.S. users can sign up to test Atlas on iPhone.

This question resolves No if no such official Atlas iOS sign-up, waitlist, or TestFlight invitation page becomes publicly available during 2025-10-23 through 2025-11-22 (inclusive).

For avoidance of doubt, mere statements that Atlas is 'coming soon' or that iOS support is planned do NOT qualify unless they are accompanied by a concrete official access mechanism (waitlist, signup, or TestFlight invitation page). Unofficial leaks, third-party reports without a corresponding official OpenAI artifact, App Store rumor pages, and non-iOS beta programs do not count.

Primary resolution sources: OpenAI official website and help center (https://openai.com/, https://help.openai.com/), OpenAI official X account or other official social channels if they directly announce/link the access point (https://x.com/OpenAI), and Apple TestFlight materials if directly linked from an official OpenAI source (https://developer.apple.com/testflight/). If the primary sources are deleted after publication, archived copies (for example, https://web.archive.org/) may be used to verify that the qualifying page or announcement was publicly available within the resolution window.

If an announced signup or beta is explicitly postponed to a date after 2025-11-22 and no qualifying access point was actually available between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22, resolve No. If the evidence is insufficient to determine whether the access point was official and publicly available in the specified window, resolve Unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: An official iOS waitlist/TestFlight/signup is a distinct operational milestone, not just an earlier version of the final App Store launch question. It would indicate that OpenAI has begun concrete iOS distribution and testing work, which should materially increase the odds of a public iOS app by December 31.

Meta announced the Llama 4 models on its newsroom / AI pages in 2025: https://ai.meta.com/blog/llama-4-multimodal-intelligence/ .

Because the ultimate market requires a publicly accessible product explicitly named Llama 5 by 2025-12-31 ET, a public Meta announcement in September centering instead on Llama 4.5 / 4.X would be a meaningful observable signal about whether Llama 5 is likely to arrive on that timetable.

1. The statement must be attributable to Meta itself, such as on Meta's official newsroom, AI blog, developer site, investor relations materials, earnings materials, official social media accounts, or an on-the-record Meta executive statement reproduced by a credible news outlet.
2. The announcement must explicitly include either the string "Llama 4.5" or "Llama 4.X" and indicate an intended 2025 launch/release timing (for example, "this year," "by year-end," or a specific 2025 date).
3. Unattributed leaks, anonymous-source-only press reports, or third-party speculation without an on-the-record Meta statement do not count.

Primary resolution sources: Meta official channels, including Meta Newsroom https://about.fb.com/news/ , Meta AI blog https://ai.meta.com/blog/ , Meta investor relations https://investor.atmeta.com/ , and official Meta/X accounts if they contain the relevant announcement.
