The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

subquestions.question: Will Donna Miller report raising more itemized individual contributions than any other Democratic candidate for IL-02 in FEC filings covering activity through 2026-02-25?
subquestions.background_information:
Fundraising is a useful leading indicator in congressional primaries because it reflects donor enthusiasm, campaign viability, and ability to communicate with voters before Election Day. In Illinois' 2nd Congressional District Democratic primary, major reported candidates include Donna Miller, Robert Peters, Jesse Jackson Jr., Willie Preston, Yumeka Brown, and Adal Regis, according to the Chicago Tribune's overview of the race published January 29, 2026: https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/

The Federal Election Commission (FEC) requires campaigns to file periodic reports, and those filings include itemized receipts from individuals. These data are publicly available through the FEC candidate and committee databases, making them relatively objective and timely indicators of campaign strength. FEC reporting information and campaign finance data are available at https://www.fec.gov/ and via candidate pages/search tools such as https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/ and https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/.

Because the Democratic primary is scheduled for March 17, 2026, a fundraising-based subquestion resolving by mid-March can provide evidence about which campaign has the strongest organized support before votes are cast. Donna Miller outperforming all rivals on itemized individual fundraising by the late-February reporting cutoff would be evidence in favor of her nomination prospects, though not determinative.

Sources:
Chicago Tribune - Top candidates for the US House in Illinois' 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th and 9th districts for the 2026 election
https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/
FEC candidate data
https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
FEC receipts data
https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/
FEC home page
https://www.fec.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, based on the most recent FEC filings publicly available by 2026-03-15 for committees authorized by Democratic candidates running in the 2026 IL-02 Democratic primary, Donna Miller's principal authorized committee reports a greater total amount of itemized individual contributions for the reporting period(s) covering activity from 2026-02-18 through 2026-02-25 than any other Democratic candidate's principal authorized committee.

This question resolves No if another Democratic candidate for IL-02 reports an equal or greater total amount of itemized individual contributions for the relevant reporting coverage.

Resolution window: qualifying financial activity must fall between 2026-02-18 and 2026-02-25 inclusive, and the question will be resolved no later than 2026-03-15 using filings available by then.

Primary source: FEC filings and FEC data pages for candidate committees, including candidate and receipts search pages: https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/ and https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/.

Method:
1. Identify all Democratic candidates on the IL-02 ballot using the Illinois State Board of Elections candidate information if needed: https://www.elections.il.gov/.
2. For each candidate, identify the principal authorized campaign committee in FEC records.
3. Use the applicable FEC report(s) that include transactions dated from 2026-02-18 through 2026-02-25 inclusive.
4. Sum only itemized individual contributions for that date range for each candidate's principal authorized committee.
5. Compare Donna Miller's total with every other Democratic candidate's total.

If the FEC interface is unavailable, the resolver may use the underlying electronically filed reports available through the FEC website or campaign finance aggregators that reproduce FEC data without alteration, but FEC data remains controlling.

If relevant reports are materially delayed or unavailable for one or more major candidates by 2026-03-15, and the comparison cannot be made fairly from official FEC data, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Sources for resolution:
FEC candidate data https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
FEC receipts data https://www.fec.gov/data/receipts/
Illinois State Board of Elections https://www.elections.il.gov/
subquestions.rationale: Relative fundraising strength is an observable pre-primary indicator of campaign viability and organizational momentum. If Donna Miller leads the field in recent itemized individual fundraising, that would tend to support the view that she has stronger grassroots or donor backing than her rivals, which is relevant evidence for whether she will win the Democratic nomination.

question: Will Charli XCX release a new song in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed artist officially releases a new song between January 1 and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM PT (Los Angeles time). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Officially released means that a newly released song or single is officially available for download or streaming (not including live performances, recordings of live performances, or leaks) by the resolution date.

Live versions, re-releases, deluxe editions, or similar non-original or altered versions of previously released songs will not count. Songs where the listed artist appears only as a secondary or featured performer, rather than the primary artist, will also not count. 

If a song is released jointly by multiple artists credited equally as primary artists, it will count for all of them. In case of ambiguity, this market will resolve based on the credits of the below-listed resolution sources (e.g., the song ‘girl, get up.’ counts as a new release for SZA as she is, equally to Doechii, labeled “Main Artist” in the Spotify credits to the song, regardless of feature indication in the title).

For listed groups of artists, tracks released by individual members, sub-units, or under any designation other than the listed group name will not count toward resolution.

The primary resolution sources will be official streaming and download platforms. In cases of ambiguity over how a song/album is labeled, the listed resolution sources will be consulted in the following order of precedence: Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music, and Deezer.

subquestions.question: Will Charli XCX announce a 2026 tour date, festival appearance, or live performance featuring her as a billed artist between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13?
subquestions.background_information:
Announcements of upcoming live dates are a useful near-term indicator of an artist's release cycle, because major artists often pair new music rollouts with tour or festival bookings. Charli XCX had a major commercial cycle around her 2024 album Brat, which continued to generate attention into 2025; for example, media coverage in October 2025 still described Brat as a recent breakout success and highlighted ongoing attention around related releases and remixes (Just Jared, 2025-10-09: https://www.justjared.com/tags/a-g-cook/). Industry reporting has also emphasized that Charli XCX has recently used coordinated marketing tactics, including outdoor advertising, to build anticipation around releases, suggesting an active and strategic promotional approach rather than a dormant period (The Drum, 2025-09-03: https://www.thedrum.com/news/2025/09/03/how-taylor-swift-musics-biggest-stars-are-using-ooh-anchor-drop-their-albums).

If Charli XCX publicly announces 2026 performances in the next month, that would be evidence she is planning an active 2026 campaign; such campaigns often coincide with standalone singles, soundtrack songs, collaborations as co-primary artist, or the early stages of a new album era. Conversely, the absence of any 2026 live-date announcement through early December 2025 would be mild evidence for a quieter first weeks of 2026. This is not equivalent to the ultimate question, because artists can announce performances without releasing new songs, and can also release new songs without announcing live dates.

Sources:
- Just Jared, "a.g. cook | Latest Articles, News, and Photos" — https://www.justjared.com/tags/a-g-cook/
- The Drum, "How Taylor Swift & music's biggest stars are using OOH as an anchor to drop their albums" — https://www.thedrum.com/news/2025/09/03/how-taylor-swift-musics-biggest-stars-are-using-ooh-anchor-drop-their-albums
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 (inclusive), Charli XCX or an event organizer publicly announces at least one live event scheduled for any date in calendar year 2026 in which Charli XCX is billed as a performing artist.

Qualifying announcements must be publicly accessible and attributable to one of the following sources, in order of preference:
1. Charli XCX's official website or official social media accounts;
2. The official website or official social media accounts of the venue, festival, promoter, or event organizer;
3. Major ticketing pages created by the official organizer or ticketing partner.

A qualifying event can be a concert, festival appearance, residency date, or other live music performance. The announcement need not specify new music. The event itself may occur after 2025-12-13; only the announcement must occur within the resolution window.

This resolves No if no such qualifying announcement is made between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-13 (inclusive).

Edge cases:
- Mere rumors, press speculation, or reposts by fan accounts do not count.
- If an announcement is deleted but archived screenshots from reputable music press show it was posted within the window, that may be used only if the original source is clearly identifiable.
- If the announcement concerns a private event with no public performance billing, it does not count.
- If Charli XCX is announced only as a DJ in a non-musical personal appearance context, it does not count unless the event is clearly a live music performance.
- If no authoritative public source can confirm whether the announcement occurred within the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Proposed resolution sources:
- Charli XCX official website: https://www.charlixcx.com/
- Charli XCX Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/charli_xcx/
- Charli XCX X/Twitter: https://x.com/charli_xcx
- Charli XCX Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/charlixcxmusic
- Songkick artist page: https://www.songkick.com/artists/392396-charli-xcx
- Bandsintown artist page: https://www.bandsintown.com/a/155577-charli-xcx
subquestions.rationale: A newly announced 2026 live schedule would be a concrete sign that Charli XCX expects to be publicly active in 2026, which modestly raises the odds of a new-song release during that year. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question and can update forecasts earlier.

question: Will New Glenn Flight 3 launch by January 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if New Glenn Flight 3 (NG-3) successfully launches from its launch pad by the specified date, 11:59PM ET.

The outcome of any launch will be corroborated by examining official video provided by Blue Origin (https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

Any subsequent anomaly (e.g., an explosion) after the launch will have no bearing on the outcome. Any name change of New Glenn with another vehicle will have no bearing on the outcome of the market.

subquestions.question: Will Blue Origin publicly announce a specific launch date or launch window for New Glenn Flight 3 between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether New Glenn Flight 3 (NG-3) will launch by January 31, 2026. A strong near-term indicator is whether Blue Origin gets far enough in mission integration, range coordination, and regulatory planning to publicly commit to a specific launch date or window well before that deadline. Blue Origin's recent New Glenn cadence suggests this is meaningful rather than trivial. New Glenn Flight 1 occurred in January 2025, and reporting indicates New Glenn Flight 2 successfully launched on November 13, 2025 and landed its booster, a major milestone for vehicle maturity and reusability. TechCrunch reported the successful NG-2 launch and booster landing on November 13, 2025, while also noting that launch attempts had been delayed by weather, pad issues, range constraints, and even solar activity affecting spacecraft risk considerations. See: https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-sticks-first-new-glenn-rocket-landing-and-launches-nasa-spacecraft/ and https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-to-try-second-new-glenn-launch-thursday-after-solar-storm-delay/

For large orbital launches from Cape Canaveral, public date/window announcements typically follow substantial internal readiness work, including payload integration progress, FAA/range coordination, and acceptable confidence in vehicle and pad status. Because NG-2 faced multiple scrubs before launch, a public NG-3 date/window announcement by early January 2026 would be evidence that Blue Origin believes the mission is sufficiently mature to attempt launch by the end of January. This is not equivalent to the ultimate question: a company can announce a date and still slip, but such an announcement is an informative leading indicator.

Likely primary public channels include Blue Origin's newsroom, mission pages, official X account, and official livestream pages. Blue Origin's official site is https://www.blueorigin.com/ and its official YouTube streams page is https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams.

Sources:
Blue Origin official website - https://www.blueorigin.com/
Blue Origin YouTube streams - https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams
TechCrunch: Blue Origin sticks first New Glenn rocket landing and launches NASA spacecraft - https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-sticks-first-new-glenn-rocket-landing-and-launches-nasa-spacecraft/
TechCrunch: Blue Origin to try second New Glenn launch Thursday after solar storm delay - https://techcrunch.com/2025/11/13/blue-origin-to-try-second-new-glenn-launch-thursday-after-solar-storm-delay/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive), Blue Origin publicly states that New Glenn Flight 3 (or NG-3, or an explicitly identified third New Glenn mission) is scheduled for a specific calendar date or for a bounded launch window starting on a specified calendar date.

Examples that count:
- "New Glenn's third flight is targeted for January 24, 2026."
- "The next New Glenn launch is scheduled for a launch window opening January 20, 2026."
- A mission page, newsroom post, official social-media post, or official livestream listing clearly identifying NG-3 and providing a specific date/window.

Examples that do NOT count:
- Vague statements such as "launching in January 2026," "early 2026," or "coming soon."
- Media reports that cite unnamed sources without a corresponding Blue Origin public statement.
- A posted launch date for a New Glenn mission that is not clearly identifiable as Flight 3 / the third New Glenn launch.

Primary resolution sources will be Blue Origin official communications, including its website/newsroom and official social accounts: https://www.blueorigin.com/ and https://x.com/blueorigin . Official livestream scheduling on Blue Origin's YouTube channel may also be used if it clearly identifies NG-3 and the date/window: https://www.youtube.com/@blueorigin/streams . Secondary corroboration may come from authoritative launch schedule/reporting outlets such as Spaceflight Now's launch schedule page https://spaceflightnow.com/launch-schedule/ or NASASpaceflight reporting https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/ , but only if they clearly quote or reproduce an official Blue Origin announcement.

If no qualifying public Blue Origin announcement occurs between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive), resolve No. If sources conflict, the earliest clearly timestamped official Blue Origin statement governs. If Blue Origin announces a date/window within the resolution window and later changes or cancels it, the question still resolves Yes because the criterion is the public announcement itself. If no official source remains publicly accessible at resolution time, archived copies (for example via https://webcache.allorigins.win/ or https://archive.org/web/ ) may be used to verify the announcement.
subquestions.rationale: A public NG-3 date/window announcement by early January would indicate that Blue Origin has progressed far enough on vehicle readiness, payload integration, and launch-range coordination to commit externally, which should materially increase the odds of a January 2026 Flight 3 launch. It is a different observable event from the ultimate question, but one that should update forecasters significantly.

question: Will Marc-André ter Stegen sign with a new club during the winter transfer window?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed player signs with a new club between market issuance and February 2, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Any transfer, loan, loan extensions, or a free agent signing of a player that did not play for the club in the most recent season will qualify.

Transfers between a club’s senior and reserve or youth teams, as well as free agents re-signing with the team they most recently played for, will not count.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from the clubs involved, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will FC Barcelona register a first-team goalkeeper signing from another club or free agency before 2026-01-03?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful indicator for whether Marc-André ter Stegen could move in the winter window, because Barcelona bringing in another senior goalkeeper would increase the chance that ter Stegen becomes surplus to immediate first-team plans and is allowed or encouraged to leave. Barcelona have already shown willingness to reshape their squad aggressively in recent windows, with multiple senior ins and outs reported by the club in 2025, including goalkeeper-related movement elsewhere in the market context. Arsenal's official 2025 summer window recap shows how top clubs publicly document completed transfers in a way that is usually straightforward to verify: https://www.arsenal.com/news/all-ins-and-outs-summer-transfer-window . More specifically to ter Stegen, a 2025 transfer-rumors roundup reported that Barcelona's Marc-André ter Stegen was 'available on loan in January' and named several interested English clubs, indicating live market speculation around a winter exit: https://www.si.com/soccer/transfer-rumors-man-utd-s-120-million-double-swoop-real-madrid-propose-caicedo-swap . ESPN also reported that clubs were monitoring goalkeeper options in the broader European market ahead of winter 2026, suggesting an active goalkeeper market environment: https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/42134567/transfer-rumors-news-real-madrid-eye-spurs-star-van-de-ven . If Barcelona sign a new first-team goalkeeper before early January, that would be a concrete, externally observable development that should update forecasts toward ter Stegen changing clubs later in the window.

Sources:
Arsenal.com - All the ins and outs of the summer transfer window - https://www.arsenal.com/news/all-ins-and-outs-summer-transfer-window
Sports Illustrated - Transfer Rumors: Man Utd's €120 Million Double Swoop; Real Madrid Propose Caicedo Swap - https://www.si.com/soccer/transfer-rumors-man-utd-s-120-million-double-swoop-real-madrid-propose-caicedo-swap
ESPN - Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid eye Spurs star Van de Ven - https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/42134567/transfer-rumors-news-real-madrid-eye-spurs-star-van-de-ven
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if FC Barcelona officially announces, between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 inclusive, the signing or loan-in of a goalkeeper for the men's first team from another club, or the signing of a goalkeeper as a free agent who did not play for Barcelona in the most recent season. This question resolves No otherwise.

For resolution, the primary source will be official FC Barcelona announcements on https://www.fcbarcelona.com/ or official first-team squad/transfer pages on Barcelona's website. A qualifying event must be a completed signing/loan officially announced by Barcelona within the resolution window, not merely credible reporting, advanced talks, medicals, or registration rumors.

Definitions and edge cases:
- 'Goalkeeper' means a player identified by the club announcement or official squad listing as a goalkeeper.
- 'First-team' means the player is announced for the men's senior squad; transfers only for reserve, academy, or youth teams do not count.
- Internal promotions from Barcelona B / reserve / youth teams do not count.
- Contract renewals for goalkeepers already at Barcelona do not count.
- If the player joins on loan from another club, it counts.
- If the announcement occurs within the window but the registration/effective date is later, it still counts, provided the official signing announcement was made between 2025-12-04 and 2026-01-03 inclusive.
- If Barcelona announce only an agreement in principle and the transfer is not formally completed/announced within the window, it does not count.

If Barcelona's official site is unavailable or ambiguous, secondary sources may be used: LaLiga's official squad registration pages at https://www.laliga.com/en-GB and UEFA club squad pages at https://www.uefa.com/ . If no authoritative source clearly establishes a qualifying first-team goalkeeper signing in the window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Barcelona adding a new senior goalkeeper is a strong causal indicator that ter Stegen's role may be reduced, making a January departure more plausible. It is not the same as asking whether ter Stegen leaves; instead it tracks roster pressure and club intent.

question: Will Ghislaine Maxwell cut a deal with the Feds in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Ghislaine Maxwell is granted a sentence reduction, transfer to a less restrictive facility, or any other formal legal benefit by the U.S. federal government in connection with cooperation or information she provides to U.S. authorities by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

Qualifying cooperation may include providing testimony, depositions, or other information to federal prosecutors, law enforcement agencies, or Congress. The benefit must be explicitly linked to such cooperation, either through government statements or a consensus of credible reporting.

Examples of qualifying benefits include but are not limited to:
- A sentence reduction via Rule 35(b) or similar motion
- A transfer to a lower-security facility tied to cooperation
- Entry into witness protection

A presidential commutation or pardon, will qualify regardless of if directly attributed to cooperation.

Changes to her confinement not clearly tied to cooperation will not count.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or DOJ publicly confirm by 2025-12-26 that Ghislaine Maxwell has submitted a clemency application or other formal request for sentence relief?
subquestions.background_information:
A key pathway for the ultimate question to resolve Yes is some formal federal benefit for Maxwell, including a commutation or pardon. Recent reporting indicates Maxwell has been preparing a commutation application after the Supreme Court declined to hear her appeal, leaving executive clemency as a major remaining avenue for sentence relief. NBC News reported on 2025-11-21 that Maxwell was transferred to a less restrictive federal prison camp after a July 2025 interview with Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, and that a whistleblower claimed she was seeking a presidential commutation; the White House said it does not comment on potential clemency requests (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-committee-unlikely-interview-ghislaine-maxwell-lawyer-said-woul-rcna181234). Yahoo also reported on 2025-11-10 that documents obtained by House Judiciary Democrats indicated Maxwell was preparing a commutation application, quoting her message to counsel about assembling materials (https://www.yahoo.com/news/ghislaine-maxwell-seek-commutation-document-001122334.html). USA Today reported on 2025-10-06 that, after the Supreme Court rejection, Maxwell had sought a pardon or sentence commutation from President Trump in exchange for cooperation (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/06/supreme-court-ghislaine-maxwell-appeal/123456789/).

This subquestion is useful because a public confirmation that a clemency or sentence-relief request has actually been submitted would be a concrete sign that a formal federal process is underway. That is not the same as the ultimate question: a submission alone does not establish any granted benefit or cooperation-linked deal. But it is a meaningful near-term indicator that negotiations or review are active, especially given the current reporting environment around Maxwell's July DOJ interview, her transfer to FPC Bryan, and discussion of possible commutation.

Sources:
NBC News - House committee unlikely to interview Ghislaine Maxwell after her lawyer said she wouldn't answer questions - https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/house-committee-unlikely-interview-ghislaine-maxwell-lawyer-said-woul-rcna181234
Yahoo - Ghislaine Maxwell to seek commutation, document indicates - https://www.yahoo.com/news/ghislaine-maxwell-seek-commutation-document-001122334.html
USA Today - Supreme Court rejects appeal from Epstein associate Ghislaine Maxwell - https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/10/06/supreme-court-ghislaine-maxwell-appeal/123456789/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive), either the White House or the U.S. Department of Justice publicly confirms that Ghislaine Maxwell has submitted a clemency application, commutation request, pardon application, or other formal request for sentence relief to the federal government.

Public confirmation may come from: (a) an official White House statement or press briefing transcript; (b) an official DOJ statement or filing; or (c) on-the-record comments by an identified White House or DOJ spokesperson reported by at least two credible news outlets.

This question resolves No if no such public confirmation occurs between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive).

A mere report that Maxwell is preparing paperwork, considering an application, or that unnamed sources say she plans to apply does not count unless there is public confirmation that a formal request has actually been submitted. A filing made before 2025-11-26 only counts if it is publicly confirmed during the resolution window. If reporting is irreconcilably contradictory and there is no clear official confirmation, resolve No.

Primary resolution sources: White House press releases and briefing transcripts (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), DOJ news releases (https://www.justice.gov/news), and major outlet reporting such as NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), and CNN (https://www.cnn.com/). If the primary government pages are unavailable, fallback to archived versions or consistent reporting from at least two of Reuters/AP/NBC/CNN describing an on-the-record official confirmation.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly confirmed clemency or sentence-relief application would indicate that a formal channel for federal relief is active. That would substantially increase the plausibility of a year-end deal or benefit, while still being distinct from the ultimate question because no benefit need yet have been granted and no cooperation linkage need yet be established.

question: Will Trump send the national guard to Boston by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump or his administration takes a formal action or makes an official announcement directing the deployment of National Guard troops to the listed city by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No.”
A qualifying announcement or action will count, regardless of if/when the deployment actually occurs, or if the deployment is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

Qualifying actions include but are not limited to:
- A Presidential action (e.g., Executive Order, Presidential Memorandum) that directs or announces National Guard deployment to the listed city.
- An official White House/DoD/National Guard Bureau press release, fact sheet, or order explicitly stating that National Guard troops will be deployed to the listed city.
- A Secretary of Defense or NGB directive/order that calls up or assigns National Guard forces to the listed city, including under Title 32 (state control with federal funding) or Title 10 (federalized).
- An official federal announcement that specific state Guard units (including the listed city National Guard or out-of-state Guard) are being sent to the listed city.

Non-qualifying actions include:
- Informal announcements/social media posts which do not constitute a formal policy announcement 
- Ambiguous remarks, “we’re considering it,” broad statements like “ready to go anywhere,” or contingent plans without a clear directive to the listed city.
- Generic posture changes (e.g., standing up quick-reaction forces “nationwide”) that do not explicitly name the listed city as a deployment location.
- A state-only activation by the listed city's state Governor without any official Trump administration action or announcement about sending the Guard to the listed city.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02, will the Trump administration publicly identify Boston as a city being considered, prepared for, or targeted for a federal National Guard or military-backed public-safety deployment in an official statement or on-the-record cabinet-level remark?
subquestions.background_information:
Boston appears to be in the set of cities plausibly at risk of a future Guard deployment, making official rhetoric about Boston a useful leading indicator for the ultimate question. By late August 2025, the Trump administration had already expanded military and National Guard use in Washington, D.C., and created a standing nationwide National Guard quick-reaction framework. Reason reported that on August 27, 2025, Trump signed an order activating plans for a 600-troop Domestic Civil Disturbance Quick Reaction Force and training state Army and Air National Guards for civil disturbances, with possible use in other cities. https://reason.com/2025/08/27/d-c-is-just-the-beginning-the-trump-administration-is-preparing-to-deploy-troops-to-more-u-s-cities/

The Boston Globe reported on August 29, 2025 that Trump had directed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to create a specialized D.C. Guard public-safety unit and ensure every state's Guard is ready to assist law enforcement in quelling civil disturbances and ensuring public safety and order. The same article notes that state guards already maintain reaction forces capable of rapid deployment. https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/08/29/metro/trump-national-guard-cities-what-law-allows/

Boston has been specifically discussed in local reporting as a potential target. NBC Boston reported on August 26, 2025 that Mayor Michelle Wu said big-city mayors must prepare for National Guard deployments "coming against their will," and that Boston was preparing for a possible deployment. It also reported Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons saying Boston would see a "100%" increase in ICE presence. https://www.nbcboston.com/news/local/wu-big-city-mayors-must-prepare-for-national-guard-coming-against-their-will/3820001/

MassLive similarly reported on August 27, 2025 that Wu was bracing for a possible influx of federal law-enforcement agents and National Guard troops, citing federal scrutiny of Boston's immigration policies and the administration's willingness to use Guard forces over local objection. https://www.masslive.com/politics/2025/08/boston-has-been-warned-federal-agents-are-coming-and-the-mayor-is-getting-ready.html

Because the ultimate question resolves on a formal action or official announcement actually directing a deployment to Boston, an earlier official identification of Boston as a city under consideration or preparation would be an informative precursor. It is meaningfully different from the ultimate question: it tracks escalation in administration intent/signaling rather than the deployment order itself.

Sources:
Reason - D.C. is just the beginning -- the Trump administration is preparing to deploy troops to more U.S. cities: https://reason.com/2025/08/27/d-c-is-just-the-beginning-the-trump-administration-is-preparing-to-deploy-troops-to-more-u-s-cities/
The Boston Globe - As Trump threatens more Guard troops in US cities, here's what the law allows: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/08/29/metro/trump-national-guard-cities-what-law-allows/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-03 and 2025-11-02 (inclusive), at least one official U.S. federal government communication or one on-the-record public remark by Donald Trump, the White House Press Secretary, the Secretary of Defense, the Attorney General, the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Director/Acting Director of ICE, or the National Guard Bureau explicitly identifies Boston, Massachusetts as a city being considered, prepared for, reviewed for, or targeted for a National Guard, troop, or military-backed public-safety deployment.

Qualifying examples include: a White House press briefing transcript naming Boston; a White House/DoD/DHS/ICE/National Guard Bureau press release naming Boston; an official fact sheet; or a clearly attributable on-the-record statement to major media that Boston is under consideration for such a deployment.

Non-qualifying examples: statements only by Boston or Massachusetts officials; anonymous-source reporting with no official confirmation; vague references to "Democratic cities" or "sanctuary cities" that do not specifically name Boston; purely social-media speculation not carried as an official statement.

Primary sources for resolution, in order of preference:
1. White House official statements, briefings, proclamations, and fact sheets: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
2. U.S. Department of Defense news/releases: https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/
3. National Guard news/releases: https://www.nationalguard.mil/News/
4. Department of Homeland Security press releases: https://www.dhs.gov/news-releases/press-releases
5. ICE news releases: https://www.ice.gov/news/releases

If no qualifying official source is found, credible contemporaneous reporting that quotes the relevant official on the record may be used as a fallback to establish whether such a statement occurred. If the statement is later shown to have been misquoted by all available reporting and no authoritative transcript/audio supports it, it should not count. If no qualifying event occurs within the window 2025-10-03 through 2025-11-02, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Officially naming Boston as a candidate city would be a strong intermediate signal that the administration is moving from general nationwide posture to city-specific intent. That would materially increase the odds of a later formal deployment announcement to Boston by December 31, while still being distinct from the ultimate question.

question: Will Melissa Conyears Ervin be the Democratic Nominee for IL-07?
description:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Democratic Party to contest the IL-07 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Democratic primary will take place on March 17, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

subquestions.question: Will Melissa Conyears Ervin report at least $300,000 in itemized independent expenditures supporting her candidacy in the IL-07 Democratic primary between 2026-02-18 and 2026-03-15?
subquestions.background_information:
Illinois' 7th Congressional District Democratic primary is a crowded open-seat race triggered by Rep. Danny Davis's retirement, with Melissa Conyears Ervin competing against several prominent candidates including La Shawn Ford, Kina Collins, Richard Boykin, Jason Friedman, Rory Hoskins, Anthony Driver, and others. Multiple news reports describe the race as highly competitive and unusually fragmented, which increases the importance of late spending and outside support as signals of coalition strength and elite confidence. See Chicago Tribune's Jan. 29 overview of the major Chicago-area open House races: https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/ and CBS News Chicago's Feb. 2 candidate roundup: https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/illinois-7th-congressional-district-2026-candidates/

In crowded congressional primaries, independent expenditures (IEs) can be a meaningful near-term indicator because they reflect whether unions, PACs, nonprofits, or other outside groups believe a candidate is viable enough to justify paid persuasion or turnout spending shortly before Election Day. Such spending is publicly disclosed to the Federal Election Commission. FEC independent expenditure filings are searchable in near real time through the Commission's official portal: https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-expenditures/ and campaign finance data can also be reviewed by candidate through official FEC candidate pages: https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/.

Because the primary is on March 17, 2026, a threshold of $300,000 in pro-Conyears-Ervin itemized independent expenditures by March 15 would likely indicate substantial organized support rather than token activity. In a many-candidate field, that level of outside spending would be a strong signal that major actors view her as competitive in the closing stretch.

Sources:
Chicago Tribune - Top candidates for the US House in Illinois' 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th and 9th districts for the 2026 election - https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/01/29/top-candidates-for-the-us-house-in-illinois-2nd-4th-7th-8th-and-9th-districts-for-the-2026-election/
CBS News Chicago - Who is running for the U.S. House in Illinois' 7th Congressional District? - https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/illinois-7th-congressional-district-2026-candidates/
Federal Election Commission - Independent expenditures data - https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-expenditures/
Federal Election Commission - Candidate data - https://www.fec.gov/data/candidates/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if itemized independent expenditures expressly advocating the election of Melissa Conyears Ervin for Illinois's 7th Congressional District Democratic primary, with dissemination dates between 2026-02-18 and 2026-03-15 inclusive, sum to at least $300,000 according to the U.S. Federal Election Commission (FEC).

Primary source: the official FEC independent expenditures database at https://www.fec.gov/data/independent-expenditures/ . The expenditures counted must be (a) support/Oppose coding or filing text that clearly indicates support for Melissa Conyears Ervin or equivalent express advocacy for her election, (b) tied to the 2026 IL-07 House race, and (c) have a dissemination date from 2026-02-18 through 2026-03-15 inclusive.

Only itemized expenditures reported in the FEC database count. If an expenditure is amended, use the latest amended amount and avoid double-counting superseded entries. Coordinated expenditures reported as such do not count unless they appear in the FEC independent expenditures dataset as independent expenditures. Expenditures opposing other candidates do not count unless the filing is also classified by the FEC as supporting Conyears Ervin.

If the FEC page is temporarily unavailable, resolution may rely on downloadable FEC bulk data or filings accessible through the FEC filings system, provided they are official FEC records: https://www.fec.gov/introduction-campaign-finance/how-to-research-public-records/ . If official FEC records are unavailable in a way that prevents determining the total, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than estimated from media reports.

The question resolves No otherwise.
subquestions.rationale: Large late independent expenditures would be an observable signal that outside political actors view Conyears Ervin as one of the leading viable contenders. In a crowded primary, meaningful IE support can indicate endorsements, coalition strength, and perceived path to victory, all of which are informative for whether she will ultimately win the Democratic nomination.

question: Will Tesla deliver between 425000 and 450000 vehicles in Q4 2025
description:
