subquestions.question: Will Tesla report in its Q3 2025 earnings materials that vehicle inventory days of supply were 18 days or less as of 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla delivered 497,000 vehicles in Q3 2025 according to contemporaneous reporting, far above Q2 2025's roughly 384,000 deliveries, with much of the surge attributed to buyers pulling purchases forward before the expiration of the U.S. federal EV tax credit. This matters for Q4 2025 because the ultimate question asks whether Tesla will still deliver 425,000-450,000 vehicles in Q4 after that likely one-time demand pull-forward. A key indicator is end-of-quarter inventory: low inventory days of supply after a very strong Q3 would suggest Tesla entered Q4 with relatively little unsold stock overhang, which is supportive of mid-400k Q4 deliveries; high inventory would suggest weaker underlying demand and greater risk of a Q4 drop below the target band.

Tesla's Q2 2025 update reported 384,122 deliveries and 410,244 production, so production exceeded deliveries by about 26,000 units in Q2, implying inventory build entering Q3 if not worked off later. See Tesla's Q2 2025 vehicle production & deliveries release: https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/tesla-q2-2025-vehicle-production-deliveries-and-date-financial-results-webcast . Tesla's investor relations site is also the authoritative source for quarterly earnings presentations, where Tesla has historically disclosed a vehicle inventory-days metric: https://ir.tesla.com/ .

The provided news indicates Tesla's Q3 2025 deliveries were about 497,000 and that Q3 production was lower than deliveries, implying inventory drawdown in Q3 rather than further build. Electrek reported Tesla announced 497,000 EV deliveries in Q3 2025: https://electrek.co/2025/10/02/tesla-tsla-announces-497000-ev-deliveries-in-q3/ . Commentary also noted analysts expected a sequential Q4 decline after the U.S. EV tax credit expiration and viewed Q3 demand as partly pulled forward, making post-Q3 inventory especially informative for Q4: https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/04/tesla-deliveries-soar-in-q3-but-what-will-q4-look/ and https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2904827/tesla-tsla-q3-deliveries-expected-to-surge-amid-strong-market .

A threshold of 18 days is chosen because it is neither trivial nor extreme: it is low enough to indicate lean channel inventory after the Q3 surge, but not so low as to require near-stockout conditions. If Tesla reports 18 days or less, that would be evidence that Q3's high deliveries were not merely the result of stuffing the channel and that Tesla may have entered Q4 with healthier sell-through dynamics.

Sources:
Tesla IR homepage — https://ir.tesla.com/
Tesla Q2 2025 vehicle production & deliveries — https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/tesla-q2-2025-vehicle-production-deliveries-and-date-financial-results-webcast
Electrek on Tesla Q3 2025 deliveries — https://electrek.co/2025/10/02/tesla-tsla-announces-497000-ev-deliveries-in-q3/
The Motley Fool on Q4 outlook after Q3 surge — https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/04/tesla-deliveries-soar-in-q3-but-what-will-q4-look/
GuruFocus citing UBS Q4 2025 delivery forecast — https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2904827/tesla-tsla-q3-deliveries-expected-to-surge-amid-strong-market
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive), Tesla publishes Q3 2025 earnings materials on its investor relations website stating that vehicle inventory days of supply as of 2025-09-30 were 18 days or less.

Primary source: Tesla's Q3 2025 shareholder deck / earnings presentation and/or associated earnings release on https://ir.tesla.com/press or https://ir.tesla.com/ .

Resolution details:
- The relevant figure is the explicit Tesla-reported metric for vehicle inventory days of supply (or an unmistakably equivalent metric) for Q3 2025 / as of quarter end 2025-09-30.
- If Tesla reports the metric as 18.0 days or any lower number, resolve Yes.
- If Tesla reports the metric above 18.0 days, resolve No.
- If Tesla publishes multiple Q3 2025 IR documents in the window and they conflict, the latest dated investor-relations document published within the 2025-10-18 to 2025-11-17 window takes precedence.
- If Tesla does not publish Q3 2025 earnings materials containing this metric between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive), resolve No.
- If Tesla publishes earnings materials in the window but omits any vehicle inventory-days metric and does not provide an unmistakably equivalent figure, resolve No rather than estimating from other data.

Proposed resolution sources:
Tesla IR press releases — https://ir.tesla.com/press
Tesla IR main site / financial materials — https://ir.tesla.com/
Tesla SEC filings page (fallback only to verify dates/documents if IR links change) — https://www.sec.gov/edgar/browse/?CIK=1318605&owner=exclude
subquestions.rationale: Q4 2025 deliveries in the 425,000-450,000 band depend not just on Q3 strength but on whether that strength left Tesla with healthy underlying demand versus a post-incentive hangover. Inventory days of supply reported right after Q3 is an early, distinct operational indicator of whether Tesla sold through inventory and entered Q4 lean. Lean inventory after a tax-credit-driven Q3 would make a mid-400k Q4 more plausible; elevated inventory would point toward a sharper Q4 drop.

question: Palmer Luckey Erebor Bank chartered in 2025?
description:
On July 2, it was reported that a group of tech billionaires led by Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey are launching a new crypto-focused U.S. bank (see: https://www.reuters.com/business/tech-billionaires-led-by-palmer-luckey-launch-new-bank-rival-svb-ft-reports-2025-07-02/). 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, a national bank charter (conditional or unconditional) is granted by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) or a relevant state banking authority (e.g. Texas Department of Banking, New York State Department of Financial Services, etc) to a legal entity publicly recognized as the Erebor bank project backed by Palmer Luckey, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

A name other than “Erebor” or a change in Palmer Luckey’s involvement will still qualify, as long as credible sources clearly identify the entity as the same project originally known as the Erebor initiative.

The resolution source will be official announcements from a relevant banking authority and Erebor, as well as a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) publicly acknowledge receipt of a charter application from the Palmer Luckey-backed Erebor bank project, or add the project to its public list of pending de novo bank charter applications, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key early indicator for whether Erebor will obtain a bank charter in 2025 is whether the relevant chartering authority publicly confirms that it has the application in hand and is processing it. Reuters reported on July 2, 2025 that Palmer Luckey and other tech investors were launching Erebor as a crypto-focused U.S. bank and that the venture was seeking a bank charter: https://www.reuters.com/business/tech-billionaires-led-by-palmer-luckey-launch-new-bank-rival-svb-ft-reports-2025-07-02/ . Business Insider later reported on August 8, 2025 that Erebor had submitted an application to the FDIC on July 28 and was awaiting preliminary approval, while also noting that the OCC generally targets a preliminary conditional decision within 120 days of a complete filing, though experts said 9–12 months is often more realistic: https://www.businessinsider.com/palmer-luckey-political-network-help-new-bank-erebor-regulatory-hurdles-2025-8 .

For national bank formation, the OCC is the principal chartering authority. The OCC maintains public materials on chartering and de novo banks, including its Licensing Manual and public notices process, which make public acknowledgment of an application a meaningful sign that a filing is sufficiently concrete to have entered the formal regulatory pipeline: https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/licensing-manuals/index-licensing-manuals.html and https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/public-notices-and-comments/index-public-notices-comments.html . If Erebor appears in OCC public materials or is explicitly acknowledged by the OCC, that would be strong evidence that chartering is progressing and would materially increase the odds of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

This is not the same as the ultimate question, because it asks about public acknowledgment of an application rather than whether a charter is granted. It is an earlier process milestone that should update forecasters meaningfully.

Sources:
Reuters - Tech billionaires led by Palmer Luckey launch new bank to rival SVB: https://www.reuters.com/business/tech-billionaires-led-by-palmer-luckey-launch-new-bank-rival-svb-ft-reports-2025-07-02/
Business Insider - Palmer Luckey's 'political network' will help his new crypto bank clear regulatory hurdles: https://www.businessinsider.com/palmer-luckey-political-network-help-new-bank-erebor-regulatory-hurdles-2025-8
OCC Licensing Manuals: https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/licensing-manuals/index-licensing-manuals.html
OCC Public Notices and Comments: https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/public-notices-and-comments/index-public-notices-comments.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), either of the following occurs: (1) the OCC publishes a public notice, application notice, pending application entry, comment solicitation, or other official public document explicitly identifying Erebor, Erebor Bank, Erebor N.A., or another legal entity that credible reporting clearly identifies as the Palmer Luckey-backed Erebor bank project, as having applied for a national bank charter; or (2) the OCC otherwise publicly confirms in an official statement, filing, press release, or website posting that it has received such a charter application from that project during or before that window.

This question also resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), a relevant state banking authority publishes an equivalent official acknowledgment for a state charter application by the same project.

This question resolves No if no such official public acknowledgment appears by 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC.

Identification standard: if the legal entity name differs from 'Erebor,' it will still count if official materials or a consensus of credible reporting clearly identify it as the same project originally reported as Erebor and backed by Palmer Luckey. Credible reporting may be used only to match entity identity, not to substitute for the required official acknowledgment.

Primary sources for resolution:
- OCC Public Notices and Comments: https://www.occ.treas.gov/topics/charters-and-licensing/public-notices-and-comments/index-public-notices-comments.html
- OCC homepage/newsroom/searchable site materials: https://www.occ.treas.gov/
- FDIC Bank Applications search/resources (for corroboration, not sufficient on their own unless they contain an official acknowledgment by the chartering authority): https://www.fdic.gov/resources/regulations/federal-register-publications/
- Relevant state banking authority websites, if a state charter route is pursued, such as Texas Department of Banking https://www.dob.texas.gov/ or New York State Department of Financial Services https://www.dfs.ny.gov/ .

Fallback criteria: if the OCC website structure changes, resolvers should use the OCC site's search function and archived copies from the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org/) to determine whether an official acknowledgment was posted within the window. If an official acknowledgment is dated within the window but discovered later, it still counts. If no official source can be found and only media reports claim acknowledgment, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Public acknowledgment by the OCC or a state banking authority is a concrete procedural milestone that suggests the application is formal, sufficiently complete, and actively in the regulatory process. That would substantially raise the probability of a 2025 charter grant while remaining distinct from the ultimate outcome itself.

question: Will Tucker Carlson interview Trump by February 28?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump is interviewed by Tucker Carlson between November 17, 2025 and February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An interview is defined as a scheduled, recorded conversation where Donald Trump answers questions posed by Tucker Carlson. Press conferences or media briefings held by the White House with Carlson in attendance will not count.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a credible consensus of reporting that Donald Trump has recorded an interview with Tucker Carlson before February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, even if that interview is not yet released.

The resolution source for this market will be publicly available video footage of the interview; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Tucker Carlson publicly announce between 2026-02-17 and 2026-02-26 that he has interviewed Donald Trump or that a Trump interview is scheduled or recorded?
subquestions.background_information:
A public announcement by Tucker Carlson that he has already interviewed Donald Trump, or that such an interview is scheduled or recorded, would be a strong near-term indicator for whether the ultimate event occurs by February 28. The ultimate market counts a scheduled, recorded conversation in which Trump answers Carlson's questions, and it can resolve Yes even before release if there is a credible consensus of reporting that the interview was recorded.

Recent reporting suggests Trump has been actively doing sit-down interviews with media figures. Trump taped a White House interview with NBC's Tom Llamas on February 4, 2026, which aired around the Super Bowl, indicating that Trump is willing and available for formal recorded interviews in the current period (Awful Announcing, 2026-02-04: https://awfulannouncing.com/nbc/donald-trump-super-bowl-interview-tom-llamas.html ; USA Today, 2026-02-08: https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/super-bowl/2026/02/08/trump-super-bowl-interview-time-how-to-watch/ ). Reporting in late January also said Trump directed aides to beef up his public schedule and include more interviews and events, suggesting a general openness to additional media appearances (AOL/AP syndication, 2026-01-29: https://www.aol.com/trump-directs-team-beef-public-110000000.html ).

At the same time, Tucker Carlson remains publicly engaged with Trump-world news and commentary. While one cited opinion article is not itself a reliable resolution source, it does indicate Carlson was publicly discussing White House developments in December 2025, showing continued relevance of a Carlson-Trump media connection (PJ Media, 2025-12-19: https://pjmedia.com/ ).

Because only 9 days remain before the latest permissible subquestion deadline and 12 days remain before the ultimate deadline, a direct public statement from Carlson would be highly informative: it would likely move forecasts substantially upward if Yes, and somewhat downward if No by the cutoff.

Sources:
Awful Announcing - Donald Trump sitting for Super Bowl interview with 'NBC Nightly News' anchor Tom Llamas - https://awfulannouncing.com/nbc/donald-trump-super-bowl-interview-tom-llamas.html
USA Today - Trump NBC interview to air before Super Bowl. Time, how to watch - https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/super-bowl/2026/02/08/trump-super-bowl-interview-time-how-to-watch/
AOL - Trump directs team to beef up his public schedule to combat questions about his stamina - https://www.aol.com/trump-directs-team-beef-public-110000000.html
PJ Media - How Trump Used Tucker Carlson's Stupidity, Gullibility, and Paranoia to Score a Free Primetime Speech - https://pjmedia.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-02-17 and 2026-02-26 inclusive, Tucker Carlson publicly states that (a) he has interviewed Donald Trump, or (b) a Tucker Carlson interview with Donald Trump is scheduled, or (c) such an interview has already been recorded.

Qualifying statements must be made in a public, attributable format by Tucker Carlson himself, including:
- a post from Tucker Carlson's verified or officially controlled social media account(s),
- an episode posted on Tucker Carlson Network or other official Tucker Carlson video/audio channel,
- a published clip or transcript from a public appearance in which Carlson clearly makes the statement.

The statement must specifically refer to Donald Trump and Tucker Carlson and indicate an interview status beyond mere desire or speculation. Examples that count: "I interviewed President Trump today," "My interview with Trump will air Friday," or "We taped an interview with Trump." Examples that do not count: "I'd like to interview Trump," "We're trying to book Trump," or third-party speculation not confirmed by Carlson.

Primary resolution sources:
- Tucker Carlson official website / network: https://tuckercarlson.com/
- Tucker Carlson official X account (or successor official account if handle changes): https://x.com/TuckerCarlson
- Tucker Carlson official YouTube channel, if active: https://www.youtube.com/@TuckerCarlson

If a qualifying statement appears on another platform, reputable archival or contemporaneous reporting quoting and embedding the statement may be used as secondary evidence. Suitable secondary sources include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), Fox News (https://www.foxnews.com/), NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/), or The Hill (https://thehill.com/).

If no qualifying public statement by Tucker Carlson is found between 2026-02-17 and 2026-02-26 inclusive, resolve No.

If evidence is irretrievably unavailable or authenticity cannot be reasonably established, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: This is a distinct observable event, not just an earlier version of the ultimate question. Carlson publicly announcing that an interview is scheduled or recorded would be one of the strongest available leading indicators that an actual interview will occur by February 28. Conversely, the absence of such an announcement by late February modestly lowers the odds.

question: "The Witcher: Season 4" Rotten Tomatoes score is between 45 and 59?
description:
This market will resolve according to the Rotten Tomatoes’ Tomatometer “All Critics” Tomatometer score for "The Witcher: Season 4" (2025) as of December 31, 2025 at 10:00AM ET.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If for any reason the resolution data is unavailable, the resolution source will be checked every 6 hours, until the actual data is available.

subquestions.question: Will "The Witcher: Season 4" have at least 20 counted critic reviews on Rotten Tomatoes by 2025-11-15?
subquestions.background_information:
"The Witcher: Season 4" premiered on Netflix on 2025-10-30, one day before this subquestion's start date. Early critical reception was weak: multiple entertainment outlets reported that Season 4 debuted at 40% on Rotten Tomatoes, based on only 5 critic reviews, making it the lowest critical debut for a mainline season of the series so far. See CBR (2025-10-30): https://www.cbr.com/the-witcher-season-4-rotten-tomatoes-score-liam-hemsworth/ and ScreenRant (2025-10-30): https://screenrant.com/the-witcher-season-4-rotten-tomatoes-score-record-low/

A low initial score based on a very small sample is often volatile. Whether the review count rises substantially in the following two weeks is informative for the ultimate question because a larger critic pool tends to make the final Tomatometer more stable. If the season quickly reaches 20+ counted reviews, the current low score is less likely to be a fluke driven by a tiny initial sample; if review accumulation remains sparse, the final score may remain more susceptible to movement from a few additional reviews. Rotten Tomatoes show pages display both the Tomatometer and the count of critic reviews used in that score. Main page for the season: https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_witcher/s04

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about review volume, not the final score band. It is a near-term indicator of how informative and stable the eventual Tomatometer is likely to be.

Sources:
CBR - The Witcher Season 4 Rotten Tomatoes Score Fails to Live Up to Henry Cavill's Legacy - https://www.cbr.com/the-witcher-season-4-rotten-tomatoes-score-liam-hemsworth/
ScreenRant - The Witcher Season 4's Rotten Tomatoes Debut Sets New Series Record - https://screenrant.com/the-witcher-season-4-rotten-tomatoes-score-record-low/
Rotten Tomatoes - The Witcher: Season 4 - https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_witcher/s04
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Rotten Tomatoes lists at least 20 counted critic reviews for "The Witcher: Season 4" at any time between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15, inclusive. It resolves No if Rotten Tomatoes does not list at least 20 counted critic reviews for the season at any time during that window.

Primary source: the Rotten Tomatoes page for "The Witcher: Season 4," specifically the displayed critic review count associated with the Tomatometer: https://www.rottentomatoes.com/tv/the_witcher/s04

Resolution procedure:
1. Check the season page and record the number of counted critic reviews shown for the Tomatometer.
2. If the page shows 20 or more reviews at any point from 2025-10-31 through 2025-11-15 inclusive, resolve Yes.
3. If as of the end of 2025-11-15 UTC the page has never shown 20 or more counted critic reviews during the window, resolve No.

Fallbacks:
- If the main season page is temporarily unavailable, use Rotten Tomatoes' season reviews page if available from the same domain and clearly tied to Season 4. Example root domain: https://www.rottentomatoes.com/
- If Rotten Tomatoes is inaccessible for the whole end of the window, use archived snapshots from the Internet Archive for the same URL taken on or after 2025-11-15 to determine the highest review count reached during the window: https://web.archive.org/
- If no reliable public record exists establishing the review count during the specified window, the question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from third-party articles.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on where the final Tomatometer settles. Review-count growth is a useful crux because it indicates how much the initial 40% score is likely to stabilize versus swing. A fast rise to 20+ critic reviews would make the eventual score band of 45-59 easier to assess; sparse review accumulation would imply more uncertainty and greater sensitivity to each additional review.

question: Will MrBeast hit 107 billion views by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the MrBeast YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast) hits the specified number of views by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.  Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the MrBeast YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast).

subquestions.question: Will the MrBeast YouTube channel gain at least 2.5 billion total views between 2025-12-10 and 2026-01-09?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question is whether the MrBeast channel will reach 107 billion total views by March 31, 2026. A useful leading indicator is whether the channel is currently adding views fast enough over a shorter, near-term window. Recent reporting suggests the channel was around 100 billion total views in early December 2025: The Mirror reported on 2025-12-08 that MrBeast had "100 billion total views" and about 451 million subscribers, citing SocialBlade-style channel statistics (https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/us-celebrity-news/10-most-popular-youtubers-2025-34266966). Separate coverage in September 2025 noted that MrBeast's Shorts had already surpassed his long-form uploads in cumulative views, with 47.3 billion Shorts views versus 46.6 billion long-form views as of August 22, 2025, implying that short-form uploads had become the main growth engine for total channel views (https://www.dailydot.com/culture/mrbeast-youtube-shorts-more-views-than-videos/). YouTube's own channel page for MrBeast publicly displays cumulative channel views and is the natural primary source for tracking whether the channel is sustaining enough momentum over the next month (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast). If the channel adds 2.5 billion or more views in roughly 30 days, that would be a strong signal that it remains on pace for multi-billion additional view growth by late Q1 2026; if not, that would weigh against the ultimate market.

Sources:
The Mirror - 10 most popular YouTubers of 2025 and how much MrBeast makes from just one video - https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/us-celebrity-news/10-most-popular-youtubers-2025-34266966
The Daily Dot - MrBeast's YouTube shorts now have more views than his videos -- here's why it matters - https://www.dailydot.com/culture/mrbeast-youtube-shorts-more-views-than-videos/
YouTube - MrBeast channel page - https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the publicly displayed cumulative total views on the MrBeast YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast) increase by at least 2,500,000,000 between 2025-12-10 and 2026-01-09, inclusive. It resolves No otherwise.

Start date and end date: The qualifying window is from 2025-12-10 through 2026-01-09 inclusive.

Primary source: the total views figure shown on the MrBeast YouTube channel page, https://www.youtube.com/@MrBeast .

Operational method: record the channel's displayed total views as of the first accessible reading on 2025-12-10 UTC and compare it with the displayed total views as of the last accessible reading on 2026-01-09 UTC. If the latter exceeds the former by at least 2,500,000,000, resolve Yes.

If the YouTube interface stops displaying channel total views or is temporarily unavailable, fall back to archived captures of the same page from the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/) or another reputable web archive showing the total views field for dates on or immediately adjacent to 2025-12-10 and 2026-01-09. If multiple captures exist on a boundary date, use the latest capture on that date. If no capture exists on the exact date, use the nearest subsequent capture within 72 hours for the start boundary and the nearest subsequent capture within 72 hours for the end boundary. If no reliable boundary readings can be established, the question should be considered unresolvable.

For avoidance of doubt, this question is about net increase in cumulative channel views during the specified window, not whether any individual video reaches a view threshold and not whether the channel hits 107 billion views.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate market depends on whether MrBeast can add enough cumulative views by late March 2026. A 31-day total-view growth metric is a direct but non-identical leading indicator of channel momentum. Strong near-term growth would update forecasters toward Yes on the ultimate question, while weak growth would update toward No.

question: Will Frank Ocean release an album in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the listed artist officially releases a new album between April 8 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM PT (Los Angeles time). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Officially released means that a newly released album is officially available for download or streaming (not including live events) by the resolution date.

Re-releases, deluxe editions, compilations, or greatest hits albums will not count, unless they contain at least 50% tracks that have never been officially released in any format prior to the album's release.

The resolution source will be any official streaming or download site, e.g. Apple Music or Spotify.

subquestions.question: Will Frank Ocean officially announce a new album or album preorder on an official Frank Ocean or Blonded channel between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A public, official album announcement is a strong near-term indicator for whether Frank Ocean will release an album before the end of 2025. Frank Ocean has not released a new studio album since Blonde in 2016, but he has continued to make occasional official moves through Blonded, merchandise drops, and archival releases. In June 2025, HYPEBEAST reported that Frank Ocean was releasing channel ORANGE on vinyl for the first time, showing that official Frank Ocean commercial activity has continued in 2025, even if that item was not a new album release: https://hypebeast.com/2025/6/things-we-loved-in-music-this-week-june-27

For major artists, late-year albums are commonly preceded by an official announcement or preorder window on artist-owned channels or DSP storefronts. Such announcements typically appear on Instagram, the Blonded website/store, Apple Music pre-add pages, or Spotify artist pages before the release date. Because the ultimate question only runs through December 31, 2025, an official announcement by November 30 would materially increase the odds of a 2025 album release, while the absence of one would be evidence against release.

Relevant official channels that have historically carried Frank Ocean releases or announcements include Frank Ocean's Instagram, the Blonded website, Spotify artist profile, and Apple Music artist page:
- Frank Ocean Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/blonded/
- Blonded official site/store: https://blonded.co/
- Frank Ocean on Spotify: https://open.spotify.com/artist/2h93pZq0e7k5yf4dywlkpM
- Frank Ocean on Apple Music: https://music.apple.com/us/artist/frank-ocean/442122051

Sources:
- HYPEBEAST, "Things We Loved In Music This Week: June 27" https://hypebeast.com/2025/6/things-we-loved-in-music-this-week-june-27
- Frank Ocean / Blonded Instagram https://www.instagram.com/blonded/
- Blonded official site https://blonded.co/
- Frank Ocean Spotify artist page https://open.spotify.com/artist/2h93pZq0e7k5yf4dywlkpM
- Frank Ocean Apple Music artist page https://music.apple.com/us/artist/frank-ocean/442122051
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, there is a public official announcement from Frank Ocean or Blonded explicitly indicating that a new album is forthcoming, or an official preorder/pre-add/pre-save page for a new Frank Ocean album becomes publicly available on an official Frank Ocean/Blonded channel or major DSP storefront.

Qualifying examples include:
- A post on https://www.instagram.com/blonded/ explicitly announcing a new Frank Ocean album.
- A new album product or preorder listing on https://blonded.co/.
- A new Frank Ocean album page on Apple Music https://music.apple.com/us/artist/frank-ocean/442122051 or Spotify https://open.spotify.com/artist/2h93pZq0e7k5yf4dywlkpM showing an upcoming album available for pre-add, pre-save, or preorder.

For Yes, the announcement must clearly refer to an album-length project by Frank Ocean. Announcements of a single, EP, vinyl reissue, merch drop, live event, radio episode, soundtrack contribution, or guest appearance do not count. Unverified leaks, media reports, or third-party retailer listings without confirmation on an official Frank Ocean/Blonded channel do not count.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement or preorder/pre-add/pre-save page appears between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources: official Frank Ocean/Blonded channels and DSP artist pages listed above. If one primary source is unavailable, archived captures from the same URL via the Internet Archive may be used as secondary evidence: https://web.archive.org/

If evidence is conflicting or a post appears and is deleted, resolvers should use timestamped archived captures or reliable screenshots that clearly show the official account, content, and posting date within the 2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30 window. If no sufficiently clear evidence is available, the question should resolve No unless a qualifying page remains publicly verifiable.
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement or preorder is a different observable event from the album release itself and is one of the strongest short-horizon indicators that a release will happen before year-end. It should meaningfully update forecasts on the ultimate question without merely restating it with an earlier deadline.

question: Will Laura Loomer join Trump administration by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump officially nominates or appoints Laura Loomer to his administration by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed or nominated by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

Nominations will qualify even if the individual is not confirmed.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Laura Loomer publicly appear at an official White House event or meeting between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
Laura Loomer is a prominent pro-Trump activist who has recently been described by multiple outlets as having informal influence over Trump personnel decisions, while also remaining outside the formal administration. In late August 2025, after Sergio Gor was moved from the Presidential Personnel Office role to an ambassadorship, Loomer openly expressed interest in serving in the personnel office, but Dan Scavino was instead chosen to lead White House hiring. This suggests Loomer is at least plausibly being considered for a government role, but has also recently been passed over for one. See The Hill on Scavino taking the personnel role and Loomer saying she would 'love to run the office of PPO' (https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5470582-scavino-white-house-personnel-role/) and Yahoo/AP-style coverage of the appointment (https://www.yahoo.com/news/trump-taps-loyalist-dan-scavino-172552645.html). 

At the same time, reporting has portrayed Loomer as an 'unofficial adviser' with some White House access and influence. The Daily Beast reported on 2025-08-21 that Loomer had positioned herself as an unofficial adviser to Trump and claimed credit for multiple staffing changes (https://www.thedailybeast.com/trump-whisperer-laura-loomer-says-moms-should-not-be-in-government/). Other reports described Loomer as a possible contender for the personnel office and as someone bringing vetting recommendations to the White House, indicating that her proximity to Trump and White House staff is an important observable signal of whether she could later receive a formal appointment. The New Republic described Scavino's selection as a 'snub' to Loomer while noting her de facto personnel influence (https://newrepublic.com/post/198718/trump-snubs-laura-loomer-white-house-hire), and Yahoo reported that some MAGA figures had floated Loomer for the PPO role (https://www.yahoo.com/news/trump-put-dan-scavino-charge-203754136.html). 

A public appearance by Loomer at an official White House event or meeting would be a stronger signal of normalized institutional access than media commentary alone. Such an appearance would not itself mean she has joined the administration, but it would likely increase the probability of later nomination or appointment by showing recognized, on-record proximity to the administration after she was recently considered for a formal role.

Sources:
The Hill - Scavino expected to be tapped for White House personnel role - https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/5470582-scavino-white-house-personnel-role/
Yahoo - Trump taps loyalist Dan Scavino to take over hiring at the White House - https://www.yahoo.com/news/trump-taps-loyalist-dan-scavino-172552645.html
Yahoo - Trump to put Dan Scavino in charge of hiring at White House - https://www.yahoo.com/news/trump-put-dan-scavino-charge-203754136.html
The Daily Beast - Trump Whisperer Loomer Says Moms Should Not Be in Government - https://www.thedailybeast.com/trump-whisperer-laura-loomer-says-moms-should-not-be-in-government/
The New Republic - Trump Snubs Laura Loomer Again With Latest White House Hire - https://newrepublic.com/post/198718/trump-snubs-laura-loomer-white-house-hire
White House official events/briefings portal - https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
C-SPAN White House events page - https://www.c-span.org/organization/?351/White-House
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Laura Loomer is publicly documented as attending, participating in, or being present at an official White House event or official White House meeting between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

For this question, an 'official White House event or meeting' means an event or meeting that is publicly acknowledged by the White House through at least one of the following: (a) a White House press release, schedule, pool report, transcript, readout, photo release, or video on https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ or another page on whitehouse.gov; (b) an official White House social media post; or (c) official video/archive coverage by C-SPAN of a White House event at https://www.c-span.org/organization/?351/White-House that clearly shows or identifies Loomer.

The appearance must be official and public. Private visits, leaks, unnamed-source reporting, or reports that she met White House staff without official/public acknowledgment do not count. Media reports alone count only if they directly cite or reproduce official White House documentation, photos, video, transcript, or pool notes establishing Loomer's presence.

Examples that count: Loomer appears in official White House event photos; she is named in a White House meeting readout; she is visible and identified in official White House or C-SPAN video of an Oval Office meeting; or her attendance is listed in a pool report for an official White House event.

Examples that do not count: reports that she advised Trump by phone; podcast interviews claiming access; attendance at campaign events, Mar-a-Lago events, or non-White House political gatherings; or attendance at White House grounds events not acknowledged through official/public documentation.

Primary resolution sources: White House official site (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), official White House social media, and C-SPAN White House coverage (https://www.c-span.org/organization/?351/White-House). Secondary sources may be used only to locate and interpret the primary materials.

If no qualifying public official White House appearance or meeting involving Laura Loomer occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive, resolve No. If relevant evidence is contradictory or insufficient to determine whether the event was official and within the window, resolve based on the preponderance of primary-source evidence. If a claimed event is announced within the window but postponed to after 2025-10-01, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly documented official White House appearance would be a meaningful early indicator of Loomer's institutional access and acceptability to senior administration figures. Since the ultimate question is about a formal nomination or appointment by year-end, evidence that she is being brought into official White House settings would likely update forecasts upward, while continued absence from such settings after being floated for personnel roles would be modest evidence against her joining.

question: Will Francis Ellis win the 2025 Internet Invitational?
description:
This polymarket will resolve according to the player who wins the 2025 Internet Invitational golf tournament. 

If the listed player is eliminated from contention for the Internet Invitational based on the official rules of the tournament, the relevant market will resolve to "No".

In the event of a tie, this market will resolve according to the official winner as determined by the Internet Invitational’s rules. If the tournament is officially declared a tie between multiple players, the market will resolve in favor of the player whose display name is listed first alphabetically in this market.

If no winner is announced by December 31, 2025, this market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source will be the official results published by Barstool Sports or affiliated Internet Invitational coverage. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Francis Ellis be listed among the top 8 players on the official Internet Invitational leaderboard at the end of play on 2025-11-09?
subquestions.background_information:
This is an early-performance indicator for whether Francis Ellis can ultimately win the 2025 Internet Invitational. In most golf-style tournaments, a player being near the top of the leaderboard shortly before the finish materially increases their win chances, while being well outside the top 8 makes winning much less likely. The available reporting indicates that the Internet Invitational is a large-field Barstool Sports event with 48 influencers and a prize pool that reportedly grew to $1.7 million before play began, suggesting a substantial field in which leaderboard position should be informative rather than trivial. Golf.com reported on 2025-10-29 that Barstool's six-part Internet Invitational featured 48 influencers and attracted nearly 2 million views in its first 24 hours: https://golf.com/news/barstool-1-million-internet-invitational/. MARCA reported on 2025-10-30 that the event blended professional athletes, internet personalities, and golf creators, and described a Ryder Cup-style format context around participants such as Paige Spiranac and Nadeshot, indicating that public-facing team and player standings are part of the event's coverage ecosystem: https://www.marca.com/en/golf/2025/10/30/paige-spiranac-clarifies-comments-after-internet-invitational-stir.html. Barstool's Francis Ellis author/profile page confirms Ellis is a named Barstool personality involved with the event and includes a post titled "I'm Part Of The Internet Invitational!" from 2025-05-13, supporting that he is an active participant: https://www.barstoolsports.com/topics/francis-ellis. Because the ultimate market resolves to the tournament winner, an independently observable subquestion about Ellis's intermediate leaderboard placement before the final resolution date is a useful crux: if he is in the top 8 by 2025-11-09, forecasters should update upward on his win chances; if not, downward.

Sources:
Golf.com - The unusual lesson from Barstool's $1 million 'Internet Invitational' - https://golf.com/news/barstool-1-million-internet-invitational/
MARCA - Paige Spiranac clarifies comments after internet invitational stir - https://www.marca.com/en/golf/2025/10/30/paige-spiranac-clarifies-comments-after-internet-invitational-stir.html
Barstool Sports - Francis Ellis - https://www.barstoolsports.com/topics/francis-ellis
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Francis Ellis is listed among the top 8 players on an official Internet Invitational individual leaderboard published or affirmed by Barstool Sports or officially affiliated Internet Invitational coverage between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-09 inclusive, with the relevant determination taken from the latest official leaderboard/status published on 2025-11-09 (UTC date). It resolves No if, on that latest official 2025-11-09 leaderboard/status, Francis Ellis is not in the top 8.

Primary source: official Barstool Sports / Internet Invitational coverage, including event pages, videos, score graphics, or social posts from official Barstool accounts: https://www.barstoolsports.com/ and https://www.youtube.com/@BarstoolSports .

Secondary sources, only if the official source is ambiguous but reporting clearly quotes or reproduces the official standings, may include Barstool-affiliated coverage pages or consensus of credible reporting such as Golf.com coverage of the event: https://golf.com/news/barstool-1-million-internet-invitational/ .

Definition notes:
- 'Top 8 players' means tied positions count. If the official leaderboard shows Ellis tied for 8th, this resolves Yes.
- If the event uses multiple pools/brackets/teams, the question refers to the best available overall individual leaderboard or standings explicitly presented as tournament-wide. A team-only standing does not count unless it also specifies individual player ranking.
- If no official individual leaderboard/status for 2025-11-09 is published, use the most recent official leaderboard published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-09 inclusive that is explicitly associated with end-of-day or end-of-play on 2025-11-09. If none exists, the question is unresolvable.
- If the event schedule changes and no play/status update occurs on 2025-11-09, the question is unresolvable rather than using a different date.
- If Francis Ellis withdraws, is eliminated, or is otherwise absent from the official leaderboard by the relevant 2025-11-09 publication, this resolves No unless the official standings still list him tied within the top 8 at end of play on that date.
subquestions.rationale: This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about Ellis's intermediate standing rather than whether he wins. Being top 8 near the end of a 48-player event is a strong, observable signal about his remaining path to victory and should meaningfully update forecasts on his chance to win the tournament.

question: Will Prince Andrew be named in newly released Epstein files by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration (including any federal court) publicly releases previously unreleased files pertaining to the illegal activities of Jeffrey Epstein which contain any mention of the listed individual between market creation and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only previously unreleased files, as of market creation, which contain novel material not previously available to the public will qualify. Documents that are merely re-released, have had redactions removed, repackaged, or newly publicized versions of already available information do not qualify.

Any mention of the listed individual in connection with Jeffrey Epstein will qualify, regardless of if connected to nefarious or illegal activities.

Previously unreleased files is inclusive of any written, audio, photo or video documentation (e.g., qualifying photos which depict the listed individual will count).

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice or a federal court publicly announce, between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 inclusive, a specific date for an additional release of previously unreleased Epstein-related records?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term predictor of whether Prince Andrew will be named in qualifying newly released Epstein files by late March is whether the disclosure process continues on a concrete public timetable. Congress required broad disclosure of unclassified Epstein-related records under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, but reporting indicates the DOJ missed the initial deadline and said that more than one million additional documents had been found and would take "several more weeks" to review and de-identify before release. That suggests continued releases are plausible, but timing remains uncertain. See Face2Face Africa (Dec. 25, 2025): https://face2faceafrica.com/article/justice-department-admits-newly-found-epstein-files-will-delay-disclosure-for-weeks and Yahoo (Dec. 23, 2025): https://www.yahoo.com/news/epstein-files-release-justice-department-posts-new-batch-documents-years-long-investigation-000000000.html

Reporting also indicates the DOJ had already released multiple batches on Dec. 19, 20, and 23, 2025, while acknowledging that many materials remained unreleased or heavily redacted. Vox reported that officials admitted they still held hundreds of thousands of unreleased documents after the statutory deadline: https://www.vox.com/politics/2025/12/20/epstein-files-release-did-nothing-to-clear-up-the-scandals-biggest-question . The Boston Globe described the underlying court and statutory backdrop for disclosure, including grand jury materials and the prohibition on withholding documents solely to avoid reputational harm to public figures: https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/12/10/metro/jeffrey-epstein-files-what-to-know/

Because the ultimate question depends on a further public release containing Prince Andrew, a concrete official announcement setting a next release date would be a useful operational indicator that the process is advancing rather than stalling indefinitely.

Sources:
Face2Face Africa - Justice Department admits newly found Epstein files will delay disclosure for weeks - https://face2faceafrica.com/article/justice-department-admits-newly-found-epstein-files-will-delay-disclosure-for-weeks
Yahoo - Justice Department posts new batch of documents from its years-long investigation - https://www.yahoo.com/news/epstein-files-release-justice-department-posts-new-batch-documents-years-long-investigation-000000000.html
Vox - The Epstein files release did nothing to clear up the scandal's biggest question - https://www.vox.com/politics/2025/12/20/epstein-files-release-did-nothing-to-clear-up-the-scandals-biggest-question
The Boston Globe - What to know about the Justice Department's Jeffrey Epstein files - https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/12/10/metro/jeffrey-epstein-files-what-to-know/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 inclusive, either (a) the U.S. Department of Justice, FBI, U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York, or White House issues a public statement on an official website or official verified social-media account announcing a specific calendar date for an additional public release of previously unreleased Epstein-related records, or (b) a federal court order or docket entry publicly sets a specific date on which additional Epstein-related materials are to be unsealed or released.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement or court action specifying a date occurs between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-26 inclusive.

For avoidance of doubt:
- General statements such as "in coming weeks," "soon," or "by year-end" do not qualify unless they specify a calendar date.
- An announcement qualifies even if the named release date itself is later than 2026-01-26, so long as the announcement occurs within the resolution window.
- The announcement must concern additional Epstein-related records not yet publicly released as of the time of announcement.
- If an announced release is later postponed, that does not negate a Yes resolution; the subquestion is about whether a date was publicly set during the window.
- If only unofficial leaks or anonymous sourcing report a planned date, that does not qualify without an official public announcement or public court record.

Primary sources for resolution:
- U.S. Department of Justice newsroom: https://www.justice.gov/news
- SDNY press releases: https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr
- FBI news: https://www.fbi.gov/news
- PACER/CourtListener for relevant federal court dockets, with CourtListener as a public fallback: https://www.courtlistener.com/

Secondary confirmation sources if needed:
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- The New York Times: https://www.nytimes.com/

If official sources are unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of at least two credible reporting outlets citing the public announcement or court record may be used.
subquestions.rationale: If officials publicly commit to a dated next release, that is evidence the disclosure pipeline is active and makes additional revelations by March more likely. If no dated next step emerges by late January despite statutory pressure and public scrutiny, that would be evidence for slower or more limited disclosure, reducing the odds that Prince Andrew is named in a qualifying new release.

question: Will Trump meet with Maria Corina Machado in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual meets with Donald Trump between January 1, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump publicly mention María Corina Machado by name in an official White House statement, briefing transcript, speech transcript, or Truth Social post between 2025-12-17 and 2026-01-13?
subquestions.background_information:
A useful early indicator for whether Trump may meet María Corina Machado in 2026 is whether he continues to publicly signal attention to her in the near term. There is already evidence of political salience and some degree of proximity between them. Reporting from November 2025 says both Trump and Machado were present at the America Business Forum in Miami, where Machado praised Trump’s stance on Nicolás Maduro, suggesting overlapping political networks and issue alignment related to Venezuela (Economic Times, 2025-11-06: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-president-donald-trump-in-miami-brags-about-the-economy-despite-an-election-night-rebuke/articleshow/121002345.cms). Other reporting says Machado won the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize, and Trump had publicly cared about that prize and international diplomacy optics, making her a more prominent international political figure in U.S. discourse (Asia Times, 2025-10-10: https://asiatimes.com/2025/10/donald-trump-may-be-a-more-serious-nobel-contender-in-2026/). India Today also reported that Trump referenced Machado’s Nobel win in the context of his own foreign-policy boasting, and that Machado dedicated the award in part to Trump, reinforcing the possibility of reciprocal public messaging (https://www.indiatoday.in/world/us-news/story/donald-trump-says-it-is-easy-for-him-to-solve-afghan-conflict-pakistan-taliban-nobel-peace-prize-claim-2650412-2025-10-18). 

At the same time, AP reporting summarized on December 10, 2025 said Machado had not appeared in public for 11 months and did not attend the Nobel ceremony in Oslo herself, which may make an in-person meeting less likely unless there is an explicit political outreach effort first (WAND/AP summary: https://www.wandtv.com/news/ap-news-summary-at-4-50-a-m-est/article_6c3df338-c95e-56f2-a8db-7f3cfbe6c4d7.html). A December 16, 2025 Council of the Americas item also says Machado gave a live video address to a Miami business conference attended by American executives and politicians including Donald Trump, indicating ongoing shared issue space even if not physically co-present in an interactive way that would obviously count as a meeting (AS/COA, 2025-12-16: https://www.as-coa.org/articles/coas-event-maria-corina-machado-mentioned-new-york-times). 

Because the ultimate question is about an in-person meeting in 2026, near-term public mentions by Trump are informative: they are not the meeting itself, but they would indicate active interest, agenda salience, and possible staff-level preparation for later contact. 

Sources:

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will there be a publicly confirmed incident between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-15 in which Venezuelan military forces illuminate, lock onto, or fire at a U.S. military aircraft or vessel with a fire-control radar, surface-to-air missile, anti-ship missile, or deck gun?
subquestions.background_information:
A key near-term crux for whether Maduro's rule survives a U.S. military engagement is whether the current crisis crosses from general military posturing into direct hostile contact short of a full qualifying engagement. Recent reporting describes a major U.S. military buildup near Venezuela, including carrier, bomber, drone, and naval deployments, alongside Venezuelan nationwide mobilization and wartime alert measures. Newsweek reported in late October that the U.S. had deployed eight warships, Marines, drones, aircraft, and Coast Guard units in the Caribbean, while Venezuela put its armed forces on full alert and activated millions of militia members (https://www.newsweek.com/us-venezuela-three-signs-point-risk-war-2025-10-24). Defense One similarly reported that U.S. assets including destroyers, an attack submarine, F-35s, and MQ-9s were operating near Venezuela, and noted that forecasters viewed a deadly maritime or aerial incident as a plausible catalyst for escalation (https://www.defenseone.com/ideas/2025/10/venezuela-us-edge-toward-war-footing-white-house-may-blink-first/401234/). Defense World reported that Venezuelan forces were on a 'state of external emergency' and that U.S. planners considered the use of Venezuelan fire-control radar on U.S. assets or direct challenges to surveillance flights especially escalatory (https://www.defenseworld.net/news/39123/Venezuela_Adopts_Wartime_Stance__Escalating_Tensions_with_U_S__in_Caribbean). Firstpost reported on 2025-11-12 that no direct U.S.-Venezuela military engagement had yet been reported, despite large mobilizations on both sides (https://www.firstpost.com/world/is-venezuela-preparing-for-a-caribbean-military-showdown-against-the-us-2025-11-12). Because the ultimate question turns on what happens if there is a U.S.-Venezuela military engagement, an earlier observable indicator is whether either side begins taking explicit weapons-employment steps against the other. A radar lock, SAM launch, anti-ship missile launch, or deck-gun fire by Venezuelan forces at U.S. forces would be a strong signal that the crisis is moving from coercive signaling toward an actual clash, which would materially raise the chance that the ultimate market's first condition is satisfied.

Sources:
Newsweek - US and Venezuela: Three signs point to risk of war - https://www.newsweek.com/us-venezuela-three-signs-point-risk-war-2025-10-24
Defense One - Venezuela, US edge toward war footing -- but the White House may blink first - https://www.defenseone.com/ideas/2025/10/venezuela-us-edge-toward-war-footing-white-house-may-blink-first/401234/
Defense World - Venezuela Adopts Wartime Stance, Escalating Tensions with U.S. in Caribbean - https://www.defenseworld.net/news/39123/Venezuela_Adopts_Wartime_Stance__Escalating_Tensions_with_U_S__in_Caribbean
Firstpost - Is Venezuela preparing for a Caribbean military showdown against the US? - https://www.firstpost.com/world/is-venezuela-preparing-for-a-caribbean-military-showdown-against-the-us-2025-11-12
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive), at least one of the following is publicly confirmed by credible reporting or an official government/military statement: (a) Venezuelan military forces used fire-control radar to illuminate or lock onto a U.S. military aircraft or vessel; (b) Venezuelan military forces fired a surface-to-air missile, anti-ship missile, or naval/coastal deck gun at a U.S. military aircraft or vessel; or (c) U.S. officials publicly state that such an incident occurred and credible reporting does not subsequently refute the core claim.

For this question, 'Venezuelan military forces' includes the FANB and its recognized components, including the Venezuelan Navy/Coast Guard and the Milicia Nacional Bolivariana if acting under military command. 'U.S. military' includes all branches of the U.S. Armed Forces, including the U.S. Coast Guard. Warning broadcasts, visual intercepts, non-fire-control radar tracking, close shadowing, escorting, or overflights alone do not count. A missile or gunshot fired only as part of an exercise, test, or ceremonial event does not count. A launch at an unidentified target counts only if credible reporting later identifies the target as a U.S. military aircraft or vessel.

Primary resolution sources will be official statements from the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/), U.S. Southern Command (https://www.southcom.mil/), the U.S. Navy (https://www.navy.mil/), and the Venezuelan Ministry of Defense or armed-forces channels if available, supplemented by Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news), and major defense reporting such as Defense One (https://www.defenseone.com/) or Naval News (https://www.navalnews.com/). If no qualifying incident is publicly confirmed in those sources during the window from 2025-11-15 through 2025-12-15, this question resolves No. If reporting remains contradictory and no preponderance of credible evidence establishes that a qualifying incident occurred within that exact window, resolve No. If a claimed incident occurred outside the window, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: This is an escalation indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question. A Venezuelan weapons lock or shot at U.S. forces would sharply increase the odds of a direct U.S.-Venezuela military engagement before year-end, which is the first prerequisite for the ultimate question. It also bears on the likely character of any engagement: if Maduro's forces initiate or visibly risk a clash, that may imply a more intense confrontation and potentially greater regime danger afterward.

question: Trump cabinet member out by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if at least one cabinet-level Donald Trump appointee from his second term leaves their position by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Voluntary resignations, removals, retirements, or departures for any reason will count.

Announcements alone will not qualify toward this market's resolution. An individual must actually have left their cabinet-level position.

Temporary or acting officials will not count toward this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least one Senate-confirmed sub-Cabinet official in a department headed by a Trump second-term Cabinet secretary cease serving in that role between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
Turnover below the Cabinet level is a useful early indicator for whether a Cabinet secretary may later leave office. High rates of departures among deputies, under secretaries, administrators, and other Senate-confirmed political appointees can signal internal conflict, failed policy rollouts, White House dissatisfaction, or broader management instability. Recent reporting indicates substantial disruption across the federal executive branch in 2025. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management said roughly 154,000 federal employees had accepted resignation or retirement incentives as of August 2025, with pay continuing through September 30 or December 31, 2025, depending on the offer; this points to unusually large-scale personnel churn across agencies. See Reuters reporting via UDN: https://www.udn.com/news/story/6813/8923180 . Reuters and other outlets also reported a second wave of deferred-resignation offers across multiple agencies in spring 2025, including Energy, Agriculture, Defense, Transportation, HUD, and GSA, with many departures timed around September 30, 2025. See Reuters/AOL: https://www.aol.com/news/several-federal-agencies-launch-deferred-195611164.html and Reuters/Yahoo: https://www.yahoo.com/news/federal-agencies-launch-second-likely-213000125.html . Reporting in late August 2025 described a broader pattern of leadership turbulence and firings among Trump appointees, including dismissals of senior officials at CDC, IRS, FEMA, Treasury, and DOJ, suggesting elevated risk of further top-level exits. See Raw Story summary of Wall Street Journal reporting: https://www.rawstory.com/trump-appointees-fired/ . If Senate-confirmed sub-Cabinet officials begin leaving during September 2025, that would be evidence of intensified instability within departments and would modestly raise the likelihood that at least one Cabinet member departs by year-end.

Sources:
UDN / Reuters - More Than 150,000 Federal Workers Accepted Resignation Incentives — https://www.udn.com/news/story/6813/8923180
AOL / Reuters - Several federal agencies launch a new 'deferred resignation' effort — https://www.aol.com/news/several-federal-agencies-launch-deferred-195611164.html
Yahoo / Reuters - Federal agencies launch second -- and likely final -- offer to leave — https://www.yahoo.com/news/federal-agencies-launch-second-likely-213000125.html
Raw Story - 'More chaos' as Trump ramps up targeting and purging his own appointees — https://www.rawstory.com/trump-appointees-fired/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if at least one person who, as of 2025-09-01, is serving in a Senate-confirmed, sub-Cabinet position within an executive department headed by a Trump second-term Cabinet secretary ceases to serve in that same role at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

For this question:
- "Senate-confirmed sub-Cabinet position" means a non-Cabinet role requiring Senate confirmation within an executive department, such as Deputy Secretary, Under Secretary, Assistant Secretary, Solicitor General, Administrator of CMS, CDC Director (if Senate-confirmed), or comparable PAS positions. It excludes the Cabinet secretary themself, acting officials, White House staff, and non-Senate-confirmed positions.
- "Ceases to serve" includes resignation, firing, removal, reassignment out of the role, retirement, or death, but not merely an announced future departure. The person must actually no longer hold the office during the window.
- "Executive department" refers to one of the departments listed at 5 U.S.C. § 101. Independent agencies are excluded unless the official is serving within such a department.

Primary resolution method:
1. Use official government evidence showing the departure occurred within the window, such as a department press release, agency leadership page update, White House announcement, or a Senate record showing a successor or replacement. Relevant official sources include department websites and leadership pages, e.g. https://www.whitehouse.gov/, https://www.commerce.gov/, https://www.energy.gov/, https://www.hhs.gov/, https://www.treasury.gov/, and other relevant department domains.
2. If official pages are unavailable or ambiguous, a consensus of at least two credible major news reports may be used, such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), or major national newspapers of record.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying departure is confirmed to have occurred between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 inclusive.

If a departure is announced during the window but takes effect after 2025-10-01, it does not count. If the evidence is too ambiguous to determine whether any qualifying official actually left office during the window, the question should resolve as unresolvable.

Resolution should be based on the earliest clearly documented date the official ceased serving, using official sources first and credible reporting as fallback.

Sources for resolution:
White House — https://www.whitehouse.gov/
U.S. Code, 5 U.S.C. § 101 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/5/101
Reuters — https://www.reuters.com/
Associated Press — https://apnews.com/
subquestions.rationale: Sub-Cabinet departures are not the same as a Cabinet secretary leaving, but they are a meaningful leading indicator of departmental instability, policy conflict, or White House dissatisfaction. If a Senate-confirmed subordinate leaves in September, that increases the chance that tensions or shakeups will reach the Cabinet level before year-end.

question: Will Dan Bongino leave the Trump administration in 2025?
description:

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

subquestions.question: Will Dan Scavino no longer be listed as White House Deputy Chief of Staff on the official White House website by 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Dan Scavino is a close Trump aide whose role appears to have expanded materially in October 2025. Multiple reports on October 12, 2025 said Trump announced that Scavino, already serving as Deputy Chief of Staff, would also take over leadership of the White House Presidential Personnel Office, replacing Sergio Gor. This office oversees selection and appointment of a large share of administration personnel, making Scavino a key gatekeeper for staffing decisions across the administration. See The Hill: https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/ and Fox News coverage: https://www.foxnews.com/politics/ .

Because Dan Bongino’s continued service in the Trump administration likely depends on internal personnel confidence, factional alignment, and who controls hiring/firing recommendations, any visible change in Scavino’s own formal standing could be an informative signal. If Scavino loses the Deputy Chief of Staff title, that would suggest unusually rapid turnover or a broader personnel shakeup near the center of the White House. Such turbulence could increase the odds of other departures, including Bongino. Conversely, if Scavino retains both influence and title through November, that may suggest relative stability in the White House personnel apparatus.

This is not a restatement of the ultimate question: it asks about the formal status of a different senior official whose personnel authority could affect Bongino’s prospects.

Sources:
The Hill - Trump picks longtime aide Dan Scavino to head White House personnel office - https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/
Fox News - Trump announces shakeup at top of WH personnel office - https://www.foxnews.com/politics/
New York Post - Trump announces Dan Scavino as new head of White House Presidential Personnel Office - https://nypost.com/
