iDownloadBlog - Apple responds to Musk App Store claims: https://www.idownloadblog.com/2025/08/13/apple-responds-to-elon-musks-claim-that-apple-favors-openai-over-other-ai-platforms-in-the-app-store/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 (inclusive), OpenAI publicly confirms that it is testing, piloting, beta testing, or otherwise allowing external users outside OpenAI employees to use a standalone social app or social feed product owned or developed by OpenAI.

For this question:
- "Publicly confirms" means a statement by OpenAI or an OpenAI executive spokesperson in an official OpenAI blog post, OpenAI social media account, press release, product page, help page, or in an on-the-record statement quoted by at least one credible technology/news outlet.
- "External users" excludes purely internal dogfooding by OpenAI employees/contractors. It includes testers, creators, partners, waitlist users, or members of the public invited into a pilot.
- "Standalone social app or social feed product" means a product whose primary function includes user-to-user posting, following, messaging, commenting, sharing, or interacting in a persistent feed/community context. A generic ChatGPT feature without social interaction does not count.
- A mere rumor, leak, reverse-engineered code string, or unnamed-source report without public confirmation from OpenAI does not count.

Primary sources for resolution:
- OpenAI News / blog: https://openai.com/news/
- OpenAI homepage / product pages: https://openai.com/
- OpenAI X account: https://x.com/OpenAI
- Sam Altman X account: https://x.com/sama

Secondary corroborating sources if needed:
- The Verge: https://www.theverge.com/
- TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/
- Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/

If no qualifying public confirmation occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 (inclusive), resolve No. If the only evidence is ambiguous and no authoritative public statement from OpenAI exists by the end of the window, resolve No. If relevant statements are made outside the window, they do not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public confirmation of external testing would be a meaningful leading indicator that OpenAI is seriously advancing a social product, without merely restating the ultimate question about App Store availability. It captures product maturity and organizational commitment several steps upstream from launch.

question: Will Google Gemini 3 score at least 40% on Humanity’s Last Exam by January 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard lists any Google Gemini 3 model with a score of at least the specified score by the specified January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source will be the official Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam.

subquestions.question: Will the official Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard list any Google Gemini model with a score of at least 36.0% by 2025-12-05?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator for whether a Google Gemini 3 model can reach 40% on Humanity’s Last Exam (HLE) by 2026-01-31, because Google’s recent HLE progress suggests the key crux is whether Google can push a Gemini-family model from the mid-30s into the 40% range within the following two months. Public reporting before 2025-11-05 indicates that Gemini 2.5 Pro scored 18.8% on HLE in mid-2025, while Gemini 2.5 Deep Think later reached 34.8%, showing rapid progress within the Gemini line. See Google coverage and secondary reports: 9to5Google on the upgraded Gemini 2.5 Pro and its HLE performance https://9to5google.com/2025/06/05/google-gemini-2-5-pro-preview-06-05/ ; Economic Times on Gemini 2.5 Pro scoring 18.8% on HLE https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/google-introduces-stable-gemini-2-5-flash-and-pro-previews-gemini-2-5-flash-lite/articleshow/121914751.cms ; ExtremeTech on Gemini 2.5 Deep Think scoring 34.8% on HLE https://www.extremetech.com/computing/googles-gemini-2-5-deep-think-uses-multiple-ai-agents-to-tackle-a-single-problem .

The ultimate market resolves using the official HLE leaderboard maintained by Scale AI, so a leaderboard-based subquestion is especially relevant and operationally clean. If a Gemini model reaches 36.0% by early December, that would be evidence that Google is already near the 40% threshold with almost two months remaining, strengthening the case for a Yes on the ultimate question. Conversely, failure to clear 36.0% by that date would suggest a larger remaining capability gap. Official leaderboard: https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam .

This is not just the ultimate question with an earlier date: it asks about a lower benchmark threshold for any Gemini model, making it a distinct capability-progress indicator rather than a direct restatement of the 40% January question.

Sources:
- Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard (Scale AI): https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam
- 9to5Google, Google rolling out upgraded Gemini 2.5 Pro preview: https://9to5google.com/2025/06/05/google-gemini-2-5-pro-preview-06-05/
- Economic Times, Google introduces stable Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro, previews Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite: https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/artificial-intelligence/google-introduces-stable-gemini-2-5-flash-and-pro-previews-gemini-2-5-flash-lite/articleshow/121914751.cms
- ExtremeTech, Google's Gemini 2.5 Deep Think Uses Multiple AI Agents to Tackle a Single Problem: https://www.extremetech.com/computing/googles-gemini-2-5-deep-think-uses-multiple-ai-agents-to-tackle-a-single-problem
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the official Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard at https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam lists any model whose name includes the word "Gemini" and whose listed organization is Google (or Google DeepMind, if that is how the leaderboard presents it), with a score of at least 36.0%, at any time between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 inclusive.

This question resolves No if, by 2025-12-05 23:59:59 UTC, no such qualifying Gemini model appears on the official leaderboard with a score of at least 36.0% during the window from 2025-11-05 through 2025-12-05 inclusive.

Primary resolution source: the official Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard, https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam .

Resolution procedure:
1. Check the official leaderboard on or immediately after 2025-12-05.
2. Use publicly visible leaderboard entries and, if needed, publicly accessible web archives or cached snapshots of that same URL captured during the resolution window to determine whether a qualifying entry appeared between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 inclusive. Acceptable fallback archival evidence includes the Internet Archive Wayback Machine for the exact leaderboard URL: https://web.archive.org/web/*/https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam .
3. If the leaderboard structure changes, use the official Scale AI HLE leaderboard page and any official linked HLE results page from Scale as the authoritative source.

Definitions and edge cases:
- "Any Google Gemini model" includes any leaderboard entry clearly branded as Gemini and attributable on the leaderboard to Google or Google DeepMind.
- The score used is the percentage score displayed by the leaderboard for that entry.
- If multiple Gemini entries qualify, one is sufficient for Yes.
- If the leaderboard becomes unavailable and no archived snapshot or official Scale replacement page exists that allows determination of whether a qualifying score appeared during the window, the question should be considered unresolvable.
- If a qualifying model first appears only after 2025-12-05, that does not count.

Sources for resolution:
- Official Humanity’s Last Exam leaderboard (Scale AI): https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam
- Wayback Machine archive for fallback verification: https://web.archive.org/web/*/https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question hinges on whether Google can close the remaining gap from the best reported Gemini HLE result near 34.8% to 40% by late January. Crossing 36.0% by early December would be strong evidence that the capability trend is continuing and that 40% is within reach on the official leaderboard. Missing 36.0% by then would suggest slower progress and lower odds of hitting 40% by the deadline.

question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ukraine publicly agrees not to join NATO by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An official pledge by Ukraine not to join NATO will qualify for a “Yes” resolution whether as a unilateral announcement or part of an agreement with the Russian Federation. 

Any agreement or pledge made before the resolution date of this market will qualify, regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO for any amount of time will count (e.g. If Ukraine not to join NATO for 10 years this will qualify).

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995 “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement is an example of a qualifying agreement. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by the Ukraine, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming a qualifying agreement has been reached will also count.

subquestions.question: Will President Volodymyr Zelenskyy or Ukraine's Presidential Office publicly state between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 that Ukraine is prepared to accept a peace arrangement that bars or suspends NATO membership for a defined period?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term public softening by Ukraine's top leadership on NATO could be a strong indicator for the ultimate question, because recent reporting suggests neutrality or a pause on NATO membership is one of the central disputed terms in ongoing peace talks. On 24 November 2025, AFP reported that Washington and Kyiv said any peace deal must uphold Ukraine's sovereignty, while noting that the original US draft had required Ukraine to pledge not to join NATO and that Ukraine sought revisions: https://www.barrons.com/news/washington-kyiv-say-a-peace-deal-must-fully-uphold-ukraine-sovereignty-e15cc17d . On 25-26 November 2025, CBS/AOL reported that Ukrainian negotiators had reached a common understanding on the 'core terms' of a US-brokered proposal, and that the framework reportedly included Ukraine abandoning its NATO membership bid in exchange for Article 5-like security assurances: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-proposal-minor-details-no-word-russia/ and https://www.aol.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-deal-only-142726737.html .

At the same time, European institutions were publicly rejecting any settlement that compromised Ukraine's sovereign choice of alliances. The European Parliament's adopted text of 27 November 2025 insisted on 'freedom of alliance choice' and robust security guarantees, highlighting that NATO-status language remained politically salient and contested: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-10-2025-0113_EN.html . Because public statements by Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office would likely precede or accompany any formal agreement, a clear acknowledgment that Ukraine is prepared to accept a bar or temporary suspension on NATO membership would be a meaningful leading indicator for whether Ukraine will in fact publicly agree not to join NATO by year-end.

Sources:
CBS News - Ukraine agrees to peace proposal, with only 'minor details' to settle, official says, but no word from Russia - https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-proposal-minor-details-no-word-russia/
AOL - Ukraine agrees to peace deal, only 'minor details' left, official says - https://www.aol.com/news/ukraine-agrees-peace-deal-only-142726737.html
Barron's/AFP - Washington, Kyiv say a peace deal must 'fully uphold' Ukraine sovereignty - https://www.barrons.com/news/washington-kyiv-say-a-peace-deal-must-fully-uphold-ukraine-sovereignty-e15cc17d
European Parliament adopted text - https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/TA-10-2025-0113_EN.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), either (a) President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, or (b) the Office of the President of Ukraine / Presidential Office of Ukraine, in a public statement, interview, speech, press release, transcript, post, or video, explicitly says that Ukraine is prepared to accept, support, or agree to a peace arrangement under which Ukraine will not join NATO, or will suspend/pause/defer seeking NATO membership, for any defined period of time.

Qualifying examples include language such as: 'Ukraine is prepared to renounce NATO membership for X years,' 'Ukraine can accept non-membership/neutrality/non-alignment as part of a peace deal,' or 'Ukraine is ready to suspend its NATO bid for X years.' The duration may be temporary or indefinite.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs within the window 2025-11-30 through 2025-12-29 inclusive.

Non-qualifying statements: (i) statements solely by foreign governments, mediators, anonymous officials, or media reports claiming Ukraine agreed, unless accompanied by a qualifying direct public statement from Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office; (ii) statements merely reaffirming that security guarantees are needed, without indicating willingness to forgo or suspend NATO membership; (iii) statements by Ukrainian ministers or negotiators other than Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office, unless the statement is simultaneously published or clearly endorsed by the Presidential Office.

Primary resolution sources: official website of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en), official presidential X/social accounts if archived or directly linked from official channels, and official video/transcript publications. Secondary sources, if needed to identify the statement, may include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP (https://apnews.com/), and BBC (https://www.bbc.com/news), but the underlying qualifying statement must still be directly attributable to Zelenskyy or the Presidential Office.

If no qualifying official/public statement is available by the end of 2025-12-29 UTC, resolve No. If alleged remarks cannot be verified from official publication, full transcript, or high-confidence video/audio published by credible outlets, they do not count.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires a public Ukrainian agreement not to join NATO by year-end. A public statement from Zelenskyy or his office indicating willingness to accept a neutrality or NATO-suspension clause would be a strong precursor and would materially update forecasts, while still being distinct from the final event because it asks about a softer preparatory signal rather than the agreement itself.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any country not already a part of the Abraham Accords formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Saudi Arabia publicly reaffirm between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that normalization with Israel requires a pathway to a Palestinian state?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia is widely viewed as the most consequential plausible future entrant to the Abraham Accords, so its stated conditions are a key near-term indicator for whether any new country is likely to join by the end of 2025. Multiple recent reports say Saudi normalization remains contingent on movement toward Palestinian statehood. Reuters reported in September 2025 that Riyadh insists any normalization must include a clear path to a Palestinian state, which conflicts with the position of Israel's current government (via Yahoo/Reuters summary: https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-abraham-accords-115050294.html ; MarketScreener/Reuters summary: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Factbox-What-are-the-Abraham-Accords-50878031/). The Seattle Times similarly reported on October 13, 2025 that Saudi expansion into the accords has stalled because the kingdom insists on a Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital (https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/what-are-the-abraham-accords-trumps-2020-mideast-deals/). Al Jazeera also reported on October 17, 2025 that Saudi Arabia continues to uphold the Arab Peace Initiative and links normalization to Palestinian statehood amid highly negative domestic sentiment toward normalization (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon-hopes-s-arabia-will-join).

A fresh Saudi public reaffirmation of that condition in November would be evidence against rapid late-2025 expansion of the accords, because it would suggest the main candidate has not softened its position. Conversely, the absence of such a reaffirmation during this window would not guarantee a deal, but it would remove one visible obstacle. This is therefore a meaningful indicator rather than a restatement of the ultimate question.

Sources:
Reuters/Yahoo factbox on the Abraham Accords — https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-abraham-accords-115050294.html
MarketScreener/Reuters factbox — https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Factbox-What-are-the-Abraham-Accords-50878031/
The Seattle Times on the Abraham Accords — https://www.seattletimes.com/nation-world/what-are-the-abraham-accords-trumps-2020-mideast-deals/
Al Jazeera on expected expansion and Saudi Arabia — https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/10/17/trump-expects-expansion-of-abraham-accords-soon-hopes-s-arabia-will-join
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), an official Saudi government statement publicly says that normalization or diplomatic relations with Israel require, as a condition, a Palestinian state, a pathway to a Palestinian state, implementation of the Arab Peace Initiative, or materially equivalent language linking normalization to Palestinian statehood.

Qualifying statements must be attributable to an official Saudi source, such as the Saudi Press Agency, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Crown Prince, the King, the Foreign Minister, or another senior Saudi official speaking in an official capacity. Official sources include, for example, https://www.spa.gov.sa/en and https://www.mofa.gov.sa/.

If no qualifying official Saudi statement is published during the window, the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources: Saudi Press Agency (https://www.spa.gov.sa/en), Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.mofa.gov.sa/), and official verified Saudi government social-media or press-release accounts linked from those sites. Secondary confirmation may come from Reuters reporting if it clearly quotes or paraphrases an official Saudi statement published during the window (https://www.reuters.com/).

Edge cases: (1) General statements supporting Palestinian rights without linking them to normalization do not count. (2) Statements by non-Saudi officials about Saudi conditions do not count unless confirmed by an official Saudi source. (3) If a statement is issued within the window but only discovered later, it still counts if the publication timestamp shows it was first published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive. (4) If all primary sources are unavailable, a consensus of at least two credible international outlets quoting the official Saudi statement may be used. (5) If a relevant event is announced during the window but explicitly described as unofficial, exploratory, or off the record, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: Saudi Arabia is the most-discussed potential new Abraham Accords entrant. Whether Riyadh publicly reiterates its Palestinian-state precondition in November is a strong near-term signal about the odds that any new country joins by year-end 2025.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Standard & Poor's, Moody's, or Fitch; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Moody's change France's sovereign outlook to Negative, or downgrade France's long-term sovereign rating, between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13?
subquestions.background_information:
A further France sovereign downgrade by another major agency in late 2025 is more likely if agencies continue to signal worsening fiscal and political risks in the near term. Moody's is one of the three major agencies relevant to the ultimate question. Reuters reported on 2025-09-05 that France was entering a series of sovereign rating reviews by Moody's, Fitch, and S&P, amid political turmoil and concern that a failed confidence vote and weak fiscal consolidation could increase downgrade risk: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3821092 .

AFP reported on 2025-09-12 that Fitch downgraded France's sovereign rating from AA- to A+, citing political instability and strained public finances, and noted debt projected to rise to 121% of GDP by 2027 from 113.2% in 2024. The same report said France's 2024 budget deficit was 5.8% of GDP, well above euro-area reference levels, and that the downgrade reflected weakened capacity to deliver fiscal consolidation: https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-0f8a3f0e . Another AFP summary the same day likewise emphasized France's 5.8% deficit, debt near 113% of GDP, and market concern over fiscal credibility: https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250912-france-risks-credit-downgrade-as-new-pm-tackles-budget .

Moody's outlook actions are informative because they often precede or substitute for near-term rating actions when an agency wants to signal elevated downgrade risk without immediately cutting the rating. If Moody's shifts France's outlook to Negative, or cuts the rating itself, that would be a concrete signal that near-term fundamentals are deteriorating enough to make an additional 2025 downgrade by a major agency more plausible.

Sources:
Reuters / Investing.com - France faces sovereign rating test amid political chaos: https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3821092
Barron's / AFP - Fitch downgrades France's credit rating in new debt blow: https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-0f8a3f0e
France 24 / AFP - France risks credit downgrade as new PM tackles budget: https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250912-france-risks-credit-downgrade-as-new-pm-tackles-budget
Moody's sovereign ratings homepage: https://ratings.moodys.com/sovereigns
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 (inclusive), Moody's publicly announces either: (a) a downgrade of France's long-term sovereign issuer/senior unsecured rating, or (b) a change in France's sovereign outlook to Negative from any non-Negative outlook. It resolves No if no such Moody's action is publicly announced during that window.

Primary resolution source: official Moody's Ratings announcements or sovereign ratings pages for France at https://ratings.moodys.com/sovereigns and any related Moody's press release or rating action notice published on https://www.moodys.com/ .

Fallback sources: a consensus of credible financial reporting clearly attributing the action to Moody's, such as Reuters, Bloomberg, AFP, or major financial newspapers, if Moody's content is paywalled or later removed. Example fallback source relevant to the topic: Reuters coverage via Investing.com at https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/france-faces-sovereign-rating-test-amid-political-chaos-3821092 .

Only actions first publicly disclosed during the window from 2025-09-13 through 2025-10-13 count. Announcements before 2025-09-13 do not count, even if markets react during the window. Announcements after 2025-10-13 do not count. If Moody's places France on review/watch but does not change the outlook to Negative and does not downgrade the rating during the window, that alone does not count for Yes. If no authoritative source can determine whether a qualifying Moody's action occurred in the window, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A negative outlook or downgrade from Moody's would be a strong near-term indicator that France's fiscal and political trajectory is worsening in the eyes of a major agency, increasing the likelihood that another major agency downgrades France by year-end.

question: Will Donald Trump visit North Korea in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits North Korea between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or South Korea's presidential office officially announce between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 that Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un are expected to meet in 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A formal announcement that Trump and Kim are expected to meet in 2025 would be a strong leading indicator for a possible Trump visit to North Korea later in the year, because arranging such a summit would usually require advance diplomatic agreement and public signaling. Recent reporting suggests there is some momentum but also substantial uncertainty. On August 26, 2025, Trump said he hoped to meet Kim Jong Un later in 2025 and said he had a "very good relationship" with Kim, according to reporting summarizing his White House remarks: https://www.latestly.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-says-he-hopes-to-meet-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-in-2025-7080638.html . Reuters-republished reporting on August 26 said South Korean President Lee Jae Myung proposed that if Trump visits South Korea for a regional forum, a meeting with Kim could be arranged later this year: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/South-Korea-s-Lee-proposes-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Korea-Kim-later-this-year-Lee-s-offi-50937129/ .

At the same time, there are reasons to doubt near-term progress. South Korea's national security adviser said on August 29 that North Korea had been "inactive in engaging in diplomacy with South Korea or the United States" and had "not shown willingness to engage in talks": https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10556864 . That makes any official announcement of an expected 2025 Trump-Kim meeting especially informative: it would signal that a key diplomatic barrier had been overcome.

This subquestion is not a restatement of whether Trump visits North Korea. Trump and Kim could be officially expected to meet in 2025 without the venue being North Korea, but such an announcement would materially increase the odds of a visit, especially because Trump's prior Kim diplomacy has included unusual venue choices and direct leader-level engagement.

Sources:
LatestLY - US President Donald Trump Says He Hopes To Meet North Korean Leader Kim Jong Un in 2025: https://www.latestly.com/world/us-president-donald-trump-says-he-hopes-to-meet-north-korean-leader-kim-jong-un-in-2025-7080638.html
MarketScreener / Reuters - South Korea's Lee proposes meeting between Trump and North Korea Kim later this year: https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/South-Korea-s-Lee-proposes-meeting-between-Trump-and-North-Korea-Kim-later-this-year-Lee-s-offi-50937129/
The Korea Herald - N. Korea appears to be inactive in engaging in diplomacy with S. Korea or US: security adviser: https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10556864
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), an official public statement from either (a) the White House / U.S. government or (b) the South Korean presidential office explicitly states that Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un are expected, planned, scheduled, agreed in principle, or likely to meet in calendar year 2025.

Qualifying examples include official press releases, briefing transcripts, pool reports, or official spokesperson statements published on WhiteHouse.gov (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), the U.S. State Department site (https://www.state.gov/), or the Republic of Korea presidential office site (https://www.president.go.kr/ or any official successor domain), provided the statement clearly indicates an expected 2025 Trump-Kim meeting.

The question also resolves Yes if Trump states via an official/verified presidential or personal account that he and Kim will meet in 2025, but only if that statement is subsequently reported or archived by an authoritative source such as the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or a consensus of Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and AP (https://apnews.com/).

The question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is made between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

Important clarifications:
- The announcement need not specify the venue; it only needs to say that a Trump-Kim meeting is expected in 2025.
- Statements merely expressing hope or desire to meet, without indicating an expected/planned/agreed meeting, do not count.
- Statements from unnamed officials reported only as anonymous sourcing do not count unless later confirmed in an official public statement within the resolution window.
- If an announcement is made within the window and later canceled, the question still resolves Yes.
- If the relevant official websites become unavailable, the fallback sources will be Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and AP (https://apnews.com/) quoting or reproducing the official statement.
- If there is no clear official statement and only ambiguous media speculation, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly announced expected Trump-Kim meeting would be a major precursor to any Trump visit to North Korea. It captures whether diplomatic channels have opened enough to support leader-level engagement, without simply asking whether the visit itself happens by an earlier date.

question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla obtain a California DMV Autonomous Vehicle Testing Permit or Deployment Permit for driverless vehicles between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for Tesla launching unsupervised FSD is regulatory authorization in major jurisdictions. California is especially relevant because Tesla is already operating a Bay Area ride-hailing service there, but reporting before 2025-09-01 indicates that service uses human drivers and that Tesla had not yet secured the permits needed for autonomous vehicle operations. Electrek reported on 2025-07-31 that Tesla's Bay Area service was powered by human drivers and that Tesla had not applied for the required California autonomous vehicle permits at that time: https://electrek.co/2025/07/31/tesla-robotaxis-are-officially-powered-by-human-drivers-as-it-launches-ride-hailing-in-bay-area/ . Breitbart similarly reported on 2025-07-29 that Tesla was awaiting regulatory approval for autonomous robotaxis in additional markets, and that California rules required an initial pilot phase: https://www.breitbart.com/tech/2025/07/29/not-so-robo-elon-musk-introduces-tesla-taxi-service-with-human-drivers-in-san-francisco/ .

In California, the DMV regulates autonomous vehicle testing and deployment permits, including driverless testing and driverless deployment. Public permit-holder lists are published by the California DMV here: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/ . Separately, the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) regulates passenger service aspects of autonomous ride-hailing and charter-party operations, with information published here: https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs . Because the ultimate question requires broad public availability of unsupervised FSD, movement by Tesla to obtain a California driverless AV permit would be strong evidence that Tesla is progressing beyond supervised driver-assist and toward legally deployable unsupervised operation.

As of 2025-09-01, public reporting suggests Tesla is still at a supervised stage in California, making any newly granted California driverless permit during September 2025 a meaningful early indicator rather than a foregone conclusion.

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the White House, U.S. State Department, or U.S. Department of Defense publicly announce between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 that the United States has agreed in principle to provide a military "backstop" for a European or multinational post-ceasefire security force in Ukraine?
subquestions.background_information:
A key live issue in late 2025 is whether Washington will provide the enabling commitment that European governments say is necessary for any credible Ukraine security architecture. Multiple reports before 2025-10-31 indicate that European-led security guarantees for Ukraine are being actively discussed, but that these plans are stalled without a U.S. role. CBC reported on 2025-09-04 that roughly 30 Western leaders discussed guarantees for Kyiv and that participants agreed any European military role would require U.S. security guarantees as a "back-stop," which President Trump had not yet formalized as of that date (https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-security-guarantees-us-help-1.7320010). Foreign Policy similarly reported on 2025-09-04 that 26 countries had committed to a postwar reassurance force for Ukraine, while Trump was described as open to security guarantees but not U.S. ground troops, instead potentially considering air support (https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/09/04/ukraine-europe-troops-security-guarantees-trump-macron-starmer/). 

Ukrainska Pravda reported on 2025-08-22 that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Andrii Yermak discussed security guarantees, with working groups developing both political-legal and military components; the article says a U.S. "backstop mechanism" with air cover was specifically being worked out (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/22/7512345/). The G7 foreign ministers also said on 2025-09-24 that they would work with the United States to provide Ukraine with "robust and credible security guarantees" (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/g7-vows-continued-support-for-ukraine-calls-for-gaza-ceasefire/3301122). 

This makes a formal U.S. announcement of a "backstop" highly relevant: it would not itself necessarily equal the ultimate Article 5-style binding security guarantee, but it would be a concrete observable step toward one. It would signal that the Trump administration is willing to move from vague support to an operational security role tied to Ukraine's defense. By contrast, if no such announcement occurs even during an active negotiation period, that is evidence against the ultimate question resolving Yes by year-end.

Sources:
CBC News - Ukraine's allies discuss security guarantees, but say U.S. must help enforce any peace deal - https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-security-guarantees-us-help-1.7320010
Foreign Policy - 26 Countries Commit to Deploying Troops to Ukraine Postwar - https://foreignpolicy.com/2025/09/04/ukraine-europe-troops-security-guarantees-trump-macron-starmer/
Ukrainska Pravda - US secretary of state and chief of Zelenskyy's office discuss security guarantees, draft expected next week - https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/08/22/7512345/
Anadolu Ajansı - G7 vows continued support for Ukraine, calls for Gaza ceasefire - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/g7-vows-continued-support-for-ukraine-calls-for-gaza-ceasefire/3301122
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), at least one of the following official U.S. government sources publicly states that the United States has agreed in principle to provide a military "backstop" for a European, allied, coalition, or multinational post-ceasefire/postwar security force or guarantee arrangement in Ukraine: (a) a White House statement, transcript, fact sheet, executive order, or readout published at https://www.whitehouse.gov/; (b) a U.S. Department of State statement, briefing, readout, or transcript published at https://www.state.gov/; or (c) a U.S. Department of Defense release, transcript, or readout published at https://www.defense.gov/.

For Yes, the announcement must explicitly describe a U.S. role as a "backstop" or use closely equivalent language indicating the United States would provide military support to underwrite or enforce a European/allied security presence for Ukraine, such as air cover, air/missile defense, strike support, rapid military response, or other direct military enabling commitments in the event of renewed attack. Mere references to consultations, planning, arms sales, training, intelligence sharing, economic support, sanctions snapback, or generic support for "security guarantees" without an announced U.S. military backstop do not qualify.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying official announcement is published between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

If there is only unconfirmed media reporting and no qualifying official U.S. government publication in the window, resolve No. If an announcement is made within the window but explicitly says discussions are ongoing and no agreement in principle has yet been reached, resolve No. If relevant official pages are unavailable at resolution time, archived versions at https://archive.org/ may be used as a fallback, together with corroboration from Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) or AP News (https://apnews.com/).

Primary sources for resolution:
White House - https://www.whitehouse.gov/
U.S. Department of State - https://www.state.gov/
U.S. Department of Defense - https://www.defense.gov/
Fallback sources:
Internet Archive - https://archive.org/
Reuters - https://www.reuters.com/
AP News - https://apnews.com/
subquestions.rationale: A publicly announced U.S. military backstop for a European-led Ukraine security arrangement would be a strong leading indicator that the administration is moving toward a more formal security commitment. It is not the same as the ultimate question, because a backstop announcement could fall short of a binding U.S. defense guarantee; however, it would materially raise the odds that such a guarantee is concluded by the end of 2025.

question: Somalians who defrauded government to fund terrorists deported?
description:
On September 18, 2025, Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson announced that eight Minneapolis defendants were indicted for defrauding Minnesota’s housing stabilization program. It is rumored that some of these funds were used to fund the Somalian terrorist group Al-Shabaab. You can read more about that here: https://www.city-journal.org/article/minnesota-welfare-fraud-somalia-al-shabaab?.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any of the Minnesota defendants who were indicted for fraud in this case are officially deported from the United States by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Deportation is defined as the formal removal of any of the indicted persons from the US by government authorities due to legal or administrative reasons. Voluntary departure, extradition, or relocation without an official deportation order will not count.

The resolution source will be credible reporting from major news outlets or official government statements.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or the Department of Justice (DOJ) publicly announce between 2025-12-22 and 2026-01-21 that at least one of the eight defendants indicted in the Minnesota Housing Stabilization Services fraud case has been placed in immigration detention or has been served with a Notice to Appear in removal proceedings?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term driver of whether any indicted defendant is deported by late February 2026 is whether federal immigration authorities take formal immigration-enforcement steps against a named defendant well before that deadline. Public evidence that a defendant has been placed in ICE custody or formally put into removal proceedings would strongly increase the odds of eventual deportation.

The ultimate question concerns eight Minneapolis-area defendants indicted in September 2025 in a Minnesota Housing Stabilization Services fraud case announced by Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson. The supplied background states that these indictments were announced on September 18, 2025, and that this was described as an early round of HSS prosecutions. The allegations have become politically salient because Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Treasury is investigating whether Minnesota welfare funds may have reached al-Shabaab, although CBS also reported that multiple federal investigators said there was no evidence of such a connection as of early December 2025. See CBS coverage at https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/minnesota-fraud-allegations-trump-walz/ and https://www.cbsnews.com/news/treasury-investigating-whether-minnesota-welfare-money-went-to-somali-terror-group-al-shabaab-bessent-says/ .

Also relevant, CBS reported on December 2, 2025 that Treasury had opened an investigation into whether Minnesota welfare money reached al-Shabaab: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/treasury-investigating-whether-minnesota-welfare-money-went-to-somali-terror-group-al-shabaab-bessent-says/ . Separately, ICE has recently been active in Minneapolis: the user-provided news summary cites a December 2, 2025 Daily Wire report claiming ICE sent more than 100 agents to Minneapolis targeting Somali nationals with deportation orders. While that outlet is not ideal as a resolution source, it suggests heightened immigration-enforcement attention in the relevant geography and community.

In immigration practice, deportation usually requires identifiable earlier steps such as arrest/detention by ICE or initiation of removal proceedings via a Notice to Appear. Because the ultimate question resolves on actual deportation by 2026-02-28, this subquestion asks about an earlier, different observable event rather than deportation itself.

Sources:

DHS News - https://www.dhs.gov/news

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-22 and 2026-01-21 (inclusive), an official public statement by ICE, DHS, DOJ, the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR), or a credible major news outlet citing named government officials reports that at least one of the eight defendants indicted in the September 2025 Minnesota Housing Stabilization Services fraud case has either: (a) been taken into ICE or other immigration detention, or (b) been served with a Notice to Appear / otherwise formally placed into U.S. removal proceedings.

This question resolves No if no such public announcement or report appears during the period from 2025-12-22 through 2026-01-21 inclusive.

For Yes, the person must be identifiable as one of the eight defendants from the referenced indictment; generic references to "Somali suspects" or "fraud defendants" without sufficient identification do not count. Mere political calls for deportation, reports of visa review, revocation of TPS generally, criminal arrest without immigration action, or speculation that removal is being considered do not count.

Primary resolution sources: official releases from ICE https://www.ice.gov/newsroom , DHS https://www.dhs.gov/news , DOJ / U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Minnesota https://www.justice.gov/usao-mn/pr , and EOIR announcements or case-status materials if publicly available https://www.justice.gov/eoir . Secondary sources: major outlets such as CBS News, AP, Reuters, or major Minnesota newspapers quoting identifiable officials. If reports conflict, official agency statements take precedence. If no sufficiently specific public information is available by 2026-01-21, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Formal immigration detention or initiation of removal proceedings is a strong leading indicator for eventual deportation by the ultimate market deadline. It is not a restatement of deportation itself, but an earlier process milestone that would meaningfully update forecasts.

question: Isar Aerospace successful orbital launch in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any launch attempt of the Spectrum rocket, developed by Isar Aerospace, results in a payload reaching a stable Earth orbit by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

"Reaching stable orbit" is defined as the successful insertion of a payload into a sustained low Earth orbit (LEO) or higher, where the payload completes at least one full revolution around Earth.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Isar Aerospace or Andøya Spaceport publicly announce, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, a specific calendar date for Spectrum's next launch attempt that falls on or before 2025-12-31?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for whether Isar Aerospace will achieve an orbital launch success in 2025, because a public commitment to a dated launch attempt by late November would suggest the vehicle, range, licensing, and operations campaign are far enough along to support a December mission. Isar's first Spectrum test flight launched from Andøya Spaceport in March 2025 and failed shortly after liftoff, though the company described the test as valuable and has said subsequent vehicles are in production. Reporting in June 2025 stated that Spectrum vehicles 2 and 3 were already in production, indicating that follow-on flight hardware exists or is being readied: https://thenextweb.com/news/isar-aerospace-raises-150mn-to-strengthen-europes-launch-capabilities .

ESA and the European Commission announced on 2025-09-01 that two Flight Ticket Initiative missions are secured on Isar Aerospace's Spectrum launcher from Andøya Spaceport, showing that institutional customers expect future Spectrum launches and that payload demand exists: https://www.esa.int/Applications/Telecommunications_Integrated_Applications/First_five_Flight_Ticket_Initiative_missions_confirmed_with_Avio_and_Isar_Aerospace .

Andøya Spaceport hosted Spectrum's debut and presents itself as the operational launch site for orbital launches from mainland Europe, so public scheduling signals from either Isar or Andøya would be highly relevant to near-term launch readiness: https://andoyaspace.no/spaceport/ .

A dated public launch announcement by late November is not the same as achieving orbit, but it is a concrete operational milestone. If no such dated announcement appears by then, that would be evidence against a successful orbital launch before year-end, because only one month would remain in 2025 for countdown, weather, range coordination, and any needed recycling after delays.

Sources:
The Next Web - Isar Aerospace raises €150mn to strengthen Europe's launch capabilities - https://thenextweb.com/news/isar-aerospace-raises-150mn-to-strengthen-europes-launch-capabilities
ESA - First five Flight Ticket Initiative missions confirmed with Avio and Isar Aerospace - https://www.esa.int/Applications/Telecommunications_Integrated_Applications/First_five_Flight_Ticket_Initiative_missions_confirmed_with_Avio_and_Isar_Aerospace
Andøya Spaceport - https://andoyaspace.no/spaceport/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive, either Isar Aerospace or Andøya Spaceport publicly announces a specific calendar date for Spectrum's next launch attempt, and the announced launch date is on or before 2025-12-31.

For this question, a "specific calendar date" means a dated target such as "December 18, 2025" or "2025-12-18." Statements such as "in December," "Q4," "before year-end," "late 2025," or announcement of only a launch window without at least one named calendar date do not count.

Eligible announcement sources are limited to:
1. Isar Aerospace's official website newsroom or blog: https://www.isaraerospace.com/ or pages therefrom.
2. Isar Aerospace official social media accounts (for example its official X or LinkedIn account) if the post is publicly accessible.
3. Andøya Spaceport's official website/news pages: https://andoyaspace.no/spaceport/ or pages therefrom.
4. Andøya Space official social media accounts if publicly accessible.

The announcement must clearly refer to Spectrum / Isar Aerospace's next launch attempt, not merely a customer mission booked on Spectrum at some unspecified future time.

If multiple announcements occur in the window, any one qualifying announcement is sufficient for Yes.

This question resolves No if no qualifying public announcement appears between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 inclusive.

If a qualifying announcement is made in the window and is later postponed, the question still resolves Yes, because the criterion is the public announcement of a specific date within the stated window, not whether the launch occurs on that date.

Primary resolution sources: official Isar Aerospace and Andøya Spaceport channels listed above. Secondary confirmation may use reputable spaceflight reporting only to verify timestamps or wording if an official post is deleted, including SpaceNews https://spacenews.com/ , European Spaceflight https://europeanspaceflight.com/ , or Space.com https://www.space.com/ . In case of conflict, archived copies of the official announcement (for example via https://archive.org/web/ ) take precedence.
subquestions.rationale: A publicly dated launch attempt announcement is a strong near-term operational signal that Spectrum's hardware, regulatory approvals, launch site coordination, and mission planning are sufficiently advanced to make a 2025 orbital success plausible. It provides more decision-relevant evidence than generic optimism or long-term contracts, while remaining distinct from the ultimate question itself.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q4 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:

Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index present situation component be at least 140.0 in the January 2026 release?
subquestions.background_information:
Consumer spending is a major driver of U.S. GDP, so near-term readings on household confidence are a useful indicator for whether Q4 2025 growth is likely to land in a moderate positive range such as 2.0%–2.5%. The provided news notes that Q3 2025 GDP growth was strong at 4.3% annualized and was powered by domestic consumption, but also that consumer sentiment/confidence had weakened late in 2025, with the Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index falling and remaining well below its earlier 2025 peak. If households still report a strong assessment of current business and labor-market conditions in January 2026, that would be evidence that consumption likely held up through late Q4 rather than slowing sharply. The Conference Board publishes both an overall Consumer Confidence Index and a Present Situation Index; the latter is especially relevant for contemporaneous spending conditions. The Conference Board's consumer confidence release page is here: https://www.conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence. Historical releases and data tables are posted on that site, and major financial data aggregators such as FRED also track related confidence series: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/. The Q3 GDP context comes from the BEA release page and contemporaneous reporting that Q3 real GDP rose 4.3% annualized after shutdown-related delays: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product and https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/us-economy-grew-much-faster-than-expected-third-quarter-delayed-report-shows. The NBC New York summary also notes that consumer confidence had recently declined, making the January reading informative rather than trivial: https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/business/money-report/spending-helped-drive-4-3-economic-growth-in-third-quarter-delayed-gdp-report-shows/6348823/.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Conference Board data/download portal root — https://www.conference-board.org/

subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is about whether Q4 2025 GDP growth lands in a fairly narrow moderate-growth band. Consumer spending is the largest GDP component, and a strong January read on households' assessment of present conditions is an informative cross-check on whether spending likely remained solid through late Q4. This is not a restatement of GDP itself; it is a distinct, timely indicator tied to the main demand engine behind recent growth.

question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
