subquestions.question: Will the UN Security Council adopt, between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 inclusive, a resolution that explicitly authorizes or endorses deployment of a multinational or international security/stabilization/peacekeeping force inside Gaza?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for foreign intervention in Gaza appears to be the creation of a formal legal-political framework. On 2025-10-14, Germany's foreign minister said talks were underway with Russia and China on a UN Security Council resolution backing Trump's Gaza plan, and specifically said such a legal framework was essential for deploying a multinational International Stabilization Force in Gaza. This directly links UNSC action to the plausibility of an eventual on-the-ground foreign security deployment in Gaza. See Anadolu Ajansı, 2025-10-14: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3718011

Recent reporting also suggests that post-ceasefire plans already contemplate an international force for Gaza, but that consensus is incomplete. Asia Times reported on 2025-10-11 that the ceasefire's later phases could include a temporary International Stabilization Force and international civil administrators, though consensus remained pending. https://asiatimes.com/2025/10/the-first-day-after-the-gaza-war/

There is also precedent for foreign actors discussing operational roles around Gaza without yet entering Gaza itself. For example, the EU announced readiness to restart its civilian mission monitoring the Rafah crossing, part of broader ceasefire support, but this is border-focused and not necessarily equivalent to a foreign security operation on the ground within Gaza as defined by the ultimate question. Anadolu Ajansı, 2025-10-13: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-vows-to-restart-civilian-mission-to-monitor-border-crossing-between-gaza-egypt/3717229

This makes a UNSC resolution an informative crux: if passed, it would strongly increase the odds of an officially acknowledged foreign ground operation in Gaza by year-end; if it fails or stalls, prospects for such intervention likely fall.

Sources:
Anadolu Ajansı - Germany says talks underway for UN Security Council resolution on Trump's Gaza plan - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/germany-says-talks-underway-for-un-security-council-resolution-on-trumps-gaza-plan/3718011
Asia Times - The first day after the Gaza war - https://asiatimes.com/2025/10/the-first-day-after-the-gaza-war/
Anadolu Ajansı - EU vows to restart civilian mission to monitor border crossing between Gaza, Egypt - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-vows-to-restart-civilian-mission-to-monitor-border-crossing-between-gaza-egypt/3717229
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 inclusive, the UN Security Council adopts a resolution that explicitly authorizes, endorses, approves, welcomes, or establishes deployment of a multinational, international, UN, or similar security / stabilization / peacekeeping force inside the Gaza Strip.

For Yes, the adopted resolution must do more than call generally for peace or humanitarian aid; it must explicitly refer to deployment of foreign or international personnel in a security, policing, monitoring, stabilization, peacekeeping, escort, protection, or similar operational role in Gaza itself.

This question resolves No if no such UNSC resolution is adopted by 2025-11-15 23:59:59 UTC.

Resolution will primarily rely on the official UN Security Council resolutions database and meeting records:
- UN Security Council resolutions search / documents: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions
- UN Digital Library Security Council documents: https://digitallibrary.un.org/

Fallback sources, if needed for timing or text confirmation, are the UN News site and official Security Council press releases:
- UN News: https://news.un.org/
- UN Security Council press statements/meetings: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/

If the Council votes on a draft but it fails, is vetoed, is postponed, or remains under negotiation without adoption during the window 2025-10-16 to 2025-11-15, the question resolves No.

If a resolution is adopted during the window but its language is ambiguous, resolution should be based on the plain text of the resolution. If the text does not explicitly connect the Council's action to deployment of an international/foreign security-type mission in Gaza, it does not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: A UNSC mandate or endorsement is one of the clearest near-term institutional prerequisites for many plausible foreign intervention scenarios in Gaza. It is not the same as the ultimate question, because it asks about a diplomatic/legal authorization step rather than troops actually beginning operations on the ground. But if it happens, it would materially raise the likelihood of qualifying foreign intervention by 2025-12-31.

question: U.S. recognizes Russian sovereignty over Crimea in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. government formally recognizes Russian sovereignty over the majority of the Crimean peninsula by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Donald Trump's March 25, 2019, recognition of Israel's sovereignty over the Golan Heights is an example of a qualifying action. 

Statement of intents, or announcements of planned recognition will not qualify. 

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of State remove or materially revise the 2018 'Crimea Declaration' from its official website between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30?
subquestions.background_information:
A meaningful early indicator of possible U.S. recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea is whether the U.S. government first backs away from its existing formal non-recognition policy. On July 25, 2018, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo issued the 'Crimea Declaration,' stating that 'the United States rejects Russia's attempted annexation of Crimea and pledges to maintain this policy until Ukraine's territorial integrity is restored.' The declaration explicitly analogized U.S. policy to the Welles Declaration on non-recognition of Soviet annexation of the Baltics. This is a standing official statement of U.S. policy and therefore a natural precursor document to watch for any reversal or softening. State Department archive: https://2017-2021.state.gov/crimea-declaration/ and current State archive copy: https://2009-2017.state.gov/r/pa/prs/ps/2018/07/284005.htm

Recent reporting indicates the issue remains live inside U.S. policy debate. The Hill reported on May 31, 2025 that former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo warned against recognizing Russian control over Crimea and specifically referenced the 2018 Crimea Declaration as the policy that should be maintained, implying that recognition had been considered by the Trump administration in 2025. https://thehill.com/policy/international/5328230-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/

The ultimate market requires formal U.S. recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea by the end of 2025. Such recognition would be much easier politically and bureaucratically if the administration first removed, superseded, or materially diluted the most prominent official U.S. non-recognition statement. Conversely, leaving the declaration untouched through November would be some evidence against near-term recognition.

Sources:
U.S. Department of State (2018 Crimea Declaration): https://2017-2021.state.gov/crimea-declaration/
U.S. Department of State archive copy: https://2009-2017.state.gov/r/pa/prs/ps/2018/07/284005.htm
The Hill - Pompeo warns against US recognizing Russian control over Crimea: https://thehill.com/policy/international/5328230-pompeo-warns-against-us-recognizing-russian-control-over-crimea/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), the U.S. Department of State's official website either (a) removes public access to the 2018 'Crimea Declaration' page without an equivalent replacement affirming non-recognition, or (b) publishes an official replacement, update, notice, or edited version that materially revises or repudiates the declaration's core non-recognition policy toward Crimea.

For purposes of this question, 'materially revise or repudiate' means an official State Department webpage or document stating, in substance, at least one of the following: that the United States no longer rejects Russia's annexation/sovereignty claim over Crimea; that the 2018 declaration is superseded or no longer reflects U.S. policy; or that the United States recognizes, accepts, or is prepared to treat Crimea as Russian sovereign territory. Mere website redesign, relocation to a new URL, archival migration, temporary outage, or changes to formatting/navigation do NOT qualify if the declaration remains publicly accessible or is replaced by substantially similar non-recognition language.

This question resolves No if no such qualifying removal or material revision occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30.

Primary sources for resolution:
- Current/archived State Department Crimea Declaration pages: https://2017-2021.state.gov/crimea-declaration/ and https://2009-2017.state.gov/r/pa/prs/ps/2018/07/284005.htm
- U.S. Department of State official site search / press statements: https://www.state.gov/ and https://www.state.gov/press-releases/

Fallback evidence if the webpage structure changes:
- Internet Archive Wayback Machine snapshots of the relevant State Department pages: https://web.archive.org/
- Official State Department X account for policy statements: https://x.com/StateDept

If the evidence is mixed, the resolution should follow the clearest official State Department publication issued within the window. If no authoritative official publication can establish a qualifying policy change within the window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: Formal recognition of Russian sovereignty over Crimea would likely require first undoing or superseding the U.S.'s existing formal non-recognition commitment. A public rollback of the 2018 Crimea Declaration is therefore a concrete, observable precursor that would strongly increase the odds of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

question: Will EJ Antoni be confirmed as BLS Commissioner in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if E.J. Antoni is confirmed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If Antoni’s nomination is formally withdrawn, or if the Senate rejects their nomination, this market will immediately resolve to “No”.

The Senate must confirm this nominee for this market to resolve to "Yes". Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information from the U.S. Senate (see: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/NominationsRejectedorWithdrawn.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Senate HELP Committee hold a nomination hearing for E.J. Antoni to be Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-28?
subquestions.background_information:
A committee hearing is a meaningful near-term indicator for whether a nominee is on track for Senate confirmation, because most executive-branch nominees need to receive committee consideration before a floor vote. The Bureau of Labor Statistics sits within the Department of Labor, and labor-related nominations are typically handled by the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), whose nominations page and hearing schedule publicly track such activity: https://www.help.senate.gov/hearings and https://www.help.senate.gov/nominations.

E.J. Antoni was nominated in mid-August 2025 after President Trump fired BLS Commissioner Erika McEntarfer. News reports before 2025-09-01 describe the nomination as controversial, with Senate Democrats publicly opposing Antoni and questioning his qualifications and views on BLS data releases. See Newsday (2025-08-16): https://www.newsday.com/business/trump-firing-data-chief-pressure-economic-numbers-upward-b6r2h8k7 and The Hill (2025-08-17): https://thehill.com/. Reporting also notes the Senate partisan balance is 53 Republicans to 47 Democrats, which makes committee and floor scheduling decisions especially relevant to Antoni’s prospects: https://coloradonewsline.com/2025/08/16/trump-taps-economist-from-far-right-foundation-to-head-agency-that-tracks-jobs-numbers/.

As of 2025-09-01, the key observable bottleneck is whether Antoni’s nomination advances into the formal Senate process via a HELP Committee hearing. A hearing by late September would be a strong signal that the White House and Senate leadership intend to move the nomination quickly; the absence of a hearing by then would be evidence of delay, resistance, or low prioritization.

Sources:
Senate HELP Committee Hearings: https://www.help.senate.gov/hearings
Senate HELP Committee Nominations: https://www.help.senate.gov/nominations
Newsday article on Antoni nomination controversy: https://www.newsday.com/business/trump-firing-data-chief-pressure-economic-numbers-upward-b6r2h8k7
Colorado Newsline article noting Senate balance and nomination context: https://coloradonewsline.com/2025/08/16/trump-taps-economist-from-far-right-foundation-to-head-agency-that-tracks-jobs-numbers/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) holds a public nomination hearing that includes E.J. Antoni’s nomination to be Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-28, inclusive.

This question resolves No if no such hearing is held during that window.

For purposes of resolution, a qualifying hearing must be publicly listed by the HELP Committee or otherwise documented in an official Senate source as a hearing at which Antoni’s nomination is considered. A business meeting, executive session, or committee vote without a hearing does not count. A hearing that is scheduled during the window but postponed beyond 2025-09-28 does not count and the question resolves No.

Primary resolution sources:
1. Senate HELP Committee hearings page: https://www.help.senate.gov/hearings
2. Senate HELP Committee nominations page: https://www.help.senate.gov/nominations
3. Congress.gov nomination page for E.J. Antoni, if available: https://www.congress.gov/

Fallback: if the HELP website is unavailable or incomplete, use the official Senate committee calendar, official hearing video/archive pages, or the Congressional Record. If official Senate sources are internally inconsistent, the earliest official publication clearly showing whether a hearing occurred within the 2025-09-01 to 2025-09-28 window will control.

Resolution date: 2025-09-28.
subquestions.rationale: A HELP Committee hearing is a concrete procedural milestone that is strongly correlated with eventual confirmation but is not merely the ultimate question with an earlier deadline. It captures whether Senate leadership is willing to spend scarce time advancing Antoni despite controversy. If forecasters disagree on confirmation, they are likely to update substantially based on whether a hearing happens by late September.

question: TikTok sale announced in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if ByteDance announces their intention to sell TikTok by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A public announcement of the intention to sell TikTok will qualify even if a sale has not been finalized. This includes any formal declaration made by ByteDance or its authorized representatives regarding their plans to sell or transfer ownership of TikTok.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from ByteDance. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will ByteDance or TikTok publicly state between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 (inclusive) that they are engaged in negotiations, discussions, or a proposed transaction to divest, sell, or transfer ownership of TikTok's U.S. operations?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator for whether ByteDance will later announce an intention to sell TikTok by the end of 2025. The ultimate question is specifically about ByteDance announcing an intention to sell TikTok. A narrower but distinct precursor is whether ByteDance or TikTok publicly acknowledges active negotiations or a proposed transaction concerning TikTok's U.S. operations before the current U.S. deadline.

As of mid-2025, the U.S. government had extended the deadline for ByteDance to divest TikTok's U.S. assets to September 17, 2025. Reuters reported that President Trump signed an executive order extending the enforcement deadline by 90 days, to September 17, 2025, while the White House said the administration wanted a deal that protects U.S. national security and keeps TikTok operating in the U.S. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-extend-deadline-bytedance-divest-tiktok-wsj-reports-2025-06-17/

There were also substantial public claims from President Trump that a buyer group existed. Reuters reported on June 29, 2025 that Trump said he had found a buyer for TikTok, describing it as a group of 'very wealthy people,' while noting the deal would likely need China's approval. https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-says-he-has-found-buyer-tiktok-2025-06-29/

However, the ultimate market resolves based on ByteDance announcing its intention to sell, not on statements by Trump or unnamed prospective buyers. That makes public acknowledgement from ByteDance or TikTok of negotiations or a proposed divestiture a meaningful crux: if ByteDance begins confirming talks or a proposed structure, that would be strong evidence that a later formal sale-intention announcement is more likely. Conversely, continued silence or denials from ByteDance close to the September 17 deadline would be evidence against the ultimate outcome.

This subquestion is not merely the main question with an earlier date. It asks about a different observable event: whether ByteDance or TikTok publicly acknowledges negotiations or a proposed divestiture process, which is often a precursor to a formal announcement of intent to sell.

Sources:
Reuters: Trump to extend deadline for ByteDance to divest TikTok to Sept. 17 https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-extend-deadline-bytedance-divest-tiktok-wsj-reports-2025-06-17/
Reuters: Trump says he has found buyer for TikTok https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-says-he-has-found-buyer-tiktok-2025-06-29/
U.S. Supreme Court case materials / background on the divest-or-ban law (general legal context) https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/24pdf/24a587_3f14.pdf
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 inclusive, ByteDance Ltd., TikTok, or an explicitly authorized representative of either company publicly states that they are engaged in negotiations, discussions, talks, or a proposed transaction to divest, sell, spin off, transfer ownership of, or otherwise separate TikTok's U.S. operations from ByteDance ownership.

Qualifying statements must be public and attributable to one of the following:
1. An official ByteDance or TikTok press release or newsroom post;
2. An official company social media account;
3. A named company spokesperson quoted by a credible news outlet;
4. A filing, court submission, or other official document issued by the company.

Examples of qualifying language include statements such as: 'we are in talks regarding a sale,' 'we are evaluating a divestiture proposal,' 'a transaction is under discussion,' or 'ownership transfer of U.S. operations is being negotiated.'

This question resolves No if no such qualifying public statement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-17 inclusive.

Statements by third parties alone (for example, the U.S. President, unnamed sources, potential buyers, or media speculation) do not count unless they are accompanied by an attributable public statement from ByteDance, TikTok, or an authorized representative. A flat denial of negotiations does not count as Yes. Ambiguous statements that mention 'compliance discussions' or 'regulatory engagement' without indicating negotiations or a proposed transaction to divest/sell/transfer ownership do not count.

Primary sources for resolution will be official ByteDance and TikTok communications:
- ByteDance newsroom or official site: https://www.bytedance.com/en/
- TikTok newsroom: https://newsroom.tiktok.com/
- TikTok official X account: https://x.com/TikTok

Secondary resolution sources, if needed, will be credible reporting that quotes named company representatives, such as:
- Reuters https://www.reuters.com/
- AP News https://apnews.com/
- The Wall Street Journal https://www.wsj.com/

If no authoritative public evidence is available by the end date, the question resolves No. If relevant company statements are issued within the window but become inaccessible later, archived versions or reproductions in Reuters/AP/WSJ quoting the statement may be used. If an event is only rumored within the window and not publicly acknowledged by the company until after 2025-09-17, it does not count.
subquestions.rationale: A public acknowledgement by ByteDance or TikTok that sale-related negotiations are underway would be a strong leading indicator that ByteDance may later announce an intention to sell TikTok. It is distinct from the ultimate question because it focuses on an earlier precursor signal—admitted deal talks or a proposed transaction structure—rather than a formal sale-intention announcement itself.

question: Trump meets Xi, Putin, and Kim by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Kim Jong Un all meet with Donald Trump between October 24, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both the listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will credible reporting by 2025-11-02 state that Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea?
subquestions.background_information:
A Trump–Xi meeting appears to be the most concrete near-term step toward the ultimate question, because the ultimate question requires Trump to meet all three leaders, and current reporting suggests Xi is the most likely of the three to meet Trump first. Multiple pre-2025-10-25 reports say Trump is traveling to Asia and has a meeting with Xi planned or seriously discussed for late October around the APEC summit in Gyeongju. AFP reported on 2025-10-24 that Trump was beginning an Asia trip and had a "pivotal meeting scheduled on October 30 in Gyeongju, South Korea, with Chinese leader Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit." https://www.barrons.com/news/trump-heads-to-asia-and-high-stakes-meeting-with-xi-5bdac5f2

Earlier reporting also described serious preparations for such a meeting. Reuters reported on 2025-09-06 that Trump and advisers were preparing for a South Korea trip and that there had been serious discussions about a bilateral Xi meeting on the sidelines of APEC, though plans were not yet final. https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-preparing-travel-south-korea-next-month-may-meet-chinas-xi-cnn-reports-2025-09-06/

The relevance is high because a confirmed Trump–Xi in-person meeting would demonstrate that at least one leg of the required trio is completed, and it would also signal that Trump’s Asia trip successfully produced leader-level diplomacy in the region. That in turn may increase the odds of opportunistic side meetings or follow-on diplomacy involving Kim Jong Un before year-end. By contrast, if the much-discussed Xi meeting fails to happen, the path to the ultimate question becomes significantly narrower. APEC itself is a plausible venue for such a meeting; the official APEC 2025 host site identifies the Republic of Korea as host of APEC 2025. https://apec2025.kr/

Sources:
Barron's/AFP, "Trump heads to Asia and high-stakes meeting with Xi" — https://www.barrons.com/news/trump-heads-to-asia-and-high-stakes-meeting-with-xi-5bdac5f2
Reuters, "Trump preparing to travel to South Korea next month, may meet China's Xi, CNN reports" — https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-preparing-travel-south-korea-next-month-may-meet-chinas-xi-cnn-reports-2025-09-06/
APEC 2025 Korea official site — https://apec2025.kr/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-02 (inclusive), there is a consensus of credible reporting that Donald Trump and Xi Jinping held an in-person bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the 2025 APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea.

For this question, an "in-person bilateral meeting" means both Trump and Xi were physically present and interacted face-to-face in a meeting described by credible sources as a meeting/talks/sit-down encounter between them. A handshake/photo-line alone does not count unless credible reporting explicitly describes it as a meeting. A phone call or video call does not count.

Primary resolution sources will be reporting from major wire services or official readouts, including Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/), AFP coverage as carried by major outlets such as Barron's (https://www.barrons.com/), the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), or China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/). If at least two of these sources clearly report that the meeting occurred within the window, resolve Yes. If by 2025-11-02 no such consensus exists, resolve No.

If reporting only says the meeting was planned, expected, canceled, postponed, or may occur after 2025-11-02, resolve No. If the reporting is irreconcilably contradictory and no consensus of credible reporting emerges, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: This is a strong early indicator because Xi is the leader with the most concretely reported near-term meeting opportunity. If Trump does not complete the Xi leg during the Asia trip, the probability of meeting all three leaders by 2025-12-31 likely falls materially.

question: EU sanctions on Israel by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union officially imposes new sanctions of any form against Israel between September 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Sanctions could include measures like tariffs, trade restrictions, financial penalties, diplomatic expulsions, travel bans, restrictions on specific individuals, or any other actions that are commonly recognized as sanctions.

Sanctions against Israeli citizens or entities which do not directly target the Israeli state or members of the Israeli government will not qualify.

The passage of an official act authorizing sanctions on Israel within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if/when the sanctions come into effect.

Only the imposition of sanctions on Israel by the EU as an entity will qualify; if individual member states of the EU apply sanctions against Israel (e.g., France imposes novel trade restrictions on Israel unilaterally), it will not be sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union; however, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the EU Foreign Affairs Council or the High Representative publicly announce, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03, a formal proposal for new EU restrictive measures specifically targeting members of the Israeli government or the Israeli state?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful early indicator because the ultimate market requires the EU as a bloc to officially impose new sanctions on Israel by the end of 2025. Before that can happen, one important observable step is whether EU institutions move from discussion and options papers to a formal public proposal for restrictive measures aimed at the Israeli government or the Israeli state. Such a proposal would not itself be the same as sanctions being imposed, but it would be a meaningful sign that the process has advanced.

As of summer 2025, reporting indicated that the EU External Action Service had prepared options that included suspension of all or part of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, targeted sanctions on Israeli ministers or military personnel, trade restrictions, an arms embargo, and suspension of scientific cooperation. Anadolu reported on 2025-07-05 that EU officials were preparing punitive options and that targeted sanctions on individuals were viewed as among the most politically feasible measures: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-prepares-sanctions-options-as-pressure-on-israel-grows/3622004

Euractiv similarly reported that an internal options paper existed and that the EU was fragmented on whether to proceed, with selective sanctions seen as more viable than broad trade steps: https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/eu-to-examine-possible-measures-against-israel-over-gaza-situation/

At the informal foreign ministers' meeting on 2025-08-30, High Representative Kaja Kallas said the EU remained divided over Gaza but also indicated that concrete measures would be proposed soon. Europa's official readout of her press remarks is a primary source for this political state of play: https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/informal-meeting-foreign-affairs-ministers-press-remarks-high-representative-kaja-kallas-after_en

Euronews reported the same day that Kallas said the options paper had already been presented, that not all member states were on board, and that Denmark and some others were exploring ways to increase pressure, including trade-related ideas concerning occupied territories: https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/08/30/eu-member-states-divided-over-gaza-at-their-copenhagen-meeting

Because the ultimate question turns on actual EU sanctions by 2025-12-31, a formal public proposal for restrictive measures against the Israeli government or state during September 2025 would be a strong near-term crux. If no such proposal materializes even after Kallas' statement that concrete measures were forthcoming, that would be evidence against the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
Anadolu Ajansı - EU prepares sanctions options as pressure on Israel grows - https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-prepares-sanctions-options-as-pressure-on-israel-grows/3622004
Euractiv - EU to examine possible measures against Israel over Gaza situation - https://www.euractiv.com/section/global-europe/news/eu-to-examine-possible-measures-against-israel-over-gaza-situation/
EEAS / Europa - Press remarks by High Representative Kaja Kallas after the informal meeting of foreign affairs ministers - https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/informal-meeting-foreign-affairs-ministers-press-remarks-high-representative-kaja-kallas-after_en
Euronews - EU Member States divided over Gaza at their Copenhagen meeting - https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2025/08/30/eu-member-states-divided-over-gaza-at-their-copenhagen-meeting
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 inclusive, either (a) the EU Foreign Affairs Council, the Council of the European Union, the European External Action Service, or the High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy publicly announces a formal proposal for new EU restrictive measures against Israel that specifically target members of the Israeli government or the Israeli state, or (b) an official EU meeting outcome document published in that window explicitly states that such a proposal has been tabled or presented.

For this question, "formal proposal" means more than a general discussion of options or political pressure. It must be described in official EU communications as a proposal, initiative, package, draft legal act, or presented restrictive-measures plan. "Restrictive measures" includes sanctions, travel bans, asset freezes, trade restrictions, suspension of agreement benefits, embargoes, or equivalent punitive EU measures. The target must be the Israeli state or members of the Israeli government; proposals aimed only at private Israeli citizens, settlers, or non-state entities do not count unless the official communication explicitly frames them as measures against Israeli government officials.

This question resolves No if no such official public proposal is announced between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 inclusive.

Primary resolution sources: official EU institutional websites, including the Council press releases and meeting conclusions (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/), EEAS statements and press remarks (https://www.eeas.europa.eu/), and the Foreign Affairs Council page/calendar if relevant (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/council-eu/configurations/fac/).

Secondary sources: if official wording is ambiguous, a consensus of at least two credible reports from major European outlets may be used to interpret whether a formal proposal was publicly announced, provided they clearly cite an EU official or document. Suitable secondary sources include Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), Euronews (https://www.euronews.com/), and Euractiv (https://www.euractiv.com/).

If an announcement occurs within the window but is later withdrawn, the question still resolves Yes because the event asked about is public announcement of a formal proposal. If reports only say that ministers discussed options, considered measures, or may propose something later, that is insufficient. If the relevant meeting is postponed beyond 2025-10-03 and no qualifying announcement occurs within the window, resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A formal EU proposal for restrictive measures is a key process milestone that would substantially increase the likelihood of actual EU sanctions on Israel by late 2025, while still being distinct from the ultimate question itself.

question: Trump eliminates capital gains tax on crypto in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to eliminate capital gains tax on any cryptocurrency assets by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If capital gains is eliminated only for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a crypto tax provision that would reduce or exempt capital gains tax on some cryptocurrency transactions be formally introduced in either chamber of Congress between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term legislative filing is a useful indicator for whether Trump could eliminate capital gains tax on crypto by the end of 2025, because statutory tax changes generally require Congress and because public introduction of bill text is a concrete sign that policymakers are trying to move such a change. There has already been visible policy momentum around crypto under Trump in 2025. Trump signed the GENIUS Act, a stablecoin framework law, in July 2025, indicating willingness to sign crypto-related legislation if it reaches his desk (reported by multiple outlets, e.g. Invezz on 2025-07-18: https://invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/ and Markets Insider on 2025-07-23: https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/currencies/coin-crcl-mstr-crypto-stocks-fall-after-trump-signs-stablecoin-bill-into-law-1034893673). Reporting in June 2025 also described a last-minute push for a de minimis crypto tax exemption in the 'One Big Beautiful Bill,' showing that crypto capital-gains relief has already been discussed legislatively, even if not enacted then (Decrypt, 2025-06-30: https://decrypt.co/327495/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption). 

As of late 2025, Congress remains the key venue for broad tax-law changes applying to US taxpayers generally. A formally introduced bill or amendment would be stronger evidence than rumors, lobbying, or speeches, because it creates public text, sponsors, and a procedural hook for committee or floor action. The relevant signal is not full enactment by October—that would be too close to the ultimate question—but whether lawmakers actually put a crypto capital-gains relief proposal into the legislative record during October. That would materially increase the odds that Trump could sign such a measure by year-end.

Potential forms of relevant tax relief discussed publicly in 2025 include a de minimis exemption for small crypto transactions, carveouts for particular crypto asset classes, or broader elimination of capital gains tax on covered crypto dispositions. Because the ultimate market resolves Yes even if only some classes of crypto become exempt, a narrower introduced provision can still be informative.

Sources:
Invezz - Crypto wrap: ETH, XRP and LTC see gains as Trump signs GENIUS Act into law — https://invezz.com/news/2025/07/18/crypto-wrap-eth-xrp-and-ltc-see-gains-as-trump-signs-genius-act-into-law/
Markets Insider - COIN, CRCL, MSTR: Crypto Stocks Fall After Trump Signs Stablecoin Bill into Law — https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/currencies/coin-crcl-mstr-crypto-stocks-fall-after-trump-signs-stablecoin-bill-into-law-1034893673
Decrypt - Trump's 'Big Beautiful Bill' May Get a 'Hail Mary' Bitcoin Tax Exemption — https://decrypt.co/327495/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption
Congress.gov — https://www.congress.gov/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate formally introduces legislation, or formally files an amendment in a publicly available congressional record, that would reduce, eliminate, or create an exemption from federal capital gains tax for at least some cryptocurrency transactions or dispositions.

For purposes of resolution:
- 'Formally introduced' means a bill or joint resolution receives an official entry on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/) with bill text, summary, or title sufficient to identify the provision, or an amendment is officially filed/published in Congress.gov or the Congressional Record (https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record).
- 'Cryptocurrency transactions or dispositions' includes sales, exchanges, payments, or other taxable dispositions of digital assets, virtual currency, cryptocurrency, Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, or similar terms used in the legislative text.
- Qualifying provisions include: full elimination of capital gains tax for covered crypto assets; a de minimis exemption for some crypto gains; exclusion of certain crypto dispositions from taxable gain; or a zero-rate treatment for covered crypto gains.
- Non-qualifying provisions include: rules only about information reporting, wash sales, staking timing, mining timing, mark-to-market accounting without any capital-gains relief, retirement-account access, securities/commodities classification, or corporate/company-specific relief not applicable to U.S. taxpayers generally.

Primary resolution source: Congress.gov bill and amendment records: https://www.congress.gov/
Secondary source if needed for amendment timing/text: Congressional Record on Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/congressional-record
Additional fallback sources if Congress.gov is temporarily incomplete: official House Clerk records (https://clerk.house.gov/) and official Senate legislative records via Senate.gov (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/).

If multiple versions exist, any one qualifying formal introduction during the window is sufficient for Yes. If a proposal is only rumored, discussed in media, circulated as a draft, or announced by lawmakers without formal filing/publication in the official legislative record during the 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-31 window, it does not qualify. If the only relevant filing occurs before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on whether Trump actually eliminates capital gains tax on crypto by the end of 2025. A formally introduced crypto tax-relief provision in October is a strong leading indicator because it shows there is real legislative vehicle text, sponsor commitment, and procedural momentum. Absence of any such filing by late October would weigh against year-end enactment.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles publicly list Tesla as holding an autonomous vehicle permit for driverless operation by 2025-09-08?
subquestions.background_information:
A key bottleneck for Tesla launching a qualifying driverless Robotaxi service is regulatory permission to operate without a human driver. Reporting before 2025-09-01 indicates Tesla's Austin rollout used human safety monitors in the passenger seat rather than a fully driverless configuration, and Texas had enacted a new law requiring a permit to operate self-driving vehicles on public roads without a human driver. CNA reported on 2025-06-22 that the new Texas law requires autonomous-vehicle operators to obtain approval from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles before operating on public streets without a human driver, with the law taking effect on 2025-09-01: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/texas-enacts-robotaxi-rules-eve-teslas-austin-rollout-5193281 . Reuters similarly reported that Texas created a permit requirement for autonomous vehicles effective September 1, 2025: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/texas-governor-signs-law-regulating-self-driving-vehicles-2025-06-21/ .

At the same time, multiple reports said Tesla's existing robotaxi offering was not yet fully driverless. The Express Tribune said Tesla's June Austin service included human 'safety monitors' in the front passenger seat: https://tribune.com.pk/story/2551981/teslas-robotaxi-wont-be-driverless-set-to-launch-with-human-monitors . Popular Mechanics likewise described the Austin fleet as operating with a safety monitor present: https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/a65200573/tesla-robotaxi-launch-human-passenger-seat/ . In California, regulators said Tesla lacked the permits for autonomous passenger service, and Tesla's Bay Area service used human drivers rather than a driverless setup: https://www.wired.com/story/tesla-robotaxi-bay-area-launch-human-driver/ and https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs .

Because the ultimate market resolves on whether Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service in 2025, public evidence that Tesla has obtained the newly required Texas permit for driverless operation would be a strong near-term indicator. If Tesla is not publicly listed as permitted in Texas shortly after the law takes effect, that would weigh against a launch in the remaining days of the market window.

Sources:
CNA - Texas enacts robotaxi rules on the eve of Tesla's Austin rollout - https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/texas-enacts-robotaxi-rules-eve-teslas-austin-rollout-5193281
Reuters - Texas governor signs law regulating self-driving vehicles - https://www.reuters.com/world/us/texas-governor-signs-law-regulating-self-driving-vehicles-2025-06-21/
Express Tribune - Tesla's robotaxi won't be driverless, set to launch with 'human monitors' - https://tribune.com.pk/story/2551981/teslas-robotaxi-wont-be-driverless-set-to-launch-with-human-monitors
Popular Mechanics - Elon Musk Promised Driverless Taxis -- Instead, You Get a Guy in the Passenger Seat - https://www.popularmechanics.com/cars/a65200573/tesla-robotaxi-launch-human-passenger-seat/
CPUC Autonomous Vehicle Programs - https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/regulatory-services/licensing/transportation-licensing-and-analysis-branch/autonomous-vehicle-programs
Wired - Tesla’s Bay Area Robotaxi Launch Isn’t Actually a Robotaxi Launch - https://www.wired.com/story/tesla-robotaxi-bay-area-launch-human-driver/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive), the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles publicly lists Tesla, Inc. (or a clearly identified Tesla-operated service/entity) as holding an active permit, approval, or equivalent authorization required under Texas's 2025 autonomous-vehicle law to operate a motor vehicle on public roads without a human driver physically present to drive it.

Primary resolution source: the Texas DMV website, including any permit holder lists, press releases, AV program pages, or official PDFs published by Texas DMV: https://www.txdmv.gov/ .

Secondary sources, if the Texas DMV publishes the decision in another official Texas source first, include the Texas Legislature's text of the enacted law and official state press releases confirming the permit status: https://capitol.texas.gov/ and https://gov.texas.gov/news . Credible reporting may be used only to identify the relevant official document, not as the final authority if official state records are available.

This question resolves No if no such public listing or official confirmation appears between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive).

Clarifications:
- A permit for testing with a human safety driver, a chauffeured service with a human driver, or any authorization that still requires a human driver physically controlling or ready to control the vehicle does not count.
- A mere application, statement of intent, or company claim that it has sought permission does not count.
- If Texas changes publication practices and no public list exists, an official Texas DMV press release or official government document explicitly stating Tesla has received the relevant driverless-operation authorization during the window will count.
- If official sources are unavailable or contradictory by 2025-09-08, and no clear determination can be made from official records, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: This is a distinct observable crux rather than a restatement of the ultimate question. The ultimate question asks whether Tesla actually launches a public fully driverless service. Obtaining a publicly visible Texas permit for driverless operation is an upstream prerequisite and a strong indicator of whether such a launch is plausible within days, especially given that Texas is the current focal market for Tesla's robotaxi efforts.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House pass at least one full-year FY2026 appropriations bill between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-29 (inclusive)?
subquestions.background_information:
This is a useful leading indicator for the ultimate question because avoiding a shutdown by January 31, 2026 depends on Congress making concrete progress on appropriations before the January 30 funding deadline. Current reporting indicates that nine of the 12 annual FY2026 appropriations bills were still unfinished after the 43-day shutdown ended in November 2025, and that stopgap funding for those remaining portions of government expires on January 30, 2026. See Washington Times, Dec. 26, 2025: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/26/stalled-spending-bills-put-congress-catch-up-mode/

As of early January 2026, congressional leaders were publicly expressing optimism that a new shutdown could be avoided, and bipartisan negotiators had reached top-line spending agreements for remaining bills. CBS News reported on Jan. 5, 2026 that Congress was advancing a minibus package and that appropriators had agreed on top-line spending levels, though obstacles remained. https://www.cbsnews.com/news/congress-government-shutdown-deadline-venezuela-operation-2026-01-05/

On Jan. 6, 2026, One America News reported lawmakers had unveiled a $174 billion bipartisan spending package covering Commerce, Justice, Energy, Water, Interior, and EPA, with a final House vote likely on Jan. 9. https://www.oann.com/newsroom/congress-debuts-174b-spending-package-as-jan-30-govt-shutdown-deadline-looms/

Other reporting suggests the perceived odds of another shutdown had fallen by early January, but not to negligible levels. Agri-Pulse wrote on Jan. 4, 2026 that Polymarket's implied likelihood had decreased from nearly 40% in mid-December to 28% as of Jan. 3. https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/22172-washington-week-ahead-congress-returns-amid-uncertainty-mid-term-politics

Because House passage of one or more full-year appropriations bills would be a concrete signal that the Republican-led House can govern around its internal divisions and move funding legislation, resolution of this subquestion should substantially inform expectations about whether there will be a shutdown by Jan. 31. It is also mildly relevant to the second leg of the ultimate question: successful House management of must-pass fiscal legislation can affect perceptions of Republican governing competence heading into the 2026 cycle, though the main informational value is about shutdown risk.

Sources:
Washington Times - Stalled spending bills put Congress in catch-up mode when lawmakers return in January - https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2025/dec/26/stalled-spending-bills-put-congress-catch-up-mode/
CBS News - Congress returns amid Venezuela operation and facing deadline to avert another government shutdown - https://www.cbsnews.com/news/congress-government-shutdown-deadline-venezuela-operation-2026-01-05/
One America News Network - Congress debuts $174B spending package as Jan. 30 govt shutdown deadline looms - https://www.oann.com/newsroom/congress-debuts-174b-spending-package-as-jan-30-govt-shutdown-deadline-looms/
Agri-Pulse - Washington Week Ahead: Congress returns amid uncertainty, mid-term politics - https://www.agri-pulse.com/articles/22172-washington-week-ahead-congress-returns-amid-uncertainty-mid-term-politics
Congress.gov - Appropriations - https://www.congress.gov/appropriations
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-29 inclusive, the U.S. House of Representatives passes at least one bill or joint legislative package that Congress.gov classifies as an FY2026 appropriations measure providing full-year appropriations through the end of fiscal year 2026 for any federal department(s) or agency(ies).

For this question, a qualifying measure must satisfy all of the following:
1. The passage vote must occur in the House during the window from 2026-01-09 through 2026-01-29 inclusive.
2. The measure must be an appropriations bill or minibus/omnibus appropriations package for FY2026, rather than a short-term continuing resolution extending funding for only a limited period.
3. The measure must provide full-year appropriations through approximately September 30, 2026 for at least one covered department or agency.

This question resolves No if no such House passage occurs between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-29 inclusive.

Primary resolution source: Congress.gov legislative records and bill pages, including roll-call status and bill summaries: https://www.congress.gov/

Suggested verification sources:
- House Clerk roll call votes: https://clerk.house.gov/Votes
- House Majority Leader schedule: https://www.majorityleader.gov/schedule/
- House Appropriations Committee: https://appropriations.house.gov/

If Congress.gov is temporarily delayed, the House Clerk's official roll-call record may be used first, with Congress.gov used as confirmation once updated. If a vote begins within the window but final official recording occurs after 2026-01-29, resolution should be based on the official date of House passage as listed by Congress.gov or the House Clerk. If no authoritative federal source clearly establishes passage of a qualifying full-year appropriations measure within the window, resolve No. If the relevant official records become unavailable and no equivalent authoritative congressional record can verify passage, the question should be treated as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A House-passed full-year appropriations bill is a concrete, near-term indicator that Congress is making real progress toward avoiding a January 30 lapse in appropriations. It is not a restatement of the shutdown question, because the government could still avoid a shutdown without such passage, or still shut down despite it. But the event is highly informative about whether Republican House leadership can assemble votes on must-pass funding legislation, which is central to the no-shutdown leg of the ultimate question.

question: Negative GDP growth in Q4 2025?
description:
"This market will resolve to 'Yes' if the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP 'Advance Estimate' for Q4 2025, scheduled for release by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on January 29, 2026, reports a growth rate below 0. Otherwise, this market will resolve to 'No'.

The GDP release will be available at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

Only the first available GDP report labeled as the 'Advance Estimate' will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates to the data will not be considered."

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis report that real personal consumption expenditures increased by less than 1.5% (annual rate) in its Advance Estimate for Q3 2025 GDP, released by 2025-10-30?
subquestions.background_information:
Household consumption is the largest component of U.S. GDP, so a weak personal consumption expenditures (PCE) reading in Q3 2025 would be an important near-term indicator that the economy may be losing momentum heading into Q4 2025. In the BEA's Q2 2025 advance GDP release, real GDP grew 3.0% at an annual rate, while real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 1.2% and the PCE price index rose 2.1% at an annual rate, indicating moderate but not especially strong underlying demand. See BEA's Q2 2025 advance release: https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-2nd-quarter-2025-advance-estimate and related GDP table materials at https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

Subsequent reporting on the Q2 second estimate said consumer spending in Q2 2025 was revised up to 1.6% annualized from 1.4%, while headline GDP was revised up to 3.3%, underscoring that consumption growth in the 1%–2% range is currently plausible and economically meaningful rather than extreme. Reuters-style coverage summarized this revision and linked some of the improvement to stronger consumer spending and AI-related business investment: https://www.zawya.com/en/world/americas/us-second-quarter-gdp-revised-higher-as-businesses-boost-investment-in-ai-q0j2q7p7.

A Q3 2025 PCE growth rate below 1.5% would therefore suggest softer domestic demand entering Q4, which would increase the chance that a shock from inventories, trade, or government spending could pull Q4 2025 headline GDP below zero. This is a useful crux because forecasters who differ on the ultimate question often disagree about whether consumer demand is resilient enough to offset other drags.

Sources:
BEA – Gross Domestic Product, 2nd Quarter 2025 Advance Estimate – https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-2nd-quarter-2025-advance-estimate
BEA – Gross Domestic Product data page – https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
Zawya/Reuters-style coverage of Q2 2025 revision – https://www.zawya.com/en/world/americas/us-second-quarter-gdp-revised-higher-as-businesses-boost-investment-in-ai-q0j2q7p7
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-30 and 2025-10-30 (inclusive), the first BEA release labeled the "Advance Estimate" for U.S. Gross Domestic Product for Q3 2025 reports that real personal consumption expenditures (consumer spending) increased by less than 1.5 percent at an annual rate.

It resolves No if, between 2025-10-30 and 2025-10-30 (inclusive), that same BEA Advance Estimate reports real personal consumption expenditures increased by 1.5 percent or more.

Primary source: the BEA Q3 2025 GDP Advance Estimate release and accompanying tables on the BEA GDP page: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product . The resolver should use the first available BEA release for Q3 2025 explicitly labeled "Advance Estimate," not later second or third estimates or annual revisions.

Operationally, use the value reported by BEA for real personal consumption expenditures growth (annual rate) in the Q3 2025 Advance Estimate tables or release text. If BEA presents the figure rounded to one decimal place, that rounded published figure governs resolution.

If the BEA does not publish a Q3 2025 Advance Estimate at any time between 2025-10-30 and 2025-10-30 (inclusive), this question should resolve as Unresolvable rather than Yes or No, because the qualifying release did not occur within the stated window.

Fallback source, only if the main release page is unavailable but the same BEA data are mirrored elsewhere on bea.gov, is any BEA-hosted PDF or table package linked from https://www.bea.gov/ or https://www.bea.gov/news/ that is clearly the Q3 2025 GDP Advance Estimate.
subquestions.rationale: Consumer spending is the core driver of domestic demand. If Q3 real PCE comes in below 1.5%, that would indicate weak momentum entering Q4 and make a negative Q4 2025 GDP print materially more plausible. This is not a restatement of the ultimate question because it tracks a different component-level indicator rather than Q4 headline GDP itself.

question: Will Russia capture Pokrovsk train station by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the Pokrovsk train station (48.284816377539386, 37.180016843748454) by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The train station will be considered captured if any part of the train station icon is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by October 31, 2025, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

Once Russia captures the train station, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Train station Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/pokrovsk+train+station.jpeg

Pokrovsk Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/Pokrovosk+Location.png

Location on Google maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/7cfvanMFiovHG2mp8

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map which will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will DeepStateMap show any Russian-controlled area on the E50/M30 highway inside Pokrovsk city limits by 2025-10-21?
subquestions.background_information:
Pokrovsk is a key logistics hub in Donetsk Oblast, and the train station sits near the center of the city. Control of a segment of the E50/M30 highway within Pokrovsk city limits would be a meaningful indicator of whether Russian forces are penetrating the urban area deeply enough to threaten or reach the train station soon after. The station itself is near 48.284816, 37.180017, while the city is centered farther west than the currently active front line shown on public mapping tools.

As of late August and September 2025, reporting suggested intense fighting around Pokrovsk but not confirmed Russian control of central Pokrovsk. Reuters reporting on 2025-09-03 noted that Ukraine's General Staff listed nearly 50 Russian attempts to break through defenses near Pokrovsk in a single day, underscoring the area as a major axis of advance: https://www.yahoo.com/news/russia-says-captures-half-ukrainian-172847943.html . Al Jazeera reported on 2025-09-04 that Dobropillia and Pokrovsk remained among the most intense battle zones and that Russia may have redeployed forces toward Donetsk for a renewed push: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/4/ukraine-knocks-out-russian-refineries-as-russia-kills-dozens-in-kyiv . The Moscow Times reported on 2025-09-17 that Russian forces had reached the outskirts of Pokrovsk but failed to secure it, and that some prior Russian advances nearby had been partially rolled back: https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/09/17/russia-inflates-battlefield-gains-after-a-costly-summer-offensive-a90427 . Meanwhile, Zelenskyy said on 2025-09-20 that Russian claims about imminent capture of Pokrovsk differed from battlefield reality: https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/09/20/7518650/ .

DeepStateMap is a widely used public control map for the war in Ukraine and is also named in the ultimate market's fallback resolution criteria. A Russian advance onto the main east-west highway inside the administrative urban area of Pokrovsk would likely imply growing pressure on the central city and raise the odds of eventual train-station capture, without merely restating the ultimate question.

Sources:
Yahoo/Reuters - Russia says it captures 'about half' of Ukrainian city Kupiansk, Kyiv denies report - https://www.yahoo.com/news/russia-says-captures-half-ukrainian-172847943.html
Al Jazeera - Ukraine knocks out Russian refineries as Russia kills dozens in Kyiv - https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/4/ukraine-knocks-out-russian-refineries-as-russia-kills-dozens-in-kyiv
The Moscow Times - Russia Inflates Battlefield Gains After a Costly Summer Offensive - https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2025/09/17/russia-inflates-battlefield-gains-after-a-costly-summer-offensive-a90427

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-21 inclusive, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) shows any area marked as Russian-controlled (typically red) overlapping the E50/M30 highway within Pokrovsk city limits.

For this question, the relevant road is the major east-west highway labeled E50/M30 on standard map layers through Pokrovsk. "Inside Pokrovsk city limits" means the portion of that highway lying within the urban area labeled Pokrovsk on widely used web maps such as Google Maps: https://maps.app.goo.gl/7cfvanMFiovHG2mp8 . If DeepStateMap's control shading clearly covers any part of that highway segment within the labeled Pokrovsk urban area during the resolution window, resolve Yes.

This question resolves No if no such Russian-controlled overlap appears on DeepStateMap at any time between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-21 inclusive.

Primary source: DeepStateMap live map and, if available, its daily map snapshots/posts: https://deepstatemap.live/ and https://t.me/DeepStateUA .

If DeepStateMap is temporarily unavailable, resolution should wait for restoration or archived snapshots for dates within the window. Reasonable archives include the Internet Archive if it captures the relevant map state: https://web.archive.org/ .

If DeepStateMap becomes permanently unavailable before 2025-10-21 and no reliable archived captures exist for the whole window, use the ISW map as a fallback only to determine whether clearly Russian-held territory reaches and overlaps the same E50/M30 segment inside Pokrovsk by map inspection: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375 . If neither source permits a confident determination, the question should be treated as unresolvable.

Temporary mapping glitches, obvious rendering errors, or one-off visual artifacts do not count. If a qualifying overlap appears and is later reversed, the question still resolves Yes, because occurrence at any time during the window is sufficient.
subquestions.rationale: The train station is in central Pokrovsk. Russian control touching the main east-west highway within the city would be a strong operational indicator that Russian forces have entered the urban core or are close to severing movement corridors, substantially increasing the chance of reaching the station before the ultimate deadline.

question: Brazil unemployment below 6.3% for Q4 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Brazil's unemployment rate for Q4 2025 is below 6.3% when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve according to IBGE's (https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego) public release of the Q4 2025 figure unemployment, expected in January 2026. If the publication of this figure is delayed beyond February 28, 2026 ET, this market will resolve according to the last published figure. 

Because this market's resolution source reports quarterly unemployment to one decimal point (e.g. 4.5%), this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

subquestions.question: Will Brazil's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate in the PNAD Contínua release covering the quarter ending in August 2025 be reported by IBGE as 5.5% or lower by 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
Brazil's labor market has tightened sharply in 2025, making near-term IBGE releases highly informative for whether Q4 2025 unemployment will end up below 6.3%. IBGE reported a record-low 5.8% unemployment rate for the quarter ending in June 2025, with employed persons at 102.3 million and average real income at a record level (Agência Brasil summarizing IBGE: https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/economia/noticia/2025-08/brazils-unemployment-falls-58-lowest-record). In mid-September, multiple reports citing the latest IBGE PNAD Contínua release said the unemployment rate for the quarter ending in July 2025 had fallen further to about 5.6%, again near or at a record low (Agência Brasil summary: https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/economia/noticia/2025-09/unemployment-falls-56-lowest-2012-shows-ibge; Exame discussion of IBGE data and economist expectations: https://exame.com/economia/brasil-atinge-pleno-emprego-com-baixa-informalidade-e-renda-recorde-do-trabalhador/). Exame also reported an economist projection that unemployment could fall to 5.5% in the quarter ending in August 2025, which is directly relevant because a realized figure at or below 5.5% would indicate the labor market entered Q4 from an exceptionally tight position. Since the ultimate question asks whether Q4 2025 unemployment will be below 6.3%, the next official PNAD Contínua print for the quarter ending in August is a strong leading indicator: if unemployment is already 5.5% or lower before Q4 is even complete, it becomes easier for the later Q4 reading to remain below 6.3% absent a sharp deterioration.

The resolution source should be IBGE's official PNAD Contínua monthly/quarterly unemployment publication page, which publishes the unemployment rate and typically includes both seasonally adjusted and unadjusted series for rolling quarters: https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/statistics/social/labor/16809-quarterly-dissemination-pnad2.html and the indicators portal at https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego. The August-ending quarter release is expected during October 2025, so it fits the required subquestion window.

Sources:
Agência Brasil - Brazil's unemployment falls to 5.8%, lowest on record - https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/economia/noticia/2025-08/brazils-unemployment-falls-58-lowest-record
Agência Brasil - Unemployment falls to 5.6%, lowest since 2012, shows IBGE - https://agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br/en/economia/noticia/2025-09/unemployment-falls-56-lowest-2012-shows-ibge
Exame - Brasil atinge 'pleno emprego' com baixa informalidade e renda recorde do trabalhador - https://exame.com/economia/brasil-atinge-pleno-emprego-com-baixa-informalidade-e-renda-recorde-do-trabalhador/
IBGE PNAD Contínua page - https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/statistics/social/labor/16809-quarterly-dissemination-pnad2.html
IBGE Indicators portal - https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, IBGE publicly releases a PNAD Contínua unemployment update for the rolling quarter ending in August 2025 and that release reports Brazil's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate as 5.5% or lower.

This question resolves No if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, IBGE publicly releases that rolling-quarter-ending-August-2025 figure and the reported seasonally adjusted unemployment rate is above 5.5%.

Primary source: IBGE official unemployment indicators/publications, especially the PNAD Contínua page and/or IBGE indicators portal:
- https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/statistics/social/labor/16809-quarterly-dissemination-pnad2.html
- https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego

If IBGE publishes the value in Portuguese but not English first, the Portuguese IBGE publication counts, provided it is on an official IBGE domain and clearly identifies the rolling quarter ending in August 2025 ("trimestre móvel encerrado em agosto de 2025") and the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate ("taxa de desocupação dessazonalizada").

If multiple IBGE tables/releases on the same publication date contain the figure, the seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate for Brazil in the main PNAD Contínua release or associated official tables controls. Resolution should use the percentage as published by IBGE to one decimal place.

If no qualifying IBGE release for the rolling quarter ending in August 2025 is published by 2025-10-31, this question should be considered unresolvable rather than inferred from media reports or unofficial calendars.
subquestions.rationale: The next official unemployment print is the most direct near-term signal of whether Brazil's labor market remains tight enough for Q4 2025 unemployment to finish below 6.3%. A reading of 5.5% or lower by late October would indicate sustained labor-market strength heading into Q4 and materially support a Yes outcome on the ultimate question.

question: Will Trump pardon Sam Bankman-Fried in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual receives a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve from Donald Trump by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for whether the individual is pardoned or not will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Sam Bankman-Fried or his legal team file any new clemency-related petition, application, or public request directed to the President of the United States or the Office of the Pardon Attorney between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
A near-term indicator for whether Donald Trump might pardon Sam Bankman-Fried in 2025 is whether there is visible movement toward clemency during October 2025. Reporting before 2025-10-01 indicates that Bankman-Fried and his parents have been seeking a pardon and consulting people connected to Trump's orbit. Decrypt reported in May 2025 that Sam Bankman-Fried was "reportedly campaigning for a pardon," with his parents and lawyers consulting with people close to Trump's inner circles: https://decrypt.co/319130/which-crypto-founders-are-seeking-pardons-from-president-trump . Coinspeaker similarly reported in May 2025 that Bankman-Fried's parents were seeking a presidential pardon and discussing options with legal experts and entities linked to Trump's administration: https://www.coinspeaker.com/sam-bankman-fried-release-earlier/ .

There is also a plausible political pathway for crypto-related clemency. Forbes reported in May 2025 that Trump had already been making significant use of pardons and commutations and that observers expected more such actions, including possible crypto-related ones: https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/05/28/trump-makes-news-with-more-pardons-and-commutations/ . Decrypt reported that Binance founder Changpeng Zhao had confirmed he was applying for a pardon, suggesting pardon-seeking by crypto figures was an active current phenomenon rather than a hypothetical one: https://decrypt.co/319130/which-crypto-founders-are-seeking-pardons-from-president-trump .

Meanwhile, Sam Bankman-Fried's direct criminal case remains active. Cointelegraph reported on 2025-09-11 that the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit scheduled oral arguments in his appeal for November 4, 2025, and noted his Bureau of Prisons projected release date as October 25, 2044: https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-court-hear-arguments-sam-bankman-fried-appeal-nov-4 . The existence of an upcoming appeal makes clemency activity especially informative: a fresh filing or public request in October 2025 would be concrete evidence that Bankman-Fried's camp is actively pursuing executive relief before year-end, which should increase the perceived odds of a Trump pardon by December 31, 2025.

Sources:
Decrypt - Which Crypto Founders Are Seeking Pardons From President Trump? https://decrypt.co/319130/which-crypto-founders-are-seeking-pardons-from-president-trump
Coinspeaker - FTX Founder Sam Bankman-Fried To Leave Jail Earlier https://www.coinspeaker.com/sam-bankman-fried-release-earlier/
Forbes - Trump Makes News With More Pardons And Commutations https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/05/28/trump-makes-news-with-more-pardons-and-commutations/
Cointelegraph - US court to hear arguments for Sam Bankman-Fried's appeal on Nov. 4 https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-court-hear-arguments-sam-bankman-fried-appeal-nov-4
U.S. Department of Justice - Office of the Pardon Attorney https://www.justice.gov/pardon
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive, there is credible public evidence that Sam Bankman-Fried, his attorneys, or an authorized representative acting on his behalf filed, submitted, or publicly announced a new clemency-related petition, application, request, or letter seeking a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve from President Donald Trump.

Qualifying evidence includes any of the following during the window 2025-10-01 through 2025-10-31: (a) an official court filing, Department of Justice filing, or Office of the Pardon Attorney record; (b) a public statement by Sam Bankman-Fried's lawyer or authorized spokesperson explicitly saying a clemency request was submitted during the window; or (c) at least two independent, credible news reports stating that a new clemency request or application was filed or submitted during the window.

This question does NOT resolve Yes merely because an older request, made before 2025-10-01, is reported on again in October. It requires a new filing, submission, or public request first made between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 inclusive.
